sourceDefinition: Herbage, (M, K,) whether fresh or dry: (M, * K, * TA:) or pasture, or herbage which beasts feed upon, (Fr, AHn, Zj, T, S, M, A, Msb, K,) of whatever kind, (AHn, Zj,) [or] not sown by men: (Msb:) it is, to cattle and other beasts, what fruit is to men: (Mujáhid, T, Msb:) or whatever grows upon the face of the earth; (Atà, Th, T, M;) whatever vegetable the earth produces: (K, * TA:) and also, green herbage, or plants: (K, * TA:) and, as some say, straw, (Jel in lxxx. 31, and TA,) because cattle eat it: (TA:) or herbage prepared for pasture and for cutting: (TA:) accord. to IF, (Msb,) dried fruits; because prepared for winter (Bd in lxxx. 31, and Msb) and for journeying: (Msb:) pl. (T, and MF from the Tes-heel of Ibn-Málik.) -A3- A^ab~a A^ab~ahu : see 1.

A^ajalN , (Msb,) It (a thing, Msb, [as, for instance, a thing purchased, and the price thereof, and a thing promised or threatened or foretold, and also payment for a thing purchased, and the fulfilment of a promise or threat or prediction, and any event,]) was, or became, delayed, postponed, kept back; [and therefore, future; ] syn. taA^ax~ara ; (K;) and A^ajala , aor. , inf. n. definition: , (S, Mughnee, K,) with the l quiescent, (Mughnee,) is written with kesr and with fet-h [to the medial letter, i.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mughnee, K,) with the l quiescent, (Mughnee,) is written with kesr and with fet-h [to the medial letter, i. e. ↓ A^ajilo as well as A^ajalo ] like nEm [which is written naEimN as well as naEamo ]: (TA:) it is a particle (Mughnee) denoting a reply; like naEamo ; (S, Mughnee, K;) importing acknowledgment of the truth of the speaker, to him who gives information; and the making a thing known, to him who asks information; and a promise, to him who seeks, or demands; (Mughnee;) i. e. It is as thou sayest [in the first case; and yes, or yea, in the same, and in the other cases]; (K voce basalN ;) therefore it occurs after such sayings as “ Zeyd stood ” and “ did Zeyd stand? ” and “ beat thou Zeyd: ” but ElMálakee restricts the information to that which is affirmative, and the saying expressive of seeking or demanding to that which is without prohibition: and it is said by some that it does not occur after an interrogation: (Mughnee:) Er-Radee says, in the Expos. of the Káfiyeh, after Z and others, that it is to denote acknowledgment of the truth of information, and does not occur after a saying in which is the meaning of seeking, or demanding: (TA:) or, accord. to Z and Ibn-Málik and others, it relates particularly to information: and accord. to Ibn-Kharoof, it occurs mostly after information: (Mughnee:) in the Expos. of the Tes-heel, it is said to be for denoting acknowledgment of the truth of information, past or other, affirmative or negative, and not to occur after an interrogation: (TA:) Akh says that it is better than naEamo (S, Mughnee, K *) after information, (Mughnee,) in acknowledging the truth of what is said; (S, Mughnee, K;) and nEm is better than it after an interrogation: (S, Mughnee, K:) so that when one says, sawofa ta*ohabu [Thou wilt, or shalt, go away], thou sayest A^ajalo [ Yes ]; and it is better than nEm : but when one says, A^ata*ohabu [Wilt thou go away?], thou sayest nEm ; and it is better than Ajl . (S.)

definition: The term, or period, of a thing: (S, K:) its assigned, appointed, or specified, term or period: this is the primary signification: (TA:) or the term, or period, and time of falling due, of a thing: (Msb:) pl.
sourceDefinition: The term, or period, of a thing: (S, K:) its assigned, appointed, or specified, term or period: this is the primary signification: (TA:) or the term, or period, and time of falling due, of a thing: (Msb:) pl. A=jaAlN . (Msb, K.) ― -b2- Hence, The period of women's waiting, before they may marry again, after divorce: as in the Kur ii. 231 and 232. (TA.) ― -b3- The period, or extremity of time, in which falls due a debt (K, TA) and the like. (TA.) You say, baAEahu A_iy~aAhu A_ilay A^ajalK [ He sold it to him for payment at an appointed period ]: and sal~ama Ald~aAraAhima fiY TaEaAmK A_ilay A^ajalK [ He delivered the money for wheat, or the like, to be given at an appointed period ]. (Msb in art. klA^ .) ― -b4- The term, or period, of death; (K;) the time in which God has eternally decreed the end of life by slaughter or otherwise: or, as some say, the whole duration of life: and its end: a man's life being thus termed: and his death, by which it terminates: (Kull p. 17:) the assigned, or appointed, duration of the life of a man. (TA.) One says, danaA A^ajaluhu , meaning His death drew near; originally, A@sotiyfaA='u AlA^ajali the completion of the duration of life. (TA.) In the Kur vi. 128, (see 2, above,) the meaning is, The term of death: or, as some say, the term of extreme old age: (TA:) or the day of resurrection. (Bd, * Jel.) The words of the Kur [vi. 2] vum~a qaDaY A^ajalFA wa A^ajalN masam~aY Einodahu mean [ Then He decreed a term, ] the term of death, and [ there is a term named with Him, ] the term of the resurrection: or the period between the creation and death, and the period between death and the resurrection; for Ajl is applied to the end of a space of time and to the whole thereof: (Bd:) or the meaning is, the period of sleep, and the period of death: (Bd, TA:) or the period of those who have passed away, and the period of those who remain and those who are to come: (Bd:) or the period of remaining in this world, and the period of remaining in the world to come: or in both instances death is meant; [ accidental, and natural; ] for the Ajl of some is by accidental means, as the sword, and drowning, and burning, and eating what disagrees, and other means of destruction; while some have their full periods granted to them and are preserved in health until they die a natural death: or the Ajl of some is that of him who dies in a state of happiness and enjoyment; and of others, that of him who reaches a limit beyond which God has no ? appointed, in the natural course of this world, any one to remain therein; and to both of these, reference is made in the Kur [xvi. 72 and] xxii. 5. (TA.) ― -b5- Sometimes, also, it means Destruction: and thus it has been explained as occurring in the Kur [vii. 184], where it is said, waA^ano EasaY A^ano yakuwna qadi A@ qotaraba A^ajaluhumo [ And that, may be, their destruction shall have drawn near ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: and ↓ A^urozN The pine-tree; syn. $ajaru AlS~anawobari : (K:) or this is called ↓ A^arorapN , and A^arozN is the pl.: (A 'Obeyd, S:) [or rather A^arozN is a coll. gen. n., and A^arozapN is the n. un.:] or the male of that kind of tree; (AHn, K;) as also ↓ A^arozapN ; (K;) and the author of the Minháj adds, it is that which does not produce fruit; but pitch ( zifot ) is extracted from its trunks and roots, and its wood is employed as a means of light, like as candles are employed; and it grows not in the land of the Arabs: A 'Obeyd says, ↓ A^arozapN is the name of a tree well known in Syria, called with us SanawobarN , because of its fruit: he says also, I have seen this kind of tree, called A^arozapN , and it is called in El-'Irák SanawobarN , but this last is the name of the fruit of the A^aroz : (TA:) or i. q. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: i. q. AlHi*aA='u [ The front, as meaning the part, place, or location, that is over against, opposite, facing, fronting, or in front ]. (Msb, and K &c. in art. H*w .) You say, huwabiA_izaAy^ihi He is over against, opposite to, facing, fronting, or in front of, him; syn. biHi*aAy^ihi , (S,) or muHaA*iyhi . (Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence, biA_izaA=y^ihi signifies also Corresponding to it; as when one says,] AlA^abojalu EiroqN mina Alfarasi wa AlbaEiyri biA_izaA='i AlA^akoHali mina AlA_inosaAni [ The Abjl is a vein of the horse and the camel, corresponding to the AkHl of man ]. (TA in art. bjl .) [You say also, waDaEa lafoZFA biA_izaA='i maEon~aY He applied a word, or phrase, as correspondent to an idea, or a meaning. ] -A2- A_izaA='N is also applied to a man, and to a woman, and to a number of persons, in senses here following. (TA.) You say, huwa A_izaA='u AlA^amori He is the manager, conductor, orderer, regulator, or superintendent, of the affair. (S, Msb, TA.) And in the same sense the word is used by Homeyd, in the phrase A_izaA='u maEaA$K [ The manager, or orderer, of the means of subsistence ], applied to a woman. (TA.) And in an instance in which a poet likens the A_izaA=' of a watering-trough or tank to the [stinking animal called] ZaribaAn : (S, TA:) in this case it means The water-drawer [of the trough or tank]. (As, IB, TA.) [But in relation to a watering-trough or tank, it generally has another meaning, which see below.] You say also, fulaAnN A_izaA='N maAlK (S) [ Such a one is ] a manager, tender, or superintendent, of cattle, or camels &c.; (K, * TA;) a good pastor thereof. (TA.) And A_izaA='u AlHarobi The vigorous wager, or prosecutor, of war. (K.) And fulaAnN A_izaA='u fulaAnK Such a one is the fellow and assistant of such a one. (TA.) And humo A_izaAw^uhumo They are their fellows, (K, TA,) who assist them, and order, or set in order, their affairs: (TA:) or they are those who order, or set in order, their affairs. (Msb.) And A_in~ahu laA_i zaA='u xayorK , and $~arK , Verily he is a possessor of goodness, and of evilness. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, AlA_izaA='u , (K,) or A_izaA='u AlEy$ , (TK,) The means of sustenance: or what has been caused, or occasioned, of plentifulness and easiness, and of superabundance, of sustenance. (K.) -A3- Also The place where the water is poured into the wateringtrough or tank; (As, S, K;) i. e. its fore part; [the part next to the well or other source whence it is filled; ] the hinder part, where the camels stand when they come to water, being called the Euqor : (S in art. Eqr :) or, accord. to AZ, a mass of stone, and what is put for protection [ of the brink of the trough or tank (as it is generally constructed of stones cemented and plastered with mud)] upon the place where the water is poured when the bucket is emptied: (S in the present art.:) or the whole ( jamiyE [said in the TA to be a mistake for jmE , but this I think extremely improbable,]) of what is between the wateringtrough or tank and the cavity of the well, [namely,] of the [ casing of stones, or bricks, called ] T~aY : (K:) or a stone, or skin, or jul~ap [i. e. a thing made of palm-leaves woven together, generally used as a receptacle for dates], put [ for protection ] upon the mouth [or part of the border where the water is poured in ] of the wateringtrough or tank: (K, * TA:) in the K, yuwDaEu EalayohaA AlHawoDu is erroneously put for ywDE EalaY fami AlHawoDi . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. A^aSorN , He, or it, (a thing, Ks,) confined, restricted, limited, kept close, kept within certain bounds or limits, shut up, imprisoned, held in custody, detained, retained, restrained, withheld, debarred, hindered, impeded, or prevented, him or it: (Ks, S, M, A, * K:) it straitened him. (TA.) You say, A^aSarotu Alr~ajula EalaY *`lika I confined, or restricted, the man to that thing, or affair. (Ks.) And A^aSarotuhu Eano HaAjatahu , and Eam~aA A^araAdahu , I withheld, restrained, or debarred, him from the thing that he wanted, and from the thing that he desired. (IAar.) ― -b2- A^aSara Albayota , aor. and inf. n. as above, He made, or put, to the tent an A_iSaAr . (K,* TK.) -A2- Also, aor. and inf. n. as above, He broke it. (ElUmawee, S, M, K.*) ― -b2- He inclined, or bent, it. (M, K* TA.) ― -b3- It inclined him, (As, S, K,) EalaY fulaAnK to such a one. (As, S.) See an ex. voce A=SirapN .

definition: A covenant, compact, or contract;
sourceDefinition: A covenant, compact, or contract; (S, K;) as also ↓ A^uSorN and ↓ A^aSorN : (K:) [see also wSorN :] any bond arising from relationship, or from a covenant or compact or contract, (Aboo-Is-hák,) and from an oath: (ISh:) a covenant, compact, or contract, which one does not fulfil, and for the neglecting and breaking of which one is punished: so in the Kur ii. 286: (I' Ab:) [see also what follows, in two places:] or a heavy, or burdensome, covenant, compact, or contract: so in the Kur iii. 75: (ISh, M:) so, too, in the same vii. 156: (T, M:) pl. A=SaArN , a pl. of pauc.: (M:) or a heavy, or burdensome, command; such as was given to the Children of Israel to slay one another: so in the Kur ii. 286, accord. to Zj. (TA.) ― -b2- A weight, or burden; (S, M, K;) as also ↓ A^uSorN and ↓ A^aSorN : (K:) so called because it restrains one from motion: (TA:) pl. as above. (M.) ― -b3- A sin; a crime; an offence; (S, M, K;) as also ↓ A^uSorN and ↓ A^aSorN : (K:) so called because of its weight, or burdensomeness: (TA:) or the sin of breaking a compact, or covenant: (Fr, Sh:) or a grievous punishment of a sin: so accord. to AM in the Kur ii. 286. (TA.) ― -b4- A thing that inclines one to a thing. (M, K.) [See also A=SirapN . It is said in the Ham (p. 321) that A^awaASiru is pl. of the former word: but it is evidently pl. of the latter.] ― -b5- A swearing by an oath which obliges one to divorce or emancipate or to pay a vow. (K, TA.) So in a trad., in which it is said, mano Halafa EalaY yamiynK A_iSorN falaA kaf~aArapa lahaA [ Whoso sweareth an oath in which is an obligation to divorce or emancipate or to pay a vow, for it there is no expiation ]: for such is the heaviest of oaths, and that from which the way of escape, or evasion, is most strait: the original meaning of ASr being a burden, and a binding. (TA.) -A2- The ear-hole: pl. A=SaArN (IAar, K) and A_iSoraAnN . (K.)

sourceDefinition: and ↓ A^ayoSarN (S, M, K) and ↓ A_iSaArapN and ↓ A=SirapN (M, K) A short rope, (S,) or small rope, (K,) by which the lower part of the [ kind of tent called ] xibaA=' is tied, or bound, (S, K,) to the peg: (S:) or a short peg, for the [ ropes called ] A^aTonaAb , with which the lower part of the [ kind of tent called ] xbA= is fastened: (M:) [or] A_iSaArN signifies also the peg, (K,) or short peg, (TA,) of the [ kind of tent-rope called ] Tunub : (K:) or a peg of the xbA=' : (Ibn-Es-Seed, TA:) pl. of the first A^uSurN (S, M) and A=SirapN ; (M;) and of the second A^ayaASiru . (S.) ISd thinks that ↓ A=SiraAt is the pl. of ↓ A=SirapN used in the first of the senses explained above in in the following verse: laEamoruka laA A^a*onuw liwaSoli daniy~apK wa laA A^ataSabaY A=SiraAti xaliyliY the poet meaning [ By thy life, I will not approach to hold loving communion, or intercourse, with an ignoble, or a low, female; ] nor will I direct my regard to the short ropes which bind [ to the pegs ] the lower part of the tent of my friend, coveting his wife, and the like: or he may mean nor will I direct my regard to the female relations of my friend, such as his paternal aunt, and his maternal aunt, and the like. (TA.) [See A=SirapN , below.] ― -b2- Also, the first, A thing by which things are tied firmly, or made firm or fast. (TA.) ― -b3- A thong of untanned hide which binds together the EaDudaAni of a camel's saddle: and A_isaArN is a dial. var. thereof. (M.) ― -b4- Also, (M, K,) and ↓ A^ayoSarN , (AZ, As, K,) A [ garment of the kind called ] kisaA=' in which dry herbage, or fodder, is collected: (M, K:) or a ksA=' filled with herbage, and tied: (AZ:) or a ksA=' in which is dry herbage, or fodder: otherwise it is not thus called: (As:) pl. [of the former] A^uSurN and A=SirapN ; (K;) and of the latter A^ayaASiru . (AZ.) ― -b5- And both words, (the former accord. to the S and M and K, and the latter accord. to As and the S and M and K,) Dry herbage, or fodder: (S, K:) or dry herbage, or fodder, collected together: (TA:) or dry herbage, or fodder, in a [ garment of the kind called ] ksA=' : otherwise it is not thus called: (As:) or dry herbage, or fodder, contained in a miHa$~ . (M.) [The following saying is cited as an ex. of the first of these significations:] lifulaAnK maHa$~N laA yujaz~u ↓ A^ayoSarahu [ To such a one belongs a place, or land, abounding with dry herbage, ] the dry herbage whereof will not be cut; (S;) meaning, because of its abundance. (TA.) ― -b6- Also, the former, A basket ( zabiyl or znobiyl , as in different copies of the K) in which goods, or commodities, ( mataAE ,) are carried: so called as being likened to the thing in which dry herbage is put. (TA.)

(S, M, A, Msb, K.) You say, balaga A^amadahu He, or it, reached, or attained, his, or its, utmost, or extreme, extent, term, &c. (Msb.) And Daraba lahu A^amadFA [ He assigned, or appointed, for him, or it, a term, or limit ]. (A.) And huwa baEiydu AlA=maAdi [ He is one whose limits are remote: A=maAdN being the pl.]. (A.) ― -b2- The period of life which one has reached; as in the saying, maA A^amaduka What is thy period of life which thou hast reached? (S.) ― -b3- Each of the two terms of the life of a man; i. e. the time of his birth, and the time of his death. (Sh, T.) El-Hasan [El-Basree], being asked by El-Hajjáj, maA A^amaduka , meaning What was the time of thy birth? answered by saying that it was two years before the expiration of 'Omar's reign as Khaleefeh. (T, L, from a trad.) ― -b4- The startingplace, and the goal, of horses in a race. (Sh, T, L.) ― -b5- (tropical:) Any space of time: (Er-Rághib:) a space of time of unknown limit. (Kull pp. 9 and 10.) ― -b6- Sometimes, (assumed tropical:) A particular time; as in the phrase A^amadu ka*aA The time of such a thing; like zamaAnu A^amadN . (Kull p. 10.) ― -b7- [It is also used for *w A^amadN , and (applied to a fem. n.) *aAt A^amadK , Having a term, or limit; limited in duration; as in the saying,] Ald~unoyaA A^amadN wAlA=xirpu A^abadN [ The present state of existence is limited in duration, but the final state of existence is everlasting ]. (Obeyd Ibn-'Omeyr, L in art. Abd .)

definition: pure raSaAS [or lead ]: or black riSiAS : (Msb:) i.
sourceDefinition: pure raSaAS [or lead ]: or black riSiAS : (Msb:) i. q. A^usorub~u ; (S, K;) i. e. raSaASN qaloEiY~N ; so says Kt; and Az says, I think it is an arabicized word: (TA:) or white Asrb~ : or black Asrb~ : or pure Asrb~ : (K:) or i. q. qazodiyrN [which is applied in the present day to tin, and pewter ]: (Kr:) El-Kásim Ibn-Maan says, I heard an Arab of the desert say, h`*aA raSaASN A=nukN , i. e. [ this is ] pure [ lead ]: (TA:) it is of the measure A^afoEulN , [originally A^aA^onukN ,] (S, K,) which is one of the forms of pls., (S,) like A^afolusN ; (Msb;) and there is no other word of this measure, (Az, S, K,) among sing. nouns, (Az, S,) except A^a$ud~N [originally A^a$odudN ], (S, Sgh, K,) and A=jurN in the dial. of those who pronounce it without teshdeed: (Sgh:) it is disputed, however, whether A^a$ud~N be a sing. or a pl.: (Az, TA:) [and as to A=jurN , see what follows:] or, accord. to some, (Msb,) A=nukN is of the measure faAEulN , (Kr, Msb,) and is the only word of that measure in Arabic: (Kr:) or it is a foreign word; and so are A=jurN and [the proper names] A=mulu and kaAbulu . (Msb.) It is said, in a trad., that he who listens to a singing female slave, A=nuk shall be poured into his ears (S, TA) on the day of resurrection. (TA.)

definition: , (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) and A^awaAhu , (M, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) and A^awaAhu , (M, Msb, K,) aor. yaA^owiY , (T, S, Msb,) imperative Aiywi (T,) inf. n. A^uwiY~u , (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) with damm, (K,) of the measure fuEuwlN , [originally A^uwuwYN ,] (S,) and A_iwiY~N , (Fr, M, K,) with kesr, (K,) and A_iwaA='N ; (S;) and Alyh ↓ A^w~Y , (M, K,) inf. n. taA^owiyapN ; (K;) and ↓ tA^w~Y ; (M, K;) and ↓ A@A^otawaY , (thus [more commonly Ay^twY ] accord. to a copy of the M,) or ↓ A@t~awaY , (K,) like A@t~axa*a , (TK,) and ↓ AiytawaY , (M, K,) both of the measure AftEl ; (TA;) and ↓ A=waY is used by some in the same sense, but rejected, in this sense, by several; (Msb;) the pronoun relating to a place of abode; (T, S, M, Msb, K;) He betook himself to it, or repaired to it, for lodging, covert, or refuge; (Mgh;) and [simply] he got him or got himself, betook himself, repaired, or resorted, to it; (T, Mgh;) he returned to it; (M;) he took up his abode in it; he lodged, or abode, or dwelt, in it. (Msb, K.) Hence, in the Kur [xi. 45], saA=wiY A_ilaY jabalK yaEoSimuniY mina AlmaA='i [ I will betake myself for refuge to a mountain that shall preserve me from the water ]. (S.) AlA^uwiY~u properly relates to living beings; but is used otherwise, metaphorically. (M.) In the saying of Lebeed, biSabuwHi SaAfiyapK waja*obi kariynapK lahu A_ibohaAmuhaA ↓ bimuwatrK taA^otaY [ With a morning-potation of clear wine ( xamorK being understood), and a female singer's straining of her chords, with a stringed instrument to which her thumb returns after the straining], he means taA^otawiY lahu , of the measure tafotaEilu , from A^awayotu A_ilayohi signifying Eudotu ; the w being changed into A [written Y ], and the Y , which is the final radical, being elided. (M. [But see another reading near the end of the first paragraph of art. Awl .]) A^awaY , aor. as above, inf. n. A^uwiYN , also signifies He turned away: and hence, [it is said,] A_i*o A^awaY Alfitoyapu A_ilaY Alkahofi [ When the young men turned away to the cave: though the verb may be here well rendered betook themselves for refuge ]. (Har p. 246.) You say also, A^awayotu A_ilaY fulaAnK , (A'Obeyd, T,) or lahu , (as afterwards written in a copy of the T,) [ I betook myself to such a one, or repaired to him, for lodging, covert, or refuge; or] I joined myself, got myself, betook myself, repaired, or resorted, to such a one: and accord. to AHeyth, A^awayotu fulaAnFA signifies the same; but he did not know A^awayotu to be syn. with A=wayotu as explained below. (T.) And A^awaY A_ilaY A@ll~`hi He returned unto God. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b2- A^awaY said of a wound: see 5. -A2- See also 4, in seven places. -A3- A^awaY lahu , (T, S, M, Mgh, K,) like rawaY , (K, TA,) but it would have been more explicit if the author of the K had said like ramaY , (TA,) [as is shown by the false reading in the CK, A^wiYa lahu karawiY~ ,] aor. yaA^wiY , (T, S, Mgh,) inf. n. A^awoyapN (S, K) and A_iy~apN , (S, Mgh, K,) with kesr, (TA,) [originally A_iwoyapN ,] the w being changed into Y because of the kesreh before it, (S,) or because combined with Y and preceded by sukoon [a mistake for “kesreh”], (IB as cited in the TA,) [in a copy of the T written Ay~ap , and in a copy of the M and in the CK Aay~ap ,] and maA^owiyapN , (S, M, K,) without teshdeed, (S, TA,) [in my copy of the Mgh written with tesh-deed,] and maA^owaAhN , (S, M, K,) He compassionated him; felt compassion, or pity, for him; (T, S, M, Mgh, K;) as also ↓ Ay^twY , (T, K,) of the measure AftEl . (TA.) In using the imperative form, you say, Aiwi lahu , [unless this be a mistranscription for Aiywi lahu ,] meaning Be thou compassionate to him. (T, TA.)

A^uwiYN , also signifies He turned away: and hence, [it is said,] A_i*o A^awaY Alfitoyapu A_ilaY Alkahofi [ When the young men turned away to the cave: though the verb may be here well rendered betook themselves for refuge ]. definition: A tumour, or swelling, or an inflation, in the navel;
sourceDefinition: A tumour, or swelling, or an inflation, in the navel; the like of which in the back is termed EujorahN : (IAar, IAth:) or the part of the navel-string which remains after it has been cut, when it is thick at the base, and fleshy at the neck, or slender part, with wind remaining in the enlarged part; as also ↓ bajarapN : (ISd, L:) or the navel, (L, K,) of a man and of a camel, (L,) whether large or not: (L, K:) and a knot in the belly: (L, K:) or a knotted vein in the belly; the like of which in the back is termed EujorapF : (L:) and (as some say, L) a knot in the face, and in the neck: (L, K:) pl. bujarN . (L.) [See also EujorapN .] ― -b2- [Hence,] *akara Eujarahu wabujarahu (tropical:) He mentioned his vices, or faults, and his whole state or case: (K:) or all his affairs; those which were apparent and those which were hidden: or his secrets: or his vices, or faults. (TA.) And A^afaDayotu A_ilayoka biEujariY wabujariY (tropical:) I have revealed to thee my vices, or faults; meaning, my whole state or case. (S.) And A^axobarotuhu biEujariY wabujariY (tropical:) I acquainted him with my vices, or faults, which I conceal from others, by reason of my confidence in him. (As.) And A^a$okuw A_ilaY A@ll~`hi EujariY wabujariY , said by 'Alee, (tropical:) I complain unto God of my sorrows and my griefs; (IAar, IAth;) meaning, all my affairs or circumstances; those which are apparent and those which are hidden. (IAth.) [See, again, EujorapN .] ― -b3- It is said in a prov., ↓ Eay~ara bujayorN bujarapo nasiYa bujayorN xabaraho , meaning (assumed tropical:) [ Bujeyr cast reproach upon ] his vices, or faults: [ Bujeyr forgot his own state or condition: ] or, as some say, they were two men: [so that the meaning is, Bujeyr reproached Bujarah: &c.:] (S:) accord. to El-Mufaddal, Bujeyr and Bujarah were two brothers, in an ancient age: but accord. to the lexicologists, the meaning is, that one affected with what is termed a bujorap in his navel reproached another for that which was in him. (Az, TA.)

definition: denotes a kind of matrimonial connection practised by people in the Time of Ignorance;
sourceDefinition: denotes a kind of matrimonial connection practised by people in the Time of Ignorance; i. e., A woman's desiring sexual intercourse with a man only to obtain offspring by him: a man of them used to say to his female slave or his wife, A^arosiliY A_ilaY fulaAn faA=sotaboDiEiY minohu [ Send thou to such a one, and demand of him sexual intercourse to obtain offspring ]; and he used to separate himself from her, and not touch her, until her pregnancy by that man became apparent: and this he did from a desire of obtaining generous offspring. (IAth, TA.) -A2- See also 4, in two places.

sourceDefinition: (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ baDoEN , (S, Msb, K,) some of the Arabs pronouncing it with kesr, (S, Msb,) [ A number under ten; and an odd number, meaning] a number between two round, or decimal, numbers; (AZ, K;) from one to ten [ exclusive of the latter ]; and from eleven to twenty [ exclusive of the latter ]; so accord. to Mebremán; (K;) i. e. Mohammad Ibn-'Alee Ibn-Ismá'eel the Lexicologist, Mebremán being his surname: (TA:) or from three to nine; (S, Msb, K [in the first and last the ns. being in the fem. gender; but in the second, masc.];) so accord. to Katádeh; (Mgh;) from three to less than ten: (Fr [the ns. of number in the masc. gender]:) or not less than three nor more than ten; (Sh [the first n. of number in the fem. gender, and the second masc.];) from three to ten: (Mgh [the ns. of number in the masc. gender]:) or to seven: (Mujáhid, Mgh:) or to five: (AO, K [the n. of number in the fem. gender]:) or from one to four: (AO, O, K [the ns. of number in the masc. gender]:) or to five; an explanation ascribed to AO: (TA:) or from four to nine; (ISd, K [the ns. of number fem.];) and this is the signification preferred by Th: (TA:) or it signifies five: (Mukátil [this n. of number masc.]:) or seven; (Mukátil, K [in the K this n. of number being fem.];) so accord. to some: (AO:) or ten: (Ed-Dahhák [this n. of number masc.]:) or an undefined number; gayoru maHoduwdK ; so says Sgh; [and the like is said in the Msb;] in the K, erroneously, gayoru maEoduwdK ; (TA;) because it means a portion, (Sgh, K,) which is undefined: (Sgh, TA:) it also signifies, with ten, [in like manner; i. e. ten and a number under ten; or the like: as] from thirteen to nineteen. (Msb.) When used as signifying from three to nine, (Mgh, Msb,) or to ten, or to seven, (Mgh,) [or to signify some number under ten, without another n. of number,] it is masc. and fem. without variation: (Mgh, Msb:) you say biDoEu rijaAlK From three to nine [&c.] men: and biDoEu nisowapK from three to nine [&c.] women: (Msb:) and biDoEu siniyna from three to nine [&c.] years: (S:) and fiY biDoEi siniyna [ in from three to nine, &c., years ]: (Kur xxx. 3:) and falabiva fiY Als~ijoni biDoEa siniyna [ And he remained in the prison from three to nine, &c., years ]. (Kur xii. 42.) But when used to denote a number above ten, (Mgh, Msb,) with a masc. n. it is with p , (↓ biDoEap ,) and with a fem. n. it is without p : (ISk, Mgh, Msb, K:) you say biDoEapa Ea$ara rajulFA From thirteen to nineteen [&c.] men: and biDoEa Ea$orapa A@moraA^apF from thirteen to nineteen [&c.] women: (S, Mgh, * TA:) like as you say valaAvapa Ea$ara rajulFA and valaAva Ea$orpa A@moraA^apF . (Mgh.) When you have passed the word denoting ten, (S, K,) [i. e.] to denote a number above twenty, (Msb,) it is not used: (S, Msb, K:) you do not say biDoEN waEi$oruwna , (S, K,) but nay~ifN waEi$oruwna ; and so in the cases of the remaining numbers: (S:) or you do say biDoEN waEi$oruwna : (Sgh, K:) accord. to AZ, (Msb,) you say biDoEapN waEi$oruwna rajulFA (Mgh, Msb, K) meaning Twenty and odd men: (AZ, TA:) and biDoEN waEi$oruwna A@moraA^apF (Mgh, Msb, K) meaning twenty and odd women: (AZ, TA:) but not the reverse: (K:) ISd says, we have not heard this, but there is no objection to it: (TA:) and Fr says, biDoEN is not mentioned save with ten and twenty to ninety; (IB, K;) not with what exceeds this: (IB:) you do not say biDoEN wamiAy^apN nor biDoEN waA^alofN , (IB, K,) but miAy^apN wanay~ifN [and A^alofN wanay~ifN ]: (IB:) it occurs in trads. with Ei$oruwna and with valaAvuwna . (TA.) ― -b2- biDoEN and ↓ baDoEN also signify A part, or portion, of the night: (K:) a time thereof. (Lh.) You say, maDaY biDoEN mina All~ayoli [ A part, or portion, of the night passed ]. (TA.) J mentions it with S [in the place of D ]; and explains it by jawo$N , q. v. (TA.)

Smt .] ― -b3- And [hence, app.,] Albalodapu One of the Mansions of the Moon, (M, K,) [namely, the Twenty-first Mansion, ] a patch of the sky, (K,) containing no stars, (M, K,) or containing only small stars, (T, * M,) between the naEaAy^im and saEod Al*~aAbiH : (M, K:) sometimes the moon declines from it, and takes as its mansion the qilaAdap : it [app. AlqlAdp , accord. to the K, but accord. to the TA Albldp ,] consists of six stars resembling a bow, (K,) in the sign of Sagittarius ( Alqawos ): (T:) or Albldp is one of the Mansions of the Moon, consisting of six stars of Sagittarius ( Alqws ), which the sun enters on the shortest day of the year: (S:) [see manaAzilu Alqamar , in art. nzl : in the K it is also said that ↓ Albaladu is a Mansion of the Moon; but this appears to be a mistake, occasioned by the accidental omission of the word Albalodapu ; though Albaladu would seem to be an appropriate name for the mansion next after the nEAy^m :] IF says that Albalodapu is a star, or an asterism, ( najomN ,) said to be the balodap , i. e. breast, of the Lion; not meaning the mansion thus called in the sign of Sagittarius: El-Hareeree finds fault with him for using this expression, [the bldp of the Lion,] but Ibn-Dhafr replies that it occurs in the language. definition: Confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course: [a pass.

(TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (K,) inf. n. A_ibohaAmN , (JK,) (assumed tropical:) It (a thing, or an affair,) was, or became, dubious, confused, or vague, (JK, K, TA,) so that one knew not the way, or manner, in which it should be engaged in, done, executed, or performed; (JK, TA;) as also ↓ Astbhm ; (JK, K, TA;) for which grammarians often use ↓ Anbhm ; but this has not been heard in the [classical] language of the Arabs: (MF, TA:) [said to be] from bahiymN denoting a colour, whatever it be, except that which is termed $uhobap , in which is no colour differing therefrom. (Har p. 50.) -A2- He closed, or locked, a door; (S, Mgh, TA;) [or, so that one could not find the way to open it; (see mubohamN ;)] and stopped it up. (TA.) [And hence,] one says of the thumb, tubohimu Alkaf~a , meaning It closes upon [the palm of] the hand, as a cover. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence also,] (assumed tropical:) He made a thing, or an affair, to be dubious, confused, or vague, (JK, TA, *) so that there was no way, or manner, of knowing it, (TA,) or so that one knew not the way, or manner, in which it should be engaged in, done, executed, or performed: (JK:) [in the former sense, or meaning (assumed tropical:) he made it to be dubious, confused, or vague, ] said of speech, or language, (K in art. gmD , &c.,) and of information, or news, or a narration; (Msb;) contr. of A^awoDaHa ; (TA in art. gmD ;) i. q. lmo yubay~ino . (Msb.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) He made, or held, a thing to be vague, or indefinite. (Mgh.) ― -b4- And, said of a prohibited thing, (assumed tropical:) He made it, or held it, to be not allowable in any manner, nor for any cause: (Az, TA:) or to be prohibited unconditionally. (Mgh.) [See mubohamN .] ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) He made a man to turn away, or withdraw, or retire, (JK, K,) Eano ka*aA from such a thing, (JK,) or Eani AlA^amori from the affair. (K.) -A3- Abhmt AlA^aroDu The land produced what is termed buhomaY : (JK, K:) or produced much thereof. (S.)

sourceDefinition: is pl. of ↓ bahomapN , (S, Msb, K,) as are also ↓ bahamN and bihaAmN , (K,) [or rather bahomN is a coll. gen. n., and ↓ bahomapN is its n. un., and ↓ bahamN is a quasi-pl. n., and] bihaAmN is pl. of bahomN , (S, Msb,) and bihaAmaAti is a pl. pl. [i. e. pl. of bihaAmN ]: (K:) ↓ bahomapN signifies A lamb, and is applied to the male and the female; (S, Msb;) or, accord. to a trad. in which it occurs, it is a name for the female; (IAth, TA;) but bihaAmN , which is applied to lambs when they are alone, as sixaAlN is to kids when they are alone, is also applied to lambs and kids together: (S, * Msb:) or, accord. to IF, bahomN signifies young lambs or goats: (Msb:) and accord. to AZ, (Msb,) or A'Obeyd, (TA,) ↓ bahomapN is applied to a lamb or goat, whether male or female, after the period when it is termed saxolapN , which is when it is just brought forth; (Msb, TA;) and its pl. is Abhm : (Msb: [so in my copy of that work, as though meant for A^abohumN ; but perhaps a mistranscription for Albahomu :]) or it is applied to a lamb or goat when just brought forth, i. e., before it is termed saxolapN : (Mgh: [and this is agreeable with its application in a trad. cited by IAth:]) or to the young one, not, as in the K, young ones, (TA,) of the sheep, and of the goat, and of an animal of the bovine kind (K, TA) both wild and not wild, alike to the male and the female, while small; or, as some say, when it has attained to youthful vigour: (TA:) Lebeed applies bihaAmN to the young ones of [ wild ] animals of the bovine kind: (S, TA:) accord. to Th, bahomN signifies young kids. (TA.) ― -b2- saEodu AlbihaAmi One of the Mansions (K, TA) of the Moon: (TA:) or two stars which are not of the Mansions of the Moon. (S and L and K in art. sEd , q. v.)

definition: A rock, or great mass of stone or of hard stone, (K, TA,) that is solid, not hollow.
sourceDefinition: A rock, or great mass of stone or of hard stone, (K, TA,) that is solid, not hollow. (TA.) ― -b2- And hence, accord. to some, (TA,) or because his condition is such that one knows not how to prevail with him, (Ham pp. 334 and 610,) A courageous man, (K, and Ham ubi suprà,) or a horseman, (AO, S,) to whom one knows not the way whence to gain access, or whence to come, (AO, S, K,) by reason of his great might, or valour: (AO, S:) or, as in the Nawádir, rajulN buhomapN signifies a man who will not be turned from a thing that he desires to do: (TA:) it is not applied as an epithet to a woman: (IJ, TA:) pl. buhamN . (S, A.) You say, huwa buhomapN mina Albuhami , meaning (assumed tropical:) He is a courageous man, of those to whom the approach is as though it were closed against his adversaries. (A, TA.) Accord. to IJ, it is an inf. n. used as an epithet, though having no verb. (TA.) [Hence,] it applies to one and to a number of persons. (Ham p. 494.) [For] it signifies also ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) An army: (S, K:) or courageous men, or courageous men clad in armour; because one knows not the way in which to fight with them: or, as some say, a company of horsemen: (TA:) pl. as above. (K.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) A difficult affair or case; (K, TA;) such that one cannot find the way to perform it, or manage it: pl. as above. (TA.) You say, waqaEa fiY buhomapK laA yut~ajahu lahaA (assumed tropical:) [ He fell into a difficult, or an embarrassing, case, which one knew not the way to manage ]. (TA.) The pl. is also explained as meaning (assumed tropical:) Dubious, confused, or vague, affairs or cases. (TA.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) Blackness. (TA.) ― -b6- And Albuhamu (assumed tropical:) The three nights in which the moon does not [ visibly ] rise. (TA.)

definition: , a word both sing.
sourceDefinition: , a word both sing. and pl., (Sb, S, K,) its alif [written Y ] being a denotative of the fem. gender, wherefore it is without tenween; (Sb, S;) or [it is written buhomFY , with tenween, for it is a coll. gen. n., and] its n. un. is buhomaApN , (S, K, and so in the JK,) its alif, some say, being a letter of quasi-coordination; but Mbr says that this is not known, and that the alif in a word of the measure fuEolY is nought but a denotative of the fem. gender; (S;) and the n. un. bhmAp is anomalous; (El-'Ash- moonee's Expos. of the Alfeeyeh of Ibn-Málik, § AltA^nyv ;) [ A species of barley-grass; app. hordeum murinum, or common wall-barley-grass; ] a certain plant, (Lth, JK, S, K,) well known; (K;) the sheep and goats, (Lth, TA,) or the camels, (JK,) are vehemently fond of it as long as it is green; (Lth, JK, TA;) but when it dries up, its prickles bristle out, and it repugns; (Lth, TA;) it is of the herbs ( buquwl ) that are termed A^aHoraAz [app. here meaning slender and sweet ] when fresh and when dry, and comes forth at first undistinguishably as to species, from the earth, like as does corn; then it becomes like corn, and puts forth prickles like those [ that compose the awn, or beard, ] of the ear of corn, which, when they enter the noses of the sheep or goats and the camels, cause pain to their noses, until men pull them out from their mouths and their noses; and when it becomes large, and dries up, it is a pasture that is fed upon until the rain of the next year falls upon it, when its seed that has fallen from its ears germinates beneath it. (AHn, TA.)

sourceDefinition: Black: (K:) pl. buhumN . (TA.) And [app. used also as a subst., signifying] A black ewe (K, TA) in which is no whiteness: pl. as above and buhomN . (TA.) ― -b2- Applied to a horse, to the male and the female, (S, * Mgh, * K,) Of one, unmixed, colour; in which is no colour differing from the rest: (S, Mgh, K:) pl. buhumN . (S.) laA A^agar~u wa laA bahiymN [ Not having a star, or blaze, on the forehead or face, nor of one, unmixed, colour, or not white nor black, (some such proposition as “This is a horse” being understood before lA ,)] is a prov. applied to a dubious, confused, or vague, affair or case. (TA.) ― -b3- A colour of one kind, (JK,) in which is no colour differing from the rest, (JK, and Har p. 50,) whatever colour it be, except that which is termed $uhobap : (Har ubi suprà:) or a colour that is clear, pure, or unmixed, not resembling any other, (AA, K, * TA,) whether it be black or any other colour, (AA, TA,) except, as Z says, that which is termed $uhobap . (TA.) ― -b4- A night in which is no light (JK, TA) until the dawn. (TA.) ― -b5- (tropical:) A sound, or voice, in which is no trilling, or quavering, or reiteration in the throat or fauces. (JK, K, * TA. *) ― -b6- Perfect, or complete, in make; as also ↓ mubohamN : pl. buhomN : so in the phrase in a trad. (respecting the day of resurrection, TA), yuHo$aru Aln~aAsu buhomFA , i. e. Mankind shall be congregated perfect, or complete, in make, without mutilation, or defect: (JK:) or the meaning here is, sound, or healthy: (S:) or not having any of the diseases or noxious affections of the present state, as blindness, and elephantiasis, and leprosy, and blindness of one eye, and lameness, &c.: (A'Obeyd, K, * TA:) or naked; (JK, K;) not having upon them anything to conceal them: (JK:) or not having with them anything (S, TA) of worldly goods or commodities. (TA.) ― -b7- (assumed tropical:) Unknown. (El-Khattábee, TA.) -A2- See also A_ibohaAmN .

definition: The thumb, and the great toe;
sourceDefinition: The thumb, and the great toe; (M, K;) the greatest A_iSobaE , (JK, T, S,) that is next to the forefinger, having two joints, so called because it closes upon [the palm of] the hand, as a cover; (T, TA;) the greatest of the A^aSaAbiE in the hand and in the foot: (M, K:) of the fem. gender, (S, Msb,) accord. to common repute; (Msb;) and sometimes masc.: (Lh, M, K:) and ↓ bahiymN signifies the same; mentioned by Az in the T, and by others; but Az adds that one should not say bihaAmN : (TA:) the pl. of AbhAm is A^abaAhiymu (JK, S, M, Msb, K) and A^abaAhimu , (M, K,) which latter is used by poetic license for the former, (M,) and A_ibohaAmaAtN . (Msb.) A^aqoSaru mino A_ibohaAmi AlD~ab~i [ Shorter than the great toe of the ( lizard called ) Db~ ], and mn AbhAm AlqaTaApi [ than the back toe of the ( bird called ) qTAp ], and mn AbhAm AlHubaAraY [ than the back toe of the ( bird called ) HbArY ], are proverbs of the Arabs. (Har p. 335.)

definition: , applied to a door, Closed, or locked, (JK, K,) so that one cannot find the way to open it: (JK, TA:) and stopped up: (TA:) or having a lock upon it, with which it is fastened.
sourceDefinition: , applied to a door, Closed, or locked, (JK, K,) so that one cannot find the way to open it: (JK, TA:) and stopped up: (TA:) or having a lock upon it, with which it is fastened. (Mgh.) ― -b2- A wall in which is no door. (TA.) ― -b3- A chest having no lock [ by means of which it may be opened ]. (IAmb, TA.) ― -b4- I. q. muSomatN [as meaning Solid; not hollow; in the CK A^aSomatu , which signifies the same]; as also ↓ A^abohamu : (K:) having no fissure in it: and ↓ the latter, applied to a heart is said to mean (assumed tropical:) impenetrable by admonition. (TA.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) A thing, or an affair, made to be dubious, confused, or vague; (JK;) [ such that there is no way, or manner, of knowing it; (see the verb;)] or such that one knows not the way, or manner, in which it should be engaged in, done, executed, or performed: (JK, S, Mgh, TA:) (assumed tropical:) speech, or language, [ that is dubious, confused, or vague, ] such that there is no way, or manner, of knowing it: (Mgh, TA:) applied to a road, (assumed tropical:) unapparent, or hardly apparent: (TA:) and, applied to the ordinance respecting the making up for the days in which one has broken a fast, [and to many other cases,] (assumed tropical:) undefined; in this instance meaning, as to whether the days may be interrupted, or whether they must be consecutive. (Mgh.) [Hence,] mubohamaAtN (assumed tropical:) Difficult things, or affairs, such that one cannot find the way to perform them. (TA.) And AlA^asomaA='u Almubohamapu , so termed by the grammarians, (assumed tropical:) The nouns of indication, (S, K,) such as h`*aA and h`w^ulaA='i and *aAka and A^uwlaAy^ika : (S:) accord. to Az, AlHuruwfu Almubohamapu signifies (assumed tropical:) the particles which have no derivatives, and of which the roots are not known, as Al~a*iY and maA and mano and Eano and the like. (TA.) ― -b6- Applied to a vow, and to [certain ordinances respecting] marriage and divorce and emancipation, (assumed tropical:) From which there is no getting out, or extricating of oneself; as though they were closed doors with locks upon them: (Mgh:) and, applied to prohibited things, (assumed tropical:) not allowable in any manner, (T, K, TA,) nor for any cause; (T, TA;) or prohibited unconditionally; (Mgh;) as the prohibition of [ the marriage with ] the mother, and the sister, (T, Mgh, * K, TA,) and the like: (T, TA:) such a woman is said to be mubohamapN EalaY Alr~ajuli (assumed tropical:) [ absolutely prohibited to the man; as though she were closed against him, or inaccessible to him ]. (Msb. [But in this last work it seems to be mvbohimapN , which is not agreeable with common usage.]) In the copies of the K, buhomN and buhumN are given as pls. of this word: but it seems that there is an omission or a misplacement in the passage; for these are said to be pls. of bahiymN , as shown above. (TA.) ― -b7- (assumed tropical:) In a state of swooning or insensibility, speechless, and without discrimination; in consequence of a blow [&c.]. (TA.) ― -b8- See also bahiymN .

definition: He followed; or went, or walked, behind, or after. (IAar, T.) You say, talawotuhu , (S, M, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. tuluw~N (S, M, Msb, K) and talowN , (Er-Rághib, MF,) I followed him or...
sourceDefinition: He followed; or went, or walked, behind, or after. (IAar, T.) You say, talawotuhu , (S, M, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. tuluw~N (S, M, Msb, K) and talowN , (Er-Rághib, MF,) I followed him or it; or went, or walked, behind, or after, him or it; (S, M, Msb, K;) namely, a man [&c.]; (S, Msb;) immediately, or without intervention; and sometimes it means bodily [or in reality ]; and sometimes, virtually, or in effect: (Er-Rághib:) and so talayotuhu ; (K;) and ↓ tal~ayotuhu , (As, * T, * K,) inf. n. tatoliyapN . (K.) The phrase, in the Kur xci. 2, waAlqamari A_i*aA talaAhaA means By the moon when its rising follows the rising thereof; i. e., the rising of the sun; at the beginning of the lunar month: (Bd:) or, when it follows in rising the setting thereof, (Bd, Jel,) on the night of the full moon: (Bd:) or, when it follows it in becoming round, and in fullness of light; (M, * Bd;) i. e., when it follows it in the way of imitation, and in respect of rank; for the moon borrows its light of the sun, and is to it in the place of a successor. (Er-Rághib.) Here, Ks pronounced tlAhA with imáleh, [either because talayotu is a dial. var. of talawotu , or] because, although it has w for its last radical letter, it occurs with words that may be so pronounced, namely, yago$aAhaA and banaAhaA . (M.) ― -b2- talawotu AlA^ibila (tropical:) I drove, or brought, or gathered, the camels together, from their several quarters: because the driver follows the driven. (A, TA.) ― -b3- huwa yatoluw fulaAnFA He imitates such a one, and follows what he does; he follows him in action. (T.) ― -b4- talaA , (T,) first pers. talawotu , (S, M, Msb, K,) aor. , (T,) inf. n. tilaAwapN , (T, S, M, Msb, K,) He read, or perused, or he recited, (T, M, K,) the Kur-án, (S, M, Msb, K,) or any discourse, or piece of language: (M, K:) or he followed it, (I'Ab, T, S, * M,) and did according to it; (I'Ab, Mujáhid, T;) namely, the Scripture: (I'Ab, Mujáhid, T, M:) or the inf. n. specially signifies the following God's revealed Scriptures, sometimes by reading, or perusing, or by reciting, and sometimes by conforming therewith [as well as by reading, &c., but not otherwise, for] every tilaAwap is qiraA='ap , but the reverse is not the case. (Er-Rághib, TA.) [You say also, talaA Ealayohi He recited, or related, to him a narrative &c.: see Kur v. 30, &c.] And fulaAnN yatoluw EalaY fulaAnK , and yaquwlu Ealayohi , Such a one lies, or says what is false, against such a one. (TA.) waA@t~abaEuwA maA tatoluwAl$~ayaATiynu , in the Kur ii. 96, means [ And they followed ] what the devils related, or rehearsed, ('Atà, T,) or spoke; (A'Obeyd, T;) or, what the devils of the Jinn, or of mankind, or of both, read, or recited, or what they followed, of the writings of enchantment: (Bd:) some here read ↓ tutal~iY . (T.) Hence the saying, laA darayota walaA talayota : (T:) or, accord. to Yoo, it is ↓ wlA A^atolayota : (T, S:) and others say that it is wlA A@y^otalayota , from A^alawotu . (T. [See these three readings explained in the latter part of the first paragraph of art. Alw .]) -A2- He remained behind, or held back. (IAar, ISk, T.) You say, talaA baEoda qawomihi He held back, or lagged behind, after his people, or company, and remained. (TA.) And talawotuhu , (AZ, A'Obeyd, T, S, M, K,) and talawotu Eanohu , (AZ, T, M, K,) aor. , (AZ, T,) inf. n. tuluw~N , (AZ, T, M,) I left him, and held back from going with him: (AZ, T:) I held back from him, or from aiding him, and left him: (AZ, A'Obeyd, T, S, M, K:) thus the verb bears two contr. significations. (K.) -A3- He bought a tilow , meaning the young one of a mule. (IAar, T, K.) -A4- taliyato liY mino Haq~iY taliy~apN , and tulaAwapN , aor. , (ISk, S,) inf. n. talFA , (TA,) There remained to me, of my right, or due, a remainder. (ISk, S.) And taliyato liY Einodahu taliy~apN There remained to me, with him, or there remained owing to me by him, a remainder. (As, T.) And taliYa mina Al$~ahori ka*aA , (M, K,) inf. n. talFA , (M,) There remained, of the month, such a portion. (M, K.)

(TA.)

definition: The body, with the limbs or members;
sourceDefinition: The body, with the limbs or members; syn. jisomN : and i. q. $axoSN [app. as meaning a person; not, as J seems to have held, a corporeal, or material, form or thing or substance, such as is seen from a distance; see jisomN ]: (K:) or, accord. to As, it has the latter meaning, i. q. $axoSN ; and jusomaAnN has the former meaning, that of jisomN (S, Msb) and jasadN : (Msb:) or, accord. to AZ, juvomaAnN is syn. with jusomaAnN , (S, Msb,) i. e. jasadN . (S.) One says, maA A^aHosana juvomaAna Alr~ajuli and jusomaAnahu , meaning [ How goodly, or beautiful, is] the body, or person, of the man ! (AZ, S.) J cites, as an ex. of this word in the sense of $xS , from a verse of Bishr, sanaAmN kajuvomaAni Albaniy~ipi A^atolaEaA observing that by Albny~p is meant the Kaabeh: but IB says that the right reading, as found in his poetry, is Albaliy~api , and A^atolaEu ; and that the meaning is, A [long] hump like the jvmAn [or body] of the she-camel that is placed [and confined without food or water until she dies] at the grave of a dead man. (TA.) One says also, jaA='anaA bivariydK kajuvomaAni AlmaA='i [ He brought us crumbled bread moistened with broth and piled up, like the body of the bird of the kind called qaTFA ]. (S.)

sourceDefinition: A bird, and a hare, and the like, that is confined or set up, to be killed; (A'Obeyd, S, Mgh;) that is made to cleave to the ground ( tujav~amu ), and then shot at, or cast at, until it is killed; (S, Mgh;) which manner of killing is forbidden: (S:) or any animal that is set up and shot at, or cast at, and [so] killed: (A'Obeyd, TA:) or a sheep, or goat, that is shot at with arrows: ('Ikrimeh, Mgh:) or a sheep, or goat, that is stoned (Sh, Mgh, TA) until it dies, and is then eaten. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, A, Msb,) inf. n. jar~N ; (S K;) and ↓ jr~r , inf. n. tajoriyrN (S K) [and app. tajir~apN , said in the TA to be of the measure tafoEilapN from Aljar~u ], with teshdeed to denote repetition or frequency of the action, or its relation to many objects, or intensiveness; (S;) and ↓ Ajtr~ , inf. n. AijotiraArN ; (S, L, K;) and ↓ Aijdr~ , inf. n. AijodiraArN ; (L, K;) in which the t is changed into d , though you do not say AijodaraA^a for AijotaraA^a , nor AijodaraHa for AijotaraHa ; (L;) and ↓ Astjr~ ; (K;) He dragged, drew, pulled, tugged, strained, extended by drawing or pulling or tugging, or stretched, (A, L, Msb, K,) a thing, (A,) or a rope, (S, Msb,) and the like. (Msb.) You say, jar~uwA A^a*oyaAlahumo They dragged along their hinder skirts. (A.) And Alr~umoHa ↓ AjAr~ He dragged, or drew along, the spear. (TA.) And AlHadiyva mino A^abaAEidi A^aToraAfihi ↓ fulaAnN yasotajir~u (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one draws forth talk, or discourse, or news, or the like, from its most remote sources ]. (A in art. bEd .) And maA Al~a*iY jar~aka A_ilaY h`*aA AlA^amori (assumed tropical:) [ What drew thee, led thee, induced thee, or caused thee, to do this thing ]. (TA in art. dEw .) ― -b2- Also jar~a , aor. , (TA,) inf. n. jar~N , (K,) (tropical:) He drove (camels and sheep or goats, TA) gently, (K, TA,) letting them pasture as they went along. (TA.) And jar~a AlA_ibila EalaY A^afowaAhihaA (tropical:) He drove the camels gently, they eating the while. (A.) ― -b3- [Hence,] ↓ halum~a jar~FA (tropical:) At thine ease. (TA.) ElMundhiree explains halhm~a jur~uwA as meaning (tropical:) Come ye at your ease; from Aljar~u in driving camels and sheep or goats, as rendered above. (TA.) You say also, kaAna *aAka EaAma ka*aA wahalum~a jar~FA A_ilaY Alyawomi (S, A, Msb, * TA) (tropical:) That was in such a year, and has continued to this day: (Msb, TA:) from Aljar~u meaning the act of “ dragging, ” &c.: (TA:) or from A^ajorarotuhu Ald~ayona , or from A^ajorarotuhu Alr~umoHa . (Msb.) jr~A is here in the accus. case as an inf. n., or as a denotative of state: but it is disputed whether this expression be classical or postclassical. (TA.) [See also art. hlm ] ― -b4- jar~a AlA^avara , said of a numerous army, means (assumed tropical:) [ It made a continuous track, so that ] it left no distinct footprints, or intervening [ untrodden ] spaces. (TA.) ― -b5- jar~ati Alxayolu AlA^aroDa bisanaAbikihaA (tropical:) The horses furrowed the ground with their hoofs. (As, A, TA.) ― -b6- jar~a jariyrapF , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. and , (K,) but the latter form is disallowed by MF as not authorised by usage nor by analogy, (TA,) inf. n. jar~N , (K,) He committed a crime, or an offence for which he should be punished, or an injurious action, (S, Msb, K, *) against ( EaliY [and A_ilaY , as in the K voce janaY ,]) another or others, (S, K,) or himself; (A, K;) [as though he drew it upon the object thereof;] syn. janaY jinaAyapF . (S, TA.) It is said in a trad., baAyaEahu EalaY A^ano laA yajur~a Ealayohi A_il~aA nafosahu [ He promised, or swore, allegiance to him on the condition that he should not inflict an injury, meaning a punishment, upon him but for an offence committed by himself; ] i. e., that he should not be punished for the crime of another, of his children or parent or family. (TA.) ― -b7- jar~a AlfaSiyla : see 4, in two places. ― -b8- [ jar~a AlHarofa fiY AlA_iEoraAbi , aor. , inf. n. jar~N , (assumed tropical:) He made the final letter to have kesreh, in inflection; i. q. xafaDa , q. v.:] Aljar~u is used in the conventional language of the Basrees; and AlxafoDu , in that of the Koofees. (Kull p. 145.) -A2- jar~N , (S, A,) inf. n. jaruwrN , (K,) (tropical:) She exceeded the [ usual ] time of pregnancy. (A.) (tropical:) She (a camel) arrived at the time [ of the year ] in which she had been covered, and then went beyond it some days without bringing forth: (S, TA:) or withheld her fœtus in her womb after the completion of the year, a month, or two months, or forty days only: (K, * TA:) Th says that she sometimes withholds her fœtus [beyond the usual time] a month. (TA. [See also jar~ato .]) (tropical:) She (a mare) exceeded eleven months and did not foal: (K, TA:) the more she exceeds the usual term, the stronger is her foal; and the longest time of excess after eleven months is fifteen nights: accord. to AO, the time of a mare's gestation, after she has ceased to be covered, to the time of her foaling, is eleven months; and if she exceed that time at all, they say of her, All~ayolapu . (TA.) (tropical:) She (a woman) went beyond nine months without bringing forth, (K, TA,) exceeding that term by four days, or three. (TA.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) It (the night, kbd ,) was, or became, long. (L in art. kbd .) ― -b3- jar~a , aor. , (TA,) inf. n. jar~N ; (K;) and ↓ Anjr~ ; (K;) (assumed tropical:) He (a camel) pastured as he went along: (IAar. K: [if so, the aor. is contr. to analogy:]) or he rode a she-camel and let her pasture [ while going along ]. (Kudot;.) ― -b4- jar~a Aln~awo'u biAlmakaAni (assumed tropical:) The nw' [or auroral setting or rising of a star or asterism supposed to occasion rain ] caused lasting rain in the place. (TA.)

definition: , (S, K,) inf. n. mujaArarapN , (TA,) or mujaAr~apN , (TK,) He delayed, or deferred, with him, or put him off, by promising him payment time after time; syn. TaAwalahu , (S,) or maA Tilahu : (K:) or...
sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) inf. n. mujaArarapN , (TA,) or mujaAr~apN , (TK,) He delayed, or deferred, with him, or put him off, by promising him payment time after time; syn. TaAwalahu , (S,) or maA Tilahu : (K:) or he put off giving him his due, and drew him from his place to another: (TA:) or i. q. jaAnaAhu , (so in copies of the K,) meaning, he committed a crime against him: (TK:) or HaAbaAhu . (TA, as from the K. [But this seems to be a mistranscription.]) It is said in a trad., laA tujaAr~ A^axaAka walaA tu$aAr~ihi , i. e. Delay not, or defer not, with thy brother, &c.: [ and do not act towards him in an evil, or inimical, manner; or do not evil to him, obliging him to do the like in return; or do not contend, or dispute, with him: ] or bring not an injury upon him: but accord. to one reading, it is laA tujaArihi , without teshdeed, from AljaroYu , and meaning, contend not with him for superiority. (TA.)

definition: He pierced him with the spear and left it in him so that he dragged it along: (S, K:) or so Ajr~hu Alr~umoHa : (A, Msb:) as though [meaning] he made him to drag along the spear.
sourceDefinition: He pierced him with the spear and left it in him so that he dragged it along: (S, K:) or so Ajr~hu Alr~umoHa : (A, Msb:) as though [meaning] he made him to drag along the spear. (TA.) ― -b2- He put the jariyr , i. e. the rope, upon his neck. (Har p. 308.) ― -b3- Ajr~hu jariyrahu [lit. He made him to drag along his rope; meaning,] (tropical:) he left him to pasture by himself, where he pleased: a prov. (L.) And Ajr~hu rasanahu [lit. He made him to drag along his halter; meaning,] (tropical:) he left him to do as he would: (S, K, TA:) he left him to his affair. (A, TA.) ― -b4- Ajr~hu Ald~ayona (tropical:) He deferred for him the payment of the debt: (S, A, K:) he left the debt to remain owed by him. (Msb.) ― -b5- Ajr~hu A^agaAniY~a (tropical:) He sang songs to him consecutively, successively, or uninterruptedly; syn. taAbaEahaA : (S, K, TA:) or (tropical:) he sang to him a song and then followed it up with consecutive songs. (A, TA.) ― -b6- Ajr~ lisaAna AlfaSiyli , (S,) or Ajr~ AlfaSiyla , (As, K, *) inf. n. A_ijoraArN ; (K;) and AlfaSiyla ↓ jar~a , (As K, *) inf. n. jar~N ; (K;) (tropical:) He slit the tongue of the young weaned camel, that it might not suck the teat: (S, K, TA:) or A_ijoraAru AlfaSiyli signifies (tropical:) the slitting the tongue of the young weaned camel, and tying upon it a piece of stick, that it may not suck the teat; because it drags along the piece of stick with its tongue: or AlA_ijoraAru is like Alt~afoliyku , signifying (assumed tropical:) a pastor's making, of coarse hair, a thing like the whirl, or hemispherical head, of a spindle, and then boring the tongue of the [ young ] camel, and inserting it therein, that it may not suck the teat: so say some: (ISk, TA:) the animal upon which the operation has been performed is said to be ↓ majoruwrN and ↓ mujar~N . (TA.) [But sometimes ↓ jar~a signifies merely He drew away a young camel from its mother: see xaliy~apN voce xaliY~N , in three places.] ― -b7- Hence, Ajr~ lisaAnahu (tropical:) He prevented him from speaking. (A.) 'Amr Ibn-MaadeeKerib Ez-Zubeydee says, falawo A^an~a qawomiY A^anoTaqatoniY rimaAHuhumo naTaqotu wal`kin~a Alr~imaAHa A^jar~ati [ And if the spears of my people had made me to speak, I had spoken; but the spears have prevented speech ]: i. e., had they fought, and shown their valour, I had mentioned that, and gloried in it, (S,) or in them; (TA;) but their spears have prevented my tongue from speaking, by their flight. (S, * TA.) -A2- Ajr~ as an intrans. verb: see 8. ― -b2- Ajr~t Albiy^oru (tropical:) The well was, or became, such as is termed jaruwr . (Ibn-Buzurj, TA.)

definition: , (S, Mgh, Msb,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. jarojarapN , (S, * K, * TA,) He (a stallion-camel) reiterated his voice, or cry, (S, * Mgh, Msb, K, *) or his braying, (TA,) in his windpipe. (S, * Mgh, Msb, K. *) ― -b2- He, or it, made, or uttered, a noise, sound, cry, or cries; he cried out; vociferated; raised a cry, or clamour. (TA.) (Mgh.) ― -b2- You say also, jarojarahu AlmaA='a He poured water down his throat so that it made a sound or sounds. (K, * TA.)

definition: (S, K) and ↓ jar~apN (K) A small piece of wood, (K,) or a piece of wood about a cubit long, (S,) having a snare at the head, (S, K,) and a cord at the middle, (S,) with which gazelles are caught: (S,...
sourceDefinition: (S, K) and ↓ jar~apN (K) A small piece of wood, (K,) or a piece of wood about a cubit long, (S,) having a snare at the head, (S, K,) and a cord at the middle, (S,) with which gazelles are caught: (S, K:) when the gazelle is caught in it, he strives with it awhile, and struggles in it, and labours at it, to escape; and when it has overcome him, and he is wearied by it, he becomes still, and remains in it; and this is what is termed [in a prov. mentioned below] his becoming at peace with it: (S, * TA:) or it is a staff, or stick, tied to a snare, which is hidden in the earth, for catching the gazelle; having cords of sinew; when his fore leg enters the snare, the cords of sinew become tied in knots upon that leg; and when he leaps to escape, and stretches out his fore leg, he strikes with that staff, or stick, his other fore leg and his hind leg, and breaks them. (AHeyth, TA.) naAwaSa Aljur~apa vum~a saAlamahaA He struggled with the jr~p and then became at peace with it [see above] is a prov. applied to him who opposes the counsel, or opinion, of a people, and then is obliged to agree: (S, * TA:) or to him who falls into a case, and struggles in it, and then becomes still. (TA.) And it is said in another prov., huwa kaAlbaAHivi Eani Aljur~api [ He is like him who searches in the earth for the ]. (AHeyth, TA.) In the phrase A_i*aA A^afolatato mino jur~atayohaA , in a saying of Ibn-Lisán-el-Hummarah, referring to sheep, [app. meaning When they escape from their two states of danger, ] by jr~tyhA he means their place of pasture ( Almajar~ ) in a severe season [when they are liable to perish], and when they are scattered, or dispersed, by night, and [liable to be] attacked, or destroyed, by the beasts of prey: so says ISk: Az says that he calls their mjr two snares, into which they might fall, and perish. (TA.)

definition: A mode, or manner, of dragging, drawing, pulling, tugging, straining, or stretching.
sourceDefinition: A mode, or manner, of dragging, drawing, pulling, tugging, straining, or stretching. (K.) -A2- The stomach of the camel, and of a clovenhoofed animal: this is the primary signification: by extension of its meaning, it has the signification next following. (Msb.) ― -b2- The cud which a camel [ or cloven-hoofed animal ] ejects from its stomach, (Az, S, * IAth, Mgh, Msb, K, *) and eats again, (K,) or chews, or ruminates, (Az, IAth, Msb,) or to chew, or ruminate; (S;) as also ↓ jar~apN : (K:) it is said to belong to the same predicament as baEor . (Mgh.) Hence the saying, laA A^afoEalu *`lika maA A@xotalafati Ald~ir~apu waAljir~apu I will not do that as long as the flow of milk and the cud go [the former] downwards and [the latter] upwards. (S, A. * [See also dir~apN .]) And Aujotulibati Ald~ir~apu biAljir~api [ The flow of milk was procured by the cud ]: alluding to the beasts' becoming full of food, and then lying down and not ceasing to ruminate until the time of milking. (IAar, TA.) And laA yaHonaqu EalaY jir~atihi (assumed tropical:) He will not bear rancour, or malice, against his subjects: : or, as some say, cross he will not conceal a secret: (TA:) and maA yaHonaqu EalaY jir~apK and maA yakoZimu ElY jir~apK (assumed tropical:) he does not speak when affected with rancour, or malice: (TA in art. Hnq :) [or the last has the contr. signification: for] laA yakoZimu EalaY jir~atihi means (tropical:) he will not be silent respecting that which is in his bosom, but will speak of it. (TA in art. kZm .) ― -b3- Also The mouthful with which the camel diverts and occupies himself until the time when his fodder is brought to him. (K.)

definition: (tropical:) A female that exceeds the [ usual ] time of pregnancy.
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) A female that exceeds the [ usual ] time of pregnancy. (A.) (tropical:) A she-camel that withholds her fœtus in her womb, after the completion of the year, a month, or two months, or forty days only; (K, * TA;) or, three months after the year: they are the most generous of camels that do so: none do so but those that usually bring forth in the season called Alr~abiyE ( AlmaraAbiyE ); not those that usually bring forth in the season called AlS~ayof ( AlmaSaAyiyf ): and only those do so that are red [or brown], and such as are of a white hue intermixed with red ( AlS~uhob ), and such as are ash-coloured: never, or scarcely ever, such as are of a dark gray colour without any admixture of white, because of the thickness of their skins, and the narrowness of their insides, and the hardness of their flesh. (IAar, TA. [See also 1: and see xaSuwfN .]) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) A she-camel that is made to incline to, and to suckle, a young one not her own; her own being about to die, they bound its fore legs to its neck, and put upon it a piece of rag, in order that she might know this piece of rag, which they then put upon another young one; after which they stopped up her nostrils, and did not unclose them until the latter young one had sucked her, and she perceived from it the odour of her milk. (L.) ― -b3- Also, applied to a horse, (S, A, K,) and a camel, (K,) (tropical:) That refuses to be led; refractory: (S, A, K:) of the measure faEuwlN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN ; or it may be in the sense of the measure faAEilN : (Az, TA:) or a slow horse, either from fatigue or from shortness of step: (A 'Obeyd, TA:) pl. jururN . (TA.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) A woman crippled; or affected by a disease that deprives her of the power of walking: (Sh, K:) because she is dragged upon the ground. definition: , (S, Mgh, Msb,) [aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, Msb,) [aor. ,] inf. n. jalaA='N , (Msb,) It (a thing, and (assumed tropical:) an affair, or a case, Mgh, or (assumed tropical:) information, or tidings, Msb,) was, or became, clear, unobscured, exposed to view, displayed, laid open, disclosed, or uncovered, (Mgh, Msb,) llin~aAsi to men, or the people; (Msb;) as also ↓ tjl~Y , said of a thing: (S, Mgh, Msb:) it ((assumed tropical:) information, or tidings, S, Msb, or (assumed tropical:) an affair, or a case, Mgh,) was, or became, apparent, or plainly apparent, overt, conspicuous, manifest, notorious, plain, obvious, or evident, (S, Mgh, Msb,) liY to me, (S,) or liln~aAsi to men, or the people. (Msb.) One says, Al$~amosu ↓ tjl~t The sun became unobscured, or exposed to view, and ceased to be eclipsed. (TA from a trad.) Er-Rághib says that ↓ waAln~ahaAri A_i*aA tajal~aY is sometimes by the thing itself; as in the phrase [in the Kur xcii. 2], falam~aA tajal~aY rab~uhu lilojabali [ By the day when it becometh clear, &c.]: and sometimes, by the case, and the action; as in the saying [in the Kur vii. 139], falam~aA tajal~aY rab~uhu lilojabali [ And when his Lord became manifested to the mountain ]: Zj says that the meaning in this instance is, appeared, and so say the Sunnees; El-Hasan says that the meaning is, tjl~Y biAln~uwri AlEaro$i [ became manifested by light, the light of the empyrean ]. (TA.) ― -b2- jalaA , [aor. ,] inf. n. jalaA='N (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and jalowN ; (K;) and ↓ AjlY ; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) He, (a man, Msb,) or they, (a company of men, Mgh, Msb,) went forth, or emigrated, (S, Mgh, Msb,) Eani Albaladi from the country, or town, (S, Msb,) and Eano A^awoTaAnihimo from their homes: (S, Mgh:) [like jal~a :] or they (a company of men) dispersed themselves, or became dispersed, Eani AlmawoDiEi , and minohu , from the place: (K:) or jlA means, in consequence of fear: and ↓ AjlY , in consequence of drought: (AZ, K:) or manozilahumo ↓ A^ajolawoA signifies they left their place of abode in consequence of fear; the verb in this case being trans. by itself: but if they have left for some other reason than fear, you say, Eano manozilihimo : (Msb:) accord. to IAar, jalaA signifies he fled, being driven away, from his home. (TA.) [See also 12.] ― -b3- jaliYa , aor. , inf. n. jalFA , He had that degree of baldness which is termed ↓ jalFA ; (K;) i. e. baldness of the fore part of the head; (S, K;) like jalahN : (S:) or baldness of half of the head; (S, K;) which is the beginning of SalaEN : (S:) or baldness less than what is termed SalaEN . (K.) And jalA Aljabiyni , inf. n. jalFA , signifies the same as jaliYa [ The part above the temple became bald ]. (A'Obeyd, TA.) -A2- jalaAhu , [aor. , inf. n., app., jilaA='N , or perhaps jalaA='N , but the former seems to be indicated by what follows;] (S, Mgh, Msb;) and ↓ jl~Ahu ; (MA;) He made it, or rendered it, clear, or unobscured; exposed it to view, displayed it, laid it open, disclosed it, or uncovered it; (S, Mgh, MA;) namely, a thing: (S, Mgh:) he made it, or rendered it, apparent, or plainly apparent, overt, conspicuous, manifest, notorious, plain, obvious, or evident; (S, Mgh, Msb, MA;) namely, (assumed tropical:) an affair, (Mgh,) or (assumed tropical:) information, or tidings. (Msb.) You say, jalaA AlEaruwsa , inf. n. jilaA='N and jilowapN (S, Msb, K) and jalowapN (Msb, K) and julowapN ; (K;) and ↓ AjtlAhA ; (S, Msb, K;) He displayed the bride, EalaY baEolihaA to her husband: (K:) or he looked at the bride displayed: (S:) and you say also, juliyato EalaY zawojihaA (TA) She mas shown to her husband, and he looked at her displayed: (Har p. 30:) and jalaAhaA zawojuhaA Her husband presented, or gave, to her a female slave (S, K) or some other thing at the time of her being displayed to him; as also ↓ jl~AhA : (K:) and jalati AlmaA$iTapu AlEaruwsa The female hairdresser adorned the bride [ to display her to her husband ]. (TA.) You also say, jalaA fulaAnN AlA^amora (tropical:) Such a one displayed, discovered, disclosed, revealed, or manifested, the affair, or case; as also ↓ jl~Ahu , and jalaA Eanohu : (K, * TA:) or jalaA fulaAnFA AlA^amori he displayed, discovered, &c., to such a one the affair, or case; as also ↓ jl~Ah [i. e. jl~Ahu AlA^amora ], and jalaA Eanohu [i. e. jlA Enh AlA^amora or jlA fulaAnFA Eani AlA^amori ]. (So accord. to the CK and my MS. copy of the K. [The reading in the TA is, in my opinion, preferable to the latter.]) And Als~aAEapa ↓ Aall~`hu yujal~iY (assumed tropical:) God will make manifest the hour, or time of the resurrection; or will make it to appear. (K in art. jlY : [but it belongs to the present art.:]) so in the Kur vii. 186. (TA.) And Eano nafosihi ↓ huwa yujal~iY (assumed tropical:) He declares, or explains, his mind. (S.) ― -b2- jalawotu Als~ayofa , inf. n. jilaA='N , (S, Msb, K, [in the CK jalA' , but it is]) with kesr, (S, Msb,) and jalowN , (K,) I removed, or cleared off, the rust from the sword; (Msb;) I polished, or furbished, the sword; (S, K;) and AlmiroA=pa the mirror; (K;) and the like; (TA;) [as, for instance,] AlfiD~apa the silver; and so jalayotuhaA . (K in art. jlY .) And jalawotu baSariY biAlkuHoli [ I cleared my sight with collyrium ]: (S:) [whence,] jalaA He applied collyrium to his eye or eyes. (IAar, TA.) And jalawotu ham~iY Ean~iY (tropical:) I removed my anxiety, or caused it to depart, from me: (S, K, * TA: *) and Eanohu Alham~a ↓ AjlY (assumed tropical:) He removed, or cleared away, from him anxiety. (Lth, TA.) And jalaA A@ll~`hu Eanohu AlmaraDa (assumed tropical:) God removed from him the disease. (TA.) ― -b3- jalaAhumo , and ↓ AjlAhm , (S, Mgh,) or jalaAhu , and ↓ AjlAhu , (Msb, K,) and ↓ AjtlAhu , (K,) He, (a man, S, Msb, or the Sultán, Mgh,) or it, (drought, K,) caused them, or him, to go forth, or emigrate; or expelled them, or him; or drove them, or him, forth; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) [from their homes, or from his home.] And jalaA Aln~aHoli , inf. n. jilaA='N , or jalaA='N , (accord. to different copies of the K,) and jlwp [thus written without any syll. signs]; and ↓ AjtlAhA ; (TA;) He smoked [ out ] the bees, in order to collect the honey; (K;) he drove away the bees by means of smoke. (TA.)

definition: (tropical:) A man who is well known, celebrated, or notable;
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) A man who is well known, celebrated, or notable; (Mgh;) of whom it is said, jalaA AlA^umuwra , i. e. he has made affairs clear, unobscured, or manifest; (S, Mgh;) or jalaA A^amoruhu , i. e. his case has become clear, unobscured, or manifest: (Mgh:) or one whose case is clear, apparent, plainly apparent, or manifest; (K, TA;) as also ↓ Aibonu A^ajolaY : (K:) applied to a man who is upon an elevated and conspicuous place; and applied by El-Hajjáj to himself, as meaning that he was one whom every one knew: (TA:) and also, (K,) for this reason, (TA,) the name of a certain man, (S, K,) well known, (K,) of the Benoo-Leyth, who was a person of great daring. (TA.) A poet says, (S,) namely, Soheym Ibn-Wetheel Er-Riyáhee, (TA,) A^anaA A@bonu jalaA waTal~aAEu Alv~anaAyaA mataY A^aDiEa AlEimaAmapa taEorifuwniY [ I am a man well known, celebrated, or notable, &c.; and he who rises to eminences, or who is accustomed to embark in, or surmount, lofty and difficult things: when I put down the turban, ye will know me ]. (S, TA.) Sb says, (TA,) jlA in this case is a verb in the pret. tense: 'Eesà Ibn- 'Omar says that when a man is named qatala or Daraba or the like, the word is imperfectly decl.; and he adduces, in evidence, this verse: others say that jlA may be here without tenween because it is imitative of a phrase, as though the poet said, A^anaA A@bonu Al~a*iY yuqaAlu lahu jalaA AlA^umuwri : (S, TA:) accord. to IB, it is without tenween because it is a verb with its agent [implied in it]. (TA.) ― -b2- Accord. to some, it signifies (assumed tropical:) The daybreak, or dawn; (Har p. 498;) and so ↓ Aibonu A^ajolaY : (TA:) accord. to Hamzeh, (assumed tropical:) the beginning of day: and accord. to some, (assumed tropical:) the moon. (Har ubi suprà)

definition: Going forth, or emigrating, from his country, or town: [like jaAl~N :] and so jaAliyapN , applied to a company of people;
sourceDefinition: Going forth, or emigrating, from his country, or town: [like jaAl~N :] and so jaAliyapN , applied to a company of people; [as also jaAl~apN ;] (Msb;) or to people who have gone forth, or emigrated, from their homes; (S;) and particularly to those tributaries, (Mgh, Msb,) namely, certain Jews, (Mgh,) whom 'Omar expelled from the country of the Arabs; (Mgh, Msb;) and afterwards, to such as have the poll-tax imposed upon them, of the people of the Bible, and of the Magians, though not having emigrated from their homes; (Mgh;) [i. e.] the free non-Muslim subjects of a Muslim government; because they were expelled by 'Omar from Arabia; (K;) the word being fem. because denoting a jamaAEap ; (Mgh;) and its pl. is jawaAlK . (Mgh, Msb.) ― -b2- Hence, (Msb,) ↓ jaAliyapN [as a subst.] is applied to The poll-tax that is exacted from the persons last mentioned above; (S, Mgh, Msb;) as also jaAl~apN : (S:) first, in this sense, applied to that which was exacted from the people expelled from Arabia by 'Omar. (Msb.) You say, AusotuEomila fulaAnN EalaY AljaAliyapi [ Such a one was employed as collector of the poll-tax ]. (S, Mgh, Msb.) -A2- See also jaAy^ilN , in art. jwl .

definition: , (S, K,) or AlmakaAna , (A, Mgh, Msb,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) or AlmakaAna , (A, Mgh, Msb,) aor. yajuwzu , (S, Msb,) inf. n. jawaAzN (S, Msb, K) and jawozN and juw^uwzN and majaAzN , (K,) He went, or passed, in, or along, the place, and left it behind; (Mgh, K;) [whether this be meant for one signification or two, does not appear; but in either case it is evident that one signification is he passed through, or over, or along, and beyond, the place; and this signification is of frequent occurrence;] as also jAz bihi ; (K;) and ↓ AjAzhu ; (Mgh;) and ↓ jAwzhu , (Mgh, K,) inf. n. jiwaAzN ; (K, TA; in the CK jawaAzN ;) and ↓ tjAwzhu ; (Mgh;) lit., he traversed, or crossed, its jawoz , i. e., middle, and passed through it: (Mgh:) or he went, or passed, in, or along, the place; (As, S, A, Msb, TA;) as also jAz bihi , and ↓ jAwzhu , (TA,) and ↓ AjAzhu , (A,) and ↓ AjtAzhu : (S: [so it appears from its being said that AijotiyaAzN is syn. with suluwkN :]) and in like manner, AlT~ariyaqa the road: (TA:) AlmwDEa ↓ jAwz and jAzhu signify the same: (TA:) or ↓ AjAzhu (As, S, Msb, K) and ↓ jAwzhu and ↓ tjAwzhu (A) signify he left it behind him, (As, S, A, K,) and traversed, or crossed, it; (As, S, A, Msb;) and ↓ jAwzhu and bihi ↓ jAwz also signify he left it behind. (TA.) You say, juzotu xilaAla Ald~iyaAri , which is like jusotu [ I passed amid, or among, the houses: (see the remarks on the letter z :) or I went to and fro amid, or among, the houses, in a hostile attack upon them: or went round about them ]. (Ibn-Umm-Kásim, TA.) And juzotu bika*aA , i. e., bihi ↓ Aijotazotu [ I passed by, and beyond, such a thing ]. (TA.) And jAz Ealayohi He passed by him, or it; syn. mar~a bihi , and Aimotar~a bihi and Ealayohi . (M and K in art. mr .) And jaAzahu He passed, or crossed, over it. (L.) jAz and ↓ AjAz are syn. [in this last sense]. (TA.) You say, AlS~iraATi ↓ A^aEaAnaka A@ll~`hu EalaY A_ijaAzapi (A, TA) May God aid thee [ to pass, or cross, over, or] to pass along, and to leave behind thee, the Sirát. (TA.) And it is said in a trad. respecting the Sirát, faA^akuwnu A^anaA Ealayohi ↓ waA^um~atiY A^aw~ala mano yujiyzu [ And I, with my people, shall be the first who will pass over it ]: yjyz being here syn. with yajuwzu . (TA.) ― -b2- juzotu Al$~aYo'a A_ilaY gayorihi : see 3. ― -b3- ↓ jAz Ald~irohamu fatajaw~azahu [ The piece of money passed, or was current, and he accepted it as current: in the TA written jAz Aldrhm ktjwzh , and without any syll. signs; but that the reading which I have adopted is right appears from what immediately follows:] a poet says, wazuy~afu [ Pieces of money whereof there are current and bad ]: and Lh mentions the saying, lamo A^ara Aln~afaqapa tajuwzu bimakaAnK kamaA tajuwzu bimak~apa [ I have not seen money for expenses pass away in a place as it passes away in Mekkeh ]: ISd says, He has not explained it, but I think that the meaning is tanofuqu . (TA.) ― -b4- jAz Al$~aYo'u , inf. n. jawaAzN , The thing was, or became, allowable; it passed for lawful: as though it kept the middle ( jawoz ) of the road. (TA.) You say, jaAza AlbayoEu , and Aln~ikaAHu , (A, Mgh,) and AlEaqodu wagayoruhu , (Msb,) [ The sale, and the marriage, and the contract, or other thing, was, or became, allowable; or] passed as right, sound, valid, or good [ in law: ] (Msb:) or had effect. (Mgh.) [And jAz lahu A^ano yafoEala ka*aA It was allowable to him to do so. And yajuwzu A^ano yakuwna ka*aA It may be so; or such a thing may be. ] -A2- jaAzahu in the sense of AjAzhu : see 4, second sentence, in two places.
