definition: -A2- AjAzhu He made him to go, or pass along;
sourceDefinition: : see 1, in six places. -A2- AjAzhu He made him to go, or pass along; as also ↓ jaAzahu : (TA:) he made him to pass through, or over, or along and beyond: (S, IF, Msb, K;) as also [ bihi ↓ jAwz , as will be shown by an ex. below, and ↓ jw~zhu , and ] ↓ jaAzahu , for which we find jAwzhu incorrectly substituted in the K. (TA.) A rájiz says, xal~uwA AlT~ariyqa Eano A^abiY say~aAraho Hat~aY yujiyza saAlimFA HimaAraho [ Leave ye the road to Aboo-Seiyárah until he make his ass to pass through, or over, safely ]. (S.) And it is said in the Kur [vii. 134, and x. 90], bibaniY A_isoraAy^iyla AlbaHora ↓ wajaAwazonaA [ And we made the Children of Israel to pass through the sea ]. (TA.) You say also lahumo A_ibilahumo ↓ jaw~aza , inf. n. tajowiyzN , He led for them their camels one by one until they passed. (K.) ― -b2- [ He made it to pass, or be current; as also ↓ jw~zhu : as in the following phrases.] A^ajazotu EalaY A@somihi i. q. jaEalotuhu jaAy^izFA [ I made his name to pass, or be current, by stamping money with it]: (ISk, S, TA:) and Darabotu [ I coined, or minted, money in his name ]. (ISd, TA.) And AlD~ar~aAbu Ald~araAhima ↓ jw~z , inf. n. tajowiyzN , [ The coiner, or minter, ] made the dirhems, or pieces of money, to pass, or be current. (Mgh.) ― -b3- He made it, or held it, to be allowable, or to pass for lawful; he allowed it, or permitted it; (S, K, TA;) as also ↓ jw~zhu : (S, TA:) syn. saw~aga : (S, K:) and syn. of A_ijaAzapN , [the inf. n. of the former verb,] A_i*onN . (K, TA: omitted in the CK.) You say, AjAz lahu maA SanaEa , (S, K, *) and lh ↓ jw~z , (S,) He made, or held, what he did to be allowable, &c. (S, K.) And AlEaqolu ↓ h`*aA mim~aA laA yujuw~izuhu [ This is of the things which reason will not allow ]. definition: The darkness of the night cleared away.
sourceDefinition: The darkness of the night cleared away. (A.) -A2- tjw~z fiY SalaAtihi He relaxed, or remitted, in his prayer; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K, TA;) and so in other things; (A;) and abridged it; and was quick in it: said to be from Aljawozu “the act of traversing, and going, or passing along:” (TA:) or did less than was sufficient in it. (Msb.) ― -b2- Hence, tjw~z fiY A^axo*i Ald~araAhimi , (A, Mgh,) or tjw~z Ald~araAhima , (K,) He accepted the dirhems, or pieces of money, as current; did not reject them: (A, Mgh:) see 1: or he accepted them as they were, or notwithstanding what was in them: (Lth, TA:) or he accepted them notwithstanding what was intermixed with them, (K, TA,) [ of bad money, ] concealed therein, and notwithstanding their fewness. (TA.) In the phrase Alt~ajaw~uzu biduwni AlHaq~i [ The accepting less than what was due ], the inf. n. is made trans. by means of bi because it implies the meaning of Alr~iDaA [which is made trans. by the same means]. (Mgh.) ↓ tajaAwazo also occurs in the sense of tajaw~azo in a trad. of Ibn-Rawáhah: h`*aA laka watajaAwazo fiY Alqasomi This is thine, or for thee, and be thou remiss, or not extreme, in, or with respect to, the division: and is allowable, though we have not heard it. (Mgh.) You say also, tajaw~aza fiY h`*aA AlA^amori maA lamo yatajaw~azo fiY gayorihi He bore patiently, or with silence and forgiveness, and with feigned neglect, or connivance, in this affair, or case, what he did not so bear in another. (K, * TA.) ― -b3- See also 6, in three places. -A3- tjw~z fiY kalaAmihi He made use of a trope, or tropes, in his speech. (S, K.) [See majaAzN , below.]

definition: The middle (S, K) of a thing, (K,) or of anything;
sourceDefinition: The middle (S, K) of a thing, (K,) or of anything; (S;) [as, for instance,] of a desert, (A,) and of a camel, (TA,) and of the night: (A, TA:) and the main part of a thing, (K,) or of the night: (TA:) pl. A^ajowaAzN ; (Sb, S, A;) beside which it has no other. (Sb.) -A2- [The walnut; or walnuts; ] a well-known fruit, (K,) which is eaten: (Msb:) a Persian word, (S,) arabicized; (S, Msb, K;) originally Gawozo : (Mgh, Msb, K:) n. un. jawozapN : (S, TA:) pl. jawozaAtN : (S, K, TA: in the CK jawozaAnN :) the tree thereof abounds in the land of the Arabs, in the province of El-Yemen, where it bears fruit and is cultivated; and in the Sarawát ( Als~arawaAt ) are trees thereof, which are not cultivated: the wood thereof is characterized by hardness and strength. (AHn. TA.) ― -b2- jawozu baw~ay , (K,) or jawozu baw~aA , with the short alif, as heard from the physicians, in Persian Gawozi buwyaA , (Mgh, under the letter b ,) [vulgarly called jawozu AlT~iybi , The nutmeg; ] a certain medicine; (K;) it is of the size of the gall-nut ( EafoS ), easily broken, with a thin coat, (Mgh, TA,) having a pleasant odour, (Mgh,) or a pleasant and sharp odour; and the best kind is the red, with a black coat, and heavy: (TA:) it is good for the [ affection of the face termed ] laqowap , strengthens the stomach and heart, and removes cold. (Sb.) -A2- [The walnut; or walnuts; ] a well-known fruit, (K,) which is eaten: (Msb:) a Persian word, (S,) arabicized; (S, Msb, K;) originally Gawozo : (Mgh, Msb, K:) n. un. jawozapN : (S, TA:) pl. jawozaAtN : (S, K, TA: in the CK jawozaAnN :) the tree thereof abounds in the land of the Arabs, in the province of El-Yemen, where it bears fruit and is cultivated; and in the Sarawát ( Als~arawaAt ) are trees thereof, which are not cultivated: the wood thereof is characterized by hardness and strength. (AHn. TA.) ― -b2- jawozu baw~ay , (K,) or jawozu baw~aA , with the short alif, as heard from the physicians, in Persian Gawozi buwyaA , (Mgh, under the letter b ,) [vulgarly called jawozu AlT~iybi , The nutmeg; ] a certain medicine; (K;) it is of the size of the gall-nut ( EafoS ), easily broken, with a thin coat, (Mgh, TA,) having a pleasant odour, (Mgh,) or a pleasant and sharp odour; and the best kind is the red, with a black coat, and heavy: (TA:) it is good for the [ affection of the face termed ] laqowap , strengthens the stomach and heart, and removes cold. (Mgh.) ― -b3- jawozu maAvilK [ The datura stramonium, or thorn-apple; ] also a certain medicine; (K;) having the property of producing torpor; resembling the jawozu AlqaYo'i (see what follows); having upon it small, thick thorns; and its seed is like that of the A^utoruj~ [or citror. ]. (TA.) ― -b5- jawozu Alhinodi [ The cocoa-nut; ] what is commonly called the naArajiyl . (TA.)

definition: (assumed tropical:) The act of watering, or giving to drink: (S:) or a single watering of, or giving drink to, camels.
sourceDefinition: (assumed tropical:) The act of watering, or giving to drink: (S:) or a single watering of, or giving drink to, camels. (TA.) definition: (assumed tropical:) A draught of water;
sourceDefinition: (assumed tropical:) A draught of water; (S, K;) as also ↓ jawozapN : (K:) or ↓ the latter signifies a single watering, or giving of water to drink; (S, K; [see an ex. in art. A*n , conj. 2;]) or such as a man passes with from one person to another: and ↓ both signify the quantity of water with which the traveller passes from one watering-place to another; as also ↓ jiyzapN . (TA.) It is said in a prov., vum~a yuw^u*~anu ↓ likul~i jaAbihK jawozapN , i. e., (assumed tropical:) For every one that comes to us for water is a single water-ing, or giving of water to drink; then he is repelled from the water: or, as in the M, then his ear is struck, to indicate to him that he has nothing more than that to receive from us. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (A, Mgh,) accord. to Aboo-Bekr, (TA,) [but see 4,] (assumed tropical:) A gift, or present: (Aboo-Bekr, S, Mgh, K:) pl. jawaAy^izu . (S, A, Mgh.) ― -b3- Hence also, (Mgh,) (tropical:) Kindness and courtesy: (K:) or kindnesses and courtesy shown to those who come to one as envoys or the like: (Mgh:) or provisions for a day and a night given to a guest at his departure after entertainment for three days. (Mgh, TA.) It is said in a trad., AlD~iyaAfapu valaAvapu A^ay~aAmK wajaAy^izatuhu yawomN walayolapN wamaA zaAda fahuwa SadaqapN , meaning, [The period of] the entertainment of a guest is three days, during the first of which the host shall take trouble to show him large kindness and courtesy, and on the second and third of which he shall offer him what he has at hand, not exceeding his usual custom; then he shall give him that wherewith to journey for the space of a day and a night; and what is after that shall be as an alms and an act of favour, which he may do if he please of neglect if he please. (TA.)

definition: A way, road, or path, (S, K, TA,) which one travels from one side [or end ] to the other;
sourceDefinition: A way, road, or path, (S, K, TA,) which one travels from one side [or end ] to the other; (K, TA;) as also ↓ majaAzapN . (TA.) You say, jaEala fulaAnN *`lika AlA^amora majaAzFA A_ilaY HaAjatihi (assumed tropical:) Such a one made that thing a way to the attainment of his want. (S, TA.) nahorK ↓ majaAzapu signifies A bridge. (A.) And ↓ majaAzapN alone [also] signifies A road ( TariyqapN ) in a saboxap [or salt tract ]. (K.) ― -b2- A privy, or place where one performs ablution; syn. mutabar~azN . (TA.) -A2- A trope; a word, or phrase, used in a sense different from that which it was originally applied to denote, by reason of some analogy, or connexion, between the two senses; as, for instance, A^asadN , properly signifying “ a lion, ” applied to “ a courageous man; ” (KT, &c.;) what passes beyond the meaning to which it is originally applied; (TA;) [being of the measure mafoEalN in the sense of the measure faAEilN ;] contr. of HaqiyqapN . (K.) [This is also called majaAzN lugawiY~N , and majaAzN lugapF ; to distinguish it from what is termed majaAzN EurofiY~N , and majaAzN EurofFA , which is A word, or phrase, so little used in a particular proper sense as to be, in that sense, conventionally regarded as tropical; as, for instance, daAb~apN in the sense of “ a man, ” or “ a human being; ” it being commonly applied to “ a beast, ” and especially to “ a horse ” or “ a mule ” or “ an ass. ”] A Haqiyqap , when little used, becomes what is termed majaAzN EurofFA . (Mz, 24th nwE .) The majaAz is either what is termed AisotiEaArapN [i. e. a metaphor ] (as A^asadN used as meaning “ a courageous man ”), or majaAzN murosalN [ a loose trope ] (as yadN used as meaning “ a benefit, ” “ benefaction, ” “ favour, ” or “ boon ”). (KT, &c.) [ majaAzN also signifies A tropical meaning. ]

definition: A commissioned agent of another;
sourceDefinition: A commissioned agent of another; an executor appointed by a will; syn. wakiylN , and waSiY~ ; because he executes what he is ordered to do: so in the conventional language of the people of El-Koofeh: (Mgh:) or a slave who has received permission to traffic. (Mgh, K.) ― -b2- The guardian and affiancer [of a woman]; syn. waliY~N . (K.) You say, h`*ihi A@moraA^apN layosa lahaA mujiyzN [ This is a woman who has no guardian and affiancer ]: and Shureyh is related to have said, A_i*aA A^anokaHa A@lomujiyzaAni faAln~ikaAHu liloA^aw~ali [ When the two guardians and affiancers give a woman in marriage, the marriage is the former's ]. (TA.) ― -b3- The manager of the affairs of an orphan. (K.)

HavowN and HavoYN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and taHovaA='N , (S,) He poured dust (Msb, TA) with his hand; (Msb;) threw it, or cast it; (TA;) or seized it with his hand and threw it; (Mgh, Msb;) Ealayohi [ upon him, or it ], (K,) and fiY wajohihi [ in his face ]: (S, Msb:) AlHavoYu and Alhayolu both signify the pouring of dust; but the former, not without [ first ] raising it; and the latter, the sending forth, or down, without raising. (Ham p. 477.) [See an ex. in a verse cited in art. AY , conj. 6.] Accord. to IAth, the saying, in a trad., AuiHovuwA fiY wujuwhi Almad~aAHiyna Alt~uraAba means (assumed tropical:) [ Repel ye with ] disappointment [ those who praise much ]: but some make it to have its overt meaning [of throw ye dust in the faces of those who praise much ]. (TA.) The verb is also used in relation to water; as in the saying, ↓ yakofiyhi A^ano yaHovuwa valaAva HavawaAtK , (Msb,) and kaAna yaHoviY valaAva HavayaAtK , (TA, [and the like is said in the Mgh,]) i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ It is sufficient for him to throw, and he used to throw, ] three handfuls [of water]. (Msb, TA.) ― -b2- HavaY said of a jerboa means He went so deep into his hole that he could not be dug out, the direction of his hole being unknown, and it being seen to be filled with dust, or earth, even with the rest of the ground. (TA in art. Hfr .) The jerboa throws up ( yaHovuw ) the dust, or earth, from his hole. (IAar, TA.) ― -b3- Havawotu lahu also means (assumed tropical:) I gave him something little in quantity, or paltry. (S, K.) -A2- You say also, HavaA Alt~uraAbu or HavaY , aor. yaHovuw and yaHoviY ; (K;) so in the copies of the K, but correctly yaHovaA , [or rather yaHovaY ,] which is extr., like jabaA [or jabaY ], aor. yajobaA [or yajobaY ], and qalaA [or qalaY ], aor. yaqolaA [or yaqolaY ]; i. e. The dust became poured; or thrown, or cast. (TA.)

definition: , (S, A, K, *) aor.

HadojN (S, K) and HidaAjN , (TA,) He bound the Hidoj upon him, i. e., upon the camel; (S, A, K;) as also ↓ AHdjhu : (K:) or he bound upon him the HidaAjap , i. e., the [ saddle called ] qatab and its apparatus; (Az, TA;) which apparatus consists of the bidaAdaAni with the two girths called the biTaAn and the Haqab , without which a camel is not [ said to be ] maHoduwj . (Sh, TA.) [See HidojN .] Accord. to J, Hadaja also signifies He bound loads, or burdens, and divided them into camel-loads: (TA:) but this is a meaning that was unknown to the Arabs. (Az, TA.) J cites as an ex. the words of ElAashà, A^alilobayoni tuHodaju A^aHomaAluhaA [ Is it for separation that her loads are bound &c.?]: but he adds that, accord. to one reading, the poet said A^ajomaAluhaA : and this [SM says] is the right reading. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, Hadaja is used to signify (tropical:) He betook himself to warring for the sake of the religion. ] 'Omar is related to have said, Hij~apN h`hunaA vum~a A@Hodijo h`hunaA Hat~aY tafonaY , meaning Perform one pilgrimage, then (tropical:) betake thyself to warring for the sake of the religion until thou become old and weak, or die; AHdj literally signifying bind the HidaAjap upon the camel. (Az, TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] Hadajahu , (TA,) inf. n. HadojN , (K,) (tropical:) He imposed upon him in a sale. (K, TA.) You say, Hadajotuhu bibayoEK sawo'K (A, TA) (tropical:) I imposed upon him with a bad sale, and bimataAEK sawo'K with bad merchandise. (TA.) The person imposed upon is likened to a camel upon which a HidaAjap is bound. (Az, TA.) ― -b4- And Hadajotuhu bimahorK vaqylK (tropical:) I imposed upon him a heavy dowry, by deceit and fraud. (A, TA.) -A2- Also, aor. , inf. n. HadojN , He cast Hadaj [or unripe and hard colocynths, or small colocynths, or small and green colocynths or melons, ] at him. (A, TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (A, TA,) Hadajahu bisahomK , (S, A,) inf. n. HadojN , (K,) (tropical:) He shot at him with an arrow. (S, A, K.) And Hadajahu biEaSFA , inf. n. HadojN , (tropical:) He beat him, or struck him, with a staff, or stick. (Ibn-ElFaraj, K, * TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] Hadajahu biAlt~uhamapi , inf. n. HadojN , (tropical:) He cast suspicion upon him. (K, * TA, * TK.) And Hadajahu bi*anobi gayorihi (S, A) (tropical:) He accused him of the crime, or offence, of another, (S, TA,) and put it upon him. (TA.) (Sh, TA.) [See HidojN .] Accord. to J, Hadaja also signifies He bound loads, or burdens, and divided them into camel-loads: (TA:) but this is a meaning that was unknown to the Arabs. (Az, TA.) J cites as an ex. the words of ElAashà, A^alilobayoni tuHodaju A^aHomaAluhaA [ Is it for separation that her loads are bound &c.?]: but he adds that, accord. to one reading, the poet said A^ajomaAluhaA : and this [SM says] is the right reading. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, Hadaja is used to signify (tropical:) He betook himself to warring for the sake of the religion. ] 'Omar is related to have said, Hij~apN h`hunaA vum~a A@Hodijo h`hunaA Hat~aY tafonaY , meaning Perform one pilgrimage, then (tropical:) betake thyself to warring for the sake of the religion until thou become old and weak, or die; AHdj literally signifying bind the HidaAjap upon the camel. (Az, TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] Hadajahu , (TA,) inf. n. HadojN , (K,) (tropical:) He imposed upon him in a sale. (K, TA.) (A, TA.) -A2- Also, aor. , inf. n. HadojN , He cast Hadaj [or unripe and hard colocynths, or small colocynths, or small and green colocynths or melons, ] at him. definition: A certain thing upon which the women of the Arabs of the desert ride;
sourceDefinition: A certain thing upon which the women of the Arabs of the desert ride; not a raHol nor a hawodaj : (Lth, TA:) a certain vehicle, or thing to ride upon, for women, (Az, S, A, K,) like the miHaf~ap , (Az, S, K,) and like the hawodaj ; (Az, TA;) as also ↓ HidaAjapN : (S, A, K:) pl. of the former HuduwjN and A^aHodaAjN (S, A, K) and HudujN ; (AAF, TA;) and pl. of the latter HadaAy^iju : (Yaakoob, S, A:) Az, however, says that ISk makes no difference between the Hidoj and the ↓ HidaAjap , though there is a difference between them accord. to the Arabs, as will be seen from what follows: Sh says that HidojN is a name given to a huwodaj bound upon a qatab [or small kind of camel's saddle ] when it is bound upon the camel at once with all its apparatus: he also says that ↓ HidaAjapN is a name given to the apparatus composed of the A^abid~ap ], pl. of bidaAdN , q. v.,] which are also called maxaAliY Alqatabi , [ and which are appertenances of the qtb ,] when they are filled, and drawn together, and bound, and tied to the qtb : [and he shows, in his explanation of the verb Hadaja , that this apparatus comprises the qatab and bidaAdaAni with the two girths called the biTaAn and the Haqab : this is what is meant in the K by the saying that ↓ AlHidaAjapu also signifies AlA^adaApu :] Aboo-Sá'id ElKilábee says that ↓ HdAjp signifies the apparatus ( AdAp ) of the qtb : and Az says that it signifies the qtb with its apparatus. (TA.) ― -b2- Also A load, or burden. (S, K.) ― -b3- And [its pl.] HuduwjN , Camels with their riHaAl [or saddles ]. (TA.)

definition: [an imperative verbal noun] meaning Beware;
sourceDefinition: [an imperative verbal noun] meaning Beware; be cautious, wary, or on thy guard; or take care. (S, A, K.) The poet (Abu-n-Nejm, TA) says, Ha*aAri mino A^aromaAHinaA Ha*aAri Beware of our spears: beware. (S, A.) And you say, sumiEato Ha*aAri fiY Easokarihimo [The cry “ Beware ” was heard in their army ]. (TA.) When the word is repeated, the second is sometimes with tenween: (K:) but this is only in poetry, when required by the metre, as in the following verse, cited by Lh: Ha*aAri Ha*aArK mino fawaArisi daArimK A^abaA xaAlidK mino qaboli A^ano tatanad~amaA [ Beware, beware of the horsemen of Dárim, O Aboo-Khálid, before that thou repent ]. (TA.) You say also, Ha*aArika , [with the k of allocution,] meaning Beware thou. (Lh, TA.) And when you caution a person [against another], ↓ Ha*araka zayodFA [ Beware thou of Zeyd ]; (K, * TA;) and Ha*aArayoka zayodFA , (K,) which latter means Beware thou, and beware thou again, of Zeyd: both then [also] being verbal nouns. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) aor. , inf. n. HazoqN , (K,) He tied, or bound, a thing (S, K) with a rope: (S:) he tied, or bound, it strongly with a rope. (TA.) ― -b2- He bound, or bound round, a foot, or a man. (K, accord. to different copies.) ― -b3- He strung a bow. (TA.) ― -b4- He pulled, or drew, a bond, and a bow-string, hard, or vehemently. (K.) ― -b5- He, or it, squeezed, pressed, compressed, or pinched, a thing. (K.) You say of a tight boot, Hazaqa rijolahu It compressed, or pinched, his foot. (K.) ― -b6- He straitened; made strait, or narrow. (TA.) ― -b7- HazaquwA bihi They surrounded, encompassed, or encircled, him, or it. (TA.) -A2- He broke wind: (K:) said of an ass. (TA.) Hence the saying of 'Alee, in disparagement of the schismatics, Hazoqu EayorK Hazoqu EayorK ; meaning “ the case is not as ye assert: ” said by El-Mufaddal to be a proverbial phrase, applied in relation to a man who relates a piece of information that is not complete nor realized. (TA.)

definition: and ↓ Huzuq~apN Short: or short in step by reason of the weakness of his body: (K:) or short, and short in step: (S:) or narrow in judgment: (K:) so As, in explanation of the latter word;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ Huzuq~apN Short: or short in step by reason of the weakness of his body: (K:) or short, and short in step: (S:) or narrow in judgment: (K:) so As, in explanation of the latter word; applied to a man and to a woman: (TA:) or this signifies short: and short and ugly: and the former, narrow in power and judgment, and avaricious, niggardly, or tenacious: (Sh, T, TA:) and the latter, (AO, TA,) or both, (K,) large-bellied and short, and, in walking, turning about his buttocks; as also ↓ A^uHozuq~apN and ↓ Hazuq~apN : [the last in the CK without teshdeed:] or [in the CK “ and ”] the first two words, and ↓ Hazuq~N and ↓ Hazuq~apN , a short man who is short in step by reason of his shortness or of the weakness of his body: or a man niggardly, or tenacious, of that which is in his hands; and the subst. [signifying the quality thus denoted] is ↓ HazaqN : (K:) also evil in disposition, (IAar, K,) and niggardly: (IAar, TA:) and straitened in circumstances: (Sh, K:) or AlHuzuq~apu [in the CK AlHuzaqapu ] signifies [sometimes] a sort of game; (K;) as in a trad., in which it is said of some girls, laEibona AlHuzuq~apa [ They played at the game of AlHzq~p ]. (TA.) Huzuq~apN Huzuq~aho taraq~a Eayona baq~aho (S, TA) is a saying of the Arabs, (S,) explained as meaning Short in step by reason of thy weakness, short in step &c., climb up, [ O eye of a gnat or musquito; ] and was said, as is related in a trad., by the Prophet, in dancing El-Hasan and El- Hoseyn; whereupon the child would climb up until he placed his feet upon the Prophet's chest: (TA:) Huzuq~apN is for A^anota Huzuq~apN , or yaA Huzuq~apu : (IAth, TA:) and taraq~a means AiroqaY , from raqiytu fiY Ald~arajapi : (S:) and Eayona baq~aho is an allusion to smallness of the eye, (IAth, TA, and Har p. 619,) as being likened to the eye of the gnat or musquito; or denotes smallness of person. (Har.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, Msb,) inf. n. Hak~N , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) [ He scratched, scraped, rubbed, grated, chafed, or fretted, it: or] he scraped off, abraded, or otherwise removed, its superficial part: (Mgh, Msb:) Hak~N signifies the act of scratching: (KL:) or the making a body to pass upon another body with collision: (K:) [as meaning scratching and the like,] it is with the nail, and with the hand, &c. (TA.) maA Hak~a ZahoriY mivolu yadiY [ Nothing has scratched my back like my hand ] is a prov., meaning that one should abstain from relying upon others: and the same meaning is intended in the following verse: maA Hak~a jilodaka mivolu Zuforiko fataw~ala A^anota jamiyEa A^amoriko [ Nothing has scratched thy skin like thy nail: so manage thou thyself all thine affair ]. (Har pp. 432 et seq.) The saying, in a trad., A_i*aA Hakakotu qaroHapF dam~ayotuhaA [lit. When I scratch a sore, I make it bleed, ] means (tropical:) when I desire an object, I attain it. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Hak~a fiY SadoriY , and ↓ AHk~ , and ↓ AHtk~ , (K,) the first whereof, which is mentioned by IDrd preceded by the negative maA , is the most approved, (TA,) (tropical:) It wrought, or operated, in, or upon, my mind: (K, TA:) said of a suggestion of the devil, that comes into one's mind. (TA.) Or Hak~a fiY Sadorihi ka*aA , aor. , means (assumed tropical:) Such a thing occurred to his mind as a thing outweighed in probability, or a matter of suspicion. (Msb.) And you say maA Hak~a fiY SadoriY (assumed tropical:) It did not make an impression upon my mind. (Har p. 648.) It is said in a trad., AlA_ivomu maA Hak~a fiY Sadorika (assumed tropical:) Sin is that which makes an impression upon thy mind, and induces a suspicion that it is an act of disobedience, because the mind is not dilated thereby. (Mgh. [See also HaAka , in arts. Hwk and Hyk ; and see Haz~a .]) You say also, maA Hak~a fiY SadoriY minohu $aYo'N (tropical:) Nothing thereof was unsettled, so as to be doubtful, in my mind. (S, TA.) And maA Hak~a fiY SadoriY ka*aA (tropical:) Such a thing did not cause dilatation [or pleasure ] in my mind. (S, K, TA.) -A2- See also 8. -A3- Hakikati Ald~aAb~apu , aor. , (Kr, K,) a verb of an unusual form, with the reduplication distinct, like laHiHato in the phrase laHiHato Eayonuhu , &c., (TA,) The beast had its hoof worn away at the edges. (K, * TA.)

definition: [ The rubbing-post;
sourceDefinition: [ The rubbing-post; i. e.] the thing that is set up in the place where camels lie down, at their watering-place, for the mangy camels to rub against it. (S, K.) Hence the saying of El-Hobáb Ibn-El-Mundhir El-Ansáree, (S,) A^anaA ju*ayoluhaA AlmuHak~aku waEu*ayoquhaA Almuraj~abu , [see ji*olN ,] meaning I am he by means of whose counsel, or advice, and forecast, relief is sought: (S, K: *) or it has another meaning, preferred by Az, i. e., that the sayer was one who had been strengthened by experience, who had experienced and known affairs, and been tried, or proved, by them, and found to be one who bore up against difficulty, strong and firm, such as would not flee from his adversary: or the meaning is, I am, exclusively of [the rest of] the Ansár, a rubbing-post for him who would oppose me, and with me should the stubborn be coupled: the dim. form is here used for the purpose of aggrandizement. (TA.) [See also HikaAkN .]

definition: A thing prohibited, or interdicted;
sourceDefinition: A thing prohibited, or interdicted; (S, K;) as also ↓ HimaA='N and ↓ HimoyapN ; (K;) and not to be approached: (S:) [and, as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant,] a place of herbage, or pasture, (Lth, Mgh, Msb, * TA, and Ham p. 539,) and of water, (Ham ibid.,) prohibited to the people, [i. e. to the public, ] (Lth, Mgh, and Ham ubi suprà,) so that they may not pasture their beasts in it, (Lth, Mgh,) nor approach it, (Mgh, Msb,) nor venture upon it: (Msb:) it was a custom of the noble among the Arabs, in the Time of Ignorance, when he alighted in a district [that pleased him], among his kinsfolk, to incite a dog to bark, and to prohibit for his own special friends or dependents the space throughout which the bark of the dog was heard, so that none else should pasture his beasts there; while he shared with the people in the other places of pasture, around it: but the Prophet forbade this: (Esh-Sháfi'ee, TA:) he said, “ There shall be no HmY except for God and for his Apostle; ” (Esh-Sháfi'ee, S, Mgh, TA;) meaning, except for the horses employed in war against the unbelievers and for the camels taken for the poor-rate: (Esh-Sháfi'ee, Mgh, TA:) afterwards, the term was applied in a general sense: (Esh-Sháfi'ee, TA:) the pl. is A^aHomaA='N (S and K in art. Hjr ) and A^aHomiyapN : (Ham p. 496:) and the dual is HimayaAni and HimawaAni ; (ISk, S, Msb, TA;) the latter irreg., (TA,) heard by Ks, but be preferred the former. (S.) You say, h`*aA $aYo'N HimFY This is a thing prohibited, or interdicted; not to be approached. (S.) And kalaA^N HimFY Herbage, or pasture, that is prohibited, or interdicted. (K.) -A2- See also HimaA='N .

definition: [act. part. n. of HamaY . And hence,] A stallion-camel that has prohibited, or interdicted, his back [to be used for bearing a rider or any burden]; ( Zahorahu ↓ HamaY ; Fr, S, K;) that is not...
sourceDefinition: [act. part. n. of HamaY . And hence,] A stallion-camel that has prohibited, or interdicted, his back [to be used for bearing a rider or any burden]; ( Zahorahu ↓ HamaY ; Fr, S, K;) that is not ridden, (Fr, S, Mgh,) nor shorn of any of his fur; (Fr, S;) that is left at liberty, not made any use of, (K,) nor debarred from pasturage (Fr, S, Mgh, K) nor from water: (K:) he is one that has long continued with a people: (S:) or whose offspring's offspring has conceived: (Fr, S Mgh:) or that has covered a certain number of times, or ten times: (K:) it is mentioned in the Kur [v. 102]. (S, Mgh. [See also baHiyrapN ]) ― -b2- AlHaAmiY is also an appellation applied to The lion; and so ↓ AlmaHomiY~u ; (K;) in the Tekmileh, AlHAmY and ↓ AlmuHomY [app. AlmuHomiY , as in a copy of the K]. (TA.) ― -b3- You say also, fulaAnN HaAmiY AlHaqiyqapi [ Such a one is the protector, or defender, of that which, or those whom, it is necessary for him, or incumbent on him, to protect, or defend ]; like HaAmiY Al*~imaAri [q. v. in art. *mr ]; and HaAmiY AlHumay~aA [explained in the next preceding paragraph]: pl. HumaApN and [coll. gen. n.] ↓ HaAmiyapN : (S:) this last word signifies a company, or party, protecting, or defending, their companions, (K,) or themselves: (TA:) and also a man who is a protector, or defender, of his companions (K) in war: (TA:) or a strenuous protector and defender of a party; for the p is to give intensiveness to the signification: (Mgh:) and you say, huwa EalaY HaAmiyapi Alqawomi , meaning He is the last of those who protect, or defend, the party in their going away (K) and in their state of defeat. (TA.) -A2- [ Hot: or vehemently hot. ] You say HadiydapN HaAmiyapN A piece of iron vehemently hot by means of fire. (Msb.) And qidoru Alqawomi HaAmiyapN tafuwru The people's cooking-pot is hot, boiling: meaning (assumed tropical:) the people are mighty, strong, or invincible, and vehemently impetuous in valour. (TA.)

definition: ― -b2- Also A great, or wide, or great and wide, mass of stone, ( HimaArapN K accord.
sourceDefinition: : see HaAmK . ― -b2- Also A great, or wide, or great and wide, mass of stone, ( HimaArapN K accord. to the TA,) or the stones, ( HijaArap , so in some copies of the K,) with which a well is cased: (K:) pl. HawaAmK : (TA:) or the latter signifies the stones &c. with which a well is cased, to protect its sides from becoming dirty and disordered: (Ham p. 62:) or great and heavy stones: and also large masses of rock which are placed in the last parts of the casing [ of a well ] if it falls out through age: they dig out hollows, and build them therein, so that they suffer not the earth to come near to the casing, but repel it: (ISh:) and all the stones [ of the casing ] of a well, matching one another, none of them larger than another. (AA.) ― -b3- The circuit of the solid hoof: (Ham p. 62:) or [the dual] HaAmiyataAni signifies the part on the right and left of the toe of the solid hoof: (AO, S:) or [the pl.] HawaAmK signifies the right and left edges of the solid hoofs; (As, TA;) between them are [ the ] nusuwr [or frogs ], like hard date-stones: (Aboo-Dáwood, TA:) or the right and left sides of the solid hoof. (K.) ― -b4- [The pl. also signifies The sides of a mountain. (Freytag, from the Deewán of Jereer.)] ― -b5- Also, the sing., i. q. A^uvofiy~apN [i. e. Any one of the three stones on which the cookingpot is placed ]: (AA, K:) pl. as above. (TA.) ― -b6- maDayotu EalaY HaAmiyatiY means I went my own way. (Sgh, K.)

HayoqN and HuyuwqN and HayaqaAnN , (K,) It surrounded, encompassed, encircled, or beset, him, or it; (S, K;) only used in relation to evil; (Bd in xvi. 36;) [as also HAq bh , aor. yaHuwqu , inf. HawoqN ;] and so bh ↓ AHAq . (Ibn-'Abbád, K.) So in the Kur [xxxv. 41], walaA yaHiyqu Almakoru Als~ay~iy^u A_il~aA biA^aholihi [ And evil artifice shall not beset any save the authors thereof ]: (S:) or this means shall not befall: (Msb:) [for] HAq bh , (Ibn-'Arafeh, Msb, K, *) aor. as above, (Msb, TA,) inf. n. HayoqN and HaAqN , (TA,) signifies [also] it clave to him, and became his due, (Ibn-'Arafeh, K,) and befell him: (Ibn- 'Arafeh, Msb, K,) and thus it is said to mean in the Kur [xi. 11, &c.], waHaAqa bihimo maA kaAnuwA bihi yasotahoziy^uwna [ And that at which they used to mock shall cleave to them, or be their due, or befall them; namely, the punishment at which they mocked.] (TA.) You say also, HAq bihimu AlEa*aAbu Punishment beset them, and befell them. (S.) And HAq bihi AlbalaA='u Trial, or trouble, beset him. (TA in art. Hq .) -A2- HAq fiyi , (K,) inf. n. HayoqN , (TA,) i. q. HAk . (K.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (Msb, K, TA,) inf. n. xaboTN , (Msb, TA, &c.,) He struck, or beat, (Msb, TA,) anything: (TA:) or he struck, or beat, it, or him, vehemently: (M, K, TA:) or xaboTN signifies a camel's striking, or beating, a thing with his fore foot: (T, TA:) or in the cases of beasts, ( dawaAb~ , [generally meaning horses and mules and asses,]) the striking, or beating, with the fore feet; not with the hind feet: and in the case of the camel, with the fore foot and the hind foot: or vehement treading; or of the fore feet of beasts ( dwAb~ ): (TA:) or, accord. to the Keshsháf, the act of striking, or beating, in a way that is not right: or, as some say, the going, or journeying, upon what is not the middle, or main part, of the road, or what is not the main road, or upon a road not open to view: or continuous, or consecutive, striking, or beating, in different ways: and afterwards tropically applied to any (tropical:) beating, or striking, that is not approved: or originally, the striking, or beating, with the fore foot or the hind foot, and the like: (MF, TA:) with the fore feet or legs, it is like ramoHN with the hind feet or legs. (TA.) You say, of a camel, xabaTa AlA^aroDa , (Msb,) or xabaTa AlA^aroDa biyadihi , (S, K,) inf. n. as above, (S,) He struck, or beat, the ground with his fore foot: (S, Msb:) or he struck, or beat, vehemently the ground with his fore foot; and ↓ txb~T and ↓ AxtbT signify the same: (K:) it is said in the O that xabaTahu signifies he struck him with his fore foot, or hand, and prostrated him, as also ↓ txb~Thu : and ↓ AxtbT , said of a camel, is syn. with xabaTa : and in the T, that birijolihi ↓ taxab~aTaniY is syn, with xabaTaniY . (TA.) Hence the trad., laA taxobiTuwA xaboTa Aljamali [lit. Ye shall not beat the ground as the camel does with his fore foot in rising]; meant to forbid a man's putting forward his foot in rising from prostration [in prayer]. (TA.) And xabaTahu , (K, TA,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) signifies also He trod him, or it, vehemently, (K, TA,) as the camel does with his fore foot. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (S,) fulaAnN yaxobiTu xaboTa Ea$owaA='a (S, * TA) (tropical:) [ Such a one goes at random, in a headstrong and reckless manner, ] like the weak-sighted she-camel that beats the ground with her fore feet ( taxobiTu ) as she goes along, not guarding herself from anything. (S, TA.) It is a prov., applied to him who turns away from a thing as though he were not cognizant of it: or to him who is continually falling into a thing. (Har p. 239.) Zuheyr says, raA^ayotu AlmanaAyaA xaboTa Ea$owaA='a mano tuSibo tumitohu wamano tuxoTiy^o yuEam~aro fayahorami I saw the fates [ treading mankind ] like the treading of the weak-sighted she-camel; whom they smote, him they killed: and whom they missed, he was made to continue in life so that he lived to extreme old age. (TA, and EM p. 132.) In like manner you say, fulaAnN yaxobiTu fiY EamoyaA='a (tropical:) Such a one undertakes what he undertakes with ignorance. (TA.) And xabaTa A^amorahu EalaY gayori baSyrapK (assumed tropical:) [ He prosecuted his affair without mental perception, or without certainty ]. (S in art. E$w , q. v.) And yaxobiTu fiY AlZ~alaAmi (tropical:) He goes in the night without a lamp, and so becomes confounded and perplexed, and unable to see his right course, and errs from the way, and perchance may fall into a well. (TA.) And xabaTa All~ayola , (K, TA,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) He went, or journeyed, in the night without direction. (K, TA.) And baAta yaxobiTu AlZ~alomaA='a (tropical:) [ He passed the night traversing the darkness without direction ]. (TA.) xaboTN is said to signify (assumed tropical:) The act of journeying, or going, without direction: or upon what is not the middle, or main part, of the road, or what is not the main road. (TA.) ― -b3- [And hence, perhaps,] xabaTahu (tropical:) He asked of him a benefit, or favour, without any tie of relationship; (K, * TA;) as also ↓ AxtbThu : (IB, K:) or this is from xaboTu waraqi Al$~ajari [explained in what follows]: (Har p. 425:) or the latter, [or both,] he came to him seeking his beneficence without any such tie: (S:) or he came to him seeking a gift; because he who does so must beat the ground with his feet: (IF:) and you also say, maEoruwfahu ↓ AxtbT . (Aboo-Málik, TA.) [The latter verb is the more common. See also 10.] ― -b4- And (tropical:) He conferred a benefit upon him without there having been any acquaintance between them, (S, K, TA,) and without there being anything to draw them near, and without there being any relationship: (TA:) and xabaTahu bixayori signifies the same: (TA:) or he bestowed on him a benefit, (K, TA,) being asked: (TA:) and you say also, bixayorK ↓ AxtbThu : (Aboo-Málik, TA:) and xabaTa fiyhimo bixayorK signifies (assumed tropical:) He benefited them. (TA.) 'Alkameh Ibn-'Abadeh says, (S, TA,) praising El-Hárith Ibn-AbeeShemir, (TA,) wafiY kul~i HaY~K qado xabaTota biniEomapK (assumed tropical:) [ And upon every tribe thou hast conferred benefit, app. meaning without being related to them ]: (S, TA:) but it is said in a marginal note to the S, that xabaT~a would be better; and so it is accord. to one relation: in the L, however, it is said that xabat~a would be more agreeable with analogy. (TA.) Accord. to AZ, xabaTotu Alr~ajula , inf. n. xaboTN , signifies (assumed tropical:) I held loving communion, commerce, or intercourse, with the man. (TA.) ― -b5- [In respect of the places which I have given to the abovementioned significations of asking and conferring a benefit, I have followed the opinion of IF; but it is said in the TA, and, I think, with greater probability, that they are from what here next follows.] ― -b6- xabaTa Alwaraqa mina Al$~ajari , aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. xaboTN , (Lth, T, Msb,) He made the leaves to fall from the trees: (Msb:) or he beat the leaves of the trees, (Lth, T,) meaning large trees of the kind called TaloH , [acacia, or mimosa, gummifera,] with a staff, or stick, (Lth,) so that they fell off, or became scattered, (Lth, T,) after which he gave them as food to camels; (Lth;) refrainfrom injuring thereby the trunks and branches of the trees: (T:) and lahu xabaTFA ↓ AxtbT signifies the same as xabaTa . (TA.) And xabaTa Al$~ajarapa , (S, K,) aor. as above, (TA,) and so the inf. n., (S,) He beat the tree with a staff, or stick, in order that its leaves might fall off: (S:) or he bound the tree, and then made its leaves to fall, (K, TA,) by beating it with a staff, or stick, to give them as food to camels and other beasts. (TA.) The leaves are stored up for the camels; and in wintertime are bruised, or broken up, for them, and moistened with water, and given to them as fodder. (Har p. 218.) Mohammad was asked, Does AlgaboT [i. e. “ the wishing for a blessing on the condition that it shall not become transferred from its possessor ”] injure [its author]? and he answered, laA A_il~aA kamaA yaDur~u AlEiDaAha AlxaboTu [ No, save as the beating off the leaves injures the trees called 'idáh ]; i. e., it only diminishes, without annulling, its author's recompense, like the beating off the leaves of the 'idáh, without cutting them down and extirpating them; for the leaves will grow again. (TA.) [See also art. gbT .] ― -b7- Hence, (A, TA,) xabaTa Alqawoma bisayofihi (tropical:) He struck the people with his sword. (A, K, TA.) ― -b8- xabaTahu Al$~ayoTaAnu (tropical:) The devil touched him with a hurt, (K, TA,) so as to corrupt him, or disorder him, and render him insane; (TA;) as also ↓ txb~Thu : (K, TA:) or the latter, [which is the more common,] the devil corrupted him, or disordered him: (S, Mgh, Msb: *) lit., struck him: (Mgh, Msb:) or prostrated him, and sported with him: or trampled upon him, and prostrated him. (TA.) It is said in the Kur [ii. 276], ↓ laA yaquwmuwna A_il~aA kamaA yaquwmu A@l~a*iY yataxab~aTuhu Al$~ayoTaAnu mina A@lomas~i (tropical:) [ They shall not rise save as he riseth whom the devil prostrateth by reason of possession, or insanity ]; i. e., as he who is affected by diabolical possession rises, in his state of possession, when he is prostrated, and falls: or it means, whom the devil corrupts, or disorders, by rendering him insane. (K, * TA.) [You say also, of a drug, AlEaqola ↓ xb~T (assumed tropical:) It disordered the intellect: see the act. part. n., below.] ― -b9- xabaTa also signifies (assumed tropical:) He (a man) threw himself down (S, L, K) where he was, (S, L,) to sleep, (S, K,) or and slept. (L.) And (assumed tropical:) He (a man) slept. (A' Obeyd, TA.) In the K, qaAma is erroneously put for naAma . (TA.) ― -b10- xabaTa EalaY AlbaAbi He knocked upon the door, or at the door. (TA.) ― -b11- xabaTa AlEiroqu The vein beat, or pulsated. (TA.)

(A, K, TA.) ― -b8- xabaTahu Al$~ayoTaAnu (tropical:) The devil touched him with a hurt, (K, TA,) so as to corrupt him, or disorder him, and render him insane; (TA;) as also ↓ txb~Thu : (K, TA:) or the latter, [which is the more common,] the devil corrupted him, or disordered him: (S, Mgh, Msb: *) lit., struck him: (Mgh, Msb:) or prostrated him, and sported with him: or trampled upon him, and prostrated him. (TA.) It is said in the Kur [ii. 276], ↓ laA yaquwmuwna A_il~aA kamaA yaquwmu A@l~a*iY yataxab~aTuhu Al$~ayoTaAnu mina A@lomas~i (tropical:) [ They shall not rise save as he riseth whom the devil prostrateth by reason of possession, or insanity ]; i. e., as he who is affected by diabolical possession rises, in his state of possession, when he is prostrated, and falls: or it means, whom the devil corrupts, or disorders, by rendering him insane. (K, * TA.) [You say also, of a drug, AlEaqola ↓ xb~T (assumed tropical:) It disordered the intellect: see the act. part. n., below.] ― -b9- xabaTa also signifies (assumed tropical:) He (a man) threw himself down (S, L, K) where he was, (S, L,) to sleep, (S, K,) or and slept. (L.) And (assumed tropical:) He (a man) slept. (A' Obeyd, TA.) In the K, qaAma is erroneously put for naAma . (TA.) ― -b10- xabaTa EalaY AlbaAbi He knocked upon the door, or at the door. (TA.) ― -b11- xabaTa AlEiroqu The vein beat, or pulsated. (TA.)

It is said in the Kur [iii. 154], wa A_ino yaxo*ulokumo famano *aA A@l~a*iY yanoSurukumo mino baEodihi [ But if He fail to aid you, or to preserve you, then who is he that will aid you after Him? ]: here 'Obeyd Ibn-'Omeyr read ↓ yuxodilokumo , with damm to the Y and kesr to the * . sourceDefinition: A lamb; syn. HamalN [q. v.]: (S, Msb:) or the male young one of the sheep-kind: or such as has pastured, and become strong: (Lth, K:) younger than the ja*aE : (Lth, TA:) so called because it depastures from this place and this: (Msb, TA: [see 1:]) fem. with p : (K:) pl. (of pauc., TA) A^axorifapN and (of mult., TA) xirofaAnN . (Msb, K, TA.) The latter pl. is sometimes used as meaning (assumed tropical:) Young and ignorant persons; like as kibaA$N is used as meaning aged and learned persons. (TA.) And hence the prov., kaA@loxaruwfi A^ayonamaA A@t~akaA^a EalaY SuwfK [ Like the lamb: wherever he reclines, he reclines upon wool ]: (JK, TA: but in the latter, At~kY :) applied to him who leads a soft and delicate life. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, (sometimes, S,) A colt; the male offspring of a mare; when he has attained the age of six months, or seven months; (S, K;) a meaning assigned to it by As, in the “ Book of the Horse; ” but unknown to Abu-l-Ghowth: (S:) or, until a year old: (ISk, K:) it is said by some to be applied to a horse: in the L it is said that the xrwf of horses is such as is brought forth in the [ season called ] xariyf : but Khálid Ibn-Jebeleh says that it means such as pastures upon the [ herbage of the season called ] xariyf : and Suh thinks that it is an epithet applied to a horse, and any beast, as meaning that depastures the trees and herbage. (TA.)

definition: Fresh ripe dates, (K, TA,) or fruits [in general], (S, TA,) gathered, or plucked;
sourceDefinition: Fresh ripe dates, (K, TA,) or fruits [in general], (S, TA,) gathered, or plucked; (S, K, TA;) as also ↓ maxoruwfN . (S, TA. See also maxorafN , last sentence. [And see xurofapN .]) ― -b2- And hence, (tropical:) Fresh milk; milk recently drawn from the udder. (Hr, TA.) ― -b3- Palm-trees ( naxolN ) whereof the quantity of the fruit that is upon them is computed by conjecture. (K. [See also xaraAy^ifu , voce xariyfapN .]) ― -b4- [The autumn; ] one of the divisions of the year, (S, Mgh,) the division (Msb) [ consisting of ] three months between the end of the qayoZ [or summer ] and the beginning of the $itaA=' [or winter ], (Lth, K, *) in which the fruits are gathered. (Lth, S, Mgh, Msb, K.) ― -b5- And hence, (Mgh, TA,) (assumed tropical:) A year: (Mgh, K, TA:) so in the saying, mano SaAma yawomFA fiY sabiyli A@ll~`hi baAEadahu A@ll~`hu mina Aln~aAri A^arobaEiyna xariyfFA A^awo saboEiyna , i. e. [ Whoso fasteth a day in the way of God, God will remove him from the fire of Hell] to the distance of a journey of forty years, or seventy. (Mgh: and similar exs. are given in the TA, from three trads.: see also an ex. voce A_in~a .) ― -b6- Also The rain of the season so called: (S, K:) or the rain, (JK,) or the first of the rain, (K,) in the beginning of the $itaA=' [or winter ], (JK, K,) which comes at the time of the cutting off of the fruit of the palmtrees: then follows the wasomiY~ , at the coming in of the winter; then, the rabiyE ; then, the Sayof ; and then, the Hamiym : so says As: El-Ghanawee says that the xryf is between the [ auroral ] rising of Al$~iEoraY [or Sirius, which commenced, in central Arabia, about the epoch of the Flight, on the 13th of July, O. S., ] and the [ auroral ] setting of AlEaroquwataAni [or AlfarogaAni , the 26th and 27th of the Mansions of the Moon, commencing, in the same region and period, on the 8th and 21st of Sept., O. S., and continuing thirteen days]: El-Ghowr and Rekeeyeh [? (imperfectly written)] and El- Hijáz are all rained upon by the xryf ; but Nejd is not: AZ says, the first rain is the wasomiY~ ; the follows the $atawiY~ ; then, the dafay^iY~ ; then, the Sayof ; then, the Hamiym ; then, the xariyf : and therefore the year is made to consist of six seasons: accord. to AHn, [who seems in this matter to differ from most others,] Alxryf is not originally the name of the division of the year; but the name of the rain of the qayoZ [or summer ]; and then the season was named thereby. (TA.) [See also nawo'N .] ― -b7- [Also The herbage of the season so called, or of the rain so called; like as rabiyEN signifies the “ herbage of the season, or of the rain, so called. ” So in the phrase used by Khálid Ibn-Jebeleh (in explaining the word xaruwf ), maA raEaY Alxariyfa Such as pastures upon the xryf .] ― -b8- Also, accord. to AA, (TA,) A rivulet, streamlet, or small channel for irrigation. (JK, K, TA.)

sourceDefinition: The place of the gathering, or plucking, or cutting off, of fruit. (Msb.) A place of abode of a people, or party, during their xariyf . (TA. [It is there added, “ as though formed from A^axorafuwA , by the rejection of the augmentative letter: ” but it is rather to be regarded as regularly formed, from xarafuwA : see 1.]) ― -b2- Also A garden; (Mgh, TA;) and so ↓ maxorafapN : (S, K:) or a garden of palm-trees; as also ↓ maxorifN and ↓ maxorafapN : (TA:) a single palm-tree: or a few palm-trees, up to ten; more than these being termed a busotaAn or a Hadiyqap : (El-Harbee, TA:) see also xariyfapN : or a small collection of palmtrees, six or seven, which a man purchases for the fruit that is [ to be ] gathered, or plucked: or any collection of palm-trees: (L, TA:) or a walled garden of palm-trees: (IAth, TA:) or palm-trees [absolutely]: (Mgh:) and an avenue between two rows of palm-trees, such that one may gather, or pluck, the fruit from whichever of them he will; (K;) as also ↓ maxorafapN : (Sh, K:) and, (S, Mgh, K,) as also ↓ maxorafapN , (S, K,) a road, (S, Mgh, K,) such as is conspicuous, clear, or open: (K:) pl. maxaArifu . (Mgh, TA.) It is said in a trad., EaAy^idu AlmariyDi EalaY maxaArifi Aljan~api Hat~aY yarojiEa , i. e. The visitor of the sick is as though he were in the gardens of Paradise until he returns: or upon the palm-trees of Paradise; gathering, or plucking, their fruits: or upon the roads of Paradise: (Mgh, * TA:) or, as some relate it, Aljn~pi ↓ ElY maxorafapi . (TA. [See also another explanation, and other readings in what follows.]) And it is said in a trad. of 'Omar, Aln~aEami ↓ tarakotukumo EalaY maxorafapi , (S,) or turikotumo , (TA,) i. e. [ I have left you, or ye have been left, ] upon a conspicuous road, like the road of the camels, (As, S, * TA,) which they have trodden with their feet so that it has become plainly apparent. (As, TA.) ― -b3- Also Gathered, or plucked, fruit of palm-trees: (As, A 'Obeyd, IAmb, K:) a correct meaning, though IKt says that the proper word in this sense is only maxoruwfN : it is like ma$orabN and maToEamN and marokabN as meaning ma$oruwbN and TaEaAmN maA^okuwlN and marokuwbN ; and may signify fresh ripe dates gathered or plucked: (IAmb, TA:) pl. as above. (As, &c.) So in the former of the two trads. mentioned above accord. to As and A 'Obeyd: (TA:) and this interpretation is corroborated by another reading, i. e., ElY Aljn~pi ↓ xurofapi : (Mgh:) another reading is, fiY Aljn~pi ↓ xiraAfi : [see xaraAfN :] and another, lahu fiY Aljan~api ↓ xariyfN , i. e. [The visitor of the sick shall have ] gathered fruits in Paradise. (TA.)

definition: The thing in which fruits are gathered;
sourceDefinition: The thing in which fruits are gathered; (S, Har p. 374;) called by the Arabs xaAfapN : (Har ib.:) a [ basket of the kind called ] mikotal , (Msb,) or zinobiyl , of small size, in which the best fresh ripe dates are gathered: (O, K:) pl. maxaArifu . (A, TA.) One says, xarajuwA A_ilaY AlmaxaArifi bAlmaxaArifi , i. e. They went forth to the gardens with the baskets ( zubul ) [ for gathering fruit ]. (A, TA.) ― -b2- And hence, (assumed tropical:) The basket ( znbyl ) in which the importunate beggar puts his food. (Har ubi suprà.)

definition: Compact, applied to flesh;
sourceDefinition: Compact, applied to flesh; (TA;) and so baZaA ↓ xaZaA , (S, TA,) likewise applied to flesh, (TA,) and to a horse, (AHeyth, TA,) [each] originally a verb, (S, TA,) and the latter an imitative sequent; and the fem. ↓ xaZaApN , applied to anything; (TA;) and xaZaApN baZaApN , applied to a woman, the [radical] Y being changed into A accord. to the dial. of Teiyi; (AHeyth, TA;) and baZK ↓ xaZK , applied to a horse; and baZiyapN ↓ xaZiyapN , applied to a woman. (AHeyth, K in art. xZY .) The Saadee says, (accord. to the TA, 'Ámir Ibn-Et-Tufeyl,) riqaAbN kaAlmawaAjini xaAZiyaAtN waA^asotaAhN EalaY AlA^akowaAri kuwmu [ Compact necks like the bleachers' beating implements, and rumps elevated upon the camels' saddles ]. (S.) In the saying of Imra-el-Keys, kamaA ↓ lahaA matonataAni xaZaAtaA A^akab~a EalaY saAEidayohi Aln~amiro [ She has two compact portions of flesh and sinew confining her back-bone, like as appear when the leopard falls prostrate upon his fore shanks ], he means xaZaAtaAni , suppressing the n for the purpose of alleviation of the utterance: (Fr, S:) or, as some say, he means ↓ xaZataA , restoring the A that fell out on account of the concurrence of two quiescent letters in the sing. [i. e. xaZaAto , for xaZato is formed from xaZaAto , which is from xaZawato ,] when the t has become movent. (S.) ― -b2- xaAZK also signifies Thick, and hard, firm, or rigid: (TA:) and [so, or simply] thick, applied to an arrow. (AHn, TA.) And one says saAEidN xaAZiY AlbaDiyEi [ A fore arm, or an upper arm, ] full of flesh. (IB, TA in art. bDE .) And rajulN xaAZiY AlbaDiyEi (As, S in art. bDE ) A fat man. (TA in that art.)

sourceDefinition: , (A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (A, Msb,) or , (Mgh,) or and , (Mgh, K,) inf. n. xalobN , (Lth, Mgh, TA,) He wounded him, or scratched him, or cut him, with his nail; (A, K;) as also ↓ Astxlbhu : (K:) he (a beast or bird of prey, TA) seized him, i. e. the prey, with his claw or talon: (K:) or he (a beast of prey) rent his skin with his dog-tooth: (TA:) or he rent it (the skin) with his dog-tooth: (Lth, Mgh, TA:) or he (a bird) cut and rent it (i. e. the skin) bimixolabihi with his talon: (Msb:) he rent it, or slit it. (K.) One says of a woman, qalabato qalobiY wa xalabato ↓ xilotiY [ She smote, or overturned, my heart, and rent my midriff, or, more probably, liver, which is regarded as a seat of passion]. (A, TA.) And xalabato fulaAnFA She (a woman) smote the ↓ xilob [app. here, also, meaning liver ] of such a one. (Ham p. 343.) ― -b2- Also It (a venomous or noxious reptile or the like, TA) bit him. (K.) ― -b3- And xalaba Aln~abaAta , aor. , inf. n. xalobN , He cut the plants, or herbage; (S, Msb;) as also ↓ Astxlbhu . (S.) ― -b4- And xalaba biAlmixolabi He worked, and cut, with the reaping-hook. (TA.) ― -b5- The root denotes the making a thing to incline: for AlT~aAy^iru yaxoluibu bimixolabihi Al$~aYo'a A_ilaY nafosihi [ The bird makes to incline, with its talon, the thing towards himself ]. (IF, Mgh.) ― -b6- [Hence,] xalaba fulaAnFA Eaqolahu , aor. and , He despoiled, or deprived, such a one of his reason: (K:) or xalaba AlmaroA^apa EaqolahaA , inf. n. xalobN , he despoiled, or deprived, the woman of her reason: and xalabato Eaqolahu , inf. n. as above, she took away his reason; as also ↓ Axtlbthu . (L.) ― -b7- And [hence,] ↓ xilaAbapN signifies The endeavouring to deceive or beguile (IF, IAth, Mgh) with blandishing speech: (IAth:) or deceiving with the tongue: (S:) or a woman's captivating the heart of a man by the most blandishing and deceiving speech. (Lth.) You say, xalabahu , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) or and (Mgh,) inf. n. xalobN (Msb, * K) and xilaAbapN , (A, K,) or this is a simple subst., (Msb,) and xilaAbN ; (K;) and ↓ Axtlbhu ; (S, A, K;) and ↓ xAlbhu ; (K;) He deceived him (S, Msb, K) with his tongue: (S:) or he despoiled, or deprived, him of his reason, bimanoTiqihi [ by his speech ]: (A:) or, followed by bimanoTiqihi , he made his heart to incline [ to him ] by the most blandishing speech. (Mgh.) It is said in a prov., A_i*aA lamo tagolibo faA@xolubo , (S, TA,) or faA@xolibo ; accord. to the former reading, which is that of As, (TA,) When thou dost not overcome, use deceit: (S, IAth, TA:) accord. to the latter reading, [it is said to mean when thou dost not overcome, ] grasp little after little; as though it were taken from mixolabN signifying “ a claw ” or “ talon. ” (TA.)

sourceDefinition: i. q. ZufurN , (K,) used in a general sense [as meaning The nail of a man, and the talon of a bird, and the claw of a beast: see also mixolabN ]: pl. A^axolaAbN only. (TA.) ― -b2- The diaphragm, or midriff; syn. HijaAbu Alqalobi ; (JK, L;) or HijaAbu Alkabidi ; (A, K;) the partition intervening between the heart and the liver; (IAar, S;) the partition between the heart and the belly; (Zj in his “ Khalk el-Insán; ”) or a small and thin piece of flesh forming a connection between the ribs [app. of one side and those of the other ]: or the liver [itself]: (K:) or its ziyaAdap [or zaAy^idap ]: (A, K:) or a white thin thing adhering to the liver: (K:) or a certain thing in, or upon, the liver, like a gud~ap : (JK:) or a small bone, resembling a man's nail, adhering to one side of the midriff, next the liver. (TA.) See 1, in two places. ― -b3- A friend; [app. because he cleaves to another;] as also xilomN . (JK.) ― -b4- [And hence, app.,] xilobu nisaA='K , (S, A, K,) a phrase like Hidovu nisaA='K and ziyru nisaA='K , (TA,) A man whom women love: (S:) or one who loves women for the sake of discourse, or for the sake of vitious or immoral conduct, or adultery, or fornication, (A, K,) and whom they love (K) in like manner: (TA:) and one who endeavours to deceive, or beguile, women [ with blandishing speech: see 1]: (TA:) pl. A^axolaAbu nisaA='K and nisaA='K ↓ xulabaA='u : (K, TA:) the latter [in the CK xilobA'u ] extr. [with respect to rule]. (TA.) -A2- I. q. wa$oYN [app. as meaning A kind of variegated, or figured, cloth or garment ]. (TA.) [See also muxal~abN .] -A3- The radish. (K, TA.) In a copy of the K, AlfaHolu is erroneously put for Alfijolu . (TA.) ― -b2- The leaves, (K,) or broad leaves, (Lth,) of the grape-vine. (Lth, K.)

sourceDefinition: (assumed tropical:) Clouds ( saHaAbN , S, K, TA) that thunder and lighten, (TA,) containing no rain: (S, K, TA:) or whereof the lightning flashes slightly, so that one hopes for their raining, but which deceive the expectation, and become dispersed: as though derived from xilaAbapN , the “ deceiving with blandishing speech. ” (IAth.) And Albaroqu Alxul~abi and baroqu xul~abK (S, K) and baroqu Alxul~abi (K) and baroqN xul~abN (A) (tropical:) Lightning with which is no rain; (S, A;) as though deceiving: (S:) that excites hope [ of rain ] and breaks its promise. (K.) Hence the saying, to him who promises and does not fulfil his promise, A_in~amaA A^anota kabaroqK xul~abK (assumed tropical:) [ Thou art only like lightning with which is no rain ] (S.). And fulaAnN xul~abN qul~abN (assumed tropical:) Such a one is sharp in intellect, clever, ingenious, skilful, knowing, or intelligent. (JK.)

definition: , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (S,) or , (Mgh, Msb,) or both, (K,) inf. n. xunuwsN , (A,) or xanosN , (Msb,) or both, (K, TA,) and xunaAsN , (TA,) He went, or drew, back or backwards; receded; retreated; retired; or retrograded: or he remained behind; held back; hung back; or lagged behind: syn. taA^ax~ara : (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K:) Eanohu from him or it: (S, K:) or mino bayoni Alqawomi from among the company of people: and hid himself: (A:) or and shrank, or drew himself together: (TA:) and ↓ Anxns signifies the same; (Msb, K;) and so ↓ Axtns ; and xanusa , aor. , is mentioned by Sgh: (TA:) or xanasa signifies he went back, &c., syn. tA^x~r : and also, he shrank, or drew himself together: (Mgh, Msb: *) and he hid himself; became hidden or absent. (TA.) You say, xanasa Alkawokabu (tropical:) The star returned, or went back, or retrograded: syn. rajaEa ; a tropical signification: (A: [and in the TA it is said that xanosN is syn. with rujuwEN , and is tropical in this sense:]) or became hidden, (K, TA,) like a gazelle in its covert, (TA,) or like the devil when he hears the mention of God: (K, TA:) or became concealed in the day-time: (TA:) and xunuwsN signifies also the being, or becoming, depressed. (Ham p. 332.) And xanasa Eani Alqawomi He held back, or hung back, from the company of people; remained behind them, not going with them; syn, taxal~afa ; (As, on the authority of an Arab of the desert, of the Benoo- 'Okeyl;) as also ↓ Anxns . (K.) [This is said in the TA to be tropical; but why, I see not.] And xanasati Aln~axolu (assumed tropical:) The palm-trees were backward to receive fecundation, ( taA^ax~arato Eano qabuwli Alt~aloqiyHi , lit, held back from receiving fecundation, ) so that it had not any effect upon them, and they did not bear fruit that year. (TA.) And yaxonisu Al$~ayoTaAnu A_i*aA samiEa *ikora A@ll~`hi The devil shrinks when he hears the mention of God. (Msb.) And xanasa mino bayoni A^aSoHaAbihi He hid himself from among his companions. (TA.) And xanasa Ean~iY (tropical:) He, or it, [app. the latter,] became hid from me. (A.) And xanasa bihi He went away with him; took him away; so that he was not seen; (ISh, K;) as also bh ↓ txn~s : (K:) and he hid him, or it. (TA.) -A2- See also 4, in four places. -A3- xanisa AlA^anofN , aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. xanasN , (S, A, Msb, K,) The nose was, or became, [ camous, or camoys, i. e.,] depressed in its bone: (Msb:) or depressed in its bone, (A,) or contracted therein, (TA,) and wide in the end: (A, TA:) or retiring from the face, with a slight elevation in the end; (S, K, TA;) xanasN being nearly the same as faTasN : (TA:) or retiring towards the head, and rising from the lip, not being long nor prominent: or its bone lay close upon the elevated part of the cheek, and it was large in the end. (TA.) See also the inf. n. voce A^axonasu . ― -b2- xanisati Alqadamu , inf. n. xanasN , The foot was, or became, flat in the hollow part of the sole, and fleshy. (TA: but only the inf. n. of the verb in this sense is there mentioned.)

definition: He made him to go back or backwards;
sourceDefinition: He made him to go back or backwards; to recede, retreat, retire, or retrograde: or he put him, or placed him, or made him to be, behind, or after: or he made him to remain behind, hold back, hang back, or lag behind: or he kept him back: or he delayed, or retarded, him: syn. A^ax~arahu : (T, A, Msb, K:) as also ↓ xanasahu , (Fr, T, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb,) [and app., accord. to the K, also,] inf. n. xanosN ; (Msb;) but the former is the more common: (TA:) and (tropical:) hid him, or it: or made him, or it, to hide himself or itself; (A;) or he left behind, (As, S:) and went away from, (S,) him, or it: (As, S:) or both signify he contracted, or drew together, or made to contract or draw together, him [or it ]: (Msb:) or the latter verb has this signification as well as that of A^ax~arahu : (Mgh:) [and so has the former also, as will be seen below:] and the former also signifies (tropical:) he hid, or concealed, him, or it; (A;) as also bihi ↓ xanasa , as mentioned above. (TA.) You say, A^axonasotu Eanohu baEoDa Haq~ihi I kept back ( A^ax~arotu ) from him part of his right, or due. (Fr, TA.) And A^axonasuwA AlT~ariyqa (tropical:) They passed beyond the road: (AA, TA:) or left it behind them: (TA:) or passed beyond it and left it behind them. (A.) And A^a$aAra biA^arobaEK waA^axonasa A_ibohaAmahu , (A,) and ↓ xanasahaA , (Mgh, Msb, K,) He [ made a sign with four fingers and ] contracted his thumb. (Mgh, Msb, K.) It is related of Mohammad, that he said, “ The month is thus and thus, ” [twice extending the fingers and thumb of each hand,] and that, the third time, A_iSobaEahu ↓ xanasa , i. e., he contracted his finger, [meaning, one of his fingers,] to inform them that the month is nine and twenty [nights with their days]. (TA.)

definition: Going back or backwards;
sourceDefinition: Going back or backwards; receding; retreating; retiring; or retrograding: or remaining behind; holding back; hanging back; or lagging behind: syn. mutaA^ax~irN : pl. xun~asN . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Alxun~asu , (in the Kur lxxxi. 15, S,) (tropical:) The stars; (S, K;) i. e., all of them; because they retire, or hide themselves, ( taxonusu ,) at setting; or because they become concealed in the day-time: (S:) or the planets: (S, K:) or the five stars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury: (Fr, S, K, Jel:) because they return, ( taxonusu , i. c., tarojiEu , Jel,) in their course: (Fr, S, Jel:) when you see a star [thereof] in the end of a sign of the zodiac, it returns to the beginning of it: (Jel:) or because of their retrogression; for they are the erratic stars ( AlkawaAkibu AlmutaHay~aripu ), which [at one time appear to] retrograde, and [at another time to] pursue a direct [and forward] course: (S:) or because they sometimes return ( txns ) in their course until they become concealed in the light of the sun: (TA:) or because they hide themselves, as the devil does at the mention of God. (K, TA.) ― -b3- And hence, i. e., from xaAnisN in the sense of mutaA^ax~irN , the saying in a trad. of El- Hajjáj, AlA_ibilu Dim~arN xin~asN , meaning, (assumed tropical:) [ Camels are lean, and lank in the belly, and] patient of thirst. (TA.) ― -b4- And All~ayaAliY Alxun~asu The three nights of the lunar month during which the moon retires [ from view ]. (TA.)

(TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Alxun~asu , (in the Kur lxxxi. 15, S,) (tropical:) The stars; (S, K;) i. e., all of them; because they retire, or hide themselves, ( taxonusu ,) at setting; or because they become concealed in the day-time: (S:) or the planets: (S, K:) or the five stars, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury: (Fr, S, K, Jel:) because they return, ( taxonusu , i. c., tarojiEu , Jel,) in their course: (Fr, S, Jel:) when you see a star [thereof] in the end of a sign of the zodiac, it returns to the beginning of it: (Jel:) or because of their retrogression; for they are the erratic stars ( AlkawaAkibu AlmutaHay~aripu ), which [at one time appear to] retrograde, and [at another time to] pursue a direct [and forward] course: (S:) or because they sometimes return ( txns ) in their course until they become concealed in the light of the sun: (TA:) or because they hide themselves, as the devil does at the mention of God. (K, TA.) ― -b3- And hence, i. e., from xaAnisN in the sense of mutaA^ax~irN , the saying in a trad. of El- Hajjáj, AlA_ibilu Dim~arN xin~asN , meaning, (assumed tropical:) [ Camels are lean, and lank in the belly, and] patient of thirst. (TA.) ― -b4- And All~ayaAliY Alxun~asu The three nights of the lunar month during which the moon retires [ from view ]. (TA.)

definition: [ Having a camous, or camoys, nose;
sourceDefinition: [ Having a camous, or camoys, nose; ] having the configuration termed xanasN in the nose: (S, Msb, K:) [see xanisa AlA^anofu :] accord. to some, having a nose of which the bone is short and the end turning back towards its bone: (TA:) fem. xanosaA='u : (S, Msb:) pl. xunosN . (S, A.) ↓ xanasN in its original application is in gazelles and bulls and cows: (TA:) all bulls and cows are xunos , (S, A, TA,) and so are all gazelles: (TA:) or ↓ xunusN , with two dammehs, (K,) but written by Sh xunosN , (TA,) is used to signify gazelles: and bulls or cows: (K:) and xanosaA='u is an epithet applied to the wild cow: (K:) also A^axonasu , to the tick: (Sgh, K:) and the lion; and so ↓ xin~awosN ; (K;) which last is an epithet so applied as relating to his face and his nose: (Fr, TA:) and the last, ↓ xn~ws , is also applied to a young pig: (As, TA:) or in this sense it is with S : (Fr, TA:) and ↓ xanaAsN is syn, with xin~awosN . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] xunosN is metaphorically applied [as an epithet] to arrows, in the following verse, describing a coat of mail: lahaA EukanN tarud~u Aln~abola xunosFA watohozaA^u biA@lomaEaAbili waA@loqiTaAEi [ It has folds which repel the arrows turned up at the points, and mock at the broad and long, and the small and broad, arrow-heads ]. (TA.) ― -b3- qadamN xanosaA='u A foot flat in the hollow part of the sole, and fleshy. (TA.)

(TA.)

sourceDefinition: see 1. ― -b2- xay~aTa Al$~ayobu fiY raA^osihi , (S, K,) inf. n. taxoyiyTN , (K,) means (tropical:) Whiteness of the hair, or hoariness, appeared upon his head (K, TA) in streaks, or lines: (TA:) it is like waxaTa : (S, TA:) or became like threads: (K:) and in like manner, fiY liHoyatihi in his beard. (TA.)

definition: Thread, or string;
sourceDefinition: Thread, or string; or a thread or string; syn. silokN ; (S, K;) the thing with which one sews; (Msb;) [often used as a coll. gen. n.; n. un. with p ;] and ↓ xiyaATN [likewise] signifies the thing with which a garment, or piece of cloth, is sewed; as also ↓ mixoyaTN ; besides having another signification, common to it with the last, namely “a needle; ” (K;) the pl. of xayoTN is A^axoyaATN [a pl. of pauc.] (IB, K) and xuyuwTN (S, Msb, K) and xuyuwTapN [both pls. of mult.]. (S, K.) It is said in a trad., waAlmixoyaTa ↓ A^ad~uwA AlxiyaATa , meaning [ Bring ye ] the xayoT and the needle. (TA.) And you say, ↓ A^aEoTiniY xiyaATFA and niSaAHFA , i. e. [ Give thou to me ] a single xayoT . (AZ, TA.) [ A^aEoTinaY xiyaATFA waniSaAHFA may, however, mean Give thou to me a needle and thread. ] ― -b2- xayoTu Alr~aqabapi (assumed tropical:) The nuxaAE [or spinal cord ] of the neck. (S, K) You say, jaAHa$a fulaAnN Eano xayoTi raqabatihi , meaning (tropical:) Such a one defended his blood. (S, O, L.) ― -b3- AlxayoTu AlA^aboyaDu and AlxayoTu AlA^asowadu , mentioned in the Kur ii. 183, mean (assumed tropical:) The true dawn, and the false dawn: (Msb:) or the whiteness of the dawn, and the blackness of night; (K, TA;) likened to a thread because of its thinness: (TA:) or the whiteness of day, and the blackness of night: (A 'Obeyd, Nh:) or the dawn that extends sideways, and the dawn that rises high, or, as some say, the blackness of night: (S:) or what appears of the true dawn, which is the musotaTiyr , and what extends with it of the darkness of night, which is the dawn termed the musotaTiyl : (Mgh:) or what first appears of the dawn spreading sideways in the horizon, and what extends with it of the darkness of the last part of the night: (Bd:) or the dawn that rises high, filling the horizon, and the dawn that appears black, extending sideways: (Aboo-Is-hák:) or the real meaning is the day and the night. (TA.) AlxayoTaAni also signifies (assumed tropical:) The night and the day. (L in art. wsd .) tabay~ana AlxayoTu mina AlxayoTi means (tropical:) [ The night became distinct from the day: or] what is termed AlxayoTu AlA^aboyaDu became distinct from what is termed AlxayoTu AlA^asowadu . (TA.) And xayoTN mina AlS~uboHi is also said to signify (assumed tropical:) A tint of the dawn. (TA.) [See bariymu AlS~uboHi in art. brm .] ― -b4- xayoTu baATilK (tropical:) What is called luEaAbu Al$~amosi and muxaATu Al$~ayoTaAni , (S, TA,) which last is explained by Z and IB as meaning what comes forth from the mouth of the spider: (TA: [the author of which says that, accord. to this explanation, this term differs from lEAb Al$ms : but in so saying he seems to be in error: both evidently signify gossamer: ]) it was applied as a surname, or nickname, to Marwán Ibn-El-Hakam; because he was tall, and loose, or uncompact, in frame: (S:) or it signifies the air; syn. AlhawaA='u [perhaps a mistranscription for AlhabaA='u , occurring in another explanation hereafter]: (K:) or light entering from an aperture in a wall [ into a dark place ] (Th, K:) or xayoTu AlbaATili signifies the scattered habaA=' [or atoms that are seen in the rays of the sun ] entering from an aperture in a wall [ into a dark place ] when the sun is hot: and one says, fulaAnN A^adaq~u mino xayoTi AlbaATili (tropical:) [ Such a one is less in estimation than the scattered atoms that are seen in the rays of the sun ]; a prov., applied to him who is in an abject state; thus related, on the authority of Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà, by Az and others; but by Sgh, erroneously, A^araq~u mino xayoTi baATilK . (TA.) ― -b5- See also what next follows, in two places.

definition: and ↓ maxoyuwTN A garment, or piece of cloth, sewed: (S, Msb, K:) the Y in the former is the w of the measure mafoEuwlN , changed into Y because of its being quiescent and the preceding letter's being with kesr;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ maxoyuwTN A garment, or piece of cloth, sewed: (S, Msb, K:) the Y in the former is the w of the measure mafoEuwlN , changed into Y because of its being quiescent and the preceding letter's being with kesr; the letter preceding it being made movent because it and the w are quiescent after the Y has fallen out; [for by dropping the Y it becomes changed from maxoyuwTN to maxowoTN ;] and it is made movent with kesr [and thus changed from maxowoTN to maxiwoTN , which necessarily becomes maxiyTN ,] in order to its being known that the letter which has dropped out is Y : some say that the Y in maxiyTN is the radical, and that the letter thrown out is the w of the measure mafoEuwlN , in order that the word with w [for its medial radical] may be known from that with Y ; [so that it is changed from maxoyuwTN to maxoyuTN , and then to maxoyoTN , and then to maxiyTN ;] but the former saying is the right, because the w is a formative augment, and it is not proper that such should be thrown out. (S.) ― -b2- Also, the former, (assumed tropical:) The whole of the exterior of the belly. (ISh.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) A place of passage; (O, L, TA;) a meaning erroneously assigned in the K to ↓ xiyaATN and ↓ maxoyaTN : (TA:) and particularly, (tropical:) of a serpent; (TA;) the place of creeping along of a serpent. (K, TA.)

definition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, Msb,) inf. n. duruwjN (S, Msb, K) and darajaAnN , (K,) said of a man, and of a [lizard of the kind called] Dab~ , (S,) He went on foot; [ went step by step; stepped along; ] or walked: (S, K:) and said of a child, he walked a little, at his first beginning to walk: (Msb, TA: *) or, said of an old man, and of a child, and of a bird of the kind called qaTFA , aor. as above, inf. n. [ duruwjN and] darojN and darajaAnN and dariyjN , he walked with a weak gait; crept along; or went, or walked, leisurely, slowly, softly, or gently. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] daraja qaronN baEoda qaronK Generation after generation passed away. (A.) And daraja Alqawomu The people passed away, or perished, none of them remaining; (S, A, K;) as also ↓ AndrjwA . (S, K.) And daraja He left no progeny, or offspring: (As, S, K:) he died, and left no progeny, or offspring: [opposed to A^aEoqaba :] but you do not say so of every one who has died: (TA:) or it signifies also [simply] he died: (Aboo-Tálib, S, A, Msb:) so in the prov., A^ako*abu mano dab~a wadaraja (S, Msb) The most lying of the living and the dead. (S.) Or daraja signifies, (K,) or signifies also, (S,) He went his way; (S, K;) and so darija , [aor. ,] like samiEa . (K.) layosa h`*aA biEu$~iki faA@dorujiY , i. e. [ This is not thy nest, therefore ] go thou away, is a saying occurring in a xuTobap of El-Hajjáj, addressed to him who applies himself to a thing not of his business to do; or to him who is at ease in an improper time; wherefore he is thus ordered to be diligent and in motion. (TA. [See also art. E$ .]) ― -b3- darajato and ↓ A^adorajato She (a camel) went beyond the year [ from the day when she was covered ] without bringing forth. (S, K.) ― -b4- darajati Alr~iyHu The wind left marks, or lines, [or ripples, ] upon the sand. (TA.) ― -b5- darajati Alr~iyHu biAlHaSaA The wind passed violently over the pebbles [app. so as to make them move along: see also 10]. (K.) -A2- darija , aor. , He rose in grade, degree, rank, condition, or station. (K, TA.) ― -b2- He kept to the plain and manifest way in religion or in speech. (K, TA.) -A3- Also (i. e. darija ) He continued to eat the kind of bird called dur~aAj . (K.) -A4- daraja as a trans. v.: see 4, in two places.

definition: [ dr~jhu , inf. n. tadoriyjN , He made him to go on foot; to go step by step; to step along; or to walk: he made him (a child) to walk a little, at his first beginning to walk: or he made him (an old...
sourceDefinition: [ dr~jhu , inf. n. tadoriyjN , He made him to go on foot; to go step by step; to step along; or to walk: he made him (a child) to walk a little, at his first beginning to walk: or he made him (an old man and a child) to walk with a weak gait; to creep along; or to go, or walk, leisurely, slowly, softly, or gently: see 1, first sentence: and see also 10, first sentence.] You say, of a child, yudar~aju EalaY AlHaAli [ He is made to walk, &c., leaning upon the go-cart ]. (S, K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] dr~jhu , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. tadoriyjN , (Msb,) He brought him near, or caused him to draw near, (S, Msb, * K,) by degrees ( EalaY Alt~adoriyji , S), or by little and little, (Msb,) A_ilaY ka*aA to such a thing, (S,) or A_ilaY AlA^amori to the thing or affair; (Msb;) as also ↓ Astdrjhu . (S, Msb, K.) ― -b3- And He exalted him, or elevated him, from one grade, or station, to another, by degrees ( EalaY Alt~adoriyji ); as also ↓ Astdrjhu . (A.) ― -b4- And hence, (tropical:) He accustomed him, or habituated him, A_ilaY ka*aA to such a thing. (A.) ― -b5- [Hence] also, inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) He fed him, namely, a sick person, when in a state of convalescence, by little and little, until he attained by degrees to the full amount of food that he ate before his illness. (TA.) ― -b6- dar~ajaniY , inf. n. as above, said of corn, or food, and of an affair, It was beyond, or it baffled, my ability, or power, to attain it, or accomplish it. (K.) ― -b7- See also 4. -A2- dr~j as an intrans. v. signifies He went on foot, or walked, [&c.,] much. (Har p. 380.) -A3- [It is also said to signify He imitated the cry of the bird called dur~aAj : see De Sacy's “ Chrest. Ar. ” 2nd ed. ii. 39.]

definition: He (God) caused people to pass away, or perish.
sourceDefinition: He (God) caused people to pass away, or perish. (TA. [See also 10.]) [Hence,] Adrjhu biAls~ayofi [ He destroyed him with the sword ]. (K in art. $mr .) ― -b2- tudoziju garoDahaA watuloHiquhu biHaqabihaA said of a she-camel when she makes her saddle with its appertenances to shift backwards [ She makes her fore girth to slip back and to become close to her kind girth ]. (TA.) Accord. to Aboo-Tálib, A_idoraAjN signifies A camel's becoming lank in the belly, so that his belly-girth shifts back to the kind girth; the load also shifting back. (TA.) ― -b3- Adrj Ald~alowa He drew up the bucket gently: (K:) drew it up, or out, by little and little. (Er-Riyáshee, TA.) ― -b4- Adrj AlA_iqaAmapa ; and ↓ darajahaA aor. , inf. n. darojN ; i. q. A^arosalahaA [i. e. He chanted the A_iqaAmap (q. v.); meaning he chanted it in a quick, or an uninterrupted, manner; for such is the usual and prescribed manner of doing so: see 1 in art. H*m : in the present day, daraja , aor. and inf. n. as above, signifies he chanted, or sang, in a trilling, or quavering, manner; and uninterruptedly, or quickly ]. (Msb.) ― -b5- [ A_idoraAjN in speaking signifies, in like manner, The conjoining of words, without pausing; i. q. waSolN , as opposed to waqofN : it occurs in this sense in the S in art. hl , &c.] ― -b6- Adrj (inf. n. A_idoraAjN , TA) also signifies He folded, folded up, or rolled up, (S, A, Msb, K,) a thing, (TA,) a writing, (S, A, Msb,) and a garment, or piece of cloth; (Msb;) as also ↓ dr~j , (K,) inf. n. tadoriyjN ; (TA;) and ↓ daraja , (K,) aor. , inf. n. darojN : (TA:) the first of these verbs is the most chaste: (L:) [it signifies also he rolled a thing like a scroll; made it into a roll, or scroll: and hence, he made it round like a scroll; he rounded it: (see A^adomaja and mudomajN and mudamolajN and Har~ada &c.:) and he wound a thing upon another thing:] also he infolded a thing; put it in, or inserted it: and he wrapped, wrapped up, or inwrapped, a thing in another thing. (L.) You say, A^adoraja AlkitaAba fiY AlkitaAbi He infolded, enclosed, or inserted, the writing in the [other] writing; or put it within it. (A, L.) And Adrj Almay~ita fiY Alkafani waAlqabori He put the dead man into the grave-clothing and the grave. (TA.) And A^adorajaniY fiY TaY~ Aln~isoyaAni (assumed tropical:) [ He, or it, infolded me in the folding of oblivion ]. (TA in art. TwY .) ― -b7- [And hence, (assumed tropical:) He foisted, or inserted spuriously, a verse or verses into a poem.] -A2- rajaEa A_idoraAjahu or EalaY A_idoraAjihi : see darajN . ― -b2- A^adorajato said of a she-camel: see 1. -A3- Adrj biAln~aAqapi He bound ( Sar~a ) the she-camel's teats (K, TA) with a ↓ durojap [app. meaning a piece of rag wrapped about them ]. (TA.)
