(Bd in vii. 181.) ― -b4- And hence, He (God) drew him near to destruction by little and little: (Bd ibid:) He brought him near to punishment by degrees, by means of respite, and the continuance of health, and the increase of favour: (Idem in lxviii. 44:) He (God) took him (a man) so that he did not reckon upon it; [ as though by degrees; ] bestowing upon him enjoyments in which he delighted, and on which he placed his reliance, and with which he became familiar so as not to be mindful of death, and then taking him in his most heedless state: such is said to be the meaning in the Kur vii. 181 and lxviii. 44: (TA:) or He bestowed upon him new favours as often as he committed new wrong actions, and caused him to forget to ask for forgiveness [ thus leading him by degrees to perdition ]: and [or as some say, TA] He took him by little and little; [or by degrees; ] not suddenly: (K:) or Aisotadorajahumo signifies He took them by little and little; [ one, or a few, at a time; ] not [ all of them together, ] suddenly. (L.) (TA.) [See also 1.]) ― -b9- AisotidoraAjN also signifies The drawing forth (in Pers. byrwn Awrdn ) speech, or words, from the mouth. (KL.) ― -b10- And The rejecting a letter, such as the w in yaEidu for yawoEidu . (Msb in art. wEd .)

sourceDefinition: : see darajN , in two places. -A2- Also, and ↓ darajN , A thing in, or upon, which one writes; (S, K;) [ a scroll, or long paper, or the like, generally composed of several pieces joined together, which is folded or rolled up: ] and ↓ mudorajN , [used as a subst.,] a writing folded or rolled up; pl. madaAriju : (Har p. 254:) and mdrjp [app. ↓ mudorajapN , from A^adoraja “ he folded ” or “ rolled up, ” with p added to transfer it from the predicament of part. ns. to that of substs.,] signifies [in like manner] a paper upon which one writes a risaAlap [or message, &c.], and which one folds, or rolls up; pl. madaAriju . (Har p. 246.) ― -b2- fiY daroji AlkitaAbi signifies fiY Tay~ihi [lit. (TA.)

definition: A way, road, or path;
sourceDefinition: A way, road, or path; (S, L, K;) as also ↓ darojN : (L:) and ↓ madorajapN (S, A) and ↓ madorajN (A, K) signify [ the same; or] a way by, or through, which one goes or passes; a way which one pursues; a course, or route; syn. ma*ohabN (S) and masolakN (S, K) and mamar~N ; (A;) and particularly the way along which a boy and the wind &c. go; as also darajN ; respecting which last, in relation to the wind, see daruwjN : (L:) or ↓ madorajN signifies a road; or a cross-road; or a bending road; and its pl. is madaArijN : (Msb:) and ↓ madorajapN is explained by Er-Rághib as signifying a beaten way or road: and it signifies also the course by which things pass, on a road &c.: and the main part of a road: and a rugged [ road such as is termed ] vaniy~ap , between mountains: (TA:) the pl. of darajN (S, L) and of ↓ darojN (L) is A^adoraAjN (S, L) and diraAjN , which occurs in a prov. cited below: (Meyd:) and the pl. of madorajapN is ↓ madaArijN : (S, TA:) A^akamapK ↓ madaAriju signifies the roads that lie across a hill such as is termed Akmp . (TA.) You say A^adoraAjaka meaning Go thy way, as thou camest. (TA from a trad.) And rajaEa darajahu (TA) and rajaEa A^adoraAjahu (Sb, S, K) and ↓ A_idoraAjahu (K) or EalaY A_idoraAjihi (IAar) He returned by the way by which he had come. (S, K, TA.) And rajaEa darajahu He returned to the thing, or affair, that he had left. (TA.) And rajaEa EalaY A^adoraAjihi and rajaEa darajahu AlA^aw~ala He returned without having been able to accomplish what he desired. (IAar.) And Aisotamar~a darajahu and A^adoraAjahu [ He kept on his way; persevered in his course ]. (TA.) And huwa EalaY daraji ka*aA He is on the way of, or to, such a thing. (TA.) And ↓ Ait~axa*uwA daArahu madorajapF and ↓ madorajFA They made his house a way through which to pass. (A.) And lih`*aA ↓ h`*aA AlA^amoru madorajapN (assumed tropical:) This thing, or affair, is a way that leads to this. (TA.) And AlHaq~i ↓ Aimo$a fiY madaAriji (tropical:) Walk thou in the ways of truth. (TA.) And *ahaba damuhu A^adoraAja Alr~iyaAHi (tropical:) His blood went for nothing; [lit., in the ways of the winds; meaning] so that no account was taken of it, and it was not avenged. (S, A, * K.) And xal~ daraja AlD~ab~i Leave thou the way of the Db~ [a species of lizard], (S, Meyd,) and oppose not thyself to him, (TA,) lest he pass between thy feet, and thou become angry ( fatanotafixa ): (S, Meyd:) a prov., applied in the case of demanding security from evil. (Meyd. [See another reading, and explanations thereof, in Har p. 220, or in Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 437.]) And mano yarud~u AlfuraAta Eano diraAjihi or A^adoraAjihi , accord. to different readings, with two different pls. of darajN ; i. e. Who will turn back Euphrates from its course? a prov. applied to an impossible affair. (Meyd.) And mano yarud~u Als~ayola EalaY A^adoraAjihi Who will turn back the torrent to its channels? another prov. so applied. (Meyd.) daraju sayolK and sayolK ↓ madoraju signify The way by which a torrent descends in the bendings of valleys. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, perhaps, as denoting a way, or means,] (assumed tropical:) A mediator between two persons for the purpose of effecting a reconciliation. (K.) ― -b3- A^anaAa daraju yadayoka means (tropical:) [ I am submissive, or obedient, to thee; ] I will not disobey thee: (A, TA: *) and drj used in this sense does not assume a dual nor a pl. form: [therefore] you say also, humo daraju yadika (tropical:) They are submissive, or obedient, to thee. (TA.) ― -b4- daraju Alr~amoli and AlmaA='i signify [ The ripples of sand and of water; ] what are seen upon sand, and upon water, when moved by the wind. (Az and TA in art. Hbk .) See daruwjN . ― -b5- See also darajapN , in two places. -A2- And see darojN .

definition: A thing which is rolled up, and inserted into a she-camel's vulva, and then [ taken forth, whereupon ] she smells it, and, thinking it to be her young one, inclines to it [ and yields her milk ]: (S:) or, accord.
sourceDefinition: A thing which is rolled up, and inserted into a she-camel's vulva, and then [ taken forth, whereupon ] she smells it, and, thinking it to be her young one, inclines to it [ and yields her milk ]: (S:) or, accord. to Aboo-Ziyád El-Kilá- bee, (S,) a thing (T, S, K) consisting of rags, (T,) or of tow and rags (S, M) and other things, (M,) which is rolled up, (T, K,) and stuffed into a she-camel's vulva, (T, S, M, K,) and into her tuel, (K,) and bound, (TA,) when they desire her to incline to the young one of another, (T, S,) having first bound her nose and her eyes: (S:) they leave her thus, (S, K,) with her eyes and nose bound, (K,) for some days, (S,) and she in consequence suffers distress like that occasioned by labour: then they loose the bandage [of her vulva] from her, and this thing comes forth from her, (S, K,) and she thinks it to be a young one; and when she has dropped it, they unbind her eyes, having prepared for her a young camel, which they bring near to her, and she thinks it to be her own young one, and inclines to it: (S:) or with the thing that comes forth from her they besmear the young one of another she-camel, and she thinks it to be her own young one, and inclines to it: (K:) the thing thus rolled up is called durojapN (T, S) and jazomN and waviyqapN ; (T;) and the thing with which her eyes are bound, gimaAmapN ; and that with which her nose is bound, SiqaAEN : (S:) the pl. [of mult.] is durajN (S, TA) and [of pauc.] A^adoraAjN : (TA:) or it signifies [or signifies also] a piece of rag containing medicine, which is put into a she-camel's vulva when she has a complaint thereof: pl. durajN . (L, K.) ― -b2- Also (tropical:) A piece of rag stuffed with cotton, which a woman in the time of the menses puts into her vulva, (K, TA,) to see if there be any remains of the blood: (MF:) likened to the drjp of a she-camel. (K.) It is said in a trad. of 'Áïsheh, kun~a yaboEavona biAAld~arajapi fiyhaA Alkurosufu [ They (women) used to send the drjp , with cotton therein ]: (IAth, K, * TA:) but accord. to one reading it is dirajap , (IAth, K,) pl. of durojN [explained above], meaning “ a thing like a small safaT , in which a woman puts her light articles and her perfumes: ” (IAth:) El-Bájee read darajap , which seems to be a mistake. (K.) ― -b3- See also 4, last sentence. -A2- And see what here next follows.

definition: , (T, S, M, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, K,) aor. , (T, M, K,) inf. n. daliyfN (T, S, M, K) and dalafN (T, M, K) and dalofN (K) and dalafaAnN (M, K) and duluwfN , (M, TA,) He walked, or went, gently, or leisurely: (S, M:) said of an old man, (As, T, S, K,) he walked, or went, (As, T, S, M, K,) with short steps, (S, M,) or in the manner of him who is shackled, (K,) as some say, (M,) at a rate above that which is termed dabiybN , (As, T, M, K,) like as does the army, or body of troops, to the [ other ] army, or body of troops. (As, T.) You say, dalafati Alkatiybapu A_ilaY Alkatiybapi fiY AlHarobi (T, S, * M, K *) meaning The army, or body of troops, went gently, or leisurely, to the [other] army, or body of troops, in war: (M:) or advanced, or went forward; syn. taqad~amat : (S, K:) [for] dalafN (T, M) accord. to A'Obeyd, or dalofN accord. to AA, (T,) signifies the act of advancing, or going forward; syn. taqad~umN : (T, M:) and one says dalafonaAhumo , (S, K,) or dalafonaA lahumo , (M, and so in one place in the TA,) meaning [as is implied in the S and K] we advanced to them; syn. taqad~amonaA : (M:) and dalafa A_ilayohi he drew near to him, or it. (TA.) dalafotu also signifies ma$ayotu [i.e. I walked; or went on foot, whether quickly or slowly ]: (Ham p. 678:) and [in like manner,] A_ilayohi ↓ tdl~f signifies ma$aY [ he walked, &c., to him, or it ]: (O, TA:) or this latter signifies tama$~aY [said in the TA, in art. m$Y , to be syn. with ma$aY ; but it rather signifies he walked with slow steps to him, or it ]; and approached, or drew near: (S, K:) but A'Obeyd says that tazal~afa is more common. (M.) ― -b2- Hence, the saying of a poet, dalafotu A_ilaY Samiymika biAlqawaAfiY meaning (assumed tropical:) I have wounded thy heart with rhymes. (Ham ubi suprá.) ― -b3- [The verb seems to bear two contr. significations; for it is said that] dalafa liA@lotizaAmiY means He hastened to take me by the hand and embrace me. definition: Low, base, vile, mean, paltry, inconsiderable, or contemptible;
sourceDefinition: Low, base, vile, mean, paltry, inconsiderable, or contemptible; (Fr, T, S, M, * Msb, K;) applied to a man &c.: (T, Msb:) and inferior, i. e. lower, baser, viler, &c., in grounds of pretension to respect or honour [or in any approvable quality ]: (Lth, T:) and such as falls short [of a thing]; used in this sense as a prefixed noun: (Ham p. 686:) [see below what is said of its usage as a prefixed noun by Lth and by Sb: and used as an epithet, scanty, or deficient; applied to anything:] and of a middling sort; between good and bad; applied to a man and to a commodity: (M:) and also high, or eminent, in rank or condition; noble, or honourable: (T, K:) thus it bears two contr. significations (K) [and significations intermediate between those two]. A poet says, A_i*aA maA EalaA Almaro'u raAma AlEalaA=' wayaqotaEu biAld~uwni mano kaAnaA duwnaA [ When the man is high in rank, or nobility, he seeks highness: and he who is low is content with that which is low ]. (S.) Accord. to the most common usage, (Msb,) or accord. to what is asserted to be the most common usage, (Lh, M,) one says rajulN mino duwnK (T, M, Msb, K) and $aYo'N mino duwnK (M, Msb) A man who is [ of a kind that is ] low, base, &c., and a thing that is [ of a kind that is ] low, base, &c.: (Msb:) but sometimes they said rajulN duwnN and $aYo'N duwnN , without mino ; (M, Msb;) and vawobN duwnN a bad [or an inferior ] garment, or piece of cloth: (M:) or one should not say rajulN duwnN ; (T, K;) for the Arabs did not use this phrase. (T.) Accord. to Lth, one says, h`*aA duwnu *aAka [ This is the inferior of that ], when meaning to denote by it low estimation, using the nom. case: (T:) [but this is uncommon, if allowable:] Sb says that duwn is not used in the nom. case as a prefixed noun: as to the saying in the Kur [lxxii. 11, an instance similar to which occurs also in vii. 167], min~aA AlS~aAliHuwna wa min~aA duwna *`lika , the meaning is, wa min~aA qawomN duwna *`lika [i. e. Of us are the righteous, and of us are a party below that party in rank or estimation ]; (M, TA;) or, as another says, dwn is here in the accus. case but in the place of a noun in the nom. case because it is generally used as an adv. n. (TA.) ― -b2- As an adv. n., duwn signifies Below, contr. of fawoq ; (S, K;) as denoting a falling short of the [ right or approved ] limit; (S;) or denoting low, or mean, estimation or condition; (Lth, T, M;) or a condition lower, baser, viler, &c., than that of another, in grounds of pretension to respect or honour [or in any approvable quality ]; (Lth, T;) [and hence, inferior to, beneath, under, or short of, another in rank, height, size, &c.;] and less than another, and more deficient than another: (Fr, T:) and also above; i. q. fawoq ; (T, K;) in highness, or eminence, of rank or condition, or in nobility; (T;) [and hence, exceeding another, and more than another:] thus bearing two contr. significations. (K.) You say, zayodN duwnaka meaning Zeyd is [ below thee, or] in a condition lower, baser, viler, &c., than thine, in grounds of pretension to respect or honour [&c.]: and when one says, “ Verily such a one is high, or eminent, in rank or condition, ” or “ is noble, ” another replies, wa duwna *`lika meaning And above that. (T.) ― -b3- Also Beneath, below in situation, or under; syn. taHot . (T, TA.) Using it in this sense, you say, duwan qadamika xad~u Eaduw~ika [ May the cheek of thine enemy be beneath thy foot ]: (T, TA:) and jalasa duwnahu [ He sat below him ]. (TA.) ― -b4- Also Before in respect of place, or in front: and [the contr., namely,] behind, or beyond. (T, M, K.) [You may say, using it in the former sense, jalasa duwnahu He sat before him, or in front of him: (see Ham p. 86:) and, using it in the latter sense,] you say, h`*aA A^amiyrN EalaY maA duwna jayoHuwna This [man] is governor, or prince, over what is beyond [the river] Jeyhoon. (TA.) ― -b5- And i. q. qabol [generally signifying Before in respect of time; but as some say, in respect of place also, which may perhaps be here meant]: (T:) and [the contr., namely,] i. q. baEod [generally meaning after in respect of time; but as some say, in respect of place also, which may perhaps be here meant]. (Fr, T, TA.) ― -b6- It signifies also Nearer than another thing: (S, Msb, K:) so in the phrase h`*aA duwna *`lika [ This is nearer than that ]; (S Msb;) or h`*aA duwnahu [ this is nearer than he, or it ]. (K.) [Hence,] one says also, Audonu duwnaka meaning Draw thou near in the space that is between me and thee: (A Heyth, T:) [or approach thou nearer to me: ] or draw thou near [or nearer ] to me. (IAar, T, M, K.) And yaziydu baguD~u AlT~arofa duwniY , a saying of a poet, means Yezeed lowers the eye towards a spot between me and him. (A Heyth, T.) [ xa$aEato duwnahu AlA^aboSaAru , also, has a similar meaning: see 1 in art. x$E . So, too, has the phrase, xaAwata Tarofahu duwniY : see 3 in art. xwt . And hence,] one says, duwna Aln~ahori jamaAEapN [ In the way of, or to, the river, or on this side of the river, or nearer than the river, is a company of men; or] before thy reaching the river [there is to be found, or encountered, a company of men ]. (K.) And duwna qatoli AlA^asadi A^ahowaAlN [ In the way of, or to, the slaying of the lion, or] before thine attaining to the slaying of the lion, terrors [are to be encountered]. (T, TA.) [And duwnahu xaroTu AlqataAdi : see 1 in art. xrT .] And HaAla duwna Al$~aYo'i [ It intervened as an obstacle in the way to the thing; or] it prevented from attaining the thing. (W p. 71.) [And layosa duwnahu $aYo'N There is nothing intervening as an obstacle in the way of, or to, him, or it. ] And [hence,] qutila duwna maAlihi , and nafosihi , and A^axiyhi , and jaArihi , He was slain in defence of his property, and of himself, and of his brother, and of his neighbour. (Occurring in a trad. commencing with the words Algariyqu $ahiydN , in the “ Jámi' es-Sagheer, ” and thus explained in the margin of a copy of that work.) [And nabaHa duwnahu is a modern phrase meaning (assumed tropical:) He defended him as though by barking in the way to him. ] ― -b7- [Hence,] also i. q. definition: , an arabicized word, (AO, M, Msb, &c.
sourceDefinition: , an arabicized word, (AO, M, Msb, &c.,) from the Pers. [ diywaAno ]; (AO, M, &c.;) [though some hold it to be of Arabic origin:] J says, (TA,) it is originally diw~aAnN , but Y is substituted for one of the w s ; as is shown by its pl., (S, Msb,) which is dawaAwiynu ; (S, M, Msb, K;) for if the Y were radical, they would say dayaAwiynu ; (S;) but accord. to IDrd and IJ, (IB, TA,) it has this latter pl. also: (M, IB, K, TA:) Sb says that the w in diywaAnN , though after Y , is not changed into Y , as it is in say~idN , because the Y in the former word is not inherent; that word being of the measure fiE~aAlN , from daw~anota ; (M;) [i. e.] it is from daw~ana Alkutuba meaning “ he collected the writings; ” as is shown by their saying ↓ duwayowiynN , (M,) which is the dim.: (Msb:) ISk says that dywAn is with kesr only [ to the d ]; (M;) but one says ↓ dayowaAnN also, (K,) which is mentioned by Ks, as postclassical, and by Sb; like bayoTaArN : (M:) the meaning is A dafotar [or register ]: (Shifá el-Ghaleel, TA:) or a collection of written leaves or papers [ forming a book, generally for registration ]: (ISk, M, Mgh, * K:) or a register of accounts; an accountbook: (Msb:) and a register of soldiers and pensioners [ and others ]: (IAth, K:) the first who instituted, or appointed, or arranged, such a book, (Mgh, Msb, K,) among the Arabs, (Msb,) for the prefects, or administrators, (Mgh, Msb,) and the Kádees, (Mgh,) is said to have been 'Omar: (Mgh, Msb, K: *) accord. to El-Máwardee, it is a register of what concerns the rights, or dues, of the state, relating to the acts of the government, and the finances, and the military and other administrators thereof: (TA:) then any book was thus called: and especially the poetry of some particular poet: so that this meaning became [conventionally regarded as] a proper signification thereof; (Shifá el-Ghaleel, TA;) i. e. a collection of poetry [of a particular poet]. (TA.) [Hence,] one says, fulaAnN mino A^aholi Ald~iywaAni , meaning Such a one is of those whose names are written in the register. (Mgh.) [Also Such a one is of the keepers of the register; or, is of the registrars. (And sometimes it has another meaning, which see below.) And hence the saying] Al$~iEoru diywaAnu AlEarabi (assumed tropical:) [ Poetry is the register of the Arabs ]: because they used to refer to it on their differing in opinion respecting genealogies and wars or fights and the appointing of stipends or allowances from the government-treasury, like as the people of the dywAn [properly so called] refer to their dywAn in a case that is doubtful to them; or because it was the depository of their sciences, and the preserver of their rules of discipline, and the mine of their histories. (Har p. 263.) ― -b2- Afterwards, also, it was applied to signify An account, or a reckoning. (Msb, TA.) ― -b3- And Writers [ of accounts or reckonings ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And A place of account or reckoning, (Msb, TA,) and of writers [ of accounts or reckonings ] (TA.) ― -b5- [Also A council, court, or tribunal: see dasotN . Hence A^aholu Ald~iywaAni sometimes means The people of the council, court, or tribunal. ― -b6- And also, in the present day, A long seat, formed of a mattress laid against the side of a room, upon the floor or upon a raised structure or frame, with cushions to lean against; or two or more of such mattresses &c. similarly placed. ]

definition: The act of creating;
sourceDefinition: The act of creating; inf. n. of *araA^a . (S, M, Msb.) ― -b2- [And used in the sense of the pass. part. n. of that verb; and alike as sing. and pl. because originally an inf. n.] *aro'u Aln~aAri , (S, K, TA,) [for *aro'N liln~aAri ,] related as occurring in a trad. (S, TA) of 'Omar, (TA,) means Created [i. e. destined ] for the fire [ of Hell ]: (S, K, TA:) but as some relate it, the phrase is *arowu Aln~aAri , meaning [either “ the children of the fire, ” agreeably with what next follows, or] “ to be scattered in the fire. ” (S, TA.) ― -b3- Also The number of [ones] offspring: one says, A^anomaYA@ll~`hu *aroA^aka May God increase [ the number of ] thine offspring; as also *arowaka . (T.) -A2- Somewhat; (M, K;) as in the saying, balaganiY *aro'N mino xabarK [ Somewhat of news, or information, reached me, or came to my knowledge ]: (K, TA:) or *aro'N mino xayorK [ somewhat of good ]: (so in some copies of the K and M:) thus *r' is written by IAth: in some copies of the K, *uro'N , with damm: (TA:) or *aro'N here means a little; and *arowN is a dial. var. thereof. (M in art. *rw .) Also A little of what is said. (TA.) -A3- A thing intervening as a separation or an obstacle: so in the saying, maA bayonanaA wa bayonahu *aro'N [ There is not anything intervening &c. between us and him, or it ]. (K, * TA.)

sourceDefinition: (T, S, M, Mgh, K) and *ir~iy~apN (M, K) and *ar~iy~apN , (K,) [or *ariy~apN , without a sheddeh to the r , accord. to the Msb in art. *r ,] always pronounced by the Arabs without ' : (S:) accord. to some, (TA,) from Al*~aro'u ; (M, TA;) so says Th; (M;) the measure of the first being fuE~uwlapN or fuE~iylapN ; [so that it is originally *ur~uw'apN or *ur~iyoy^apN ;] (TA;) but the ' is suppressed because of frequency of usage: (M:) accord. to others, from Al*~ar~u , signifying “ the act of scattering; ” because God scattered the *r~y~p upon the earth; and the measure is fuEoliy~apN or fuE~uwlapN , [if the latter,] the word being originally *ur~uwrapN , the last r being changed into Y , in a manner similar to the case of taqaD~ati AlEuqaAbi [in which taqaD~aDat becomes taqaD~ayat and then taqaD~at ; so that *ur~uwrapN becomes *ur~uwyapN and then *ur~iy~apN ]: (TA:) Children, or offspring, (T, S, Mgh, K,) of a man, and used as a sing. also, (Mgh,) or of men and of jinn, or genii: (S, K:) pl. [ *ur~iy~aAtN (see art. *r ) and sometimes] *araAriY~u . (S.) Hence, habo liY mino ladunoka *ur~iy~apF Tay~ibapF [in the Kur iii. 33, meaning Give me, from Thee, a good offspring ]. (Mgh.) And in a trad. of Ibn-'Omar, fajaEalaniY fiY Al*~ur~iy~api means And he put me among the little ones, or young ones. (Mgh.) ― -b2- It is also applied to signify Progenitors: as in the saying, in the Kur [xxxvi. 41], HamalonaA *ur~iy~atahumo fiY A@lofuloki Alma$oHuwni [ We carried their progenitors in the laden ark ]. (T.) ― -b3- And it is used also to signify Women; [because they are the sources of offspring;] (T, Mgh, TA;) like as samaA='N is used to signify “ rain: ” (TA:) as in the saying of 'Omar, Huj~uwA biAl*~ur~iy~api [ Perform ye the pilgrimage with the women ]. (T, Mgh, TA. [See his saying in full, voce riboqN .])

(Mgh. [See also 1, last sentence.])

definition: Sharpness, or acuteness, of mind, (S, Msb, TA,) with quickness of perception, and of intelligence, understanding, sagacity, skill, or knowledge: (TA:) or completeness of intelligence, with quickness...
sourceDefinition: Sharpness, or acuteness, of mind, (S, Msb, TA,) with quickness of perception, and of intelligence, understanding, sagacity, skill, or knowledge: (TA:) or completeness of intelligence, with quickness of apprehension: (Msb:) or quickness of intelligence, understanding, sagacity, skill, or knowledge: (K:) or quickness of perception, and sharpness, or acuteness, of understanding: thus applied, it is like the phrase fulaAnN $uEolapu naArK : (Er-Rághib, TA:) or quickness in drawing conclusions. (TA. [See *ihonN : and see also 1.]) [It app. signifies also Sharpness of spirit; as a quality of a camel and the like. See *akiY~N .] ― -b2- Also Age: (S, K:) or full, or complete, age: so says Mbr in the “ Kámil: ” (TA:) contr. of fataA='N : (Ham p. 217:) accord. to Az, its primary signification, universally, is a state of completeness: and Al*~akaA='u fiY Als~in~ means completeness of age: accord. to Kh, it means the age of completeness of strength, [app. in a horse, or any solid-hoofed animal, for he says that it is] when a year has passed after the quruwH [or finishing of teething ]: (TA:) or *akaA='u Als~in~i means the utmost term of youthfulness; from the primary signification of the root, which is “ a state of completeness. ” (Mgh.) Hence the saying of El-Hajjáj, furirotu Eano *akaA='K [ I have been examined as to age; app. meaning (assumed tropical:) my abilities have been tested and proved ]: and balagati Ald~aAb~apu Al*~akaA='a The beast attained to [ fulness of ] age (S, TA.) sourceDefinition: , applied to a man, (TA,) Old, or advanced in age, and big-bodied, or corpulent: (K, TA:) [or full-grown, or of full age: see *akaA='N :] or an old man, but only such as is much experienced and disciplined: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and accord. to ISd, anything [i. e. any animal] old, or advanced in age: by some especially applied to a solid-hoofed animal; and said to mean one that has passed the quruwH [or finishing of teething ] by a year: (TA:) or ma*aAkK , (S, K, TA,) which is its pl., (S, TA,) [(like as mu*ak~iyaAtN is pl. of the fem.,) and also pl. of its syn. ↓ mu*okK ,] signifies, applied to horses, (S, K, TA,) of generous race, advanced in age, (TA,) that have passed a year, or two years, after their quruwH : (S, K, TA:) the sing. is like muxolifN applied to a camel: (S, TA:) or mu*ak~K signifies a horse of full age and of complete strength; as also ↓ mu*okK : (Ham p. 217:) or a horse whose run becomes spent ( ya*ohibu ), and [ then, but not before he has exhausted his power, ] stops. (TA.) It is said in a prov., jaroYu Almu*ak~iyaAtu gilaAbN [ The running of the horses that have attained to their full age and strength is a contending for superiority ]: (Meyd, and so in some copies of the S:) it may mean that the horse in this case contends for superiority with him that runs with him; or that his second run is always more than his first, and his third than his second: (Meyd:) or, as some relate it, gilaA='N ; (Meyd, and so in other copies of the S in this art., and in the S and K in art glw ;) meaning that the running of such horses is several bowshots: (Meyd, and S and K in art. glw :) it is applied to him who is described as entering into contests for excellence with his compeers. (Meyd.) ― -b2- [Hence,] ↓ saHaAbapN mu*okiyapN , (K,) or, as in the Tekmileh, mu*ak~iyapN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) A cloud that has rained time after time. (K, TA.)

definition: It (a thing, S) inclined, bent, or declined.
sourceDefinition: It (a thing, S) inclined, bent, or declined. (S, K.) Hence the prov., A_i*aA A@rojaHan~a $aASiyFA faA@rofaEo yadFA (S, Meyd,) or A@rojaEan~a , or A@joraEan~a , accord. to different readings, the last being formed by transposition from the second, (Meyd,) i. e. When he (a man, Meyd) inclines, (S, Meyd,) or falls, (Meyd,) raising his legs, then hold thou back [thine arm, or thy hand, ] from him; meaning, when he becomes lowly, humble, or submissive, to thee, hold thou back from him: (S, Meyd:) or it is said to a man fighting with another, and means when thou overcomest him, and he lies on his side, and falls, and raises his legs, then hold thou back thine arm, or thy hand, from him: (TA in art. rjEn , in explanation of the second reading:) [or when he is prostrated, and stretched upon the ground: for,] accord. to As, ArjHn~ and ArjEn~ signify he was prostrated, and stretched upon the ground. (TA in art. rjEn .) And you say, ArjHn~ Als~aHaAbu baEoda tabas~uqK The clouds became heavy, and inclined [ downwards ], after being high. (TA.) ― -b2- Also It (a thing, S) fell at once. (S, K.) ― -b3- And It (a thing, S) shook; quivered; or was, or became, in a state of commotion. (S, K.) ― -b4- And ArjHn~ Als~araAbu i. q. AirotafaEa [i. e. The mirage became upraised, withdrawn, or removed ]. (K.)

definition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. rizoqN , (S,) or razoqN , (IB, K,) the latter being the proper inf. n., (K,) and the former a simple subst. but also used as an inf. n., (TA,) God caused what is termed rizoq [q. v.] to come to him: (K:) or God gave him. (S, IB.) [The verb is doubly trans.: when the second objective complement is implied, the phrase generally means God caused the means of subsistence to come to him; i. e., gave him, granted him, or bestowed upon him, the means of subsistence; or supplied, provided, or blessed, him therewith: when the second objective complement is expressed, this word is generally one signifying the means of subsistence or the like, property, or offspring.] One says also, razaqa AlT~aAy^iru faroxahu , aor. , inf. n. razoqN , [ The bird fed its young one. ] (TA.) And razaqa AlA^amiyru Aljunoda The commander gave their subsistence-money, pay, or allowances, to the army: and razaqa Aljunoda razoqapF He gave the army their subsistence-money, &c., once: and ruziquwA razoqatayoni They were given their subsistence-money, &c., twice. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence ruziqa also signifies It (a place) was rained upon. ] Lebeed says, ruziqato maraAbiyEa Aln~ujuwmi waSaAbahaA wadoqu Alr~awaAEidi jawoduhaA warihaAmuhaA meaning muTirato ; (TA;) i. e. They were rained upon with the rain of the A^anowaA=' [pl. of nawo'N q. v.] of the rabiyE , and the rain of the thundering clouds fell upon them, the copious thereof and the drizzling and lasting thereof. (EM pp. 140 and 141.) ― -b3- And razaqa fulaAnFA He thanked such a one; was thankful, or grateful, to him; or acknowledged his beneficence: of the dial. of Azd, (K,) i. e. Azd-Shanooah. (TA.) One says, faEalotu *`lika lam~aA razaqotaniY i. e. lam~aA $akarotaniY [ I did that since, or because, thou thankedst me ]. (TA.) And hence, in the Kur [lvi. 81], watajoEaluwna rizoqakumo A^an~akumo taka*~ibuwna [ And do ye make your thanking to be that ye disacknowledge the benefit received, as being from God?]; (K;) i. e., accord. to Ibn-'Arafeh, do ye, instead of acknowledging what God has bestowed upon you, and being thankful for it, attribute it to another than Him? or, accord. to Az and others, [as J also says in the S,] the meaning is, tajoEaluwna $akora riziqokumu Alt~ako*iyba [ do ye make the thanking for your sustenance to be disacknowledgment? ]: (TA:) and some read $akorakumo [for rizoqakumo ]. (Bd.)

definition: A thing whereby one profits, or from which one derives advantage;
sourceDefinition: A thing whereby one profits, or from which one derives advantage; (S, K;) as also ↓ murotazaqN , (K, TA,) in the pass. form: (TA: [in the CK, erroneously, murotaziq :]) and a gift; and especially, of God: (S:) or [especially, and according to general usage,] the means of subsistence, or of the support and growth of the body, which God sends to [ mankind and other ] animals; [ sustenance, victuals, food, or provisions; or a supply thereof from God: ] but with the Moatezileh it means a thing possessed and eaten by the deserving; so that it does not apply to what is unlawful: (TA:) pl. A^arozaAqN : (S, Msb, K:) and what are thus termed are of two kinds; apparent, [or material, ] which are for the bodies, such as aliments; and unapparent, [or intellectual, ] which are for the hearts and minds, such as the several sorts of knowledge and of science: (TA:) or rizoqN properly signifies a portion, share, or lot; or particularly, of something good, or excellent; syn. HaZ~N : and is conventionally made to apply to a thing by which an animal is enabled to profit: (Bd in ii. 2:) and [hence] it signifies also a daily allowance of food or the like; and so ↓ rizoqapN of which the pl. is rizaqN : (TA:) [the subsistencemoney, pay, or allowance, of a soldier; or] what is given forth to the soldier at the commencement of every month, or day by day: or, accord. to ElKarkhee, AlEaTaA='u is what is assigned to those who fight; and Alr~azoqu , to the poor: (Mgh: [but see EaTaA='N :]) and ↓ razaqaAtN , pl. of ↓ razaqapN , which is the inf. n. of unity of raraqa , signifies the portions of subsistence-money, pay, or allowances, (syn. A^aTomaAE ,) of soldiers: (S, K:) one says, kamo rizoquka fiY Al$~ahori How much is thy allowance of food, or the like, [or thy subsistence-money, or pay, ] in the month? (TA:) and A^axa*uwA A^arozaAqahumo [ They took, or received, their portions of subsistence-money, &c.,] (S, Msb, K) is said of soldiers. (S.) Alr~izoqu AlHasanu means A thing [or provision ] that comes to one without toil in the seeking thereof: or, as some say, a thing [or provision ] that is found without one's looking, or watching, for it, and without one's reckoning upon it, and without one's earning it, or labouring to earn it. (KT.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) Rain (S, K) is sometimes thus called; as in the Kur xlv. 4 and li. 22: this being an amplification in language; as when one says, “ The dates are in the bottom of the well; ” meaning thereby “ the [water for] watering the palm-trees. ” (S.)

definition: He charged him with the watching, or guarding, of such a thing.

(A, TA.) You say, A^aroSadotu lahu AlEuqowbapa (tropical:) I prepared for him punishment: properly signifying I put punishment in his road, or way. (L.) definition: -A2- Also A road, or way;
sourceDefinition: : see raASidN , in three places. -A2- Also A road, or way; (Msb;) and so ↓ maroSadN , (TA,) both signify the same, (M,) and ↓ mroSaAdN (S, K, TA) and ↓ murotaSadN : (TA:) and ↓ miroSaAdN , (IAmb, K,) or ↓ maroSadN , (S,) or both, (M, A,) and ↓ murotaSadN and raSadN , (A,) a place where one lies in wait, or watches, (IAmb, S, M, A, K,) for an enemy: (IAmb, K:) the pl. of raSadN is A^aroSaAdN ; (Msb;) and the pl. of ↓ maroSadN is maraASidu , (TA,) which signifies also lurking places of serpents. (M, L.) You say, ↓ qaEada lahu biAlmaroSadi and ↓ biAlmiroSaAdi and ↓ biAlmurotaSadi (A, Msb) and biAlr~aSadi (A) He lay in wait for him in the way. (A, * Msb.) And A^anaA laka biAlr~aSadi and ↓ biAlmiroSaAdi (tropical:) [ I am in the place of lying in wait for thee ], meaning thou canst not escape me. (A.) And 'Adee says, ↓ waA_in~a AlmanaAyaA lil~rijaAli bimroSadi (tropical:) [ And verily deaths are in a place of lying in wait for men, so that they cannot escape them]. (TA.) ↓ waA@qoEuduwA lahumo kul~a maroSadK , in the Kur [ix. 5], means And lie ye in wait for them in every road, or way; (AM, TA;) accord. to Fr, in their way to the Sacred House. (TA.) And ↓ A_in~a rab~aka labiA@lomiroSaAdi , in the Kur [lxxxix. 13], means Verily thy Lord is in the way; i. e., in the way by which thou goest; (TA;) so that none of thine actions escapeth Him: (Msb:) or it means that He watcheth, or lieth in wait, to punish him who disbelieveth in Him and turneth away from Him: (Zj, TA:) or that He watcheth every man to recompense him for his deeds: (Ibn-'Arafeh, TA:) or, accord. to El-Aamash, AlmrSAd is here a name applied to three bridges behind the SiraAT ; on one of which is security; on another, mercy; and on the third, the Lord. (L, TA.) -A3- Also A small quantity of rain: (S, K:) one says, bihaA raSadN mino HayFA [ In it, namely, the land ( AlA^aroD ), is a small quantity of rain ]: (S:) and so ↓ raSodN : (TA:) or both signify rain that comes after other rain: or rain that falls first, before other rain coming: or the first of rain: or, accord. to IAar, the former word signifies rain such as is termed EihaAd , after which other rain is looked for; and if other rain follow it, herbage is produced: one shower thereof is termed ↓ raSadapN and ↓ raSodapN ; the latter mentioned by Th: (M:) or ↓ raSodapN signifies a shower, or what falls at once, of rain [app. in any case]: (S, K:) the pl. of raSadN is A^aroSaAdN (S, M, K) and riSaAdN , (M,) the latter mentioned on the authority of A'Obeyd: (TA:) [or] the latter is pl. of ↓ raSodapN . (S.) ― -b2- Also A small quantity of herbage, (S, M, K,) in land upon which one hopes for the fall of the rain of the season called Alr~abiyE . (M.)

definition: Sitting [or lying in wait ] for one in the road, or way: (Msb:) or watching, or waiting;
sourceDefinition: Sitting [or lying in wait ] for one in the road, or way: (Msb:) or watching, or waiting; li$aYo'K for a thing: (S:) or one lying in wait, or in a place of watching, or in a road or way, for the purpose of guarding: (Mgh:) pl. raASiduwna , (K,) and ↓ raSadN , like as xadamN is pl. of xaAdimN , (Mgh, Msb,) and HarasN of HaArisN ; (Mgh;) or [rather] raSadN is syn. with raASiduwna , (S, * A, * K,) or with murotaSiduwna , [which has the same meaning,] and is a quasi-pl. n., (M,) a word like HarasN (S, A) and xadamN , (A,) and used alike as sing. and pl. [and masc.] and fem.; and sometimes they said A^aroSaAdN ; (S;) and raSadapN also is used as a pl. of raASiadN , agreeably with analogy; (Mgh;) and ruS~adN likewise appears to be a pl. of the same. (Ham p. 415.) One says, ↓ fulaAnN yaxaAfu raSadFA mino qud~aAmihi waTalabFA mino waraAy^ihi i. e. [ Such a one fears ] an enemy lying in wait [ before him, and pursuers behind him ]. (A.) By ↓ raSadFA in the Kur lxxii. last verse but one, are meant watchers over an angel sent down with a revelation, lest one of the jinn, or genii, should overhear the revelation and acquaint therewith the diviners, who would acquaint other men therewith, and thus become equal to the prophets. (M, L.) ― -b2- Hence, (TA,) Alr~aASidu is an appellation of The Lion. (K, TA.)

definition: signifies (tropical:) The breaking off from, or quitting, another in anger: (S, K, TA:) and the cutting off another from friendly, or loving, communion;
sourceDefinition: signifies (tropical:) The breaking off from, or quitting, another in anger: (S, K, TA:) and the cutting off another from friendly, or loving, communion; cutting one, or ceasing to speak to him; or forsaking, abandoning, deserting, or shunning or avoiding, one: and the becoming alienated, or estranged; or the going, removing, retiring, or withdrawing, to a distance, far away, or far off, one from another: (K, TA:) [or] rAgmhu signifies (assumed tropical:) He left, forsook, abandoned, or relinquished, him, or separated himself from him, against his [the latter's] wish: (Mgh:) or he broke off from him, or quitted him, in anger: (Msb:) and A^aholahu ↓ Argm (tropical:) He cut off his family from loving communion, or forsook them, or deserted them, against their wish. (TA.) It is said in a trad., liyuraAgimu rab~ahu A_ino A^adoxala A^abawayohi Aln~aAra , i. e. (tropical:) He will assuredly break off in anger from his Lord [ if he cause his two parents to enter the fire of Hell ]. (TA.) And you say, raAgama fulaAnN qawomahu (tropical:) Such a one retired apart from his people, or party; or disagreed with them; or opposed them; (S, K, * TA;) and went forth from them; (S, TA;) and cut them off from friendly, or loving, communion; or forsook them; and treated them, or regarded them, with enmity, or hostility. (K, TA.) ― -b2- And fulaAnN laA yuraAgimu $ayoy^FA (assumed tropical:) Such a one does not want, need, or require, and is not unable to attain, anything. (JK, TA.)

sourceDefinition: [ He cast it upon the ragaAm , i. e. earth, or dust: and he made it to cleave to the earth, or dust ]. You say, Argm All~uqomapa mino fiyhi He cast the morsel from his mouth upon the earth, or dust. (TA.) And it is said in a trad. of 'Áïsheh, respecting the material for dyeing the hair, and the hands of women, Ausolutiyhi waA^arogimiyhi [ Wipe thou it off from thy hand, or hands, and cast it upon the earth, or dust ]. (S. [There said to be from the phrase here next following.]) You say also, Argm A^anofahu He, (i. e. God, JK, S,) or it, (i. e. abasement, or humility, or submissiveness, K, * TA, *) made his nose to cleave to the ragaAm , i. e. earth, or dust; (JK, * S, TA;) [or may He (i. e. God) make his nose to cleave to the earth, or dust; ] and ↓ ragama A^anofahu signifies the same [app. in this (the proper) sense, as well as in that next following]. definition: and ↓ rugomN and ↓ rigomN are inf.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ rugomN and ↓ rigomN are inf. ns. of ragima and ragama said of the nose; and ↓ marogamapN is syn. therewith; (S;) as is also ↓ marogamN . (TA.) One says to another, [by way of imprecation,] ragomFA [for ragima A^anofuka ragamFA May thy nose cleave fast to the earth, or dust; meant to be understood in the proper sense, or in a tropical sense explained by what follows]; (JK, M, K;) and [sometimes] dagomFA is added, (M,) which is an imitative sequent to ragomFA . (K in art. dgm .) And liA^anofihi Alr~agomu and ↓ Almarogamapu [ May cleaving to the earth, or dust, befall his nose; which may likewise be meant to be understood properly, or tropically]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] the first also signifies, (IAar, K, TA,) and so ↓ marogamapN also, (TA,) (tropical:) Abasement. (IAar, Mgh, K, TA.) The Prophet said, ↓ buEivotu marogamapF , (S,) i. e. (tropical:) I was sent for abasement to the believers in a plurality of gods, [or] by reason of dislike or disapproval [of their state; agreeably with the explanation next following]. (TA.) ― -b3- ragomN and ↓ rugomN (Msb, K, TA) and ↓ rigomN and ↓ marogamapN (K, TA) also signify (tropical:) Dislike, disapproval, or hatred. (Msb, K, TA.) You say, faEalahu ragomFA or ↓ rugomFA or ↓ rigomFA , (TA,) and EalaY ragomK , (ISh, TA,) and ElY ragomihi , and ElY Alr~agomi minohu , (TA,) and ElY ragomi A^anofihi and A^anofihi ↓ rugomi , (Msb,) and ElY Alr~agomi mino A^anofihi , (S,) i. e. (tropical:) [ He did it against his wish; in spite of him; or] notwithstanding his dislike, or disapproval, or hatred. (Msb, TA.) ― -b4- Hat~aY yaxoruja ↓ manohu Alr~ugomu , [or Alr~agomu , in the TA without the vowel-sign,] occurring in a trad., means (assumed tropical:) In order that he may become humble and abased, and the pride of the Devil may go forth from him. (Mgh, TA.) -A2- See also ragaAmN .

definition: (S, Mgh, K, TA) and ↓ mutarag~amN (JK, TA) and ↓ marogamN , (JK,) thus accord.
sourceDefinition: (S, Mgh, K, TA) and ↓ mutarag~amN (JK, TA) and ↓ marogamN , (JK,) thus accord. to one reading in the Kur iv. 101, (Ksh,) or ↓ murag~amN , (TA, [perhaps a mistranscription,]) (assumed tropical:) A road by the travelling of which one leaves, or separates himself from, his people, against their wish, or so as to displease them: (Ksh and Bd in iv. 101:) and a place to which one emigrates: (Zj and Ksh and Jel ibid.:) or a place to which one shifts, removes, or becomes transferred: (Bd ibid.:) or a way by which one goes or goes away: (Fr, JK, S, K:) and a place to which one flees; a place of refuge: (Fr, S, Mgh, K:) and i. q. muDoTarabN [meaning a place in which one goes to and fro seeking the means of subsistence: see art. Drb ]: (Fr, JK, S, K:) and a fortress, or fortified place; syn. HiSonN . (IAar, K.) It is said in the Kur, [iv. 101, of him who emigrates for the cause of God's religion], yajidN fiY AlA^aroDi muraAgamFA kaviyrFA [ He shall find in the earth many a road &c.]. (S, TA.) And a poet says, A_ilaY baladK gayori daAniY AlmaHal~i baEiydi AlmuraAgami waAlmuDoTarabo [ To a country not near in respect of the place of alighting, remote in respect of the road &c. and of the region in which people go to and fro seeking the means of subsistence ]. (Zj, TA.)

definition: Weak, or feeble: (S, JM, KL:) so as applied to a man: (TA:) and thin, or of little thickness or depth: (JM:) anything little, or small, in quantity;
sourceDefinition: Weak, or feeble: (S, JM, KL:) so as applied to a man: (TA:) and thin, or of little thickness or depth: (JM:) anything little, or small, in quantity; and slender: applied to water [that is little in quantity, and shallow ], and to herbage, and to science: (Sh, TA:) feeble, or weak, and incorrect; applied to a word or an expression; (PS in art. jzl ;) contr. of jazolN : (S and K in that art.:) [and unsound, invalid, or incorrect; applied to information, an announcement, &c.: see 1.] You say vawobN rakiyku Aln~asoji A garment, or piece of cloth, weak in respect of texture. (S, * TA.) And A_in~ahu yubogiDu AlwulaApa Alr~akakapa [ Verily he hates weak rulers, or magistrates ]: occurring in a trad.: rakakapN being pl. of rakiykN , like as [its syn.] DaEafapN is pl. of DaEiyfN . (TA. [See also a similar saying in what follows.]) And rajulN rakiyku AlEilomi , (K,) and AlEaqoli , (TA,) A man having little knowledge, (K,) and intelligence. (TA.) And rakiykN and ↓ rukaAkN , (K,) the latter of which has a stronger signification than the former, like TuwaAlN in relation to TawiylN , (TA,) and ↓ rukaAkapN , (K,) which has a still stronger signification, (TA,) and ↓ A^arak~u , (K,) all applied to a man, (TA,) signify Low, ignoble, vile, mean, sordid, or possessing no manly qualities; weak in his intellect, and in his judgment or opinion: or one who is not jealous (K, TA) of his wife; i. q. day~uwvN : (TA:) or one who is not revered, respected, or feared, by his wife, or his family: (K:) accord. to AZ, rakiykN and ↓ rukaAkapN signify one esteemed weak by the women, not revered or respected or feared by them, and not jealous of them: (TA:) the epithet similarly applied to a woman is rakiykN likewise, and ↓ rukaAkapN : and the pl. is rikaAkN . (K.) It is said in a trad., ↓ A_in~ahu laEana Alr~ukaAkapa , (S, * TA, [in one of my copies of the S written Alr~akaAkapa , and in the other copy without the vowel-signs,]) meaning Verily he cursed him who is not jealous of his wife. (S.) And in another trad., A_in~a A@ll~`ha yubogiDu ↓ Als~uloTaAna Alr~ukaAkapa , i. e. [ Verily God hateth the sovereign, or ruling, power ] that is weak. (TA.) ― -b2- rakiykapN , [fem. of rakiykN ,] as an epithet applied to land: see murak~N . -A2- Also Felt, or pressed [ lightly with the hand; see 1]; and so ↓ marokwkN . (TA.)

You say, raAEati AlHinoTapu , (S, Msb, K,) aor. tariyEu , inf. n. rayoEN [&c.]; (Msb;) and ↓ A^araAEat , (S, K,) which latter is said by Az to be more commonly used than the former; (TA;) and AlT~aEaAmu ↓ ray~aEa [which is the same as ray~aEati AlHinoTapu ]; (TA;) The wheat increased, or augmented; or received increase and blessing from God; or throve by the blessing of God: (S, Msb, K, TA:) and in like manner one says of other things. (Msb.) And raAEati Al$~ajarapu , and ↓ ArAEt , but the former is rare, The tree became abundant in its produce, or fruit. (AHn.) And sometimes they said, (S,) AlA_ibilu ↓ ArAEt (S, IF, K) (tropical:) The camels had many young ones; (S;) they increased, and had many young ones. (IF, K.) One says also, raAEa AlT~aEaAmu , and ↓ ArAE , The wheat became redundant; or had a part, or portion, redundant; [app. meaning, over and above the original measure; ] in the kneading and the making of bread; syn. SaAra lahu ziyaAdapN . (S.) [See the first sentence above; and see rayoEN , below.] And raAEa fiY yadiY ka*aA Such a thing was redundant, or remained over and above, in my hand; as also raAqa ; syn. zaAda : (L in this art., and TA in art. rwE :) Sgh has mistranscribed the explanation, zAd , in his two books, [the TS and the O,] writing faAda ; and the author of the K has imitated him in mentioning this in art. rwE , instead of the present art., which is its proper place, but has written for the explanation A^afaAda . (TA.) -A2- raAEa , aor. yariyEu , (IDrd, S, K,) inf. n. rayoEN , (S, TA,) He, or it, returned; went, or came, back; reverted: (IDrd, S, K:) and raAEa , aor. yaruwEu , (IDrd, and K in art. rwE ,) inf. n. ruwaAEN , (K in that art.,) signifies the same; (IDrd, and K in art. rwE ;) or it returned to its place: (TA in that art.:) but the former verb is the more common. (TA in the present art.) One says, of camels that have run away, SaAHa EalayohaA Alr~aAEiY faraAEato A_ilayohi [ The pastor cried out at them, and ] they returned to him. (TA.) And waEaZotuhu faA^abiY A^ano yariyEa [ I exhorted him, but he refused ] to return, or revert. (TA.) And fulaAnN maA yariyEu bikalaAmika walA biSawotika Such a one does not return, or revert, by reason of thy speech nor by reason of thy voice. (TA.) And you say of vomit, raAEa minohu $aYo'N Somewhat of it returned: (S:) and raAEa Ealayohi it returned to his inside. (TA.) And in like manner one says of anything that returns to him, raAEa , aor. yariyEu . (TA.) ― -b2- raAEuwA , They drew, gathered, or collected, themselves together; (Ibn- 'Abbád, TA;) as also ↓ try~EwA ; and ↓ ry~EwA , (Ibn-'Abbád, K,) inf. n. taroyiyEN . (TA.) ― -b3- See also 5. -A3- It became rent: so in the saying of El-Kumeyt, A_i*aA HiySa minohu jaAnibN raAEa jaAnibN [ When a side thereof is sewed up, a side becomes rent ]. (S.) -A4- [It is also said that] raAEa , aor. yariyEu , is like rad~a [app. as signifying He returned a reply, or an answer, to a person; for it is mentioned immediately after rayoEN as syn. with marojuwEN ]. (TA.)

(K, TA.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) He became confounded, or perplexed, [ as though vacillating, or wavering, ] and unable to see his right course; as also ↓ AstrAE . [See the part. n., below.] ― -b6- taray~aEato yadaAhu biAljuwdi (tropical:) His two hands overflowed with bounty, [ as though they went hither and thither, ] for one cause after another. (TA.)

definition: [see 1, of which it is an inf.
sourceDefinition: [see 1, of which it is an inf. n.] Increase; syn. ziyaAdapN [which may be meant to include the third of the significations here following]; as in the saying, h`*aA TaEaAmN kaviyru Alr~ayoEi [ This is wheat of much increase ]. (Mgh.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) Revenue arising from the increase of land: because it is an augmentation. (Mgh.) ― -b3- (tropical:) Milk; as in the phrase, naAqapN kaviyrapN rayoEuhaA (tropical:) [ A she-camel whose milk is abundant ]. (A, TA.) ― -b4- Redundance; a part, or portion, redundant; a surplus; or a residue; syn. faDolN ; of anything; as of flour, or meal, (Msb, K,) over and above the measure of the wheat; (Msb;) and of dough [when it has risen]; and of seed for sowing [when it has been sown]; and the like. (K.) Hence it is said, in a trad. of I'Ab, respecting the expiation of an oath, likul~i misokiynK mud~N mino HinoTapK rayoEuhu A_idaAmuhu [ To every poor man, a mudd of wheat: the redundance, or redundant part or portion, thereof shall be for its seasoning ]: i. e., it is not necessary for the person to give, with the mudd, seasoning; but the redundance that shall arise, of the flour, or meal, of the mudd [of wheat], when he shall have ground it, therewith shall the seasoning be bought. (TA.) Hence also, the trad. of 'Omar, AimolikuwA AlEajiyna faA_in~ahu A^aHadu Alr~ayoEayoni (assumed tropical:) Knead ye well, or thoroughly, or soundly, the dough; for this action is one of the rayoEaAni [here meaning the two causes of redundance; the other cause being the grinding]. (TA.) [Hence also,] rayoEu Ald~iroEi The redundant parts of the two sleeves of the coat of mail, (S, A, K, TA,) over [ and beyond ] the ends of the fingers; (TA;) and of the skirt thereof. (A, TA.) ― -b5- See also riyEN . ― -b6- Also, (K,) and ↓ rayoEaAnN , [which latter is the more common in this sense,] (S, K,) (tropical:) The first (S, K) and most excel-lent (K) part of anything: (S, K:) said in the B to be a metaphorical application from rayoEN as signifying a high, or an elevated, place. (TA.) Hence, (S, TA,) rayoEu Al$~abaAbi , by poetic license written ↓ rayaE , (TA,) or Al$~abaAbi ↓ rayoEaAnu , (S, A, L, TA,) (tropical:) The first, or prime, (S, A, TA,) and most excellent, (A, TA,) part, or period, of youth or youthfulness or youthful vigour: (S, A, TA:) or this is from rayoEN in relation to wheat: (A, TA:) or from AlmaTari ↓ rayoEaAnu (assumed tropical:) the first of rain. (L, TA.) Hence also, (S,) Als~araAbi ↓ rayoEaAnu (S, Sgh, L) (assumed tropical:) The first of the mirage; (S, Sgh;) what comes and goes thereof; (Sgh;) or such as is in a state of commotion or agitation, quivering, vibrating, or moving to and fro. (L.) [Hence also,] rayoEu AlD~uHaY (tropical:) The whiteness, and beautiful splendour, of the first part of the day after sunrise. (K, TA.) ― -b7- naAqapN lahaA rayoEN (tropical:) A she-camel having one pace, or rate of going, [app. a quicker pace, ] after another. (TA.) ― -b8- fulaAnN layosa lahu rayoEN i. e. marojuwEN [app. meaning Such a one has no reply, or answer, to give: or, perhaps, to such a one there is no reply, or answer, to be given]. (K, * TA.) -A2- Also Fright, or fear; (K;) like rawoEN . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: (Fr, S, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ rayoEN , (Fr, K,) the former occurring, (S,) or the latter accord. to one reading, (TA,) in the Kur [xxvi. 128], (S, TA,) High, or elevated, land or ground: (S, K:) or a high, or an elevated, place; (so in some copies of the S and in the Msb;) which latter signification is also assigned to ↓ riyEapN ; (TA;) and whence the phrase, kamo riyEu A^aroDika , meaning what is the elevation of thy land? definition: A sea full, or flowing with much water, and rising high: (S, TA:) and a valley flowing with a copious and high tide of water: and ↓ zax~aArN , also, is applied as an epithet to a sea [in a similar, but intensive, sense].
sourceDefinition: A sea full, or flowing with much water, and rising high: (S, TA:) and a valley flowing with a copious and high tide of water: and ↓ zax~aArN , also, is applied as an epithet to a sea [in a similar, but intensive, sense]. (TA.) [Hence,] one says, fulaAnN baHorN zaAxirN wabadorN zaAhirN (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one is a full sea, meaning bountiful, and a shining full moon, meaning illustrious ]. (A, TA.) The saying of the Hudhalee, describing a woman, jawaAdN biquwti AlbaToni waAlEiroqu zaAxiru means Liberal with the food of the belly in the time of hunger, when [ the vein is full, and] the blood and the tempers are excited: or it means, and her lineage is high; for the vein of the generous flows fully with generousness. sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. zafiyrN (S, A, K) and raforN (K) and A_izofiyrN , (M, [like A_iroziyzN , app. an inf. n., or perhaps a simple subst.,]) He drew in his breath to the utmost, by reason of distress: (S:) it originally signifies he drew back his breath vehemently, so that his ribs became swollen out: (Er-Rághib:) zafiyrN is the beginning of the cry of the ass, (Lth, S, A, Er-Rághib,) and of the like, (Lth,) and is generally used in this sense; (Er-Rághib;) and $ahiyqN is the ending thereof; (Lth, S, A, Er-Rághib;) for the former is the drawing in of the breath, and the latter is the sending it forth: (Lth, S:) or the verb signifies he sent forth his breath, after prolonging it: (M, K:) or he sent forth his breath with a prolonged sound: [i. e., he sighed, or uttered a long sigh, or sighed vehemently; or he groaned: ] or he filled his chest, by reason of grief, and then sent forth his breath: (TA:) or he breathed, raising his voice, like one moaning, or in grief. (Har p. 20.) ― -b2- [Hence,] zafarati Aln~aAru (assumed tropical:) The fire made a sound to be heard from its burning, or its fierce burning: (K:) and this [sounding] is termed zafiyrN . (TA.) [See also HadomN ; where zaforN , its inf. n., is expl., on the authority of AZ, as signifying The flaming, or blazing, of fire.] And AlbaHoru yazofiru bitamaw~ujihi (tropical:) [ The sea makes a roaring by its tumultuousness ]. (A, TA.) ― -b3- zafarati AlA^aroDu (assumed tropical:) The land put forth its plants, or herbage. (TA.) -A2- zafara , aor. , (S, A, K,) inf. n. zaforN ; (S, K;) and ↓ Azdfr ; (S, K;) He carried, (S, A, K,) a thing, (K,) or a load, or burden, (S, A,) as, for ex., a filled water-skin. (TA.) You say, yazofiruwna Eanohu AlA^avoqaAla [ They bear, or carry, or take off from him, and carry, his burdens ]. (A.) ― -b2- He drew, (K, TA,) and carried, (TA,) water. (K, TA.)

definition: A drawing-in of the breath to the utmost, by reason of distress: (S:) [or a drawing-back of the breath vehemently, so that the ribs become swollen out: (see 1:)] or an emission of the breath after prolonging it;
sourceDefinition: A drawing-in of the breath to the utmost, by reason of distress: (S:) [or a drawing-back of the breath vehemently, so that the ribs become swollen out: (see 1:)] or an emission of the breath after prolonging it; as also ↓ zuforapN and ↓ muzodafarN and ↓ muzaf~arN , (K, TA,) or ↓ muzofarN , (as in a copy of the K,) and ↓ muzaf~arapN : (CK, but omitted in the TA and in my MS. copy of the K:) [or an emission of the breath with a prolonged sound; i. e., a sigh, or a long or vehement sigh; or a groan: or an emission of the breath after filling the chest with it by reason of grief: (see, again, 1:)] pl. zafaraAtN , because it is a subst., not an epithet; but sometimes, by poetic license, zaforaAtN . El-Jaadee says, yarojiEo EalaY diq~apK walaAhaDami xiyTa EalaYzaforapK fatam~a walamo meaning As though he were sewed up after a drawing-in of the breath to the utmost, by reason of distress, so that he seemed to be constantly so drawing in his breath, on account of the largeness of his belly, [ and did not become restored to slenderness nor lankness of the belly. ] (S.) And another says, fatasotariyHu Aln~afosu mino zaforaAtihaA [ And the soul finds rest from its drawing-in of the breath to the utmost, by reason of distress; or from its sighs, &c. ]. (TA.) ― -b4- One says also, of a camel, or other beast, maA A^a$ad~a zaforatahu , meaning How strong is the knitting together of his joints! (TA.)

definition: One who is of the vanawiy~ap [or asserters of the doctrine of Dualism ]: (S, O, K:) or one who asserts his belief in [ the two principles of ] Light and Darkness: or one who does not believe in the...
sourceDefinition: One who is of the vanawiy~ap [or asserters of the doctrine of Dualism ]: (S, O, K:) or one who asserts his belief in [ the two principles of ] Light and Darkness: or one who does not believe in the world to come, nor in the Deity: (O, K:) or one who does not believe in the world to come nor in the unity of the Creator: (T, Msb:) or one who conceals unbelief and makes an outward show of belief: (K:) an arabicized word, (S, Msb,) originally Pers., so they say, (Msb,) from Alz~anodu , which is a book belonging to them [i. e. the book of Zoroaster]: (PS:) [or from the Pers. zanodiyk , meaning magian, or fire-worshipper: and this seems to be its primary meaning; as De Sacy says in his “ Chrest. Ar., ” 2nd ed., ii. 274:] or, accord. to IDrd, it is an arabicized word from the Persian zinodah , (Mgh, [thus in my copy, app. for zanodaho , in which the h may be, as it is in many other instances, an affix denoting some kind of relationship,]) or zanoda kiro , (TA, as from the L, [but not very clearly written, and with an erasure, such as to suggest that the original and right reading may be zanodo Giyro , which may be rendered holder of the Zend, but]) which is expl. as meaning he [ who ] asserts his belief in the eternity, or the endlessness, of the present world: (Mgh, TA:) or it is arabicized from zano diyn i. e. woman's religion: (O, K:) or the right explanation is this: that it is a term of relation to the zanod , which is the book of Mánee the Magian, who was in the time of Bahrám the son of Hurmuz the son of Sáboor [or Shápoor], and who claimed to be successor to the Messiah, on whom be peace; and, desiring fame, composed this book, which he hid in a tree, and then took forth: Alz~anodu , in their language, is “ explanation; ” and he meant that this was the explanation of the book of Zará- dusht [or Zoroaster] the Persian; and in it he held that there are two gods, Light and Darkness, Light creating good, and Darkness creating evil: (TA:) or, accord. to the “ Mefáteeh el-'Uloom, ” zinodiyqN means a follower of Mánee, and also a follower of Mezdek, who (i. e. Mezdek) appeared in the days of Kubádh, and asserted that possessions and women were in common, and put forth a book which he called znd , which is the book of the Magians, that was brought by Zará- dusht, whom they assert to have been a prophet: and the companions of Mezdek were named in relation to [this] znd ; which word, being arabicized, was converted into zinodiyqN : (Mgh:) Th says that zinodiyqN is not of the [genuine] language of the Arabs; (Mgh, TA;) and when the Arabs desire to express the meaning in which it is commonly used, (Mgh, * Msb, TA,) which is one who does not hold any religion, and who asserts his belief in the endlessness of time, (Msb,) they say muloHidN , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) i. e. [ a deviater from the right religion, or] an impugner of religions, (Msb,) and dahoriY~N : (Mgh, TA:) some say that it is from Alz~anodaqapu ; because the zndyq straitens himself: (L, TA:) an Arab of the desert is related to have explained it as meaning one who looks much into things, or affairs: (Msb:) the pl. is zanaAdiqapN and zanaAdiyqu ; (S, O, Msb, K;) the latter being the original pl., and the p of the former being a substitute for the suppressed Y of the latter. (S, O.)

sourceDefinition: , said of seed-produce, It increased, or augmented; received increase and blessing from God; or throve by the blessing of God: (JK, TA:) [or,] said of herbage, aor. yazohuw , inf. n. zahowN , it attained its full growth: (Msb:) or it put forth its fruit: or it became tall: (TA:) and, said of palm-trees, ( naxolN , S, Msb, K, TA,) and likewise of plants, (TA,) aor. as above, (Msb, TA,) and so the inf. n., (S, Msb, TA,) they became tall; (K, TA;) became tall and fullgrown; or became of their full height, and blossomed; (TA;) and ↓ AzhY signifies the same: (K:) or both signify they (i. e. palm-trees) showed redness, and yellowness, in their fruit; (S, Msb;) the latter verb mentioned by AZ, but [it is said that] As did not know it: (S: [see, however, what follows:]) or, as some say, the former signifies they put forth their fruit; and ↓ the latter, as expl. next before: (Msb:) accord. to Abu-lKhattáb and Lth, one says of palm-trees ( naxol ) only yuzohiY ; not yazohuw : and As [is related to have] said, [contr. to what has been asserted of him above,] that when redness appears in [the fruit of] palm-trees, one says AzhY . (TA.) And zahaA Alt~amoru , (JK,) or Albusoru ; and ↓ AzhY ; (Mgh, K;) and ↓ zh~Y , (K,) inf. n. tazohiyapN ; (TA;) [ The dates, or dates beginning to ripen, ] showed their goodness by redness, and yellowness: (JK:) became red, and yellow: (Mgh:) became coloured. (K.) Hence the trad., nahaY Eano bayoEi vamari Aln~axoli Hat~aY yazohuwa , or ↓ yuzohiYa , [ He forbade the selling of the fruit of the palm-trees until its becoming red or yellow ], thus differently related. (Mgh.) ― -b2- You say also, zahaA AlgulaAmu , (K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) The boy grew up; or attained to youthful vigour, or the prime of manhood. (K.) ― -b3- And zahati Al$~aApu , (JK, S, K,) aor. as above, (S,) and so the inf. n., (JK, S,) The ewe, or she-goat, became large in her udder: (JK:) or secreted milk in her udder, and was near to bringing forth. (AZ, S, K. *) ― -b4- And zahati Alr~iyHu The wind rose, blew, or became in a state of commotion. (S.) ― -b5- And zahati AlA_ibilu , (JK, S, M, K,) aor. as above, (JK, M,) and so the inf. n., (S, M,) The camels journeyed, after coming to water, (JK, S, M, K,) a night or more, (JK, S, M,) so says A'Obeyd, (S,) or a night or two nights. (K.) And The camels passed along, ( mar~at ,) so in the copies of the K, but correctly mad~at [i. e. made much advance in journeying ], as in the M, (TA,) in search of pasturage, after they had drunk, (K, TA,) not pasturing around the water. (TA.) The verb used in relation to camels is also trans., as will be shown below. (S, &c.) -A2- zahowN [as inf. n. of the trans. v. zahaA , aor. yazohaY ,] primarily signifies The act of raising, or elevating: and the act of shaking; or putting in motion, or into a state of commotion: whence zahaAhu Als~araAbu and zahati Alr~iyHu Aln~abaAta [both expl. in what follows]. (Har p. 171.) You say, zahati AlA^amowaAju Als~afiynapa The waves raised the ship. (TA.) And zahaA Als~araAbu Al$~aYo'a , aor. yazohaAhu , The mirage raised, or elevated, [ to the eye, ] the thing [seen in it or beyond it; or rather, made it to appear tall, and as though quivering, vibrating, or playing up and down; as is perhaps meant to be indicated by the citation above from Har]; syn. rafaEahu ; written only [thus] with A [in the pret. and in the aor.]: (S:) and Als~araAbu yazohaY Alqubuwra waAlHumuwla The mirage is as though it raised the tombs and the women's camel-vehicles; or elevated them; expl. by the words kaA^an~ahu yarofaEuhaA . (TA.) ― -b2- And zahaA AlmirowaHapa , said of a person fanning, He put in motion the fan; or put it into a state of commotion; as also ↓ zah~aAhaA . (TA.) And zahati AlriyHu Al$~ajara , (S,) or Aln~abaAta , (K, * TA,) aor. tazohaAhu , (S, TA,) inf. n. zahowN , (K, TA,) The wind shook, or put in motion or into a state of commotion, (S, K, * TA,) the trees, (S,) or the plants, or herbage, after the dew or rain ( gib~a Aln~adaY ). (K, TA.) ― -b3- And zahaAhu , (S, TA,) inf. n. zahowN ; (K, TA;) and ↓ AzdhAhu , (S, TA,) inf. n. AizodihaA='N ; (K, TA;) [not AzhAhu , as in the TK, followed by Freytag;] i. q. Aisotaxaf~ahu : (S, K, * TA:) and tahaAwana bihi : (S:) [the former of these two explanations as meaning He, or it, incited him, or excited him, to briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness; or to lightness, levity, or unsteadiness: and the latter of them, or both of them, for the former is often syn. with the latter, as meaning he held him, or it, in little, or light, estimation or account, or in contempt; he contemned, or despised, him, or it: but of this latter meaning I do not remember to have met with any ex.:] and bihi ↓ AzdhY signifies the same as AzdhAh (TA) meaning tahaAwana bihi . (JK.) You say, zahaAhu Al$~aYo'u and ↓ AzdhAhu , meaning [agreeably with the former of the two explanations in the sentence immediately preceding] Aisotaxaf~ahu TarabFA : (Har p. 359:) and ↓ yazodahiyniY as meaning [agreeably with the same explanation] yasotafiz~uniY and yasotaxif~uniY : (Id. p. 131:) and Alqawoma ↓ AzdhY as meaning [in like manner] Aisotaxaf~ahumo mina AlT~arabi ; and also as meaning He pleased the people, or party: (Id. p. 427:) and ↓ AizodahaAhu also as meaning Hamalahu EalaY Alz~ahowi [ He incited him, or excited him, to pride, or conceit, or the like ]: (Id. p. 131:) and zahaAhu Alkiboru (K) Pride rendered him self-conceited. (TK.) 'Omar Ibn-'Abee-Rabeea says, walam~aA taqaAwaDonaA AlHadiyva waA^asofarato wujuwhN zahaAhaA AlHusonu A^ano tataqan~aEaA meaning And when we discoursed together, and faces shone, beauty excited the possessors of them to levity ( Aisotaxaf~a A^arobaAbahaA ) and prevented their veiling them with the qinaAE [or head-covering ], by reason of self-admiration: or, as some say, the hA in zhAhA refers to a woman mentioned before, not to wjwh ; and the meaning is, beauty excited her &c.: and thus the women of the Arabs used to do when they were beautiful: or you may consider the complement of lam~aA as suppressed; as though he said, when we did all that, we behaved with mutual familiarity, or the like; for the complements of lawo and lam~aA and Hiyna may be suppressed, and their vagueness by reason of their suppression is more forcible in respect of the meaning: A^ano tataqan~aEaA means mino A^ano tataqan~aEaA ; for they often suppress the preposition with A^ano : (Ham pp. 552-3:) [J gives two readings of this verse, accord to one of my copies of the S: one is with tanaAzaEaA in the place of taqaAwaDonaA , and A^a$oraqato in the place of A^asofarato ; which make no difference in the meaning: but this is omitted in my other copy: the other is as follows:] falam~aA tawaAfaqonaA sal~amotu A^aqobalato wujuwhN zahaAhaA AlHusonu A^ano tataqan~aEaA [ And when we agreed together, and I saluted, faces advanced, which beauty excited &c, or the possessors of which beauty excited &c.]. (S.) And hence their saying, bixadiyEapK ↓ fulaAnN laA yuzodahaY [ Such a one will not be incited, or excited, to briskness, &c., by means of deceit, or guile ]. (S.) And AlfaraHu ↓ AzdhAhu , meaning Aisotaxaf~ahu [ Joy incited him, &c.]. (MA.) [And hence, perhaps, may be derived most of the following significations.] ― -b4- zahaA AlT~al~u Alnawora The Tl~ [or fine drizzling rain ] made the flowers, or blossoms, to increase in beauty of aspect. (TA.) ― -b5- zahaA Als~iraAja , (K,) aor. yzhwhu [perhaps a mistranscription for yazohaAhu ], inf. n. zahowN , (TA,) He made the srAj [or lamp, or lighted wick, ] to give a bright light. (K.) ― -b6- zahawotu AlA_ibila I made the camels to journey, after coming to water, (A 'Obeyd, JK, S, K,) a night or more, (A 'Obeyd, JK, S,) or a night or two nights. (K.) Thus the verb in relation to camels is trans. as well as intrans. (S.) ― -b7- zahaA biAls~ayofu He made a sign with the sword by waving it, or brandishing it. (K, TA.) ― -b8- zahaA biAlEaSaA He struck with the staff, or stick. (K.) ― -b9- zahaA bimiAy^api riTolK He computed, or computed by conjecture, [ to be of the weight of ] a hundred pounds. (K.) You say, zahaAhu bimiAy^api riTolK meaning xrzh [a mistake for Hazarahu i. e. He computed it, &c., to be of the weight of a hundred pounds ]. (TK. In the TA, zhA flAn bmAy^p rTl , [ Al$~aYo'a or the like being omitted by an oversight,] aor. yazohaAhu [which indicates an omission after flAn ].) And zahawotu Alqawoma I computed, or computed by conjecture, the number of the people, or party. (JK.) -A3- zuhiYa , (JK, S, K,) like EuniYa ; (S, K;) and zahaA , (IDrd, S, K,) like daEaA , but this is rare, (K,) and was dissallowed by As in the sense of zuhiYa , (TA in art. nxw ,) aor. yazohuw , inf. n. zahowN ; (IDrd, S;) and ↓ A^azohaY ; (K;) said of a man, (JK, S,) He behaved proudly, haughtily, or insolently; (S, K, * TA;) he was proud, vain, and boastful; (K;) or was pleased with himself, or self-conceited: (JK:) AzdhY [i. e. ↓ AuzoduhiYa ], in like manner, means takab~ara : (Har p. 264: [but this more properly signifies, as shown above by an explanation of AizodahaAhu , he was incited, or excited, to lightness, levity, or unsteadiness: ]) the first of these verbs [may be originally pass. of zahaA in the phrase zahaAhu Alkiboru , mentioned before, but, as J says,] is one of a class of verbs used in the pass. form though having the sense of the act. form: in using it imperatively, you say, lituzoha yaA rajulu [ Behave thou proudly, &c., O man; see art. t ]; and like this is the aor. [used as an imperative] of every verb of which the agent is not named; for when it is reduced to its essential import, you thereby command something, other than the person whom you address, to affect, or befall, that person; and the third person of the [aor. used as an] imperative is never without l , as when you say, liyaqumo zayodN : (S, TA:) J also says, (TA,) I said to an Arab of the desert, of [the tribe of] Benoo-Suleym, What is the meaning of zuhiYa Alr~ajulu ? and he answered, The man was pleased with himself, or self-conceited: I said, Dost thou say, zahaA as meaning Aifotaxara [ He gloried, or boasted, &c.]? and he answered, As for us, we do not say it. (S, TA.) One says also, zuhiYa fulaAnN bika*aA i. e. nuxiYa [ Such a one gloried, or boasted, and magnified himself, or behaved proudly, by reason of such a thing ]; as though meaning zahaAhu AlA_iEojaAbu binafosihi [i. e. self-conceit elevated him by reason of such a thing]. (Har p. 171.) ― -b2- And one says, zuhiYa Al$~aYo'u biEayonayoka or liEayonayoka The thing was beautiful in aspect in, or to, thine eyes. (S, accord. to different copies. [The meaning is there shown by what immediately precedes. In three copies of the S, I find the verb in this phrase thus written, zuhiYa ; and only in the PS, zhA , for zahaA , which is the form given by Golius: Freytag writes the phrase zahaY Al$Y bEynk .])

sourceDefinition: [is the inf. n. of zahaA (q. v.): and also has the significations here following. ― -b2- ] Pride [as implying self-elevation]: (JK, S, K:) vanity, or vain behaviour: (K:) boasting, or glorying: (S, K:) and wrongdoing, injustice, injuriousness, or tyranny. (TA.) ― -b3- A false, or vain, saying; syn. baATilN ; (S, K, and Ham p. 24;) a lie, or falsehood; (JK, S, K, and Ham * ubi suprà;) or an exaggeration in speech. (Ham ubi suprà.) You say, qaAla zahowFA [ He said a false, or vain, saying, &c.]. (Ham ubi suprà.) ― -b4- A beautiful aspect. (S, K.) ― -b5- The blossoms, or flowers, of a plant. (Lth, K.) ― -b6- The brightness of a plant (K, TA) by its becoming red or yellow; (TA;) as also ↓ zuhuw~N , (K, TA,) like Euluw~N , (TA,) [in the CK kAlz~ahowi is here put in the place of kaAlz~uhuw~i ,] and ↓ zahaA='N , (K, TA,) like saHaAbN , as the unrestricted mention of it requires, but in some of the copies of the K with damm [i. e. zuhaA='N ]. (TA.) ― -b7- Also, [or nabaAtN zahowN , as in the TK,] A plant beautiful and bright, (K,) or fresh. (TA.) ― -b8- And Dates beginning to ripen ( busorN ) that are becoming coloured ( mulaw~inN ), (so in some copies of the S and K, and in the Mgh, or mutalaw~inN [which signifies the same], Har p. 416), or that have become coloured ( mulaw~anN ); (so in other copies of the S and K;) as also ↓ zuhuw~N , (K, TA,) like Euluw~N , thus in the handwriting of Az in the T: (TA:) [here, again, in the CK we find kAlz~ahowi put in the place of kaAlz~uhuw~i : or perhaps it should be ↓ kaAlz~uhowi ; as appears from what follows in the next sentence:] in this sense, zahowN is an inf. n. used as a subst. (Mgh.) One says, when redness and yellowness appear in palm-trees, qado Zahara fiyhi Alz~ahowu [ Dates becoming, or become, red, or yellow, have appeared in them; i. e. fiY Aln~axoli ]: and the people of El-Hijáz say, ↓ Alz~uhowu , with damm: (S:) [Fei says,] the subst. from zahaA Aln~axolu meaning “ the palm-trees showed redness and yellowness in their fruit ” is Alzhw [i. e. ↓ Alz~uhowu ], with damm; and AHát says that this term is used only when the colour of the date has become free from admixture in redness or yellowness. (Msb.) ― -b9- You say also vawobN zahowN A red and beautiful garment or piece of cloth: and viyaAbN zahowapN and ↓ zaAhiyapN [ red and beautiful garments &c.]. (JK.)

definition: Number, or amount.
sourceDefinition: Number, or amount. (JK, Msb.) You say, kamo zuhaAw^uhumo How many is their number? or how much is their amount? (Msb, TA:) or, the computation of them? (TA.) And humo zuhaA='u miAy^apK [ They are as many as a hundred; ] they are the number, or amount, of a hundred; (El-Fárábee, S, Mgh, Msb, K; *) or their number, or amount, is a hundred: (Mgh:) and miAy^apK ↓ zihaA='u , also, with kesr: (El-Fárábee, Msb:) but the saying of the [common] people humo zuhaA=' EalaY miAy^ap is not [correct] Arabic. (Msb.) ― -b2- Also A large number: whence in a trad. respecting the time of the resurrection, A_i*aA samiEotumo binaAsK mino qibali Alma$oriqi A^uwliY zuhaA='K i. e. [ When ye hear of men coming from the direction of the east, ] having a large number. (TA.) ― -b3- And zuhaA='u Al$~aYo'i signifies The $axoS [i. e. corporeal form or figure or substance, which one sees from a distance, ] of the thing. (TA.)

definition: [meaning More, and most, proud, vain, boastful, or self-conceited, is, like maA A^azohaAhu (q.
sourceDefinition: [meaning More, and most, proud, vain, boastful, or self-conceited, is, like maA A^azohaAhu (q. v.), from zahaA as syn. with zuhiYa ; not from the latter of these two verbs]. You say A^azohaY mino guraAbK [ More proud, &c., than a crow ]; (S, Meyd;) because the crow, in walking, ceases not to go with a proud, or self-conceited, gait, and to look at itself: and mino waEilK [ than a mountain-goat ]: and mn TaAw^uwsK [ than a peacock ]: and diykK and *ubaAbK and vaworK and vaEolabK [ a cock and a fly and a bull and a fox ]: all these are provs. (Meyd.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, M, A, &c.,) aor. (S, M, Msb) and , (M, TA,) inf. n. saborN ; (S, M, Msb, K;) and ↓ Astbrhu ; (K;) He probed the wound; measured its depth with the misobaAr , i. e., with an iron or other instrument; (A, Mgh:) tried, (K,) or examined, (S,) or endeavoured to learn, (Msb,) its depth; (S, Msb, K;) examined its extent. (M.) ― -b2- sabarahu (assumed tropical:) He determined, or computed by conjecture or by the eye, its measure, quantity, size, or bulk. (M, K, * TA.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) He tried, proved, or tested, it; proved it by experiment or experience; (S, M, TA;) namely, anything; as also ↓ Astbrhu . (S.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) He elicited its true, or real, condition. (TA.) ― -b5- It is related in the trad. of the cave, that Aboo-Bekr said to Mohammad, laA tadoxulohu Hat~aY A^asoburahu qabolaka (assumed tropical:) Do not thou enter it until I explore it before thee, and see if there be in it any one, or anything that may hurt. (TA.) ― -b6- mafaAzapN laA tusobaru (tropical:) A desert of which the extent cannot be known. (A.) ― -b7- sabarotu fulaAnFA (tropical:) [ I searched into such a one ]. (A.) ― -b8- A^amorN EaZiymN laA yusobaru (tropical:) [ A great affair, of which the uttermost cannot be known ]. (A.) ― -b9- Ausoburo liY maA Einodahu (assumed tropical:) Learn thou for me what he has [ in his mind, or in his possession ]. (M.) ― -b10- sabarotu Alqawoma , aor. and , inf. n. saborN , (assumed tropical:) I observed the people attentively, with investigation, one after another, that I might know their number. (Msb.)

(M.) ― -b2- (tropical:) Form, or appearance; figure, feature, or lineaments; external state or condition; state with regard to apparel and the like; (S, M, K;) or goodly form or appearance &c.; (K;) aspect; garb, or habit; (TA;) colour, or complexion; (M, K;) beauty; (K;) brightness of countenance: (M:) pl. of both as above. (M.) ― -b3- IAar says, I heard Aboo-Ziyád El-Kilábee say, I returned from Marw to the desert, and one of its people said to me, A^am~aA Als~iboru faHaDariY~N waA^am~aA All~isaAnu fabadawiY~N (tropical:) As to garb and appearance, [thou art like] an inhabitant of a town; but as to tongue, an inhabitant of the desert. (S, * TA.) ― -b4- You say, fulaAnN Hasanu AlHibori waAls~ibori (tropical:) Such a one is beautiful and of goodly appearance. (S.) [See also HiborN .] ― -b5- A woman of the desert said, A^aEojabaniY siboru fulaAnK (tropical:) The good condition, and flourishing state of body, of such a one pleased me: and raA^ayotuhu say~iy^a Als~ibori (tropical:) I saw him to have an altered and ill appearance of body: thus she assigned to sbr two significations. (TA.) ― -b6- One says also, A_in~ahu laHasanu Als~ibori (tropical:) Verily he is goodly in complexion and appearance. (TA.) ― -b7- siborN also signifies (tropical:) A characteristic by which one knows the generousness or ungenerousness of a beast. (AZ, M.) ― -b8- And (assumed tropical:) One's knowledge of the fruitfulness or unfruitfulness [or the good or bad condition ] of a beast. (AZ, TA.) ― -b9- Also (assumed tropical:) Likeness; syn. $abahN . (K, TA. [In some copies of the K, sub~apN , which is an evident mistake.]) So in the phrase, occurring in a trad., galaba Ealayohimo siboru A^abiY bakorK (assumed tropical:) The likeness ( $abah ) of Aboo-Bekr predominated in them. (IAar, TA.) One says also, Earafahu bisibori A^abiyhi (assumed tropical:) He knew him by the appearance and likeness of his father. (TA.) ― -b10- Also the former ( siborN ), Enmity, (K,) accord. to El-Muärrij; but Az says that this is strange. (TA.)
