definition: and ↓ misobaArN A probe;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ misobaArN A probe; an instrument with which a wound is probed; (S, M, K;) as also ↓ misobarN : (Ham p. 818:) a twist like a wick, (T, Msb,) or a similar thing, (Msb,) which is put into a wound (T, Msb) to ascertain its depth; (Msb;) an iron or other instrument with which the depth of a wound is measured: (A, Mgh:) pl. of the first, suburN ; and of ↓ the second, masaAbiyru . (Msb.) It is said in a prov., maA Eurifa ↓ lawo laA AlmisobaAru gaworu AljuroHi [ Were it not for the probe, the depth of the wound would not be known ]. (A.) And ↓ baEiydu AlmisobaAri is applied as an epithet to a woman's vulva [or vagina, in an obvious sense,] by Ibn-Habeeb: and accord. to the K, to a woman [in allusion to her vagina]. (TA in art. xjY .)

definition: Water that is altered, changed in odour, or stinking;
sourceDefinition: Water that is altered, changed in odour, or stinking; syn. mutagay~irN : turbid, thick, or muddy: as also ↓ sajisN , (K, TA,) and ↓ sajosN : (TA:) or corrupted, and stirred up; as also ↓ musaj~asN : or the last signifies made turbid, thick, or muddy, and stirred up: the [only] form mentioned in the S is ↓ sajasN : but Aboo-Sahl says that ↓ sajisN is the form learned by him in reading under Aboo-Usámeh in the Musannaf; and as to ↓ sajasN , it is only an inf. n. (TA, from a note in the handwriting of Aboo-Zekereeyà.) ― -b2- Hence the saying, (TA,) laA A=tiyka sajiysa A@ll~ayaAliY I will not come to thee to the end of nights: (TA:) or ever; (S, K;) as also sajiysa All~ayaAliYi wa AlA^ay~aAmi , (TA,) and sjiysa AlA^awojasi , (S, K,) and sajiysa AlA^awojusi , (K,) and sajiysa EujayosK : (S, K:) or while time lasts; as also sajiysa Ald~ahori , and sajiysa AlA^awojasi : (A:) it is from sajiysN meaning “ turbid, ” because water thus termed is the last that remains: Eujayos is a corroborative; and Eajosu All~ayoli signifies “ the last part of the night: ” (TA:) or sajiysa All~ayaAliY means while the nights glide along continuously. (Ham p. 243.)

definition: , (S, K, TA,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, K, TA,) aor. , (K, TA,) inf. n. saHofN , (S, TA,) He pared it, or peeled it, off; (S, K, TA;) namely, a thing; (TA;) and [particularly] the fat from the back (S, K) of the sheep or goat, (S, TA,) not of the she-camel, as is indicated by the context in the K, (TA,) by reason of its abundance, after which he roasted it, (S, TA,) i. e., accord. to the S, the fat, but correctly the sheep or goat: (TA:) so says ISK. (S, TA.) ― -b2- And saHafahu , (Lth, TA,) inf. n. as above, (Lth, K, TA,) He removed it, or stripped it off, namely, hair from skin, so that none of it remained. (Lth, K, TA.) ― -b3- Hence, (TA,) saHafati AlA_ibilu (tropical:) The camels ate what they would. definition: A minister, or servant, of the Kaabeh, (S, Mgh, L, Msb, K,) and [so in the S and L, but in the K “ or ”] of the temple of idols;
sourceDefinition: A minister, or servant, of the Kaabeh, (S, Mgh, L, Msb, K,) and [so in the S and L, but in the K “ or ”] of the temple of idols; (S, L, K;) and one who performs the office of doorkeeper, or chamberlain: (K:) pl. sadanapN : (S, Mgh, L, Msb, K:) or sadanapN signifies the doorkeepers, or chamberlains, ( Huj~aAb , [pl. of HaAjib ,]) of the House [ of God, i. e. the Kaabeh ]; and the intendants of the idols in the Time of Ignorance; the latter being the primary application: (M, L:) but IB says that there is this difference between the saAdin and the HaAjib ; that the latter precludes, and his license to do so belongs to another; whereas the sAdn precludes, and his license to do so belongs to himself. (L.)

definition: , aor. , inf. n. siraEN (S, Msb, K) and saraEN (TA [and mentioned in the K, but app. as a simple subst.,]) and siroEN and saroEN and saraAEapN (TA) and suroEapN , (K,) or this last is a simple subst....
sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. siraEN (S, Msb, K) and saraEN (TA [and mentioned in the K, but app. as a simple subst.,]) and siroEN and saroEN and saraAEapN (TA) and suroEapN , (K,) or this last is a simple subst. from A^asoraEa , (Msb,) [but it is also generally used as syn. with the inf. ns. before mentioned when they are employed as simple substs., and is more common than any of them,] He, or it, was quick, expeditious, hasty, speedy, rapid, swift, or fleet: [in course, tendency, action, speech, &c.:] (S, K:) or, said of a man, i. q. A^asoraEa [which may mean as above, or he hastened, made haste, or sped, ] in his speech and in his actions: (IAar, TA:) but Sb makes a difference between saruEa and A^asoraEa : see the latter below: (TA:) one says also sariEa , aor. ; a dial. var. of saruEa : and ↓ tsr~E , said of an affair, or event, signifies the same as saruEa . (TA.) One says, Als~iraEa Als~iraEa like AlwaHaA='a AlwaHaA='a , (S, K,) i. e. [Make thou] haste; or haste to be first, or before, or beforehand: haste; or haste to be first, &c. (S and TA in art. wHY .) And saruEa maA faEalota *aAka , (S, * TA,) and saroEa , which is a contraction of the former; for the Arabs contract by the suppression of dammeh and kesreh because they are difficult of pronunciation, saying faxo*N for faxi*N and EaDodN for EaDodN , but one should not say HajorN for HajarN , (S, TA,) or the like, accord. to the Basrees, though the Koofees allow the contraction in the case of fet-hah also, as in salofa for salafa ; (M in art. slf ;) and one says also suroEa , as a contraction of saruEa ; all meaning saroEaAna [i. e. Quick was thy doing that: or how quick was thy doing that! or, which is nearly the same, excellently quick was thy doing that; for saruEa is similar to qaDuwa and ramuwa , denoting excellence]. (TA.)

definition: signifies The hastening with another;
sourceDefinition: signifies The hastening with another; or vying, or striving, with another, in hastening; or hastening to be, or get, before another or others; (S, K;) A_ilaY $aYo'K to a thing; (S;) as also ↓ tasaAruEN ; syn. mubaAdarapN ; (S, K;) with which, also, [not, however, as it is expl. above, but in the sense of buduwrN , i. e. simply the hastening to a thing,] ↓ A_isoraAEN is syn. (TA.) One says, saAraEuwA A_ilaY ka*aA and A_ilayohi ↓ tsArEwA , [ They hastened, one with another, &c., to such a thing, ] both signifying the same. (S.) And [of a single person,] sArE A_ilaY Al$~aYo'i He hastened to the thing; syn. bAdr . (Msb.) And it is said in the Kur [iii. 127], wasaAriEuwA A_ilaY magofirapK mino rab~ikumo [ And vie ye, one with another, in hastening to obtain forgiveness from your Lord ]. (TA.) And again, [iii. 170,] A@l~a*iyna yusaAriEuwna fiY Alkufori Who fall into unbelief hastily, or quickly, (Bd, Jel,) and eagerly. (Bd.)

definition: is originally trans.
sourceDefinition: is originally trans.; (S, K;) [signifying He quickened, or hastened, himself, or his going, &c.;] and hence the saying, in a trad., A_i*aA mar~a A^aHadukumo biTirobaAlK maAy^ilK faloyusoriEi Alma$oYa [ When any one of you passes by a high wall, or the like, that is inclining, let him quicken, or hasten, the pace, or going ]. (K, * TA.) But [it is used also elliptically, as meaning He hastened, in an intrans. sense; he made haste; he sped; he went quickly; and hence] you say, AsrE fiY Als~ayori , (S, K,) like saruEa [ He was quick, expeditious, hasty, speedy, rapid, swift, or fleet, in going, journeying, or pace ]: (K:) or [rather he hastened, made haste, or sped, therein; for] AsrE signifies he endeavoured, or sought, and affected, to be quick, &c., as though he hastened the pace, or going; but ↓ saruEa denotes what is as it were an innate quality: (Sb:) the verb being originally trans., when you say of one AsrE fY Alsyr it is as though [meaning] he urged himself forward with haste; or he quickened, or hastened, the pace, or going; and it is only because the meaning is understood by the persons addressing one another, that the objective complement is not expressed: (Lth, K:) or the verb may be trans. by means of a particle and without a particle: or when made immediately trans., the phrase may be meant to be understood as elliptical. (TA.) [Accord. to Fei,] AsrE fiY ma$oyihi , &c., inf. n. A_isoraAEN , is originally AsrE ma$oyahu [ He quickened, or hastened, his pace, or going ]; fY being redundant; or AsrE AlHarakapa fiY ma$oyihi [ he quickened, or hastened, the motion in his going ]: and AsrE A_ilayohi means AsrE AlmuDiY~a A_ilayohi [ he quickened, or hastened, the going to him ]. (Msb.) ↓ sr~E is syn. with AsrE . (TA.) And you say, A_ilaY Al$~ar~i ↓ tsr~E , (S, K,) meaning He hastened, or made haste, to [do] evil, or mischief; (K;) as also tzr~E . (Sgh and K in art. zrE .) And ↓ tsr~E biAlA^amori He hastened to do the thing, or affair; syn. baAdara bihi . (TA.) See also 3. ― -b2- AsrE A_ilayohi occurs in a trad. as meaning He was quick, or hasty, in being angry with him, or in blaming him, or in reviling him. (Mgh.) ― -b3- AsrE bihi : see [its contr.] baT~aA^a bihi . ― -b4- A^asoraEuwA signifies also, Their beasts on which they rode were, or became, quick, swift, or fleet. (AZ, S, K.) -A2- maA A^asoraEa maA SanaEota ka*aA [ How quick was thy doing that! ]. (S, K.)

sourceDefinition: and suroEaAna and siroEaAna (S, K) and ↓ saruEaAna , the last with damm to the r (IAar,) occurring in the phrase srEAna *aA xuruwjFA , (IAar, S, K,) meaning saruEa *aA xuruwjFA [ Quick is this in coming forth: or how quick is this in coming forth! or, which is nearly the same, excellently quick &c.], (S, K,) are dial. vars., changed from the original form, which is saruEa , and, for this reason, (S,) made indecl., with the final vowel of saruEa for their termination. (S, K.) The word srEAn is used as a simple enunciative [placed before its inchoative], and also as an enunciative denoting wonder: [see buToA=na :] and hence the saying, (K,) lasaroEaAna maA SanaEota ka*aA How quick was thy doing that! (S, K.) The saying saraEaAna *aA A_ihaAlapN originated from the fact that a man had a lean ewe, her snivel running from her nostrils by reason of her leanness, and it being said to him “ What is this? ” he answered, “ Her grease: ” whereupon the asker said as above: the last word is in the accus. case as a denotative of state; and the meaning is, Quick, or how quick, is this snivel [coming forth] in the state of melted grease! or the last word is a specificative, under the supposition that the action is transferred [from its proper agent, which thus becomes a specificative], as in the phrase taSab~aba zayodN EaraqFA ; and the meaning to be understood is, Quick, or how quick, is the melted grease of this! the saying is applied to him who tells of a thing's coming to pass before its time: (O, K:) it is a prov. definition: Quick, expeditious, hasty, speedy, rapid, swift, or fleet;
sourceDefinition: Quick, expeditious, hasty, speedy, rapid, swift, or fleet; [in course, tendency, action, speech, &c.;] (S, Msb, * TA;) as also ↓ sariEN [and ↓ saroEN ] and ↓ suraAEN , of which the fem. is with p , and ↓ saroEaAnu , of which the fem. is saroEaY ; (TA;) i. q. ↓ musoriEN , (K,) which signifies as above; (TA;) [and which also signifies hastening, making haste, or speeding; ] and ↓ misoraEN , also, signifies quick, &c., ( sariyE ,) to [do] good or evil: (K:) the pl. of sryE is suroEaAnN , (K,) and siraAEN is [also a pl. of the same,] syn. with musoriEuwna . (Msb.) You say, farasN sariyEN and ↓ suraAEN [ A quick, swift, or fleet, horse ]: (IB:) and ↓ HijorN suraAEapN meaning sariyEapN [ a quick, swift, or fleet, mare ]. (K.) And ↓ AisoEa EalaY rijolika Als~aroEaY [ Go thou quickly; lit. go thou, or walk thou, or run thou, upon thy quick, or swift, leg ]. (Fr.) And ↓ jaA='a saroEFA meaning sariyEFA [ He, or it, came quickly, hastily, speedily, &c.]. (TA.) And God is said [in the Kur ii. 198, &c.] to be sariyEu AlHisaAbi [ Quick in reckoning ], meaning that his reckoning will inevitably come to pass; or that one reckoning will not divert Him from another reckoning, nor one thing from another thing; or that his actions are quick, none of them being later than He desireth, because it is done without manual operation and without effort, so that He will reckon with mankind, after raising them from death and congregating them, in the twinkling of an eye, without numbering, or calculating: (K:) and [in like manner He is said in the same, chap. vi., last verse, to be] sariyEu AlEiqaAbi [ quick in punishing ]. (El-Mufradát, B.) ― -b2- Also A certain kind of going, or pace; coupled with sunobukN , which signifies another kind thereof. (Ibn-Habeeb, TA.) ― -b3- [ Als~ariyEu The ninth metre ( baHor ) in prosody, in which each hemistich originally consisted of musotafoEiluno musotafoEiluno mafoEuwlaAtu .] ― -b4- And A^abuw sariyEK The [ shrub called ] Earofaj : or the fire that is therein. (K. [See zaHofapN .]) -A2- Also A shoot, or twig, that falls from the ba$aAm [or tree of the balsam of Mekkeh ]: pl. siroEaAnN and suroEaAnN . (K.)

definition: and ↓ saAkibN and ↓ sakuwbN and ↓ sayokabN (K) and ↓ sakiybN (CK [omitted in the TA and in my MS.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ saAkibN and ↓ sakuwbN and ↓ sayokabN (K) and ↓ sakiybN (CK [omitted in the TA and in my MS. copy of the K]) and ↓ A^usokuwbN (K) Water poured out or forth, or being poured out or forth: or poured out or forth, (K, TA,) running upon the surface of the earth without any excavation: (TA:) or the first signifies water poured out or forth; and is an inf. n. used as an epithet, like Sab~N and gaworN applied as epithets to water: and ↓ sakuwbN , water running upon the surface of the earth without any excavation: and ↓ A^usokuwbN , water pouring out or forth, or being poured out or forth; (S;) or, as some say, pouring much: (Har pp. 469 et seq.:) and also this last, running water: (TA:) or this signifies daAy^imu AlhaTalaAni [i. e. continually pouring, or continually pouring dispersedly and in large drops; as also sakobN ; for hence it appears evident that AlhaTalaAnu Ald~aAy^imu as an explanation of Als~akobu and AlA^usokuwbu in the K is a mistake for Ald~aAy^imu AlhaTalaAni ]; and is applied as an epithet to water and to blood; (A;) and also [probably in this sense] to clouds ( saHaAbN ); and to a wound made with a spear or the like ( TaEonapN ): and ↓ saAkibN is applied as an epithet to tears ( damoEN ). (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence] sakobN applied to a horse means (tropical:) Wide in step: (S, A, K:) or fleet, or swift, or excellent in running; (A, K;) that runs much: (Mgh, TA:) or light, or active: and ↓ A^usokuwbN , so applied, has one or another of these meanings: (A:) or the former, thus applied, that runs vehemently; as also fayoDN ; likened to water pouring forth: (EthThaalebee, TA:) also, (K, TA,) applied to a horse and a man and a boy, (TA,) (assumed tropical:) light of spirit; and brisk, lively, or sprightly, (K, TA,) in work, or action. (TA.) Als~akobu was the name of the first horse possessed by the Prophet; (Mgh, * K;) as also ↓ Als~akabu : and the name of a horse of Shebeeb Ibn-Mo'áwiyeh. (K.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] (assumed tropical:) A certain sort of clothes, or garments, (T, S, K,) thin so as to resemble dust, and as though resembling pouring water by reason of its thinness; and so, accord. to IAar, ↓ sakabN . (T, TA.) ― -b4- Applied to a man, (assumed tropical:) Tall; (K;) a dial. var. of saqobN [q. v.]. (TA.) ― -b5- And (tropical:) A necessary thing or affair: (A, K, TA:) and (tropical:) a disgrace ( sub~apN ) that is necessary, or unavoidable. (A, TA.) Lakeet Ibn-Zurárah said to his brother Maabad, when he required him to ransom him with two hundred camels, he being a captive, numiyTu Eanoka $ayoy^FA yakuwnu EalaY A^aholi bayotika sub~apF sakobFA , meaning (tropical:) [ We will put away from thee a thing that would be to the people of thy house ] a necessary, or an unavoidable, disgrace. (TA.) -A2- Also Copper, or brass; syn. nuHaAsN : or lead: (IAar, K:) and so ↓ sakabN , (K,) in the latter sense, or in both senses, or in all the senses. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: : see the next preceding paragraph, latter half, in three places. -A2- Also A certain kind of tree, (S, K,) of sweet odour, (S,) as though its odour were that of [ the perfume called ] xaluwq [q. v.], growing apart from others, upon a single root, having a downy substance, and leaves like those of the SaEotar [ a species of origanum, or marjoram ], except in being more green: it grows in the plains and the valleys; and what has dried up thereof is of no use to any one: it has a fruit which is eaten, and the people of El-Hijáz make of it a [ beverage such as is termed ] nabiy* : its fruit does not grow forth in one year, but only in several years: AHn says that the sakab is a herb that rises to the height of a cubit, having dustcoloured leaves like those of the hinodabaA=' [or endive ], and a blossom intensely white, of the form of that of the firosik [i. e. peach, or a species or variety thereof ]: (TA:) n. un. with p : (S, TA:) As mentions the sakab as one of the plants of the plain, or soft, tracts. (TA.) ― -b2- It is also said to be The [ plant called ] ryH [app. ray~iH or riyH which seem to be coll. gen. ns. of each of which the n. un. is with p (see ray~iHapN )], having a yellow blossom. (TA.) ― -b3- And The anemone ( $aqaAy^iqu Aln~uEomaAni ). (K.) ― -b4- And One of the trees of the hot season. (TA.)

definition: , (IAar, MA, Msb,) or AlmakaAna , (K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (IAar, MA, Msb,) or AlmakaAna , (K,) aor. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. suluwkN (MA, Msb, K) and salokN , (K, [but I doubt this latter's being correctly used as an inf. n. of the verb in the sense here immediately following,]) He travelled, (MA,) or went along in, (Msb,) the road, (IAar, MA, Msb,) or the place: (K:) or salaka AlmakaAna he entered into the place. (TK.) [In these and similar instances, it seems that the prep. fiY is suppressed, and the noun therefore put in the accus. case, as in daxala Albayota &c.: for it is said that] salaka as meaning He entered ( daxala ) is intrans.: (Kull p. 206:) ↓ Anslk [likewise] has this meaning: (S:) ↓ Aslk as an intrans. verb [in the sense of salaka ] is extr. (Msb.) [ salaka TariyqFA is also often used tropically, as meaning (tropical:) He pursued a course of conduct or the like. ] -A2- And salakahu AlT~ariyqa , (IAar, Msb,) or AlmakaAna , and fiyhi , (K,) [inf. n. salokN ;] and A_iy~aAhu ↓ Aslkhu , (Msb, K,) this also is allowable, (IAar, TA,) and fiyhi , and Ealayohi ; (K;) He made him [ to travel or] to go along in [or to enter ] the road, (IAar, * Msb,) or the place: (K:) and so salaka bihi AlT~ariyqa : (Msb:) and ↓ sl~khu , inf. n. tasoliykN , signifies the same as [ salakahu thus used, and] Aslkhu . (TA.) And slakatu Al$~aYo'a fiY Al$~aYo'i , (S, Msb,) inf. n. salokN , (S,) I made the thing to enter, or I inserted it, or introduced it, into the thing: (S:) or I made the thing to go, or pass, through the thing: (Msb:) and ↓ A^asolakotuhu signifies the same. (S. [See an ex. of the latter verb in a verse of 'Abd-Menáf Ibn-Riba El-Hudhalee, voce A_i*aA ; cited there and here also in the S.]) You say, salaka AlxayoTa fiY AlA_iborapi He inserted the thread into the needle. (MA.) And salaka yadahu fiY Aljayobi He inserted [ his hand, or arm, into the opening at the neck and bosom of the shirt ]; as also ↓ A^asolakahaA : (K:) and so into the skin for milk or water, and the like. (TA.) And it is said in the Kur [xxvi. 200], ka*`lika salakonaAhu fiY quluwbi Almujorimiyna Thus we have caused it to enter [ into the hearts of the sinners ]. (S.) And in the same [xxxix. 22], fasalakahu yanaAbiyEa fiY AlA^aroDi [ And hath caused it to enter into springs in the earth ]. (TA.)

definition: Thread, or string, (S, Mgh, K,) with which one sews: (K:) or upon which beads are strung;
sourceDefinition: Thread, or string, (S, Mgh, K,) with which one sews: (K:) or upon which beads are strung; (Ham p. 42;) [ but ] not having beads upon it; for if it have, it is termed simoTN : (S and Mgh in art. smT :) [in the present day it signifies wire: ] a pl. [or rather a coll. gen. n.] of which the sing. [or n. un.] is ↓ silokapN : the pl. [of pauc.] of silokN is A^asolaAkN and [of mult.] suluwkN . (K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] one says, h`*aA kalaAmN raqiyqu Als~iloki (tropical:) This is speech, or language, [ subtile; or] abstruse in its course, or tenour; i. e. ↓ xafiY~u Almasolaki . (TA.) ― -b3- And maA A^anota bimunojaridi Als~iloki , (AZ, TA in art. jrd ,) or bimutajar~idi Als~iloki , (so in a copy of the A in that art.,) said to one who is shy, or bashful, (assumed tropical:) meaning [ Thou art ] not free from shyness in appearing [ before others ]: (AZ, TA in that art.:) or (tropical:) thou art not celebrated, or well-known. (A and TA in that art.) -A2- Also The first of what is emitted by the she-camel [ from her udder ], before the libaA^ [or biestings ]. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.)

definition: A thread, or string, having upon it beads (S, Mgh) or pearls;
sourceDefinition: A thread, or string, having upon it beads (S, Mgh) or pearls; (Mgh;) otherwise it is called silokN : (S, Mgh:) a string of beads or the like; (M, K;) so called because it is hung, or suspended; (M;) a single string thereof; like yako rasano [in Persian]; a necklace of two strings thereof being called *aAtu simoTayoni : (IDrd:) or it signifies, (M,) or signifies also, (K,) a necklace longer than the mixonaqap : (IDrd, M, K:) or [simply] a necklace: (Msb:) pl. sumuwTN : (M, K:) which also signifies the things that are suspended ( maEaAliyqu ) from necklaces. (TA.) ― -b2- A thong, or strap, that is suspended from the horse's saddle; (S, K;) sing. of sumuwTN . (S.) ― -b3- The redundant part of the turban, which is left hanging down upon the breast and the shoulder-blades: (K:) pl. as above. (TA.) ― -b4- A coat of mail which the horseman hangs upon the hinder part of his horse. (M, K.) ― -b5- (tropical:) A trail, or long and elevated tract, ( Habol ,) of sand, (K, TA,) regularly disposed, as though it were a necklace. (TA.) -A2- See also sumuTN , in two places.

sourceDefinition: , (M, K,) and ↓ samiyTN , (S, M, K,) and ↓ A^asomaATN , (M, K,) which last is pl. of samiyTN , (TA,) A sandal, or sole, that is of a single piece [ of leather, not of two or more pieces sewed together, one upon another ], ( TaAqN waAHidN , S, TA,) in which is no patch: (S, M, K:) or the last, (S,) or all, (M,) not having a second piece sewed on to it; (AZ, S, M;) as also ↓ simoTN . (M, K.) ― -b4- naAqapN sumuTN , (Kr, M, K,) and ↓ A^asomaATN , (K,) A she-camel without any brand, or mark made by a hot iron. (Kr, M, K.) -A2- sumuTN is also a pl. of simaATN [q. v.]. (K.)

definition: A rank of people: (M, K:) or a side, or lateral part or portion: (Msb:) each of the two sides, or lateral portions, of men, and of palmtrees.
sourceDefinition: A rank of people: (M, K:) or a side, or lateral part or portion: (Msb:) each of the two sides, or lateral portions, of men, and of palmtrees. (S, Msb.) You say, qaAma bayona Als~imaATayoni He stood between the two ranks. (TA.) And qaAma Alqawoma Hawolahu simaATayoni The people stood around him in two ranks. (TA.) And humo EalaY simaATK waAHidK They are according to one order. (K.) And ma$aY bayona Als~imaATayoni He walked between the two sides. (S, Msb.) And xu*uwA simaATaYi AlT~ariY~i Take ye the two sides of the fresh, or moist. (TA.) And AijoEali AlA^amora simaATFA waAHidFA Make thou the affair, or case, [ uniform, or] one uniform thing. (Fr, TA in art. bA^j .) ― -b2- The part of a valley which is between the upper extremity and the lower: (M, K:) pl. sumuTN . (K) ― -b3- simaATu AlT~aEaAmi The thing upon which food is spread: (K:) pronounced by the vulgar sumaAT : [and applied by them to such as is long, prepared for a large company of people: ] pl. A^asomiTapN [a pl. of pauc.] and simaATaAtN . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: is syn. with EaraDa [signifying It showed, or presented, its side: and hence, it presented itself; it occurred ]. (A, O, L.) One says of a gazelle, (S, K,) or of a bird, (S, * A, Msb,) or some other thing, (IF, S, Msb, as implied by explanations of the part. n. saAniHN ,) sanaHa (S, A, Msb, K) liY , (S,) or lahu , (A,) and Ealayohi , (L,) and sanaHahu , (A,) aor. , (S, L,) inf. n. sunuwHN (S, L, K) and sunoHN and sunuHN ; (L;) and ↓ sAnH , inf. n. sinaAHN ; (S, TA;) [ It presented to me, or to him, its right side, or its left side, in its passage; ] it passed along from the direction of my [or his ] left hand to the direction of my [or his ] right hand: (S:) or it passed along from the direction of [ my or] his right hand (A, L, Msb) to the direction of [ my or] his left hand: (L, Msb: *) contr. of baraHa (K. [See saAniHN , below.]) And sanaHa liY fiY AlmanaAmi He presented himself to me in sleep; syn. EaraDa : occurring in a saying of 'Alee, referring to the Prophet. (O.) And sanaHa liY raA^oYN (S, A, Msb, K) fiY ka*aA , (S, Msb,) aor. , inf. n. sunuwHN and sunoHN and sunuHN , (K, TA,) the second with damm and sukoon and the third with two dammehs, (TA, [but written in the CK sanoH and sunoH ,]) (tropical:) An idea, or an opinion, presented itself, or occurred, syn. EaraDa , (S, A, K,) or appeared, syn. Zahara , (Msb,) to me, (S, A, * Msb, K,) respect ing such a thing. (S, Msb.) sanaHa is also said of poetry, (L, K,) meaning (assumed tropical:) It presented itself, or occurred, syn. EaraDa , to me ( liY ): (L:) or it became easy; (L, K;) and in this last sense, said of a thing, aor. , inf. n. sunuwHN (Msb.) And it is related in a trad. of 'Áïsheh, that she said, [referring to the Prophet,] A^akorahu A^ano A^asonaHahu , mean ing I dislike that I should confront him with my hands [engaged] in prayer; from sanaHa as signify ing EaraDa . (L.) ― -b2- sanaHa bika*aA (assumed tropical:) He mentioned such a thing obliquely, or indirectly, (S, K,) in terms understood by the person addressed but uninteligible to others, (S,) not speaking explicitly. (K.) ― -b3- sanaHa AlxaATiru bihi i. q. jaAda (assumed tropical:) [ The mind granted it liberally ]. (Msb.) -A2- sanaHahu He turned him away, or back, (O, K,) Eam~aA A^araAda [ from that which he desired, or meant ], (O,) or Eano raA^oyihi [ from his opinion ]. (K.) ― -b2- And sanaHa bihi and Ealayohi He caused him to fall into straitness, or difficulty; or into sin, or crime; syn. A^aHorajahu ; (K, TA; in the CK, [erroneously,] A^axorajahu ;) [i. e. A^awoqaEahu fiY AlHaraji ;] and did evil to him. (K.)

definition: (S, A, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: (S, A, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ saniyHN (S, A, K) both signify the same, (S, A, K,) applied to a gazelle, (S, K, *) or to a bird, (S, A, Msb,) &c., (S, Msb,) Turning its right side towards the spectator; thus expl. by Ru-beh to Yoo, in the presence of AO; i. e. passing from the direction of the left hand of the spectator towards the direction of his right hand: (S:) or coming from the direction of the right side of the spectator (Aboo-'Amr Esh-Sheybánee, IF, A, L, Msb) towards the direction of his left hand; turning towards him its left side, which is that termed AlA_inosiY~u : contr. of baAriHN [q. v.]: (Aboo- 'Amr Esh-Sheybánee, L:) the pl. [of the former] is sawaAniHu and saAniHaAtN and [of either] sunuHN : and this last is also employed to signify auspicious and inauspicious gazelles [&c.], accord. to the different opinions of the Arabs. (L.) The Arabs [who apply the epithet in the latter of the two senses first explained] regard the saAniH as a good omen, and the baAriH as an evil omen; (Aboo-'Amr Esh-Sheybánee, S, L;) because one cannot shoot at the latter without turning himself: (S in art. brH :) but some of them hold the reverse of this: (Aboo-'Amr Esh-Sheybánee, L:) the people of Nejd hold the sAnH to be a good omen; but sometimes a Nejdee adopts the [contr.] opinion of the Hijázee. (IB, TA,) It is said in a prov., mano liY biAls~aAniHi baEoda AlbaAriHi [expl. in art. brH ]. (S, K.) ― -b2- [It is said in Har p. 671 that Als~aAniHu also signifies AlmtTy~r AlmtfA~l , as though meaning The person auguring, or who augurs, evil or good, from birds: but I think that the right reading is AlmutaTay~aru bihi waAlmutafaA^~alu bihi mina AlT~uyuwri , i. e. what is regarded as an evil omen and as a good omen, of birds. ]

definition: , (S, Msb,) or fiyhi , (K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb,) or fiyhi , (K,) aor. yasohuw , inf. n. sahowN (S, Msb, K) and suhuw~N , (M, K,) He was, or became, unmindful, forgetful, neglectful, or heedless, of it, or inadvertent to it; (S, Msb;) namely, a thing; syn. gafala Eanohu : (S, * Msb:) or he forgot it, or neglected it, ( nasiyahu ,) and was, or became, unmindful, forgetful, &c., of it, or inadvertent to it, ( gafala Eanohu ,) his mind adverting to another thing or affair or case; (K, TA;) thus expl. in the M and T; so that Als~ahowu and Algafolapu and Aln~isoyaAnu are made to be one [in signification]; (TA;) but accord. to Esh-Shiháb, Als~ahowu is a slight gafolap [or unmindfulness &c.] of that which is within the scope of the retentive faculty, such as when one's attention is roused by the least rousing thereof; whereas AlnsyAn denotes its passing away from the memory entirely; though all are used in one sense by a careless reliance upon the understanding of the reader or hearer: in the Msb it is said that a distinction is made between Als~aAhiY and Aln~aAsiY by the latter's being applied to him who, when he is reminded, remembers, and the former's being applied to him who is in the contrary case: accord. to IAth, sahaAfiY Al$~aYo'i means he neglected, or omitted, the thing unknowingly; and sahaA Eanohu , he neglected, or omitted, it knowingly: or, as some say, Als~ahowu is the doing wrong from unmindfulness ( Eano gafolap ); as when an insane person reviles another, which is pardonable; and as when one drinks wine and then some unpleasing action proceeds from him unintentionally, which is punishable. (TA.) One says, sahaAfiY AlS~alaApi , and EanohaA , i. q. gafala [ He was, or became, unmindful in prayer, and of it ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, app., as implying an unexpected event,] Hamalato sahowFA She (a woman, S) conceived in menstruis. (Az, S, Z, K.) And Hamalato bihi A^um~uhu sahowFA His mother conceived him in menstruis. (JK.) ― -b3- Als~ahowu also signifies Als~ukuwnu (JK, S, K) and All~iynu (JK, S,) [app. as an inf. n., i. e. as meaning The being still, or quiet, and gentle; though it is immediately added in the S that the pl. is sihaA='N ; for it seems that an early transcriber of the S has omitted to insert after All~aynu the words waAls~aAkinu waAll~ay~inu : see sahowN below]. One says, faEalahu sahowFA rahowFA He did it voluntarily, without its being asked, or demanded; (K, TA;) and without constraint: (TA:) or quietly, or calmly, without being hard, or difficult. (TA in art. rhw .) And sahaA A_ilayohi He looked at him, or it, with motionless eye. (Msb, TA.) And AlEayonu tasohuw fiyhi The eye expatiates in it; syn. tanobasiTu . (JK.) -A2- sahaAwapN , as denoting a quality of a camel, The being easy to ride; (K;) an inf. n., of which the verb is sahuwa . (TA.) -A3- maAlN laA yusohaY walaA yunohaY [ Cattle ] of which the end is not to be reached. (AA, JK, S, K.) You say, yaraAHu EalaY baniY fulaAnK mina AlmaAli maA laA yusohaYwalaA yunohaY [ There returns from the place of pasture in the evening, or afternoon, to the sons of such a one, of cattle, ] what is not to be numbered for multitude: (T, TA:) or what is not to be computed, or computed by conjecture. (IAar, TA.) And *ahabato tamiymu falaA tusohaY walaA tunohaY , meaning laA tu*okaru [i. e. Temeem went away, and will not be remembered, or will not be mentioned ]: a saying of El-Ahmar. (TA.)

definition: [an inf. n. used as an epithet,] Easy; applied to a man, and to an affair, (K, TA,) and to an object of want: (TA:) and so [the fem.] sahowapN , applied to a mare; and applied to a she-mule as...
sourceDefinition: [an inf. n. used as an epithet,] Easy; applied to a man, and to an affair, (K, TA,) and to an object of want: (TA:) and so [the fem.] sahowapN , applied to a mare; and applied to a she-mule as meaning easy in pace, that does not fatigue her rider: the epithet sahowN , however, is not applied to a he-mule: so in the T: (TA:) [but] it is applied to a he-camel, meaning easy to ride: and sahowapN to a she-camel, (K, TA,) meaning gentle, easy to ride: and raAhK ↓ saAhK , applied to a he-camel, means [likewise] gentle in pace; and so [the pls.] sawaAhK rawaAhK applied to camels: (TA:) [and so ↓ sahowaA='u applied to a mare; for] a certain mare was named Als~ahowaA='u because of the gentleness of her pace. (TA.) Also, applied to water, Cool, sweet, or limpid; easy of descent in the throat. (K, * TA.) And qawosN sahowapN A bow that is compliant, (K, TA,) and easy. (TA.) And riyHN sahowN A gentle wind: [or a quiet, gentle wind: ] pl. sihaA='N : (TA:) a poet (said to be El-Hárith Ibn- 'Owf, TA) says, tanaAwaHati Alr~ayaAHu lifaqodi EamorKw wakaAnato qabola maholikihi sihaA='aA i. e. [ The winds blew violently for the loss of 'Amr; but they were before his death ] quiet and gentle. (S, TA.) One says also A^aroDN sahowapN Soft land, without barrenness. (TA.) -A2- And Als~ahowu means The moon, in the language of the Nabathæans. (JK.)

definition: An instance, or a case, of unmindfulness, forgetfulness, neglectfulness, heedlessness, or inadvertence.
sourceDefinition: An instance, or a case, of unmindfulness, forgetfulness, neglectfulness, heedlessness, or inadvertence. (Msb.) -A2- A rock, or great mass of stone, (K,) in the dial. of Teiyi, who call nothing else by this name: so in the M: or, accord. to the T, in that dial., the rock, or great mass of stone, upon which the waterer [app. of camels ] stands: (TA:) or a rock, or great mass of stone, standing up, not having any foundation [app. meaning not partly imbedded ] in the ground: and in the dial. of Teiyi, a single stone, great or small. (JK.) ― -b2- A bayot [app. here meaning booth, or the like, ] which the Arabs of the desert set up at the water, and by the shade of which they shelter themselves. (TA.) A Suf~ap [or kind of roofed vestibule, or the like, or a covering for shade and shelter ], (K, TA,) between two houses: (TA:) or a thing like the Suf~ap , which is before, or in the front of, houses: (As, JK, S:) or [in some copies of the K “ and ”] a kind of closet ( muixodaE ) between two chambers, (K, TA,) in which the waterers of the camels shelter themselves: or, as some say, a small wall which is build between the two [ opposite main ] walls of the chamber, the roof being placed over the whole; what is in the middle [or main part ] of the chamber being [ called ] a sahowap ; [see EarosN ;] and what is within it, [app. behind, ] a muixodaE : (TA:) or the like of a raf~ and TaAq , [app. meaning a kind of arched construction with a flat top which forms a shelf, against a wall; or simply a shelf, or ledge projecting from a wall, (see raf~N and TaAqN ,)] in which, or upon which, a thing is placed: (ISd, K:) or a small bayot [or chamber ], (S, K,) descending into the earth, having its roof elevated above the ground, (S,) resembling a small xizaAnap [or closet, or storeroom ], (S, K,) in which are [ deposited ] the household-goods, or furniture and utensils; thus as heard by A'Obeyd from more than one of the people of El-Yemen: (S:) or it signifies, (K,) or signifies also, (JK,) four sticks, or pieces of wood, (JK, K,) or three, (K,) which are placed crosswise, one upon another, and upon which is then put anything of the household-goods, or furniture and utensils: (JK, K:) so in the M: (TA:) and (accord. to the T, TA) i. q. kanoduwjN , (K,) which means a small closet or store-room: (TA:) and i. q. rawo$anN and kuw~apN [i. e. a window, or mural aperture ]: and a [ kind of curtained canopy, or the like, such as is called ] Hajalap : and a curtain, or screen, before the court, or yard, of a house, (K, TA,) and sometimes, surrounding the house, like a wall: (TA:) its pl. (in all of these senses, K, TA) is sihaA='N (JK, K, TA) and sahawaAtN . (JK.)

definition: Unmindful, forgetful, neglectful, heedless, or inadvertent;
sourceDefinition: Unmindful, forgetful, neglectful, heedless, or inadvertent; (JK, S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ sahowaAnu ; (S, K;) whence the prov., A_in~a AlmuwaS~ayona banuw sahowaAno (S) i. e. Only the unmindful [lit. the sons of the unmindful ] are such as require to be enjoined: (S, Meyd:) or, as some say, by bnw shwAn are meant all mankind; because all become unmindful: but the most correct explanation is, that those who are enjoined to do a thing are subject to unmindfulness: it is applied to him who is unmindful of pursuing that which he is commanded to do: and shwAn may be syn. with [the inf. n.] sahowN ; or it may be an epithet, syn. with saAhK , and is applied to Adam, because he forgot his cove- nant, so that bnw shwAn may mean the sons of Adam, and hence, the unmindful. (Meyd. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 3-4.]) ― -b2- See also sahwN .

definition: A thing, an affair, or a business;
sourceDefinition: A thing, an affair, or a business; syn. A^amorN ; (S, L, K;) and xaTobN [in the same sense, or in that next following]: (L, K:) a great thing or affair: (Har p. 274:) state, condition, case, quality, or manner of being; syn. HaAlN : (S, L:) [also property, or nature: and importance attaching to a person or thing:] pl. $uw^uwnN and $iy^aAnN , (L, K,) the latter mentioned by IJ on the authority of AAF, and $uwnN occurs in poetry for the former of these, or as another pl. originally $uw^onN , of the measure fuEolN . (L.) It is said in the Kur [lv. 29], kul~a yam K huwa fiY $aA^onK [ Every day He is employing Himself in an affair of some kind]: expl. as meaning that, of his business ( mino $aA^onihi [which may also be rendered “ of his property ”]) it is to render mighty one who is brought low, and to bring low one who is mighty, and to enrich one who is poor, and to impoverish one who is rich; and no affair occupies him so as to divert him from an affair ( laA ya$oEaluhu $aA^onN Eano $aA^onK ). (L.) [And one says, maA $aA^onuka What is thy affair? or what is thy case? And $aA^onaka , for Ai$oA^ano $aA^onaka i. e. Pursue thy way or course, or thy affair; or do what thou dost well; or keep to thy affair: or the like: and to this is often added, wamaA turiydu i. e. and what thou wilt, or wishest, or desirest. And mino $aA^onihi A^ano yafoEala ka*aA It is of his business, or of his property, or nature, to do, or that he should do, such a thing. And rajulN saholu Al$~aA^oni (a phrase occurring in the S and K in art. h$ ) A man of easy nature. And lahu $aA^onN , sometimes meaning There is for him, or he has, a great thing or affair to perform or transact: but more commonly, great importance attaches to him, or to it: see 1, last sentence. And a grandee, or a prince, is said to be EaZiymu Al$~aA^oni i. e. Of great importance or rank or dignity. ] -A2- Also [ A suture of the skull; i. e.] the place of junction of the qabaAy^il [or principal bones, namely, the frontal, occipital, and two parietal, bones, ] of the head: (K:) sing. of $uw^uwnN , (Mgh,) which signifies the places of junction, (As, S, Mgh, L,) and of meeting, (S, L,) of the qabaAy^il (As, S, Mgh, L) of the head; (S, L;) between every two of which qbAy^l is a $aA^on : (As, L:) [it is fancifully said that] from them come the tears: (As, S, L:) the pl. is also expl. as meaning the salaAsil [i. e. sutures as being likened to the slAsl (or lines) of writing] that unite the qbAy^l : by Lth, as the namaAnim [likewise meaning sutures resembling lines of writing ] of the skull; between the qbAy^l : by AHát, as the $uEab [meaning serrated edges ] that unite the qbAy^l of the head. (L.) ― -b2- And The channel by which the tears flow, or run, to the eye: pl. [of pauc.] A^a$ow^unN and [of mult.] $uw^uwnN : (L, K:) [perhaps thus called because supposed to come from the sutures of the skull: but they may have been supposed to come thence because tears are called maA='u Al$~uw^uwni (as in a verse cited voce rasama ); for this phrase may have been misunderstood as signifying “ the water of the sutures of the skull, ” whereas it seems to be properly rendered “ the water of the channels of the tears: ”] it is said that the $uw^uwn connect the qbAy^l of the head [expl. above] to the eye: Lth says that they are the ducts ( Euruwq ) of the tears from [ the interior of ] the head to the eye: and Th, that they are certain ducts ( Erwq ) above the qbAy^l , which become strong by degrees as the man advances in age: (L: [but it seems that Th has confounded explanations of $w^wn in two different senses:]) accord. to ISk, (S,) or AA and others, (L,) the $aA^onaAni are two ducts ( EiroqaAni ) descending from [ the upper part of ] the head to the eyebrows and then to the eyes. (S, L.) ― -b3- [The pl. $uw^uwnN is also expl. as though meaning Tears themselves, in a phrase mentioned voce *ay^irN (q. v.), on the authority of the K.] ― -b4- And $uw^uwnN Alxamori means (assumed tropical:) The effluvia of wine that creep ( maA dab~a mina Alxamori ) in the veins of the body. (L.) ― -b5- $aA^onN also signifies A vein of earth in a mountain, (L, K,) i. e. a cleft therein, (L,) in which palm-trees are planted; (L, K;) or in which trees of the kind called naboE grow; or that produces plants, or herbage: (L:) pl. $uw^uwnN : (L, K:) which is said by ISd to mean lines, or streaks, in a mountain: or, as some say, cracks, or clefts: and to these cracks, or clefts, the poet Keys Ibn-Kuráa likens [imaginary] clefts in the liver, occasioned by love. (L.)

sourceDefinition: A species of tree, (As, IDrd, ISd, Msb,) of those that grow upon the mountains, (As,) or a certain plant, (S, K,) of sweet odour, (S, Msb, K,) but bitter to the taste, (S, Msb,) with which one tans, (S, K,) growing in the mountains of El-Ghowr (ADk, Msb) and Tihámeh and Nejd; (ADk;) a kind of tree like the dwarf-apple-tree, (AHn, Mgh,) in size, (AHn,) the leaves of which are like those of the xilaAf [q. v.], (AHn, Mgh,) and are used for tanning therewith, (Mgh,) without thorns, and having a small rose-coloured [ fruit of the kind called ] baramap , in which are three or four black grains, resembling the $iyniyz [q. v.], which, when scattered, are eaten by the pigeons: n. un. with p . (AHn:) the word occurs in a trad. as the name of a tan: Az says that it is a mistake for $ab~ , though he knew not whether the $av~ were used for tanning, or not: (TA:) [Mtr, however, says that] $ib~ is a mistake in this case, for it is a species of zaAj , and is a dye, not a tan: (Mgh:) accord. to some, (TA,) the $av~ is the wild nut ( jawozu Albar~i ). (K [in which this last is mentioned as a distinct signification] and TA.) [See also $ab~N .] -A2- The honey-bee. (AA, K.) -A3- A broken portion of the head of a mountain, remaining in a form like the [ kind of acroterial ornament of a wall called ] $urofap : pl. $ivaAvN . (K.) -A4- Also Many, or much, of anything. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: ; fem. $ajoEaA='u : see $ujaAEN , in four places. You say also, labuw^apN $ajoEaA='u A bold lioness. (TA.) ― -b2- Applied to a man, accord. to some, it signifies, (S,) or it signifies also, (K,) In whom is lightness, or unsteadiness, like what is termed hawajN , (S, K,) by reason of his strength. (S.) See also $ajiEN . ― -b3- Mad; or possessed by a devil: (TA:) Lth says that, applied to a man, it signifies one who is as though there were in him madness, or diabolical possession; but Az says that this is a mistake; for, were this its meaning, the poets would not have used it in praise. (TA, in another part of the art.) ― -b4- Tall: (IDrd, Msb, K:) and so the fem. applied to a woman. (IDrd, Msb.) ― -b5- Bulky; big-bodied; or stout: or, as some say, youthful; or in a state of youthful vigour. (TA.) ― -b6- The lion. (Lth, S, K.) ― -b7- It is said in the K that AlA^a$ojaEu also signifies Ald~ahoru [i. e. Time; or fortune; &c.]; and J says that this is what the poet means by the expression, A^a$ojaEu A^ax~aA*N : but this cannot be the correct meaning, for the poet, namely El-Aashà, says, biA^a$ojaEa A^ax~aA*K EalaY Ald~ahori Hukomuhu by AlA$jE meaning himself, or some other thing. (TA.) -A2- Also, (S, K,) and A_i$ojaEN , (K,) or the latter accord. to some, but this was not known to Abu-l-Ghowth, (S,) sing. of A^a$aAjiEu , [in some copies of the S written A^a$aAjiyEu , but the former, which, as is mentioned in the TA, is found in the handwriting of J, is that which is commonly known,] which signifies [The knuckles nearest to the wrist; this being what is meant by] the bases ( A^uSuwl ) of the fingers, which are connected with the tendons of the outer side of the hand: (S, K:) in the T, we find the heads ( ruw^uws ) of the fingers, instead of ASwl : (TA:) or A$jE in the hand and foot [but see what follows] signifies the tendons extended above the sulaAmaY [here meaning the metacarpal and metatarsal bones ] from the wrist to the bases ( A^uSuwl ) of the fingers or toes, which are called A^aTonaAbu AlA^aSaAbiEi , above the outer side of the hand: or the bone which connects the finger with the wrist; [i. e. the metacarpal bone; ] every finger having to it a bone thus called: he who says that the A^a$aAjiE [so here instead of A$jE as above] are the tendons calls those bones the A^usonaAE . (TA.) Aboo-Bekr is described as EaAriY AlA^a$aAjiEi Eano mafaASili AlA^aSaAbiEi , meaning Having little flesh upon what are thus termed: or having their tendons apparent. (TA.) [See also raAjibapN and burojumapN .] -A3- A^a$ojaEu mino diykK [ More courageous than a cock ] is one of the proverbs of the Arabs. (Mgh.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, M, Msb,) inf. n. $uruwqN (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and $aroqN , (S, Msb,) The sun rose; (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ A^a$oraqat : (K:) the sun rose from the east; and in like manner one says of the moon, and of the stars: (M:) or the sun rose so that its light began to fall upon the earth and trees: (T and TA in art. *r :) and ↓ A$rqt signifies, as distinguished from $araqat , (S, M, Mgh, Msb,) or signifies also, (K, TA,) for both verbs are correctly expl. in the K as above, (TA,) it shone, or gave its light, (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K, TA,) and spread (M, TA) upon the earth, or ground: (TA:) or, as some say, $araqat , and ↓ A$rqt are syn., (M, Msb,) as meaning it (the sun) shone: (M:) and $aroqN [as inf. n. of the former verb] signifies the shining of the sun. (K.) ― -b2- And $araqa Aln~axolu , and ↓ A$rq , The palm-trees showed redness in their fruit: (M, K: *) or showed the colours of their dates. (AHn, M.) [See also $ariqa in what follows.] -A2- $araqa Al$~aApa , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, O, Msb,) inf. n. $aroqN , He slit the ear of the sheep, or goat, (S, O, Msb, K,) in the manner expl. voce $aroqaA='u . (Msb.) ― -b2- And $araqa Alv~amarapa , (Az, K,) inf. n. $aroqN , (IAmb, Az, TA,) He plucked the fruit: (Az, K, TA:) or cut it. (IAmb, Az, TA.) One says in crying baAqil~aA=' [or beans], $aroqu AlgadaApi TariY~N The cutting of the morning, fresh! meaning what has been cut, and picked, in the morning. (IAmb, Az, TA.) -A3- $ariqa , [aor. ,] inf. n. $araqN , It (a place) was, or became, bright by reason of the sun's shining upon it; as also ↓ A$rq ; (M, TA;) [whence,] A@loA^aroDu binuwri rab~ihaA ↓ waA^a$oraqati occurs in the Kur [xxxix. 69 as meaning And the earth shall shine with the light of its Lord ]: (M:) [in other instances,] A^a$oraqati AlA^aroDu means The earth was, or became, bright with the sunshine. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, perhaps, or, though not immediately, from what here next follows, some other applications of this verb, to denote redness.] ― -b3- $ariqa biriyqihi , (S, M, Msb, K,) and biAlmaA='i , and the like, (M,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. $araqN , (M, Msb,) He (a man, M, Msb) was, or became, choked with his spittle, (S, M, Msb, K,) and with water, &c. (M.) [And jariDa and gaS~a and $ajiYa are sometimes used in the same sense in relation to spittle &c.] ― -b4- [Hence,] $ariqa AljuroHu biAld~ami (assumed tropical:) The wound became [ choked or] filled with blood. (Msb.) ― -b5- And $ariqa AlmawoDiEu biA^aholihi (tropical:) The place became [ choked or] filled and straitened by its occupants. (TA.) ― -b6- And $ariqa Aljasadu biAlT~iybi (tropical:) [ The body became choked in its pores with perfume ]. (TA.) ― -b7- [And $ariqa Alv~awobu biAljaAdiY~i (assumed tropical:) The garment, or piece of cloth, became glutted, or saturated, with the dye of saffron: see the part. n. $ariqN .] ― -b8- And $ariqato Eayonuhu (tropical:) His eye became red [ being surcharged with blood ]; as also ↓ Ai$oraworaqatN : (M, TA:) and so $ariqa Ald~amu fiY Eayonihi : (K, TA:) or this last signifies the blood appeared in his eye: (M:) and $ariqato biAld~ami it (the eye) had the blood apparent in it, [ as though it were choked therewith, ] without its running from it. (TA.) ― -b9- And $ariqa lawonuhu , inf. n. $araqN , (assumed tropical:) His colour, or complexion, became red, by reason of shame, or shame and confusion. (TA.) ― -b10- And [hence, app.,] $ariqa Al$~aYo'u , inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) The thing became intensely red, with blood, or with a beautiful red colour. (M, TA.) ― -b11- And also (assumed tropical:) The thing became mixed, commingled, or blended. (M, TA.) ― -b12- $ariqati Al$~amosu , inf. n. as above, means (tropical:) The sun had a duskiness blended with it, and it [app. the duskiness] then became little: (TA:) or it was near to setting: (M, K:) or became feeble in its light; (O, K;) app. from $ariqN applied to flesh-meat as meaning “ red, having no grease, or gravy, ” and applied to a garment, or piece of cloth, as meaning “ red, that has become glutted, or saturated, ( $ariqa ,) with dye; ” because its colour, in the last part of the day, when it is setting, becomes red. (O.) ― -b13- The phrase yuw^ax~iruwna AlS~alaApa A_ilaY $araqi AlmawotaY , (S, M, O, K, [in the CK, erroneously, $aroqi ,]) occurring in a trad., (S, M, O,) in a saying of the Prophet, (O, K,) is expl. as meaning Who postpone, or defer, the prayer until there remains not, (S, M, O, K,) of the sun, (S,) or of the day, (M, O, K,) save as much as remains (S, M, O, K) of the life, (S,) or of the breath, (M, O, K, [but in the CK, nafosi is put in the place of nafasi ,]) of the dying who is choked with his spittle: (S, M, O, K:) or the meaning is, until the sun is [ but just ] above the walls, and [ diffusing its feeble light ] among the graves (M, O, K *) as though it were a great expanse of water. (M, O.) AZ says, yukorahu AlS~alaApu bi$araqi AlmawotaY means Prayer is disapproved when the sun becomes yellow: and faEalotu *`lika bi$araqi AlmawotaY I did that when the sun was becoming yellow. (TA.) -A4- $ariqati Al$~aApu , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. $araqN , (S, Msb,) The sheep, or goat, had its ear slit (S, Msb, K) in the manner expl. voce $aroqaA='u . (Msb, K.)

rawSourceText: , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, M, Msb,) inf. n. $uruwqN (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and $aroqN , (S, Msb,) The sun rose; (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ A^a$oraqat : (K:) the sun rose from the east; and in like manner one says of the moon, and of the stars: (M:) or the sun rose so that its light began to fall upon the earth and trees: (T and TA in art. *r :) and ↓ A$rqt signifies, as distinguished from $araqat , (S, M, Mgh, Msb,) or signifies also, (K, TA,) for both verbs are correctly expl. in the K as above, (TA,) it shone, or gave its light, (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K, TA,) and spread (M, TA) upon the earth, or ground: (TA:) or, as some say, $araqat , and ↓ A$rqt are syn., (M, Msb,) as meaning it (the sun) shone: (M:) and $aroqN [as inf. n. of the former verb] signifies the shining of the sun. (K.) ― -b2- And $araqa Aln~axolu , and ↓ A$rq , The palm-trees showed redness in their fruit: (M, K: *) or showed the colours of their dates. (AHn, M.) [See also $ariqa in what follows.] -A2- $araqa Al$~aApa , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, O, Msb,) inf. n. $aroqN , He slit the ear of the sheep, or goat, (S, O, Msb, K,) in the manner expl. voce $aroqaA='u . (Msb.) ― -b2- And $araqa Alv~amarapa , (Az, K,) inf. n. $aroqN , (IAmb, Az, TA,) He plucked the fruit: (Az, K, TA:) or cut it. (IAmb, Az, TA.) One says in crying baAqil~aA=' [or beans], $aroqu AlgadaApi TariY~N The cutting of the morning, fresh! meaning what has been cut, and picked, in the morning. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, perhaps, or, though not immediately, from what here next follows, some other applications of this verb, to denote redness.] ― -b3- $ariqa biriyqihi , (S, M, Msb, K,) and biAlmaA='i , and the like, (M,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. $araqN , (M, Msb,) He (a man, M, Msb) was, or became, choked with his spittle, (S, M, Msb, K,) and with water, &c. (M.) [And jariDa and gaS~a and $ajiYa are sometimes used in the same sense in relation to spittle &c.] ― -b4- [Hence,] $ariqa AljuroHu biAld~ami (assumed tropical:) The wound became [ choked or] filled with blood. (Msb.) ― -b5- And $ariqa AlmawoDiEu biA^aholihi (tropical:) The place became [ choked or] filled and straitened by its occupants. (TA.) ― -b6- And $ariqa Aljasadu biAlT~iybi (tropical:) [ The body became choked in its pores with perfume ]. (TA.) ― -b7- [And $ariqa Alv~awobu biAljaAdiY~i (assumed tropical:) The garment, or piece of cloth, became glutted, or saturated, with the dye of saffron: see the part. n. $ariqN .] ― -b8- And $ariqato Eayonuhu (tropical:) His eye became red [ being surcharged with blood ]; as also ↓ Ai$oraworaqatN : (M, TA:) and so $ariqa Ald~amu fiY Eayonihi : (K, TA:) or this last signifies the blood appeared in his eye: (M:) and $ariqato biAld~ami it (the eye) had the blood apparent in it, [ as though it were choked therewith, ] without its running from it. (TA.) ― -b9- And $ariqa lawonuhu , inf. n. $araqN , (assumed tropical:) His colour, or complexion, became red, by reason of shame, or shame and confusion. (TA.) ― -b10- And [hence, app.,] $ariqa Al$~aYo'u , inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) The thing became intensely red, with blood, or with a beautiful red colour. (M, TA.) ― -b11- And also (assumed tropical:) The thing became mixed, commingled, or blended. (M, TA.) ― -b12- $ariqati Al$~amosu , inf. n. as above, means (tropical:) The sun had a duskiness blended with it, and it [app. the duskiness] then became little: (TA:) or it was near to setting: (M, K:) or became feeble in its light; (O, K;) app. from $ariqN applied to flesh-meat as meaning “ red, having no grease, or gravy, ” and applied to a garment, or piece of cloth, as meaning “ red, that has become glutted, or saturated, ( $ariqa ,) with dye; ” because its colour, in the last part of the day, when it is setting, becomes red. (M, O.) AZ says, yukorahu AlS~alaApu bi$araqi AlmawotaY means Prayer is disapproved when the sun becomes yellow: and faEalotu *`lika bi$araqi AlmawotaY I did that when the sun was becoming yellow. (TA.) -A4- $ariqati Al$~aApu , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. $araqN , (S, Msb,) The sheep, or goat, had its ear slit (S, Msb, K) in the manner expl. voce $aroqaA='u . (Msb, K.)

definition: , (TA,) inf. n. ta$oriyqN , (S, O, K,) He took to the direction of the east, or place of sunrise: (S, O, K, TA:) he went to the east: he came to the east: (M, TA:) and he directed himself to the...
sourceDefinition: , (TA,) inf. n. ta$oriyqN , (S, O, K,) He took to the direction of the east, or place of sunrise: (S, O, K, TA:) he went to the east: he came to the east: (M, TA:) and he directed himself to the east. (TA.) ― -b2- And He prayed at sunrise: and hence, app., He performed the prayer of the festival of the sacrifice: (TA:) or this meaning is from $araqati Al$~amosu . (Mgh: it is also mentioned in the M.) ― -b3- $r~qt AlA^aroDu , inf. n. as above, The land became affected with drought, and dryness of the earth, being [ parched by the sun and ] not reached by water: whence the term ↓ $araAqiY~ [q. v.] in the dial. of Egypt. (TA.) ― -b4- ta$oriyqN also signifies The being beautiful, and [ sunny or] shining in face. (Sh, O, K.) -A2- $r~q All~aHoma , (M, Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. as above, (S, M, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) He cut the flesh-meat into strips, and dried it in the sun, or spread it in the sun to dry: (S, M, Mgh, O, Msb, K:) or [simply] he cut it into pieces, and into strips. (Msb.) [In like manner also] ta$oriyqu Al$~aEiyri signifies The throwing barley in a sunny place in order that it may dry. (Mgh.) And one says of the [wild] bull, yu$ar~iqu matonahu , meaning He exposes his back to the sun in order that what is upon it of the dew of night may dry: in this sense the phrase is used by Aboo-Dhu-eyb. (M.) ― -b2- A^ay~aAmu Alt~a$oriyqi is an appellation of The three days next after the day of sacrifice: (S, M, O, Msb:) [i. e. the eleventh and twelfth and thirteenth days of Dhu-l-Hijjeh:] these days were so called because the flesh of the victims was therein cut into strips, and dried in the sun, or spread in the sun to dry: (S, M, Mgh, O, Msb, K: *) or because the victims were not sacrificed until the sun rose: (IAar, S, O, K:) or from the prayer of the day of sacrifice, which they follow: (Mgh:) or because they used to say, [on that day,] (S, M, O,) in the Time of Ignorance, (M,) vabiyro kayomaA nugiyro ↓ A^a$oriqo , (S, M, O,) which means Enter thou upon the time of sunrise, Thebeer, (addressing one of the mountains of Mekkeh, M, * Mgh,) that we may push, or press, on, or forward, (M, Mgh, Msb,) to return from Minè: (M: [see also 4 in art. gwr :]) Aboo- Haneefeh used to hold that Alt~a$oriyq means Alt~akobiyr [i. e. the saying Aall~`hu A^akobaro ]; but none beside him has held this opinion. (TA.) It is said in a trad. that the days thus called are days of eating and drinking, and of celebrating the praises of God. (O.) ― -b3- $r~q Alv~awoba (assumed tropical:) He made [or dyed ] the garment, or piece of cloth, yellow: (Ibn-'Abbád, O:) [or he dyed it red: (see the pass. part. n., below:)] or ta$oriyqN signifies the dyeing with saffron, (M, L,) so that the thing dyed is saturated, (L,) or not so that the thing is saturated: (so in a copy of the M:) it is not with safflower. (M, L. [See also 4, last signification.]) -A3- $r~q AlaHowaD is sometimes said for Sar~ajahu , meaning He plastered the watering-trough, or tank, with $aAruwq [q. v.], or SaAruwj . (M in art. Srj .)

definition: (AHeyth, Fr, A'Obeyd, S, K) and ↓ $aquwrN (AHeyth, As, Abu-l-Jarráh, S, K) A want;
sourceDefinition: (AHeyth, Fr, A'Obeyd, S, K) and ↓ $aquwrN (AHeyth, As, Abu-l-Jarráh, S, K) A want; or a needful, or requisite, thing, affair, or business: (S, K:) or the former signifies wants: (Ham p. 716:) A'Obeyd says that the former word is the more correct, because $uquwrN signifies things, or affairs, that cleave to the heart, disquieting it; and is pl. of ↓ $aqorN ; and that ↓ $aquwrN , with fet-h, has the signification of an epithet [meaning cleaving to the heart and disquieting it ]: (S:) or, accord. to some, this latter signifies grief, mourning, sorrow, or sadness; disquietude of mind: or disquietude of mind that causes one to be sleepless: the former is also expl. as signifying a man's case, and his secret: and ↓ both are also said to signify tidings: and a man's state, or condition. (TA.) One says, A^axobarotuhu bi$uquwriY I acquainted him with my want; like as one says A^afoDayotu A_ilayohi biEujariY wabujariY : (S:) or I acquainted him with my tidings. (TA.) And A^afoDayotu A_ilayohi bi$uquwriY I acquainted him with my case, and with what I kept secret from others; (TA;) and so nafaDotu lahu $uquwriY : (Ham p. 716:) or I revealed to him my secret, and acquainted him with all my affairs. (Mgh.) And ↓ bav~ahu $aquwrahu , and $uquwrahu , He complained to him of his state, or condition. (M, TA.)

definition: Plastered with $iyd ;
sourceDefinition: Plastered with $iyd ; and so, as some say, ↓ mu$ay~adN : (T:) or built with gypsum: (Msb:) or made with $yd , (S, A, K,) i. e. gypsum; and so, some say, ↓ mu$ay~adN : (A:) or the latter signifies raised high, or made lofty; (A 'Obeyd, S, A, K;) and so the former, applied to a place, (A,) or building: (TA:) the former has this meaning in the Kur xxii. 44: (Jel:) J says in the S, Ks says, ma$iydN is applied to a sing., from the saying in the Kur, [ubi suprà,] waqaSorK ma$iydK ; and ↓ mu$ay~adN , to a pl., from the saying in the same, [iv. 80,] fiY buruwjK mu$ay~adapK : but this is a mistake: what Ks says is that mu$ay~adapN , with p and teshdeed, is a pl. [i. e. a lexicological, not a grammatical, pl.] of mu$ay~adN : (IB, K: *) or the saying of Ks [if as quoted in the S] may be expl. accord. to the opinion of those who hold that ma$iydN and mu$ay~adN both signify plastered with $iyd , on the supposition that the Arabs did not use ma$iydapN as applied to a pl., but only to a sing.: (Az, L:) [for] Fr says that the pass. part. n. of the unaugmented verb only is used when applied to a sing. and not denoting repetition, or muchness; but either this or the pass. part. n. of the verb of the measure faE~ala may be used when applied to a sing. and denoting repetition, or muchness, and when applied to a pl.: thus you say kabo$N ma*obuwHN [“ a slaughtered ram ”]; but not mu*ab~aHN ; but you may say vawobN muxar~aqN [as meaning “ a garment in which holes have been repeatedly made, ” or “ in which many holes have been made, ” or “ much pierced with holes, ” as well as vawobN maxoruwqN meaning “ a garment in which a hole has been made, ” or “ in which holes have been made, ”] and kibaA$N mu*ab~aHapN [“ slaughtered rams ”]: and hence you may say ↓ qaSorN mu$ay~adN ; because ta$oyiydN denotes building, and the act of building is repeated, and a building becomes high by degrees. (L.)

sourceDefinition: [part. n. of SabaA^a : and as such signifying] One who departs from his religion to another religion. (Msb.) The Arabs used to call the Prophet AlS~aAbiY [for AlS~aAbiy^u ], because he departed from the religion of Kureysh to El-Islám; and him who entered the religion of El-Islám, maSobuw~N , changing the ' to w ; and the Muslims [collectively], AlS~ubaApN , as though pl. of AlS~aAbiYi , without ' , like quDaApN and guzaApN pls. of qaADK and gaAzK . (TA.) And [the pl.] AlS~aAbiy^uwna in the Kur [v. 73, &c.,] is said by Zj to mean Those who depart from one religion to another. (TA.) ― -b2- Then this appellation, SaAbiy^N , was applied to [ Any individual of ] a certain sect of the unbelievers, [ the Sabians, ] said to worship the stars secretly, and openly to profess themselves to belong to the Christians: they are called AlS~aAbiy^apu and AlD~aAbiy^uwna : and they assert that they are of the religion of Sábi the son of Sheyth [or Seth ] the son of Adam: their appellation may also be pronounced AlS~aAbiyuwna , and thus Náfi' read it [in the Kur]: (Msb:) or the SaAbiy^uwna are a certain class of the people who possess revealed scripture: (S:) or a people whose religion resembles that of the Christians, except that their kibleh is towards the place whence blows the [ south, or southerly, wind called ] januwb : (Lth, T, TA:) [or] whose kibleh is from ( mino [or this may mean some point of ]) the place whence blows the [ north, or northerly, wind called ] $amaAl at midday: (M, K:) or, accord. to some, their kibleh is the Kaabeh: (MF:) and they assert that they are of the religion of Noah, (Lth, T, M, K,) lyingly: (Lth, T, M:) in the R it is said that they are thus called in relation to Sábi the son of Lámak [or Lamech], the brother of Noah: Bd says, it is said that they are worshippers of the angels: and it is said that they are worshippers of the stars: and that their appellation is Arabic; from SabaA^a “ he departed from a religion; ” or from SabaA “ he inclined, ” because of their inclining from truth to falsehood. (MF, TA.)

sourceDefinition: a word of well-known meaning, (S, M, K,) [ Soap; ] a compound with which clothes [ &c. ] are washed: the best of which is made of pure olive-oil and clear potash and good jiyr [meaning lime ], well cooked [i. e. boiled ], and dried, and cut into particular shapes: the magoribiY~ sort is not cut, nor well cooked [or boiled ], but is like cooked starch: (TA:) it is hot and dry; and produces a pleasurable sensation in the body; (K;) but the washing the head with it hastens hoariness: (TA: [in which many other supposed properties of it are mentioned:]) IDrd says the word is not of the language of the Arabs: (TA:) [Fei, in the Msb, fancifully derives it from Sabana AlkaA^osa , because it removes filths and impurities:] MF says that it is one of the words common to all languages, Arabic and Persian and Turkish and others [as Greek &c.]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] SuAbuwnu Alhumuwmi is a term for (assumed tropical:) Wine. (TA voce tiroyaAqN , q. v.)

definition: -A2- Sd~r baEiyrahu , (K,) inf.
sourceDefinition: : see 4. -A2- Sd~r baEiyrahu , (K,) inf. n. taSodiyrN , (TA,) He tied a cord from the girth of his camel to the part behind [or beyond ] the callous lump on his breast: (K, TA:) or, accord. to Lth, (L,) one says, Sd~r Eano baEiyrihi , (M, L,) and the meaning is, he tied a cord from the taSodiyr [or breast-girth ] to the part behind [or beyond ] the callous lump on the breast of his camel, to keep the tSdyr in its place, when it had become loose in consequence of the animal's having become lank in the belly: the cord above mentioned is called sinaAfN [q. v.]. (Lth, L.) ― -b2- And Sd~r EalaY AlbaEiyri [app. He put the breast-girth upon the camel ]: from Alt~aSodiyru , i. e. “ the girth ” [thus called]. (MA.) ― -b3- Sud~ira His (a horse's) breast became wetted with sweat. (S.) See 5. ― -b4- Sd~rhu , (TA,) or Sd~rhu fiY Almajolisi , (S,) (assumed tropical:) He placed him, or seated him, in the upper, or highest, part in the sitting-room, or sitting-place. (TA.) And Sud~ira He was advanced, or promoted. (A.) ― -b5- Sd~r kitaAbahu , (S, K,) inf. n. as above, (K,) (tropical:) He put to his book, or writing, a Sador , (S, K, TA,) i. e. a title, or a commencement. (TA.) And Sd~r kitaAbahu bika*aA (tropical:) [ He commenced his book, or writing, with such a thing ]. (A.) -A3- See also 5, where it is expl. as intrans., in two places.

definition: signifies The returning, or going back, [app.
sourceDefinition: signifies The returning, or going back, [app. with another, from water, &c.] (KL.) [The verb is probably trans., agreeably with general analogy, in all its senses; SAdrhu app. signifying primarily He returned, or went back, with him from water &c. ― -b2- Ibr D thinks that it signifies also (assumed tropical:) He vied, or contended, with him for precedence, or priority. ] -A2- Also (assumed tropical:) The exacting a fine or the like [app. from another: or the suing, or prosecuting, another, for a debt &c. ]. (KL.) You say, SAdrhu EalaY ka*aA mina AlmaAli (S, * K, * TA) (assumed tropical:) He desired, or sought, to obtain from him; or he demanded of him; or he sued, or prosecuted, him for; such a sum, or such an amount, of property. (K, * TA.) ― -b2- And SaAdarotuhu EalaY ka*a A waka*aA (assumed tropical:) I released him from my reckoning with him on such and such terms agreed upon by both. (TA in art. frq .) And Suwdira EalaY maAlK yuw^ad~iyhi (assumed tropical:) He (an agent) was released from being reckoned with ( fuwriqa ) on the condition of his paying certain property for which he became responsible: a phrase of the registrars of accounts. (TA in the present art.)

definition: He [a man, TA) erected his chest in sitting.
sourceDefinition: He [a man, TA) erected his chest in sitting. (M, K.) ― -b2- (tropical:) He [a horse) outreached the other horses with his chest; (M, K, * TA;) as also ↓ Sd~r , (S, * M, MA, K,) inf. n. taSodiyrN : the latter verb is afterwards expl. in the K as meaning baraza biraA^osihi ; but this is a mistake. (TA.) Tufeyl says, describing a horse, mino EaraqK ↓ kaA^an~ahu baEoda maA Sad~arona siydN tamaT~ara jinoHa All~ayoli maboluwlu As though he were, after they had outreached with their chests, from a row of [other] horses, [ a wolf that had exposed himself to rain during a portion of the night, and had become wetted: ] but accord. to one relation, it is ↓ Sud~irona , meaning their breasts were wetted [ mino EaraqK ] by reason of sweat: the former reading, however is the better. (S.) ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) He sat, or became placed or seated, in the upper, or highest, part in the sitting-room, or sitting-place. (S, * K, * TA.) And He became advanced, or promoted. (A.) tSd~r liA^umuwri Aln~aAsi (assumed tropical:) [ He became advanced to the foremost place for the conducting of the affairs of the people ]. (Har p. 194.)

definition: Anything that fronts, or faces, one.
sourceDefinition: Anything that fronts, or faces, one. (M, K.) ― -b2- And hence, (M,) The Sador [i. e. breast, or chest, or bosom, ] of a man, [often meaning his mind, ] (M, Msb, K,) and of other than man: (Msb:) of the masc. gender: (Lh, S, M, K:) pl. SuduwrN , (S, M, Msb,) the only pl. form. (M.) [See also SudorapN .] As to the saying of the poet, (S, M,) El-Aashà, (S,) wata$oraqu biAlqawoli Al~a*iY qado A^a*aEotuhu kamaA $ariqato Sadoru AlqanaApi mina Ald~ami [ And thou becomest, or wilt become, red by reason of the saying that I have published, like as the fore part of the spear becomes red from blood ], (S, * M,) he has made Sdr fem. because the Sdr of the qnAp is a part of the qnAp ; for they [sometimes] make a noun fem. when it is prefixed to a fem. noun: (S:) or if you will, you may say that he has made Sdr fem. because he meant [thereby] the qnAp ; and if you will, you may say that the Sdr of a qnAp is a qnAp . (M.) [Hence,] banaAtu AlS~adori (tropical:) The spaces between the bones of the breast. (M, TA.) [And also] (assumed tropical:) Anxieties. (T in art. bnY .) And *aAtu AlS~uduwri (assumed tropical:) What is in the minds. (Ksh and Bd and Jel in iii. 115, &c.) And DaAqa Sadoruhu (assumed tropical:) His bosom, or mind, became strait, or contracted. (Msb in art. Dyq . [See the Kur xv. 97 and xxvi. 12.]) And $araHa biAlkufori SadorFA (assumed tropical:) He opened and dilated his bosom, meaning, was pleased, with infidelity. (Jel in xvi. 108. [See also the similar phrases $araHa A@ll~`hu Sadorahu liloA_isolaAmi and liqabuwli Alxayori expl. in art. $rH .]) And Aino$araHa Sadoruhu (assumed tropical:) His bosom became dilated or enlarged [ with joy ]. (S in art. $rH .) And waAsiEu AlS~adori and raHiybu AlS~adori (assumed tropical:) Ample, or dilated, in the breast, or bosom; [meaning free-minded; free from distress of mind; without care: and free from narrowness of mind; liberal, munificent, or generous. ] (S and TA in art. rHb .) [And Day~iqu AlS~adori (assumed tropical:) Having the bosom, or mind, strait, or contracted. ] And rajulN baEiydu AlS~adori (tropical:) A man who is not to be turned, or bent, or inclined. (M.) In the saying halo yasotaTiyEu mano bihi SadorN A_il~aA A^ano yanofiva [meaning Is he who has the disease of the chest ( daA='u AlS~adori ) able to do without spitting? ], if it be correct, the prefixed noun [ dA=' ] is suppressed. (Mgh.) [ Sadoru Ald~ajaAjapi , as said by Freytag, is the name of (assumed tropical:) The star γ of Cygnus. ] ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) The upper, or uppermost, part of the front of anything. (M, K.) [Hence,] Suduwru AlwaAdiY (assumed tropical:) The higher, or upper, parts, and fronts, or fore parts, of the valley; (M, K;) as also SadaAy^iruhu , which is pl. of ↓ SadaArapN , (K,) or ↓ SidaArapN , (as in a copy of the M,) or ↓ SaAdirapN , (as in the L,) or of ↓ SadiyrapN . (M, L, K.) And Sadoru Almajolisi (assumed tropical:) The upper, or highest, part [or end ] of the sitting-room, or sitting-place: (TA:) the elevated part thereof. (Msb.) ― -b4- [(assumed tropical:) The fore part of anything. (assumed tropical:) The prow, or fore part, of a ship.] (assumed tropical:) The fore part of the foot, between the toes and the [ protuberant part called the ] HimaArap . (M.) (assumed tropical:) The fore part of the sandal, before the [ hole through which is put the thong called the $iraAk , i. e. the hole called the ] xurot . (M.) (tropical:) The part of the arrow that is above the middle, as far as the mrA$ : (so in a copy of the A: [an evident mistranscription for raA^os , i. e. head: ]) or the part of the arrow that is beyond the middle, as far as the slender part, (S, M, Msb, K,) which is next the head; (M;) so called because it is the fore part when it is shot: (S, Msb, K:) and likewise of the spear [as in the verse cited above in this paragraph]. (M.) yawomN kaSadori Alr~umoHi [lit. (assumed tropical:) A day like the fore part of the spear ] means (assumed tropical:) a day of straitness and distress: accord. to Th, it is a day by which war, or battle, is peculiarly distinguished. (M, L.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) The first, first part, or commencement, of anything; (S, M, K;) even (assumed tropical:) of the day, (M, Msb,) and (assumed tropical:) of the night, and (assumed tropical:) of the winter, and (assumed tropical:) of the summer, and (assumed tropical:) the like, (M,) and (tropical:) of an affair. (A. [See an ex. voce EajuzN .]) (tropical:) The title of a book or writing: and the first part, or commencement, thereof. (TA.) [(assumed tropical:) The first foot of the first hemistich of a verse.] And The first hemistich (altogether) of a verse. (O voce EajuzN .) definition: He examined its SafaHaAt [or sides ];
sourceDefinition: He examined its SafaHaAt [or sides ]; i. e. a thing's: (S:) or he considered it carefully, or attentively, and examined its SafaHaAt . (A, Mgh.) And taSaf~aHotu AlkitaAba I turned over, or examined, the SafaHaAt , meaning pages, of the book; as also ↓ SafaHotuhu , inf. n. SafoHN : (Msb:) and waraqa AlmuSoHafi ↓ SafaHotu I examined the leaves of the muSoHaf [i. e. volume, or book, or copy of the Kur-án, ] one by one. (O, K.) And tSf~H Alqawoma , (Lth, A,) and ↓ SafaHahumo , (Lth, O, Msb, K,) He looked at the people, seeking for a particular man: (Lth:) or he examined the states, or conditions, of the people, and looked among them, to ascertain whether such a one was to be seen: (A; in explanation of the former:) or he made the people to pass before him, and examined them, one by one: (O, K; in explanation of the latter:) or he beheld [or looked at ] the SafaHaAt [or sides ] of the faces of the people. (Msb.) And tSf~H wujuwha Alqawomi He examined carefully, or attentively, the faces of the people, looking at their (the people's) external appearances and forms, and seeking to make himself acquainted with their cases: and he looked at the faces of the people, seeking to know them; as also ↓ SafaHahaA . (Lth, TA.) And tSf~H AlA^amora , (A, TA,) and tSf~H fiY AlA^amori , (K, TA,) and AlA^amora ↓ SafaHa , (TA,) and SafaHa fiY AlA^amori , (K, TA,) He looked into the affair, or case. (K, TA.)

definition: , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) of a thing, (S, A, Mgh,) or of anything;
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) of a thing, (S, A, Mgh,) or of anything; (Msb;) and ↓ SafoHapN , (S, A, Mgh, Msb,) of a thing, (Mgh,) or of anything; (S, A, Msb;) The side; or lateral, or outward, part or portion; syn. of the former naAHiyapN ; (S, A;) or of the same, (K,) or of the latter, (S, A,) or of each, (Mgh, Msb,) jaAnibN : (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K:) and both signify also the face, or surface, or front, of a thing: (Mgh:) pl. [of the former SifaAHN , as below, and] of the latter SafaHaAtN . (Msb.) SafoHaA Al$~aYo'i signifies The two sides of the thing; syn. jaAnibaAhu . (TA.) And SafoHu AlA_inosaAni The side of the human being; (S, O, K; *) as also ↓ SafoHatuhu . (O.) And hence, baEiyrihi ↓ Sal~aY A_ilaY SafoHapi [ He prayed towards the side of his camel ]. (Mgh.) And SafoHN and ↓ SufoHN signify The EuroD [i. e. side ] (S, O, and K accord. to the TA, but in the CK and in my MS. copy of the K EaroD , [which in this instance I think a mistake,]) of the face: (S, O, K:) and so of a sword; (K, TA; [in the former of which, in art. ErD , the EuroD of a sword is said to be its SafoH ;]) or the EaroD [i. e. breadth, or width, ] (S, O, Msb, and so accord. to the CK and my MS. copy of the K,) of a sword; (S, O, Msb, K;) i. e. contr. of Tuwl ; (Msb;) [but it may be well rendered its side, or its flat, and so ↓ SafoHapN , for SM says that] SafoHataA Als~ayofi signifies the two faces, or surfaces, of the sword: (TA:) one says, naZara A_ilayohi biSafoHi wajohihi (S, A) and ↓ biSufoHi wjhh (S) [ He looked towards him with the side of his face turned towards him] and ↓ biSafoHatihi [which means the same]: (A:) but accord. to AO, one says, Als~ayofi ↓ Darabahu biSufoHi [ He struck him with the side, or flat, of the sword ], and the vulgar say biSafoHi Alsyf , with fet-h: (S:) the pl. [of SafoHN ] is SifaAHN (K, TA) and [that of ↓ SufoHN is] A^aSofaAHN . (TA.) Alr~ajuli ↓ SafoHapN signifies The side ( EuroD ) of the breast of the man. (L.) And one says, janobihi ↓ Darabahu EalaY SafoHapi [ He struck him on the surface, or flat part, of his side; and so ElY SafoHi jnbh ; but the former is the more common]. (A.) And Als~ayofi ↓ jalaA SafoHataY [ He polished the two sides, or surfaces, of the sword ]. (A.) And Alwaraqapi ↓ kataba fiY SafoHataYi [ He wrote upon the two sides, or faces, of the piece of paper ]. (A.) AlkitaAbi ↓ SafaHaAtu signifies The pages, or faces of the leaves, of the book. (Msb.) And SafoHu Alkaf~i The face [i. e. palm ] of the hand. (L.) And SafoHaA Alkatifi The two parts of the scapula that slope down from the Eayor [or spine thereof ]: pl. SifaAHN . (L.) And SafoHu Aljabali The part of the mountain where the side thereof rests upon the ground; (S, K;) its safoH [q. v.]: (JM:) pl. SifaAHN . (S.)
