definition: A short spear; (A;) a small spear, between a staff and a spear, (O, K,) longer than a staff and shorter than a spear, (S,) said to be of the measure of half a spear, or somewhat more, having a head...
sourceDefinition: A short spear; (A;) a small spear, between a staff and a spear, (O, K,) longer than a staff and shorter than a spear, (S,) said to be of the measure of half a spear, or somewhat more, having a head like that of the spear; (TA;) or a staff shorter than a spear; (Msb;) and, as some say, (TA,) having a zuj~ [i. e. a pointed iron foot at the lower extremity ], (S, O, Msb, K, TA,) like that of the spear: (S, O, TA:) the old man leans, or stays himself, upon it; and it is nearly like the Euk~aAzap [q. v.]: (TA:) or it is like the Euk~aAzap , which is a staff having a zuj~ : (Mgh:) pl. ↓ EanazN , [or rather this is a coll. gen. n., of which EanazapN is the n. un.,] and EanazaAtN . (Msb.) The Prophet is related to have prayed towards an Eanazap . (Mgh. [See sutorapN .]) ― -b2- Also The Had~ [by which may be meant either the edge or point ] of a faA^os [which means a hoe and an adz and an axe, and also a pickaxe]: (O, K:) or the long Had~ [or iron point ] of the miloTaAs , which is a long double-headed pickaxe. (ISh, TA in art. lTs .) -A2- Also A certain beast, (O, K,) found in the desert, slender in the muzzle, smaller than the dog, of the beasts of prey, (O,) that seizes the camel in his rump, (O, K,) and is seldom seen; asserted by the Arabs to be a devil: (O:) or, (K,) accord. to Aboo-Leyleh, (O,) it is like the weasel (O, K) in size: (O:) it approaches the she-camel when she is lying down, (O, K,) then springs, (O,) and enters into her vulva, and conceals itself therein, (O, K,) until it reaches the womb, (O,) whereupon the she-camel (O, K) dies on the spot (K) or aborts and dies on the spot. (O.)

Eawo*N (O, L, K) and EiyaA*N and maEaA*N (O, L, Msb, K) and maEaA*apN ; (O, K;) and bihi ↓ tEw~* ; (O, L, Msb, K; *) and bihi ↓ AstEA* ; (S, A, O, L, Msb, K; *) He sought protection, or preservation, by him; sought, or took, refuge in him; had recourse to him for protection, preservation, or refuge; sought his protection, or preservation; confided or trusted or put his trust in him, or relied upon him, for protection, or preservation; (S, A, O, L, Msb, K;) namely, God, (S, A, O, L, Msb,) or a man; (S, O;) [and in like manner used in relation to a place; mino ka*aA and Eanohu from such a thing; or followed by mino A^ano , or only A^ano , and a mansoob aorist.] ↓ A_in~amaA qaAlahaA taEaw~u*FA , occurring in a trad., means He only said it (referring to the profession of the faith) to seek protection, or preservation, thereby from slaughter; not being sincere in his profession of El-Islám. (L.) And one says, maEaA*a A@ll~`hi , (S, A, O, L, K,) and maEaA*apa A@ll~`hi , (S, O, L, K,) and maEaA*a wajohi A@ll~`hi , and maEaA*apa wajohi A@ll~`hi , (S, O, L,) and EiyaA*a A@ll~`hi , (A,) meaning A^aEuw*u biA@ll~`hi maEaA*FA [ I seek protection, or preservation, by God; &c.; which is equivalent to the saying may God protect me, or preserve me ]: (S, A, O, L, K:) maEaA*FA [as also maEaA*apF ] being here used instead of the verb because it is an inf. n., though [accord. to some] not employed as such [in other cases], like as is the case in the phrase suboHaAna A@ll~`hi . (S, O, L.) [One says also, maEaA*a A@ll~`hi A^ano A^afoEala ka*aA , for mino A^ano A^afoEala ka*aA , I seek preservation by God, &c., from my doing such a thing; as though meaning may God preserve me from doing such a thing: see an ex. in the Kur xii. 79: and] some reckon maEaA*a A@ll~`hi among the forms of oaths. (MF.) [In like manner also,] Eawo*N biA@ll~`hi minoka means A^aEuw*u biA@ll~`hi minoka [ I seek protection, or preservation, by God, &c., from thee ]. (S, O, L, K. *) [See also the phrase EaAy^i*FA biA@ll~`hi , voce EaAy^i*N .] ― -b2- EaA*ato biwaladihaA (assumed tropical:) She (a camel) stayed with her young one, and attended to it affectionately, as long as it remained little, is as though it were an inverted phrase, meaning EaA*a bihaA waladuhaA [ her young sought protection by her: or it may be from what next follows]. (TA.) ― -b3- EA* biAlEaZomi (tropical:) It (flesh-meat) clave to the bone: (S, O, L, K: *) a tropical phrase. (A.) ― -b4- And EaA*ato , [aor. taEuw*u ,] (L, K,) inf. n. (S, O, L, K.) One says, hiYa fiYEiyaA*ihaA She is in the early stage of the period after having brought forth. (S, O, L.)

definition: (S, A, O, L, K) and ↓ taEowiy*N (S, O, L, K) and ↓ maEaA*apN (S, A, L, K) are syn.
sourceDefinition: (S, A, O, L, K) and ↓ taEowiy*N (S, O, L, K) and ↓ maEaA*apN (S, A, L, K) are syn., (S, A, O, L, K,) signifying A kind of amulet, phylactery, or charm, bearing an inscription, which is hung upon a man [ or woman or child or horse &c. ], to charm the wearer against the evil eye and against fright and diabolical possession, and which is forbidden to be hung upon the person, (L,) unless inscribed with something from the Kur-án or with the names of God, for in this case there is no harm in it: (S and Mgh voce tamiymapN :) accord. to some of the etymologists, originally signifying an amulet, a phylactery, or a charm, upon which is [ an inscription commencing with the word ] A^aEuw*u ; and afterwards applied in a general manner [as meaning any amulet ]; (MF;) i. q. ruqoyapN , (K,) or tamiymapN : (A:) or those who imagine that the ↓ maEaA*ap is the same as the tmymp are in error; for the latter is a bead: (Mgh in art. tm :) [in some instances] the ↓ taEowiy* is a thing made of silver, of a round shape like the moon, but partly hollowed out in the form of the horse-shoe, tied by a string to the neck of a child, as a preservative, and in some instances engraved with an inscription: (Har p. 49:) the pl. of Euw*apN is Euwa*N ; that of ↓ taEowiy*N is taEaAwiy*u ; and that of ↓ maEaA*apN is maEaA*aAtN . (L.)

definition: Birds taking refuge in a mountain or in some other place;
sourceDefinition: Birds taking refuge in a mountain or in some other place; as also ↓ EiyaA*N : [each app. a pl. of EaAy^i*N ; like as nuw~amN and niyaAmN are pls. of naAy^imN :] (L, K:) Bakhdaj says, Euw~a*aA ↓ kaAlT~ayori yanojuwna EiyaA*FA [ Like birds saving themselves, taking refuge in a mountain or in some other place ]; repeating the epithet for the sake of emphasis: or EyA*A may be here an inf. n. (A.) [See also dux~alN .] ― -b3- Euw~a*u All~aHomi (tropical:) The parts of flesh-meat that cleave to the bone: (S, A, O, L, K: *) such are the sweetest of flesh-meat. (S, A, O, L.)

sourceDefinition: [part. n. of 1]. EaAy^i*N biA@ll~`hi occurs in a trad. as meaning A^anaA EaAy^i*N [i. e. I am seeking protection, or preservation, by God; &c.]. (L.) And one says, Aall~`hum~a EaAy^i*FA bika mino kul~i suwo'K , meaning, accord. to Az, A^aEuw*u bika EaAy^i*FA [lit. O God, I seek protection, or preservation, by Thee, &c., seeking, &c., from every evil ]: but accord. to Sb, in the phrase EaAy^i*FA biA@ll~`hi mino $ar~ihaA , the word EAy^*A is put in the place of the inf. n. [as an absolute complement of A^aEuw*u understood; so that the meaning is, I seek protection, or preservation, by God, with earnest seeking &c., from her, or its, evil, or mischief ]. definition: The place of the collar (S, O, L, K) of a horse.
sourceDefinition: The place of the collar (S, O, L, K) of a horse. (S, O, L.) [App. so called because it is a place where charms, or amulets, are often suspended.] And AlmuEaw~a*u , (A'Obeyd, L,) or daAy^irapu AlmuEaw~a*i , (S, O, L,) The feather, or curling portion of the coat of a horse, that is in the place of the collar: (A'Obeyd, L:) it is a dAy^rp approved. (A'Obeyd, S, O, L.) ― -b2- Also, (accord. to the K,) or ↓ muEaw~i*N , (accord. to the O,) A she-camel that does not cease to remain in one place. (O, K.) [SM says that the word thus expl. in the K is a mistranscription for mEw~d ; by which he means muEaw~id , part. n. of Eaw~ada said of a camel; but this I doubt; for muEaw~idN has not the meaning here assigned to mEw~* .] ― -b3- See also Euw~a*N , in four places.

definition: He saw him, , or it ;
sourceDefinition: He saw him, , or it ; or he looked , looked at or towards , [or eyed ,] trying whether he could see, him, or it ; syn. A^aboSarahu . (TA.) He saw him (a man) with certainty . (K.) (K, TA.) -b3- Said of a skin, (assumed tropical:) It had thin circles, or rings , or round places , [ likened to eyes ,] (Fr,S,TA,) rendering it faulty: (S:) or, said of a water-skin, it was , or became, thin by reason of oldness: (TA:) [or it became lacerated, or worn in holes; as is shown by what here follows.] One says also, taEay~anato A^axofaAfu AlA^ibili , meaning (assumed tropical:) The feet of the camels became lacerated [ in the soles ], or worn in holes, or blistered; like the water-skin of which one says tEy~n . (IAar, TA.) -A6- tEy~n also signifies (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, clear, or distinct. (KL.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) It was or became, individuated, or particularized; i. e., distinguished from the generality, or aggregate. (KL,) [Thus signifying, it is quasi-pass. of Eay~anahu . Hence it means (assumed tropical:) It had, or assumed, the quality of individuality. And (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, particularized. or specified, by words; mentioned particularly, or specially. And tEy~n lahu It was appointed, or prescribed, for him, or was assigned to him, particularly or peculiarly. And tEy~n Ealayohi (assumed tropical:) It was appointed against him, upon him, particularly. And hence.] one says, tEy~n Ealayohi Al$~ay^o , meaning lazimahu biEayonihi , [i. e. : The thing was, or became, incumbent, or obligatory, on him in particular ] (S, K. -A7- See also the next paragraph.

definition: is a homonym, applying to various things (Msb:) in the K.
sourceDefinition: is a homonym, applying to various things (Msb:) in the K. forty-seven meanings are assigned to it; but it is said by MF that its meanings exceed a hundred; those occurring in the Kur-án are seventeen. (TA.,) By that which is app. its primary application, and which is by many affirmed to be so,(TA,) AlEayonu signifies The eye: the organ of sight: (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA [in the S expl. by HaAs~apu Alr~uw^oyapi , evidently used in this sense; in the Mgh, by AlmuboSirapu ; in the Msb and K, by AlbaASirapu ; and in a mater place in the K. by HaAs~apu Alr~uw^oyap , app. as meaning the sense of sight; ]) also denoted [emphatically] by the term AljaAriHapu [i. e. the organ ]; (TA;) it is that with which the looker sees: (ISk, TA;) and is of a human being and of any other animal: (TA;) it is of the fem. gender; (S, K:) and the pl. [of mult.] as EuyuwnN , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) also pronounced EuywnN , (K, [in which watukosaru , immediately following EuyuwnN , has been erroneously supposed by Golius and Freytag to relate to the sing.,]) and [of pause A^aEoyaAnN and A^aEoyunN , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) which last is asserted by Lh to be sometimes a pl. of mult., as it is in the Kur vii. [178 and] 194; (TA.) and pl. pl. A^aEoyunaAtN : (K:) the dim. is ↓ EuyayonapN , (S.) Hence the saying in a trad. of 'Alee, qaAsa EayonFA bibayoDapK jaEala EalayohaA xuTuwTFA [ He measured the reach of an eye by means of an egg upon which he made lines ]. (Mgh.) And [hence also] one says, biEayonK m~aA A^arayan~aka [lit. With some eye I will assuredly see thee ]: it is said to one whom you send, and require to be quick; and means (assumed tropical:) pause not for anything, for it is as though I were looking at thee. (TA. [See also art. rA^Y .]) And laqiytuhu Eayona Eun~apK [ I met him so that ] I saw him with [or before ] my eye, he not seeing me. (S, TA.) [And raA^ayotuhu Eayona Eun~apK or Eun~apa , which see in art. En . And A^aEoTayotuhu Eayona Eun~apa and Eun~ap , which also see in art. En .] And raA^ayotuhu EaroDa EayonK I saw him, or it, obviously; nearly. (TA, voce EaroDN , q. v.) And haA huwa EaroDu EayonK [or EaroDa EayonK ?] i. e. [ Lo, he, or it, is ] near [ before thee ]: and in like manner, huwa min~iY Eayonu Eun~apK [or Eayona Eun~apK ? i. e. He is near before me ]. (K.) And laqiytuhu A^aw~ala EayonK , (S, K,) and A^aw~ala *iY EayonK and ↓ EaAy^inapK , (TA,) I met him, or it, the first thing: (S, K, TA:) and before every [ other ] thing; as also ↓ A^aw~ala EaAy^inapK and A^adonaY EaAy^inapK : (S:) or this last means the nearest thing perceived by the eye. (TA.) And faEalotu *aAka Eamoda EayonK and EamodFA EalaY EayonK (assumed tropical:) I did that purposely, with seriousness, or earnestness, and certainty: (S:) or SanaEa *`lika EalaY EayonK and EalaY Eayonayoni , (K, TA,) and Eamoda EayonK and Eamoda Eayonayoni , (K,) or EalaY Eamodi EayonK and EalaY Eamodi Eayonayoni , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He did that purposely, (Lh, K, TA,) with seriousness, or earnestness, and certainty. (K.) And huwa Eabodu EayonK (tropical:) He is like the slave to thee as long as thou seest him, (S, K, * TA,) but not when thou art absent; and so huwa Eabodu AlEayoni : (S:) or he is a man who pretends, or feigns, to thee, his doing that which he does not perform: (TA:) and (K, TA) in this sense, (TA,) one says also, huwa Sadiyqu EayonK i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ He is a friend, or a true friend, ] as long as thou seest him: (K, TA:) and huwa A^axuw EayonK (assumed tropical:) He is one who acts as a friend hypocritically with thee. (TA.) A^anota EalaY EayoniY is said in relation to honouring and protecting: (S, K, TA:) [accordingly I would render it (tropical:) Thou art entitled to be honoured and protected by me above my eye: for the eye is esteemed the most excellent of the organs, (as is said in this art. in the TA,) and it is that which most needs protection:] A^anota EalaY raA^osiY is said in relation to honouring only. (TA.) And the Arabs say, EalaY EayoniY qaSadotu zayodFA , meaning thereby the regarding with solicitude mixed with fear [so that I would render it (assumed tropical:) As one to be regarded with solicitude mixed with fear above my eye I made Zeyd the object to which my mind was directed ]. (TA.) [See another ex. of EalaY EayoniY (in which it cannot be rendered as above) in a later part of this paragraph.] naEima A@ll~`hu bika EayonFA [in the CK naE~ama , which is wrong,] means the same as A^anoEamahaA . (K. [See both in art. nEm .]) qur~apu AlEayoni [signifying maA qar~ato bihi AlEayonu , as expl. in the M and K in art. qr , i. e. That by which, or in consequence of which, the eye becomes cool, or refrigerated, or refreshed, &c.,] is a phrase used as meaning (assumed tropical:) A man's child or offspring. (TA.) faqaA^a Eayonahu [properly signifying He put out his eye, or blinded it, &c.,] means [sometimes] (tropical:) he struck him; or struck him vehemently with a broad thing, or with anything; or slapped him with his hand: ( Sak~ahu :) or he was rough, rude, or ungentle, to him in speech. (TA.) Aal~a*iY fiyhi EayonaAka means Thy head. (TA. [There mentioned preceded by lAtHrman : thus dubiously, and perhaps incorrectly, written. What is means, or should be, I know not.]) ― -b2- Eayonu Alv~awori (assumed tropical:) ( The eye of the Bull; ] the great red star [a] that is upon the southern eye of Taurus, and also [ more commonly ] called Ald~abaraAnu . (Kzw, Descr. of Taurus.) [And Eayonu Alr~aAmiY (assumed tropical:) The eye of Sagittarius; app. the two stars v, on the eye thereof. ] ― -b3- Eayonu Albaqari (assumed tropical:) [ The buphthalmum, or ox-eye; ] the [ plant called ] bahaAr [q. v.]. (S in art. bhr .) And Euyuwnu Albaqari (tropical:) A sort of grapes, (S, K, TA,) black, (K, TA,) but not intensely so, large in the berries, (TA,) and round, (K, TA,) which are converted into raisins, and are not very sweet: so says AHn: thus called as being likened to the eyes of the animals termed baqar : (TA:) they are found in Syria: (S:) or said by some to be peculiar to Syria. (TA.) And Certain black A_ij~aAS [or plums ]: (K, TA:) thus called for the same reason. (TA.) ― -b4- Eayonu Alhir~i (assumed tropical:) [ Cat's-eye; ] a certain stone, well known, of no utility. (TA.) -A2- [ fataHa hayona Aln~aAri means (assumed tropical:) He made an opening in the live coals of the fire, that had become compacted; in order that it might burn up well. (See 1 in art. sxw and sxY .)] ― -b2- And EayonN signifies also (assumed tropical:) The Eayon [i. e. eye ] of the needle: such as is narrow is termed Eayonu Safiy~ap [in which the latter word is app. a proper name, and, as such and of the fem. gender, imperfectly decl., i. e., in this case, written Safiy~apa ]. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, as being likened to the organ [of sight] in form, or appearance, (tropical:) A [ small round hole or] place of perforation in a [leathern water-bag such as is called] mazaAdap . (TA.) And (tropical:) Thin circles, or rings, or round places, in a skin, (S, K, TA,) which are a fault therein, (S, TA,) like A^aEoyun [or eyes; or one of such thin circles &c.]; being likened to the organ [of sight] in form. (TA.) [See 10.] And (K) (tropical:) A fault, or defect, (K, TA,) of this description, in a skin. (TA.) ― -b4- And (tropical:) The small hollow or cavity of the knee; (S, K; in [some of] the copies of the latter of which, Alr~akiy~ap is erroneously put for Alr~ukobap ; TA;) likened to the socket of the eye: (TA:) each knee has EayonaAni [i. e. two small hollows or cavities, the articular depressions for the condyles of the femur ], in the fore part thereof, at [ the joint of ] the saAq . (S, TA.) ― -b5- And (tropical:) The piece of skin [or small leathern receptacle ] in which are put the bunoduq [or bullets ] (K, TA) that are shot from the qawos [app. meaning the large kind of cross-bow, called balista, or ballista ]: (K, * TA:) likened to the organ [of sight] in form. (TA.) ― -b6- [In the B, accord. to the TA, it is also expl. as meaning the snAm : but this, I think, is most probably a mistranscription for saAm (q. v.) as signifying (assumed tropical:) The hollow, or cavity, in the ground, thus called, in which water remains, or stagnates, and collects. ] And (tropical:) The place [or aperture ] whence the water of a qanaAp [i. e. pipe, or the like, ] pours forth: (K, TA:) as being likened to the organ [of sight] because of the water that is in it. (TA.) And, (K, TA,) for the same reason, (TA,) (tropical:) The place whence issues the water of a well. (TA.) And, (S, Msb, K, &c.,) for the same reason, as is said by Er-Rághib, (TA,) (tropical:) The Eayon , (S, Msb,) or source, or spring, (K, TA,) of water, (S, Msb, K, TA,) that wells forth from the earth, or ground, and runs: (TA:) [and accord. to the Msb, it app. signifies a running spring: ] of the fem. gender: (TA:) pl. EuyuwnN and A^aEoyunN , (Msb, K,) and accord. to ISk, sometimes the Arabs said, as a pl. thereof, A^aEoyaAnN , but this is rare. (Msb.) Hence a saying, in a trad., cited and expl. voce saAhirN . (TA.) Also (assumed tropical:) Abundance of water of a well. (TA.) And A drop of water. (TA.) Eayonu AlmaA='i , [ originally signifying “ the source of water, ”] accord. to Th, means (assumed tropical:) Life for men; thus in the following verse: A^uwlaAy^ika Eayonu AlmaA='i fiyhimo waEinodahumo mina Alxiyfapi AlmanojaApu waAlmutaHaw~alu (assumed tropical:) [ Those, life for men is among them; and with them are the means of safety, and the place of removal, from fear ]: accord. to the A, Eayonu AlmaA='i fiyhimo means good, or means of attaining good, and provision of corn, or abundance of the produce of the earth, are among them. (TA.) ― -b7- Also (assumed tropical:) The Eayon [meaning eye, or bud, (thus called in the present day,)] of a tree. (Es-Subkee, TA.) ― -b8- [And (tropical:) Sprouting herbage; as being likened to the eye or eyes:] one says, naZarati AlbilaAdu biEayonK or biEayonayoni [lit. (tropical:) The lands looked with an eye or with two eyes ], meaning, had their herbage come forth: (K:) or it is said when their herbage comes forth: or, as in the A, when that which cattle depasture comes forth without [as yet] becoming firm [in the ground, or firmly rooted]: taken from the saying of the Arabs, A_i*aA saqaTati Aljabohapu naZarati AlA^aroDu biA_iHodaY EayonayohaA faA_i*aA saqaTati AlS~arofapu naZarato bihimaA jamiyEFA (assumed tropical:) [lit. When El-Jebheh (the 10th Mansion of the Moon) sets aurorally (i. e. about the 11th of Feb., O. S.), the land looks with one of its eyes; the, when Es-Sarfeh (the 12th Mansion) sets aurorally (about the 9th of March), it looks with both of them ]. (TA. [See also art. nZr .]) -A3- EayonN also, (S, Msb, K, &c.,) as being likened to the organ of sight, (TA,) signifies (tropical:) A spy; and ↓ *uw AlEuyayonatayoni [in the CK *uw AlEayonatayoni ], in like manner, signifies the spy, (S, K, TA,) and ↓ *uw AlEuwayonatayoni likewise, and *uw AlEayonayoni : (TA:) he who looks for a people, or party: (M, TA:) the watcher, or observer; (S, * K, * TA;) or the scout: (S, * Msb, K, * TA:) masc. and fem.: (M, TA:) accord. to the opinion of ISd, made by some to accord with a part [i. e. the eye], and therefore fem.; and by some, to accord with the whole [person], and therefore masc.: (TA:) pl. EuyuwnN and A^aEoyunN , and, accord. to ISk, sometimes A^aEoyaAnN . (Msb.) ― -b2- And i. q. mukaA$ifN [app. as meaning (assumed tropical:) A discoverer, or revealer, of tidings &c.]. (Es-Subkee, TA.) -A4- [And (assumed tropical:) An eye as meaning a look, i. e. an act of looking: and hence, a stroke of an evil eye: or, simply, an evil eye: a meaning of frequent occurrence.] A^aSaAbato fulaAnFA EayonN (assumed tropical:) [ An evil eye smote such a one ] is said of a person when an enemy or an envier has looked at him and produced such an effect upon him that he has fallen sick in consequence thereof (TA.) [ Eayonu AlkamaAli is applied to an eye believed to have the power of killing by its glance: see an ex. voce faqaA^a .] ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) Sight with the eye [or before the eyes; or ocular view ]: thus in the saying, laA A^aTolubu A^avarFA baEoda EayonK (assumed tropical:) [ I will not seek a trace, or vestige, (or, as we rather say in English, a shadow, ) after an ocular view ]: (S, TA:) or the meaning is, after suffering a reality, or substance, to escape me: (Har pp. 120 and 174: [this latter rendering being agreeable with explanations of EayonN which will be found in a later part of this paragraph:]) i. e. I will not leave the thing when I see it ocularly, and seek the trace or vestige, thereof, after its [the thing's] disappearing from me: and the origin of it was the fact that a man saw the slayer of his brother, and when he desired to slay him, he [the latter] said, “ I will ransom myself with a hundred she-camels; ” whereupon he [the other] said, lasotu A^aTolubu A^avarFA baEoda EayonK ; and slew him: (TA:) it is a prov., thus, or, as some relate it, laA taTolubo . (Har p. 120.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) Look, or view. (K, TA.) It is said in the Kur [xx. 40], waAltuSonaEa EalaY EayoniY , (S, TA,) and it has been expl. as there having this meaning [i. e. (assumed tropical:) And this I did that thou mightest be reared and nourished in my view ], as in the B; or, as Th says, that thou mightest be reared where I should see thee: (TA:) or the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) in my watch, or guard, (Bd, * Jel,) and my keeping, or protection. (Jel. [It is implied by the context in the S, that EalaY EayoniY is said in this instance in relation to honouring and protecting, as it is in a phrase mentioned in the first quarter of this paragraph; but my rendering of it there is obviously inapplicable here. See also 1 in art. SnE .]) And in like manner it has been expl. as used in the Kur [xi. 39], waA@SonaEi A@lofuloka biA^aEoyuninaA (assumed tropical:) [ And make thou the ark in our view ]. (TA.) [In like manner, also,] faA^otuwA bihi EalaY A^aEoyuni A@ln~aAsi , in the Kur [xxi. 62], means EalaY manoZarihimo (assumed tropical:) [i. e. Then bring ye him in the view of the people; mnZr being here evidently an inf. n.]; (B, TA:) or [ bring ye him ] openly, or conspicuously. (Jel.) -A5- And (assumed tropical:) The manoZar [as meaning aspect, or outward appearance ], (S, K,) and $aAhid [meaning the same as being an evidence of the intrinsic qualities], (S,) of a man. (S, K.) So in the saying of El-Hajjáj to El-Hasan [ElBasree, when he (the former) had asked maA A^amaduka “ What was the time of thy birth? ” and the latter had answered (see A^amadN )], laEayonuka A^akobaru mino A^amadika (assumed tropical:) [ Verily thy aspect is greater than thy age ], A^amadika meaning sin~ika . (S.) And it is said in a prov., A_in~a AljawaAda Eayonuhu furaAruhu (assumed tropical:) [ Verily the fleet and excellent horse, his aspect is ( equivalent to ) the examination of his teeth ]: (S, TA: [accord. to the latter, Eayonuhu meaning $aAhiduhu :]) i. e. his external appearance renders it needless for thee to try him and to examine his teeth. (S and K in art. fr , q. v.) -A6- Also, [by a synecdoche, as when it means “ a spy, ”] (assumed tropical:) A human being: (K:) and any one: (S, K:) [in which sense, as when it means “ a spy, ” it may be masc. or fem.:] and human beings: (S:) or a company [ of people ]; (K;) as also ↓ EayanN : (S, K:) and the people of a house or dwelling: (K:) and so ↓ EayanN ; (S, K;) and the people of a town or country; as also ↓ EayanN . (K.) One says, maA bihaA EayonN (assumed tropical:) There is not in it any one; (S, K, TA;) [i. e. biAld~aAri in the house, or dwelling; ] as also ↓ EayanN , (TA,) and ↓ EaAy^inN , (S, TA,) and ↓ EaAy^inapN : (TA:) and maA bihaA EayonN taTorifu [virtually meaning the same, but fit. There is not in it an eye twinkling ]. (TA.) And ↓ maA raA^ayotu vam~a EaAy^inapF i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ I was not there ] a human being. (TA.) And baladN qaliylu AlEayoni (assumed tropical:) [ A town, or country, ] having few human beings, (S.) or few people. (TA.) -A7- And (assumed tropical:) A lord, chief, or chief personage: (K, TA:) in [some of] the copies of the K, Alsd~ or Al$d~ is erroneously put for Als~ay~idu : (TA:) the great, or great and noble, person of a people or party: (K, TA:) and the head, chief, or commander, of an army: (TA:) the pl. is A^aEoyaAnN : (TA:) which signifies [ lords, chiefs, or chief personages: &c.: and] the eminent, or high-born, or noble, individuals (S, Mgh, Msb, TA) of a people, or party, (S, Mgh,) or of men; (Msb;) and the most excellent persons. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (Mgh, Msb,) as pl. of EayonN , (K,) A^aEoyaAnN signifies also A Brothers from the same father and mother: (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) this brotherhood is termed ↓ muEaAyanapN : (S, K:) and A^awolaAdu AlA^aEoyaAni means the sons of the same father and mother. (Msb in art. El . [See Eal~apN .]) ― -b3- Also. the sing., (assumed tropical:) The choice, or best, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) of a thing, (S, K,) or of goods, or household-goods, or furniture and utensils, (Mgh, Msb, TA,) and of camels, or cattle, or other property, (TA,) and so ↓ EiynapN , (S, K, TA,) of which the pl. is EiyanN , (TA,) like EiymapN : (S:) ↓ Eiynapu Alxayoli signifies (assumed tropical:) the fleet and excellent of horses. (Lh, TA.) And (assumed tropical:) Highly prized, in much request, or excellent. (TA.) And, as applied to a deenár, (assumed tropical:) Outweighing, so that the balance inclines with it. (TA.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) i. q. maAlN , (K, TA,) [i. e. Property, or such as consists of camels or cattle, ] when of a choice. or of the best, sort. (TA.) -A8- And (assumed tropical:) Such as is ready, or at hand, (K, TA,) present, (TA,) or within one's power, or reach, (S, TA,) of property. (S, K, TA.) And (assumed tropical:) Anything present, or ready, (K, TA,) found before one. (TA.) You say, biEotuhu EayonFA biEayonK (assumed tropical:) I sold it ready merchandise for ready money. (Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) Ready money; cash: or simply money: syn. naqodN : (T, Mgh, Msb, TA:) not EaroDN [q. v.]: (Mgh:) and sometimes, daraAhimu . (Msb.) So in the saying EayonN gayoru dayoni (assumed tropical:) [ Ready money, not debt ]. (TA.) And [hence also] one says, Ai$otarayota biAld~ayoni A^awo biAlEayoni (assumed tropical:) [ Didst thou buy on credit or with ready money? ]. (Msb.) ― -b3- And A A present gift. (Mgh, TA.) So in the saying (Mgh, TA) of a rájiz (TA) satirizing a man, (Mgh,) waEayonuhu kaAlkaAliy^i AlD~imaAri [ And his present gift is a thing not hoped for, like the unseen debt of which the payment is deferred by the creditor: ] meaning, his present gift is like the absent that is not hoped for. (Mgh, TA.) [And hence, app.,] A^aSaAbatohu EayonN mino Euyuwni A@ll~`hi , occurring in a trad., means, xaAS~apN mino xawaAS~i A@ll~`hi [i. e. (assumed tropical:) A particular, or special, gift of God betided him ]. (TA.) ― -b4- Also (assumed tropical:) A deenár: (S, K:) or deenárs; (Az, TA;) [i. e.] coined gold; (Mgh, Msb; *) different from wariqN [which signifies “ coined silver or “ dirhems ”]. (Mgh.) They said, Ealayohi miAy^apN EayonFA (assumed tropical:) [ On him is incumbent the payment of a hundred deenars ]: but properly one should say EayonN , because it is identical with what precedes it (Sb, TA.) ― -b5- And The half of a dánik [app. deducted ] from seven deenars: (K, TA:) mentioned by Az. (TA.) ― -b6- And (tropical:) Gold, (K, TA,) in a general sense; as being likened to the organ [of sight], in that the former is the most excellent of the metals, like as the latter is the most excellence of the organs. (TA.) -A9- And (tropical:) The sun itself; (A, K, TA;) as being likened to the organ [of sight], because the former is the most noble of the stars, like as the latter is the most noble of the organs. (TA:) or (K, TA) the Eayon of the sun; (S, Msb, TA;) i. e. the $uEaAE thereof; (K, TA,) [meaning its rays, or beams, ] upon which the eye will act remain fixed: (TA:) or [more commonly] the Eayon means the quroS [q. v., that is disk ] of the sun. (KL.) [Using it in the first of these senses.] one says, TalaEati AlEayonu (tropical:) [ The sun rose ], and gaAbati AlEayonu [ The sun set ]. (Lh, TA.) -A10- And (assumed tropical:) A thing's nafos [i. e. its self ]; (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA;) and its *aAt [which means the same]; (K, TA:) and its $axoS , which means nearly, or rather exactly, the same as its *At ; (TA;) [and likewise a man's person, as does also ↓ EiyaAnN , (see exs. in Har pp. 20 and 45,) and the material substance of a thing;] and its A^aSol [as meaning its essence, or constituent substance ]: (TA:) pl. A^aEoyaAnN , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) not A^aEoyunN nor EuyuwnN . (Mgh, TA.) One says, huwa huwa EayonFA and huwa huwa biEayonihi (assumed tropical:) ( It is it itself, or he is he himself ]: (S, TA:) bi when prefixed to Eayon , [thus] used as a corroborative, being redundant. (Mughnee in art. bi .) And laA A=xu*u A_il~aA dirohamiY biEayonihi (assumed tropical:) [ I will not take aught save my dirhem itself ]. (S.) And A^axa*otu maAliY biEayonihi (assumed tropical:) I took my property itself. (Msb.) And h*ihi A^aEoyaAnu daraAhimika (Lh, TA) and daraAhimuka biA^aEoyaAnihaA (Lh, Mgh, * Msb, TA) (assumed tropical:) These are thy dirhems themselves ]. And humo A_ixowatuka biA^aEoyaAnihimo (assumed tropical:) [ They are thy brothers themselves ]. (Msb.) And Eayonu Alr~ibaA occurs in a trad. as meaning (assumed tropical:) Usury itself. (TA.) [ mawoDiEN biEayonihi , a phrase very frequently occurring in the L and TA &c., means (assumed tropical:) A certain, or particular, place: and in a similar manner biEayonihi is used after the mention of a plant &c.] One says also jaA='a biAlA^amori mino EayonK SaAfiyapK i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ He brought forth, brought to light, or declared, the affair ] from its very essence. (TA.) And biAlHaq~i biEayonihi means (assumed tropical:) With truth, clearly and manifestly. (TA.) [In grammar, Aisomu EayonK means (assumed tropical:) A real substantive; the name of a real thing; also termed Aisomu *aAtK ; and sometimes termed EayonN alone: opposed to Aisomu maEonFY i. e. an ideal substantive.] -A11- EayonN vaAqibapN means (assumed tropical:) Certain, or sure, news or information. (A and TA in art. vqb .) -A12- And AlEayonu [sometimes] signifies (assumed tropical:) Knowledge; [or rather sure, or certain, and manifest, knowledge; ] which is also termed Eayonu Alyaqiyni . (TA.) -A13- And (assumed tropical:) Might ( AlEiz~u ). (TA.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) Health and safety ( AlEaAfiyapu ). (TA.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) Thirst; and so Algayonu . (TA in art. gyn .) -A14- And (assumed tropical:) The Suwrap [which generally means form, or the like: but it has many other significations; one of which is essence, before mentioned as a meaning of EayonN ]. (TA.) -A15- And it signifies also Aln~aAHiyapN [app. as meaning (assumed tropical:) The part, or point, towards which one directs himself ]: (K, TA:) or, accord. to some, particularly that of the qibolap [i. e. that towards which one directs his face in prayer ]: (TA:) [or] it signifies also the true direction of the qibolap : (K, TA:) or the part that is on the right of the qibolap of El-'Irák: [whence] one says, na$aA^ati Als~aHaAbapu mino qibali AlEayoni (assumed tropical:) [ The cloud rose from the part on the right of the qblp of El- 'Irák ]: (S: [see also xasofN :]) or this means, from the direction of the qblp of El-'Irak; and the Arabs say that this scarcely ever, or never, breaks its promise [of giving rain]: when it rises from the direction of the sea, and then goes northward, one says EayonN gudayoqapN ; and this is usually most disposed to rain: (TA:) gudayoqap is a dim. of magnification, meaning abounding with water. (TA in art. gdq .) Also (assumed tropical:) The clouds ( saHaAb ) that have come from the direction of the qibolap : (K, * TA:) or, from the direction of the qblp of El- 'Irák: or, from the right thereof: (K, TA:) and it is said in the B to signify [simply] Als~aHaAbu [the clouds ]; (TA;) and so Algayonu . (TA in art. gyn .) And, accord. to Th, maTaru AlEayoni signifies (assumed tropical:) The rain that is from the direction of the qibolap : or, from the direction of the qblp of El-'Irák: or, from the right thereof. (TA.) The saying of the Arabs muTironaA biAlEayoni (assumed tropical:) [ We were, or have been, rained upon by the Eyn ] is allowed by some, but disapproved by others. (TA.) ― -b2- And [hence, app.,] (assumed tropical:) The rain that continues during some days, (S, K, TA,) some say five, and some say six, or more, (TA,) without clearing away. (S, K, TA.) -A16- EayonN signifies also (assumed tropical:) Usury; syn. ribFA ; (K, TA; [see also Eayonu Alr~ibaA above;]) and so ↓ EiynapN . (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) An inclining in the balance; (Kh, Mgh, K, TA;) said to be the case in which one of the two scales thereof outweighs the other: (TA:) one says, fiY AlmiyzaAni EayonN , meaning (assumed tropical:) In the balance is an unevenness; (S, TA;) a little inclining in the tongue thereof: and the word is fem. (TA.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) The tongue [or cock, itself,] of the balance. (TA.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) A scale of a balance; i. e. either of the two scales thereof. (TA.) Also (assumed tropical:) A small bayot [meaning partition, or part divided from the rest, ] in a chest. (TA.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) A miHa$~ap [app. meaning a thing in which Ha$iy$ , or dry herbage, is put ]. (TA.) ― -b3- [And (assumed tropical:) Either half, or one side, of a xuroj , or pair of saddle-bags. ] And A certain bird, (K, TA,) yellow in the belly, A^axoDar [generally in a case of this kind meaning of a dingy, or dark, ash-colour or dust-colour ] in the back; of the size of the [ species of collared turtle-dove called ] qumoriY~ . (TA.) Also (assumed tropical:) [The letter E ;] one of the letters of the alphabet, (S, K,) of those termed Haloqiy~ap and mahojuwrap . (K. [See art. E .]) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) The middle [ radical letter ] of a word [ of the triliteral-radical class; the root of such a word being represented by fEl ]. (TA.) ― -b3- In the calculation by means of the letters A , b , j , d , &c., it denotes Seventy. (TA.)

Eayonu Alv~awori (assumed tropical:) ( The eye of the Bull; ] the great red star [a] that is upon the southern eye of Taurus, and also [ more commonly ] called Ald~abaraAnu . (Kzw, Descr. of Taurus.) [And Eayonu Alr~aAmiY (assumed tropical:) The eye of Sagittarius; app. the two stars v, on the eye thereof. ]

Eayonu Albaqari (assumed tropical:) [ The buphthalmum, or ox-eye; ] the [ plant called ] bahaAr [q. v.]. (S in art. bhr .) And Euyuwnu Albaqari (tropical:) A sort of grapes, (S, K, TA,) black, (K, TA,) but not intensely so, large in the berries, (TA,) and round, (K, TA,) which are converted into raisins, and are not very sweet: so says AHn: thus called as being likened to the eyes of the animals termed baqar : (TA:) they are found in Syria: (S:) or said by some to be peculiar to Syria. (TA.) And...
Eayonu Alhir~i (assumed tropical:) [ Cat's-eye; ] a certain stone, well known, of no utility. (TA.)

rawSourceText: is a homonym, applying to various things (Msb:) in the K. forty-seven meanings are assigned to it; but it is said by MF that its meanings exceed a hundred; those occurring in the Kur-án are seventeen. (TA.,) By that which is app. its primary application, and which is by many affirmed to be so,(TA,) AlEayonu signifies The eye: the organ of sight: (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA [in the S expl. by HaAs~apu Alr~uw^oyapi , evidently used in this sense; in the Mgh, by AlmuboSirapu ; in the Msb and K, by AlbaASirapu ; and in a mater place in the K. by HaAs~apu Alr~uw^oyap , app. as meaning the sense of sight; ]) also denoted [emphatically] by the term AljaAriHapu [i. e. the organ ]; (TA;) it is that with which the looker sees: (ISk, TA;) and is of a human being and of any other animal: (TA;) it is of the fem. gender; (S, K:) and the pl. [of mult.] as EuyuwnN , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) also pronounced EuywnN , (K, [in which watukosaru , immediately following EuyuwnN , has been erroneously supposed by Golius and Freytag to relate to the sing.,]) and [of pause A^aEoyaAnN and A^aEoyunN , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) which last is asserted by Lh to be sometimes a pl. of mult., as it is in the Kur vii. [178 and] 194; (TA.) and pl. pl. A^aEoyunaAtN : (K:) the dim. is ↓ EuyayonapN , (S.) Hence the saying in a trad. of 'Alee, qaAsa EayonFA bibayoDapK jaEala EalayohaA xuTuwTFA [ He measured the reach of an eye by means of an egg upon which he made lines ]. (Mgh.) And [hence also] one says, biEayonK m~aA A^arayan~aka [lit. With some eye I will assuredly see thee ]: it is said to one whom you send, and require to be quick; and means (assumed tropical:) pause not for anything, for it is as though I were looking at thee. (TA. [See also art. rA^Y .]) And laqiytuhu Eayona Eun~apK [ I met him so that ] I saw him with [or before ] my eye, he not seeing me. (S, TA.) [And raA^ayotuhu Eayona Eun~apK or Eun~apa , which see in art. En . And A^aEoTayotuhu Eayona Eun~apa and Eun~ap , which also see in art. En .] And raA^ayotuhu EaroDa EayonK I saw him, or it, obviously; nearly. (TA, voce EaroDN , q. v.) And haA huwa EaroDu EayonK [or EaroDa EayonK ?] i. e. And faEalotu *aAka Eamoda EayonK and EamodFA EalaY EayonK (assumed tropical:) I did that purposely, with seriousness, or earnestness, and certainty: (S:) or SanaEa *`lika EalaY EayonK and EalaY Eayonayoni , (K, TA,) and Eamoda EayonK and Eamoda Eayonayoni , (K,) or EalaY Eamodi EayonK and EalaY Eamodi Eayonayoni , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He did that purposely, (Lh, K, TA,) with seriousness, or earnestness, and certainty. (K.) And huwa Eabodu EayonK (tropical:) He is like the slave to thee as long as thou seest him, (S, K, * TA,) but not when thou art absent; and so huwa Eabodu AlEayoni : (S:) or he is a man who pretends, or feigns, to thee, his doing that which he does not perform: (TA:) and (K, TA) in this sense, (TA,) one says also, huwa Sadiyqu EayonK i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ He is a friend, or a true friend, ] as long as thou seest him: (K, TA:) and huwa A^axuw EayonK (assumed tropical:) He is one who acts as a friend hypocritically with thee. (TA.) A^anota EalaY EayoniY is said in relation to honouring and protecting: (S, K, TA:) [accordingly I would render it (tropical:) Thou art entitled to be honoured and protected by me above my eye: for the eye is esteemed the most excellent of the organs, (as is said in this art. in the TA,) and it is that which most needs protection:] A^anota EalaY raA^osiY is said in relation to honouring only. (TA.) And the Arabs say, EalaY EayoniY qaSadotu zayodFA , meaning thereby the regarding with solicitude mixed with fear [so that I would render it (assumed tropical:) As one to be regarded with solicitude mixed with fear above my eye I made Zeyd the object to which my mind was directed ]. (TA.) [See another ex. of EalaY EayoniY (in which it cannot be rendered as above) in a later part of this paragraph.] naEima A@ll~`hu bika EayonFA [in the CK naE~ama , which is wrong,] means the same as A^anoEamahaA . (K. [See both in art. nEm .]) qur~apu AlEayoni [signifying maA qar~ato bihi AlEayonu , as expl. in the M and K in art. qr , i. e. That by which, or in consequence of which, the eye becomes cool, or refrigerated, or refreshed, &c.,] is a phrase used as meaning (assumed tropical:) A man's child or offspring. (TA.) faqaA^a Eayonahu [properly signifying He put out his eye, or blinded it, &c.,] means [sometimes] (tropical:) he struck him; or struck him vehemently with a broad thing, or with anything; or slapped him with his hand: ( Sak~ahu :) or he was rough, rude, or ungentle, to him in speech. (TA.) Aal~a*iY fiyhi EayonaAka means Thy head. (TA. [There mentioned preceded by lAtHrman : thus dubiously, and perhaps incorrectly, written. What is means, or should be, I know not.]) ― -b2- Eayonu Alv~awori (assumed tropical:) ( The eye of the Bull; ] the great red star [a] that is upon the southern eye of Taurus, and also [ more commonly ] called Ald~abaraAnu . (Kzw, Descr. of Taurus.) [And Eayonu Alr~aAmiY (assumed tropical:) The eye of Sagittarius; app. the two stars v, on the eye thereof. ] ― -b3- Eayonu Albaqari (assumed tropical:) [ The buphthalmum, or ox-eye; ] the [ plant called ] bahaAr [q. v.]. (S in art. bhr .) And Euyuwnu Albaqari (tropical:) A sort of grapes, (S, K, TA,) black, (K, TA,) but not intensely so, large in the berries, (TA,) and round, (K, TA,) which are converted into raisins, and are not very sweet: so says AHn: thus called as being likened to the eyes of the animals termed baqar : (TA:) they are found in Syria: (S:) or said by some to be peculiar to Syria. (TA.) And Certain black A_ij~aAS [or plums ]: (K, TA:) thus called for the same reason. (TA.) ― -b4- Eayonu Alhir~i (assumed tropical:) [ Cat's-eye; ] a certain stone, well known, of no utility. (TA.) -A2- [ fataHa hayona Aln~aAri means (assumed tropical:) He made an opening in the live coals of the fire, that had become compacted; in order that it might burn up well. (See 1 in art. sxw and sxY .)] ― -b2- And EayonN signifies also (assumed tropical:) The Eayon [i. e. eye ] of the needle: such as is narrow is termed Eayonu Safiy~ap [in which the latter word is app. a proper name, and, as such and of the fem. gender, imperfectly decl., i. e., in this case, written Safiy~apa ]. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, as being likened to the organ [of sight] in form, or appearance, (tropical:) A [ small round hole or] place of perforation in a [leathern water-bag such as is called] mazaAdap . (TA.) And (tropical:) Thin circles, or rings, or round places, in a skin, (S, K, TA,) which are a fault therein, (S, TA,) like A^aEoyun [or eyes; or one of such thin circles &c.]; being likened to the organ [of sight] in form. (TA.) [See 10.] And (K) (tropical:) A fault, or defect, (K, TA,) of this description, in a skin. (TA.) ― -b4- And (tropical:) The small hollow or cavity of the knee; (S, K; in [some of] the copies of the latter of which, Alr~akiy~ap is erroneously put for Alr~ukobap ; TA;) likened to the socket of the eye: (TA:) each knee has EayonaAni [i. e. two small hollows or cavities, the articular depressions for the condyles of the femur ], in the fore part thereof, at [ the joint of ] the saAq . (S, TA.) ― -b5- And (tropical:) The piece of skin [or small leathern receptacle ] in which are put the bunoduq [or bullets ] (K, TA) that are shot from the qawos [app. meaning the large kind of cross-bow, called balista, or ballista ]: (K, * TA:) likened to the organ [of sight] in form. (TA.) ― -b6- [In the B, accord. to the TA, it is also expl. as meaning the snAm : but this, I think, is most probably a mistranscription for saAm (q. v.) as signifying (assumed tropical:) The hollow, or cavity, in the ground, thus called, in which water remains, or stagnates, and collects. ] And (tropical:) The place [or aperture ] whence the water of a qanaAp [i. e. pipe, or the like, ] pours forth: (K, TA:) as being likened to the organ [of sight] because of the water that is in it. (TA.) And, (K, TA,) for the same reason, (TA,) (tropical:) The place whence issues the water of a well. (TA.) And, (S, Msb, K, &c.,) for the same reason, as is said by Er-Rághib, (TA,) (tropical:) The Eayon , (S, Msb,) or source, or spring, (K, TA,) of water, (S, Msb, K, TA,) that wells forth from the earth, or ground, and runs: (TA:) [and accord. to the Msb, it app. signifies a running spring: ] of the fem. gender: (TA:) pl. EuyuwnN and A^aEoyunN , (Msb, K,) and accord. to ISk, sometimes the Arabs said, as a pl. thereof, A^aEoyaAnN , but this is rare. (Msb.) Hence a saying, in a trad., cited and expl. voce saAhirN . (TA.) Also (assumed tropical:) Abundance of water of a well. (TA.) And A drop of water. (TA.) Eayonu AlmaA='i , [ originally signifying “ the source of water, ”] accord. to Th, means (assumed tropical:) Life for men; thus in the following verse: A^uwlaAy^ika Eayonu AlmaA='i fiyhimo waEinodahumo mina Alxiyfapi AlmanojaApu waAlmutaHaw~alu (assumed tropical:) [ Those, life for men is among them; and with them are the means of safety, and the place of removal, from fear ]: accord. to the A, Eayonu AlmaA='i fiyhimo means good, or means of attaining good, and provision of corn, or abundance of the produce of the earth, are among them. (TA.) ― -b7- Also (assumed tropical:) The Eayon [meaning eye, or bud, (thus called in the present day,)] of a tree. (Es-Subkee, TA.) ― -b8- [And (tropical:) Sprouting herbage; as being likened to the eye or eyes:] one says, naZarati AlbilaAdu biEayonK or biEayonayoni [lit. (tropical:) The lands looked with an eye or with two eyes ], meaning, had their herbage come forth: (K:) or it is said when their herbage comes forth: or, as in the A, when that which cattle depasture comes forth without [as yet] becoming firm [in the ground, or firmly rooted]: taken from the saying of the Arabs, A_i*aA saqaTati Aljabohapu naZarati AlA^aroDu biA_iHodaY EayonayohaA faA_i*aA saqaTati AlS~arofapu naZarato bihimaA jamiyEFA (assumed tropical:) [lit. When El-Jebheh (the 10th Mansion of the Moon) sets aurorally (i. e. about the 11th of Feb., O. S.), the land looks with one of its eyes; the, when Es-Sarfeh (the 12th Mansion) sets aurorally (about the 9th of March), it looks with both of them ]. (TA. [See also art. nZr .]) -A3- EayonN also, (S, Msb, K, &c.,) as being likened to the organ of sight, (TA,) signifies (tropical:) A spy; and ↓ *uw AlEuyayonatayoni [in the CK *uw AlEayonatayoni ], in like manner, signifies the spy, (S, K, TA,) and ↓ *uw AlEuwayonatayoni likewise, and *uw AlEayonayoni : (TA:) he who looks for a people, or party: (M, TA:) the watcher, or observer; (S, * K, * TA;) or the scout: (S, * Msb, K, * TA:) masc. and fem.: (M, TA:) accord. to the opinion of ISd, made by some to accord with a part [i. e. the eye], and therefore fem.; and by some, to accord with the whole [person], and therefore masc.: (TA:) pl. EuyuwnN and A^aEoyunN , and, accord. to ISk, sometimes A^aEoyaAnN . (Msb.) ― -b2- And i. q. mukaA$ifN [app. as meaning (assumed tropical:) A discoverer, or revealer, of tidings &c.]. (Es-Subkee, TA.) -A4- [And (assumed tropical:) An eye as meaning a look, i. e. an act of looking: and hence, a stroke of an evil eye: or, simply, an evil eye: a meaning of frequent occurrence.] A^aSaAbato fulaAnFA EayonN (assumed tropical:) [ An evil eye smote such a one ] is said of a person when an enemy or an envier has looked at him and produced such an effect upon him that he has fallen sick in consequence thereof (TA.) [ Eayonu AlkamaAli is applied to an eye believed to have the power of killing by its glance: see an ex. voce faqaA^a .] ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) Sight with the eye [or before the eyes; or ocular view ]: thus in the saying, laA A^aTolubu A^avarFA baEoda EayonK (assumed tropical:) [ I will not seek a trace, or vestige, (or, as we rather say in English, a shadow, ) after an ocular view ]: (S, TA:) or the meaning is, after suffering a reality, or substance, to escape me: (Har pp. 120 and 174: [this latter rendering being agreeable with explanations of EayonN which will be found in a later part of this paragraph:]) i. e. I will not leave the thing when I see it ocularly, and seek the trace or vestige, thereof, after its [the thing's] disappearing from me: and the origin of it was the fact that a man saw the slayer of his brother, and when he desired to slay him, he [the latter] said, “ I will ransom myself with a hundred she-camels; ” whereupon he [the other] said, lasotu A^aTolubu A^avarFA baEoda EayonK ; and slew him: (TA:) it is a prov., thus, or, as some relate it, laA taTolubo . (Har p. 120.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) Look, or view. (K, TA.) It is said in the Kur [xx. 40], waAltuSonaEa EalaY EayoniY , (S, TA,) and it has been expl. as there having this meaning [i. e. (assumed tropical:) And this I did that thou mightest be reared and nourished in my view ], as in the B; or, as Th says, that thou mightest be reared where I should see thee: (TA:) or the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) in my watch, or guard, (Bd, * Jel,) and my keeping, or protection. (Jel. [It is implied by the context in the S, that EalaY EayoniY is said in this instance in relation to honouring and protecting, as it is in a phrase mentioned in the first quarter of this paragraph; but my rendering of it there is obviously inapplicable here. See also 1 in art. SnE .]) And in like manner it has been expl. as used in the Kur [xi. 39], waA@SonaEi A@lofuloka biA^aEoyuninaA (assumed tropical:) [ And make thou the ark in our view ]. (TA.) [In like manner, also,] faA^otuwA bihi EalaY A^aEoyuni A@ln~aAsi , in the Kur [xxi. 62], means EalaY manoZarihimo (assumed tropical:) [i. e. Then bring ye him in the view of the people; mnZr being here evidently an inf. n.]; (B, TA:) or [ bring ye him ] openly, or conspicuously. (Jel.) -A5- And (assumed tropical:) The manoZar [as meaning aspect, or outward appearance ], (S, K,) and $aAhid [meaning the same as being an evidence of the intrinsic qualities], (S,) of a man. (S, K.) So in the saying of El-Hajjáj to El-Hasan [ElBasree, when he (the former) had asked maA A^amaduka “ What was the time of thy birth? ” and the latter had answered (see A^amadN )], laEayonuka A^akobaru mino A^amadika (assumed tropical:) [ Verily thy aspect is greater than thy age ], A^amadika meaning sin~ika . (S.) And it is said in a prov., A_in~a AljawaAda Eayonuhu furaAruhu (assumed tropical:) [ Verily the fleet and excellent horse, his aspect is ( equivalent to ) the examination of his teeth ]: (S, TA: [accord. to the latter, Eayonuhu meaning $aAhiduhu :]) i. e. his external appearance renders it needless for thee to try him and to examine his teeth. (S and K in art. fr , q. v.) -A6- Also, [by a synecdoche, as when it means “ a spy, ”] (assumed tropical:) A human being: (K:) and any one: (S, K:) [in which sense, as when it means “ a spy, ” it may be masc. or fem.:] and human beings: (S:) or a company [ of people ]; (K;) as also ↓ EayanN : (S, K:) and the people of a house or dwelling: (K:) and so ↓ EayanN ; (S, K;) and the people of a town or country; as also ↓ EayanN . (K.) One says, maA bihaA EayonN (assumed tropical:) There is not in it any one; (S, K, TA;) [i. e. biAld~aAri in the house, or dwelling; ] as also ↓ EayanN , (TA,) and ↓ EaAy^inN , (S, TA,) and ↓ EaAy^inapN : (TA:) and maA bihaA EayonN taTorifu [virtually meaning the same, but fit. There is not in it an eye twinkling ]. (TA.) And ↓ maA raA^ayotu vam~a EaAy^inapF i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ I was not there ] a human being. (TA.) And baladN qaliylu AlEayoni (assumed tropical:) [ A town, or country, ] having few human beings, (S.) or few people. (TA.) -A7- And (assumed tropical:) A lord, chief, or chief personage: (K, TA:) in [some of] the copies of the K, Alsd~ or Al$d~ is erroneously put for Als~ay~idu : (TA:) the great, or great and noble, person of a people or party: (K, TA:) and the head, chief, or commander, of an army: (TA:) the pl. is A^aEoyaAnN : (TA:) which signifies [ lords, chiefs, or chief personages: &c.: and] the eminent, or high-born, or noble, individuals (S, Mgh, Msb, TA) of a people, or party, (S, Mgh,) or of men; (Msb;) and the most excellent persons. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (Mgh, Msb,) as pl. of EayonN , (K,) A^aEoyaAnN signifies also A Brothers from the same father and mother: (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) this brotherhood is termed ↓ muEaAyanapN : (S, K:) and A^awolaAdu AlA^aEoyaAni means the sons of the same father and mother. (Msb in art. El . [See Eal~apN .]) ― -b3- Also. the sing., (assumed tropical:) The choice, or best, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) of a thing, (S, K,) or of goods, or household-goods, or furniture and utensils, (Mgh, Msb, TA,) and of camels, or cattle, or other property, (TA,) and so ↓ EiynapN , (S, K, TA,) of which the pl. is EiyanN , (TA,) like EiymapN : (S:) ↓ Eiynapu Alxayoli signifies (assumed tropical:) the fleet and excellent of horses. (Lh, TA.) And (assumed tropical:) Highly prized, in much request, or excellent. (TA.) And, as applied to a deenár, (assumed tropical:) Outweighing, so that the balance inclines with it. (TA.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) i. q. maAlN , (K, TA,) [i. e. Property, or such as consists of camels or cattle, ] when of a choice. or of the best, sort. (TA.) -A8- And (assumed tropical:) Such as is ready, or at hand, (K, TA,) present, (TA,) or within one's power, or reach, (S, TA,) of property. (S, K, TA.) (Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) Ready money; cash: or simply money: syn. naqodN : (T, Mgh, Msb, TA:) not EaroDN [q. v.]: (Mgh:) and sometimes, daraAhimu . (Msb.) So in the saying EayonN gayoru dayoni (assumed tropical:) [ Ready money, not debt ]. (TA.) And [hence also] one says, Ai$otarayota biAld~ayoni A^awo biAlEayoni (assumed tropical:) [ Didst thou buy on credit or with ready money? ]. (Msb.) ― -b3- And A A present gift. (Mgh, TA.) (assumed tropical:) A particular, or special, gift of God betided him ]. (TA.) ― -b4- Also (assumed tropical:) A deenár: (S, K:) or deenárs; (Az, TA;) [i. e.] coined gold; (Mgh, Msb; *) different from wariqN [which signifies “ coined silver or “ dirhems ”]. (Mgh.) (TA.) ― -b6- And (tropical:) Gold, (K, TA,) in a general sense; as being likened to the organ [of sight], in that the former is the most excellent of the metals, like as the latter is the most excellence of the organs. (TA.) -A9- And (tropical:) The sun itself; (A, K, TA;) as being likened to the organ [of sight], because the former is the most noble of the stars, like as the latter is the most noble of the organs. A^aEoyaAnN , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) not A^aEoyunN nor EuyuwnN . (Mgh, TA.) One says, huwa huwa EayonFA and huwa huwa biEayonihi (assumed tropical:) ( It is it itself, or he is he himself ]: (S, TA:) bi when prefixed to Eayon , [thus] used as a corroborative, being redundant. And A^axa*otu maAliY biEayonihi (assumed tropical:) I took my property itself. (Msb.) And h*ihi A^aEoyaAnu daraAhimika (Lh, TA) and daraAhimuka biA^aEoyaAnihaA (Lh, Mgh, * Msb, TA) (assumed tropical:) These are thy dirhems themselves ]. And humo A_ixowatuka biA^aEoyaAnihimo (assumed tropical:) [ They are thy brothers themselves ]. (Msb.) And Eayonu Alr~ibaA occurs in a trad. as meaning (assumed tropical:) Usury itself. (TA.) [ mawoDiEN biEayonihi , a phrase very frequently occurring in the L and TA &c., means (assumed tropical:) A certain, or particular, place: and in a similar manner biEayonihi is used after the mention of a plant &c.] One says also jaA='a biAlA^amori mino EayonK SaAfiyapK i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ He brought forth, brought to light, or declared, the affair ] from its very essence. (TA.) And biAlHaq~i biEayonihi means (assumed tropical:) With truth, clearly and manifestly. (TA.) [In grammar, Aisomu EayonK means (assumed tropical:) A real substantive; the name of a real thing; also termed Aisomu *aAtK ; and sometimes termed EayonN alone: opposed to Aisomu maEonFY i. e. an ideal substantive.] -A11- EayonN vaAqibapN means (assumed tropical:) Certain, or sure, news or information. (TA.) -A13- And (assumed tropical:) Might ( AlEiz~u ). (TA.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) Health and safety ( AlEaAfiyapu ). (TA.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) Thirst; and so Algayonu . (TA in art. gyn .) -A14- And (assumed tropical:) The Suwrap [which generally means form, or the like: but it has many other significations; one of which is essence, before mentioned as a meaning of EayonN ]. (TA.) -A15- And it signifies also Aln~aAHiyapN [app. as meaning (assumed tropical:) The part, or point, towards which one directs himself ]: (K, TA:) or, accord. to some, particularly that of the qibolap [i. e. that towards which one directs his face in prayer ]: (TA:) [or] it signifies also the true direction of the qibolap : (K, TA:) or the part that is on the right of the qibolap of El-'Irák: [whence] one says, na$aA^ati Als~aHaAbapu mino qibali AlEayoni (assumed tropical:) [ The cloud rose from the part on the right of the qblp of El- 'Irák ]: (S: [see also xasofN :]) or this means, from the direction of the qblp of El-'Irak; and the Arabs say that this scarcely ever, or never, breaks its promise [of giving rain]: when it rises from the direction of the sea, and then goes northward, one says EayonN gudayoqapN ; and this is usually most disposed to rain: (TA:) gudayoqap is a dim. of magnification, meaning abounding with water. (TA.) The saying of the Arabs muTironaA biAlEayoni (assumed tropical:) [ We were, or have been, rained upon by the Eyn ] is allowed by some, but disapproved by others. (TA.) ― -b2- And [hence, app.,] (assumed tropical:) The rain that continues during some days, (S, K, TA,) some say five, and some say six, or more, (TA,) without clearing away. (S, K, TA.) -A16- EayonN signifies also (assumed tropical:) Usury; syn. ribFA ; (K, TA; [see also Eayonu Alr~ibaA above;]) and so ↓ EiynapN . (TA.) (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA.) And one says, baAEahu biEiynapK meaning binasiyoy^apK [i. e. He sold it upon credit, for payment at a future time ]: (A, Mgh: [see 8:]) or, as some say, [and more commonly,] AlEiynapu is the buying what one has sold for less than that for which one has sold it: and ↓ AlEayanu signifies the same: (Mgh:) or, accord. to Az, the selling a commodity for a certain price to be paid at a certain period, and then buying it for less than that price with ready money: [see 2, last quarter:] this is unlawful when the buyer makes it a condition with the seller that he shall buy it for a certain price; but when there is no condition between them, it is allowable accord. to Esh-Sháfi'ee, though forbidden by some others; and he used to call it the sister of usury: and the sale of a commodity by the purchaser [ thereof upon credit ] to other than the seller of it, on the spot (lit. in the sitting-place ), is also termed EiynapN ; but is lawful by common consent: (Msb:) or it is the case of a man's coming to another man to ask of him a loan, which the latter does not desire to grant, coveting profit, which is not to be obtained by a loan, wherefore he says, “ I will sell to thee this garment for twelve dirhems upon credit, for payment at a certain time, and its value is ten [ which thou mayest obtain by selling it for ready money ]. ” (KT: in some copies of which the word thus expl. is [erroneously] written AlEayoniy~apu instead of AlEiynapu .) (TA.)

definition: Smitten with the [ evil ] eye;
sourceDefinition: Smitten with the [ evil ] eye; as also ↓ maEoyuwnN , the complete form: (S, TA:) or, accord. to Ez-Zejjájee, the former has this meaning, but ↓ AlmaEoyuwnu means Aal~a*iY fiyhi EayonN [in which the last word is probably a mistranscription for EayobN ; so that the meaning is, in whom is a fault, or defect ], (L, TA.) A poet says, (S,) namely, 'Abbás, (TA,) qado kaAna qawomuka yaHosabuwnaka say~idFA ↓ waA_ixalu A^in~aka say~idN maEoyuwnu [ Thy people, or party, used to reckon thee a chief; but I think that them art a chief smitten with the evil eye, or, perhaps, in whom is a fault, or defect ]. (S, TA.) ― -b2- maA='N maEiynN and ↓ maEoyuwnN (S, K:) (assumed tropical:) Water of which one has reached the springs or sources, by digging: (S:) or water that is apparent ( ZaAhirN , for which the CK has ZAhrN ), (K, TA,) seen by the eye, (TA,) running upon the surface of the earth: (K, TA:) Bedr Ibn-'Ámir El-Hudhalee says. ↓ maA='N yujim~u liHaAfirK maEoyuwni [meaning Water collecting for a digger of which the springs have been reached by digging ]; the last word, it as said, being put by him in the gen. case because of the proximity [to a word in that case, agreeably with a poetic license of which there are many exs.], maEoyuwnN , as it is an epithet relating to m=' : Respecting the measure of maEiynN , which IB derives from Eayonu AlmaA='i . and explain as meaning having the source apparent, there are differences of opinion; some say that it is an instance of mafoEuwlN though not having a verb; and some, that of the measure faEiylN , from AlmEonu signifying the drawing of water. (TA.) In the saying A_ino kaAnati Alba$aru maEiynFA laA tunozaHu , meaning [ If the well be one ] having a running spring, ( that willnot be entirely exhausted, ] mEynA is made masc. to accord with the word [ b}r , which is masc. in form though fem. by usage]; or it is thus because it is imagined to be of the measure faEiyl , in the sense of the measure mafoEuwl ; or because it is for *aAta maEiynK , i. e. [ having ] water running upon the surface of the earth. (Mgh.) In the Kur xxxvii. 44. [and in like manner in lvi. 18.] maEiyn is used as meaning (assumed tropical:) Wine running upon the surface of the earth, like rivers of water. (Jel.) ― -b3- EayonN ↓ maEoyuwnapN means (assumed tropical:) A spring, or source, having a continued increase of water (Aboo-Sa'eed, TA.)

sourceDefinition: (assumed tropical:) A garment figured with eyes (S in art. brj :) or a garment in the figuring of which are small taraAbiyE [app. meaning quadrangular forms (in the CK tarobiyE )] like the eyes of wild animals. (K.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) A bull having a blackness between his eyes: (K:) or a bull; so called because of the largeness of his eyes: or so called because having spots of black and white, as though there were eyes upon his skin. (Ham p. 293.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) Locusts ( jaraAd ) which, when stripped of the integument, are seen to be white and red: mentioned by Az in art. ynE , on the authority of ISh. (TA.) -A2- [Also, as pass. part. n. of 2, (assumed tropical:) Individuated, or particularized; i. e. distinguished from the generality, or aggregate: &c.: see the verb. (Msb.)

(Mgh, K, TA) from AlAigotisaAlu , (Mgh, TA,) or, as some say. the latter is the inf. n. and the former is the subst., (MF, TA,) He washed it; with water ( biAlmaA='i ): (MA:) gasolu Al$~Yo'i signifies the removing of dirt, or filth, and the like thereof, from the thing, by making water to run over it. (Mgh.) You say, gasala Aljiloda kul~ahu [ He washed the skin, all of it ], and Almay~ita [ the dead body]: and ↓ gs~l has the like, but an intensive, meaning. (Msb.) Edw , conj. 3.] ― -b5- gasala AlmaroA^apa signifies (tropical:) He compressed the woman ( jaAmaEahaA ); (Az, Mgh, O, TA;) like EasalahaA , with E ; (Az, Mgh, TA;) much or little; (TA;) and ↓ gas~alahaA signifies the same: (Mgh, O, TA:) or both signify he did so much. definition: It is said in a trad.
sourceDefinition: It is said in a trad., AlEayonu Haq~N faA_i*aA A@sotugosilotumo ↓ faA@gosiluwA [ The evil eye is a truth; so when ye are asked to wash, wash ye ]: i. e., when he who was smitten by the eye of any one demanded [the performance of what is here meant], he brought to the smiter therewith a bowl in which was water, and he [the latter] would put his hand into it, and rinse his mouth [with some of it], then spit it out into the bowl; then he would wash his face in it; then he would put in his left hand, and pour upon his right hand; then he would put in his right hand, and pour upon his left hand; [then he would put in his left hand (a clause omitted in my original),] and pour upon his right elbow; then he would put in his right hand, and pour upon his left elbow; then he would put in his left hand, and pour upon his right foot; then he would put in his right hand, and pour upon his left foot; then he would put in his left hand, and pour upon his right knee; then he would put in his right hand, and pour upon his left knee; then he would wash what is termed daAxilapu AlA_izaAri [expl. in art. dxl ]: and he would not put the bowl upon the ground: then he would pour that used water upon the head of the person smitten with the eye, from behind him, with one pouring; and he would be cured, with the permission of God. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: : see AlgusaAlapu . ― -b2- Algisoliynu (in the Kur [lxix. 36], TA) What is washed off of the flesh and the blood of the inmates of the fire [ of Hell ]; (Akh, S, O;) [for] what comes forth from any wound, or sore, when it is washed, is termed gisoliyn : (TA:) what is washed off from the bodies of the unbelievers, in the fire: (Msb:) or what flows from the skins of the inmates of the fire, (K, TA,) such as thick purulent matter &c.; thus expl. by Fr and Seer; (TA;) as though it were washed from them: (Sb, TA:) accord. to Mujáhid, a certain food of the inmates of the fire; and El-Kelbee says that it is what the fire has cooked, of their flesh, and has fallen off, and is eaten by them: (TA:) and, (K,) accord. to Ed-Dahhák, (O, TA,) a species of trees in the fire; (O, K, TA;) and so he says of AlD~ariyEu : (O, TA:) and, (K,) accord. to Lth, (O, TA,) what is intensely hot: (O, K, TA:) the Y and n are augmentative. (S, O, Msb.)

sourceDefinition: i. q. ↓ magosuwlN [i. e. Washed ]; (S, O, Msb, K;) applied to a thing, (S, O,) and to a dead body; (Lh, Msb, TA;) and the former is also applied as an epithet to a fem. n., as is also gasiylapN ; (S, O, K;) or this last is used after the manner of substs., like naTiyHapN and *abiyHapN ; not as is said in the S [and O] after the manner of epithets: (IB, TA:) the pl. of gasiylN is gasoliY and gusalaA='u ; (Lh, K, TA;) and the pl. of gasiylapN [and app. of gasiylN used a fem. epithet] is gasaAlaY or gusaAlaY . (K accord. to different copies.) Han- dhaleh Ibn-er-Ráhib was called gasiylu AlmalaAy^ikapi [ The washed of the angels ], because he died a martyr on the day of Ohod, and the angels washed him, (S, O, Msb,) accord. to the Prophet, who said that he saw them washing him. (O.) ― -b2- See also gusalapN . ― -b3- [It is now used as meaning Clothes, or the like, put together to be washed. ]

sourceDefinition: : see 2. ― -b2- AgmD Eayonayohi , (Mgh,) or AlEayona , (Msb,) inf. n. A_igomaADN ; (S, Msb;) and ↓ gam~aDahumaA , (Mgh,) or gam~aDahaA , (Msb,) inf. n. tagomiyDN ; (S, Msb;) He shut, or closed, (Mgh, Msb,) [ his eyes, or] his eyelids, (Mgh,) or [ the eye, or] the eyelids. (Msb.) ― -b3- [Hence,] maA A^agomaDotu , (A, TA,) and ↓ maA gam~aDotu , (TA,) I have not slept; (TA;) and ↓ maA A@gotamaDotu [signifies the same]; (JK;) and so maA A@kotaHalotu A_igomaADFA , (ISd, K,) and ↓ tagomaADFA (S, Sgh, K) and tagomiyDFA , (S, K,) [two inf. ns. of 2,] and ↓ gamaADFA , and ↓ gimaADFA , and ↓ gumoDFA with damm, (S, Sgh, K,) [and app. ↓ gumaADFA , and ↓ gumuwDFA , and ↓ gamoDFA , for] IB says that gamoDN and gumuwDN and gumaADN are inf. ns. of a verb not used: (TA:) and maA *uqotu ↓ gumoDFA , [in a copy of the A ↓ gamoDFA ,] and ↓ gamaA DFA , I have not tasted sleep. (JK.) [And hence,] Albaroqu ↓ AgtmD (tropical:) The lightning ceased to gleam; as though sleeping. (TA.) ― -b4- You say also, AgmD Tarofahu Ean~iY , and ↓ gm~Dhu , He shut, or closed, his eye, or eyes, at, or upon, or against, me: and AgmD Ealayohi , and ↓ gm~D , he shut, or closed, his eyes at, or upon, or against, him, or it. (TA.) ― -b5- And [hence,] AgmD Eanohu , and Ealayohi , (tropical:) [ He shut his eyes at it, or upon it, or against it ], namely a thing that he had heard: a metonymical phrase, denoting patience. (TA.) And AgmD Eanohu (tropical:) He connived at it; feigned himself neglectful of it; passed it by; (A, Mgh, Msb, TA;) as also Eanohu ↓ gm~D , inf. n. tagomiyDN ; and ↓ gamaDa ; and ↓ AgtmD ; namely a thing that he had heard; and an evil action: (A, TA:) and Eayonayohi ↓ gm~D Eanohu he feigned himself blind to it. (TA.) And AgmD Eanohu fiY AlbayoEi , (S, K,) or Al$~iraA='i , (S, TA,) (tropical:) He acted, or affected to act, in an easy, or a facile, manner towards him, ( tasaAhala Ealayohi ,) in selling, (S, K,) or buying; (S;) as also ↓ gamaDa Eanohu , (S, K,) aor. . (K.) And A^agomiDo liY fiymaA biEotaniY , (S, A, K, TA,) in [some of] the copies of the K like AiDoribo , [i. e. ↓ AigomiDo ,] but the former is the right reading, (TA,) [though the latter is perhaps allowable, as will presently be seen,] meaning, (A, TA,) or as though it meant, (S, K, TA,) (tropical:) Give thou to me more of what thou hast sold to me, on account of its badness; or [so in the A, but in the S and K “ and, ”] lower thou to me the price thereof; (S, A, K, TA;) as also liY fiyhi ↓ gam~iDo . (K, TA.) And AgmD fiY AlbayoEi (tropical:) He demanded that another should give him more of the thing sold; and that he should lower the price [ thereof ]; and he complied with his demand. (IAth.) And AgmD fiY Als~iloEapi (tropical:) He demanded a lowering of the price of the commodity, on account of its badness. (TA.) It is said in the Kur [ii. 270], walasotumo biA=xi*iyhi A_il~aA A^ano tugomiDuwA fiyhi , (S, A, * K,) or, accord. to one reading, ↓ tagomiDuwA , (TA,) i. e. (tropical:) When ye do not take it unless ye lower the price; (Lth, Zj, * K;) meaning, EalaY A_igomaADK , or biA_igomaADK . (Fr.) ― -b6- [Hence also,] fulaAnN EalaY h`*aA AlA^amori ↓ gam~aDa (assumed tropical:) Such a one executed, performed, or accomplished, this affair: or kept, or applied himself, constantly, or perseveringly, to it; ( maDaY Ealayohi ;) [as though he shut his eyes at it;] knowing what was in it. (O, K.) And Aln~aAqapu ↓ gam~aDati , (S, A, K,) inf. n. tagomiyDN , (K,) The she-camel, being driven away ( rud~ato , as in the K, and in some copies of the S, or *iydato , as in other copies of the S, and in the A, as is said in the TA,) from the watering-trough, (S, K,) rushed upon the driver, ( Al*~aAy^id , [in the CK, erroneously, AlzAy^id ,]) closing her eyes, and came to the water. (S, A, K.) ↓ tagomiyDN also signifies The embarking [ in an affair ], or undertaking [ it ], blindly. definition: (S, M, A, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: (S, M, A, Msb, K, &c.) and fawaAdN , which is strange, (K,) but said by Esh-Shiháb to be a dial var., and to be without reason disallowed by AHát; (TA;) of the masc. gender only; (Lh, M, L, K, &c.;) The heart; syn. qalobN [q. v.]; (S, M, A, L, Msb, K, &c.;) of man, and of an animal other than man: (M, L:) so called because of its tafaA^~ud (T, M, L, K) i. e. tawaq~ud [or ardour]; (M, L, K;) or because of its pulsation, and commotion; [for which reason also the heart is said to be called Alqalobu , from Alt~aqal~ubu ;] for it is said that the primary meaning of ↓ faA^odN is “ motion, ” and the “ putting in motion: ” (MF, TA:) or the heart is thus called only when its tafaA^~ud , i. e. its tawaq~ud , is regarded: and most authors make a distinction between fuw^aAd and qalobN ; the latter of which is said to have a more special signification than the former: (TA:) and the former is said to be [the pericardium, ] the gi$aA=' , (L, TA,) or the wiEaA=' , (TA,) of the qalob : (L, TA:) or the middle thereof: (L:) or the interior thereof: (TA:) the qalob being its Hab~ap [q. v.], (L, TA,) or its suwayodaA=' : (L:) or fuw^aAdN signifies the appendages of the mariYo' [or œsophagus ], consisting of the liver and lungs and qalob [or heart ]: (K:) pl. A^afoy^idapN , (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) the only pl. thereof known to Sb. (M, L.) ― -b2- Also The mind, or intellect: and this, it is said, may be the meaning of the phrase [in the Kur liii. 11], maA ka*aba A@lofuw^aAdu maA raA^aY , (TA,) or mA ka*~aba , another reading, i. e. [ The mind ] did not disacknowledge, or deem improbable, what he saw. (Jel.) [Hence,] Hid~apu Alfuw^aAdi i. q. *akaA='N [meaning Sharpness, or acuteness, of mind, in a man: and sharpness of spirit in a beast]. (S in art. *kw .) [And Hadiydu Alfuw^aAdi i. q. *akiy^~N meaning Sharp, or acute, in mind, applied to a man: and sharp in spirit, applied to a beast:] one says farasN Hadiydapu Alfuw^aAdi [ A mare sharp in spirit ]; and in like manner naAqapN [ a she-camel ]: (S and K in art. rwE :) and naAqapN ruwaAEapu Alfuw^aAdi , and ruwaAEu Alfuw^aAdi , a quick, spirited, vigorous, she-camel; sharp in spirit; syn. $ahomapN *akiy~apN . (K in that art.) [And TaAra fuw^aAduhu His mind or intellect, fled: and his courage. (See $aEaAEN : and TaAra .)]

sourceDefinition: Anything, (Msb, TA,) or any evil thing, (S,) excessive, immoderate, enormous, exorbitant, beyond measure, exceeding the proper bounds or limits, (S, O, Msb, TA,) or overmuch: (O, K, TA:) anything not agreeable with truth, and with rule or measure: (TA:) foul, evil, bad, abominable, or unseemly; [ gross, immodest, lewd, or obscene; ] applied to a thing or an affair, (Mgh, Msb,) and to speech or language. (TA.) It is said in a trad., He was asked respecting the blood of fleas, [whether it rendered a garment impure,] and said A_ino lamo yakuno faAHi$FA falaA baA^osa bihi If it is not excessive, or beyond measure, there is no harm in it. sourceDefinition: [ An excess; an enormity; anything exceeding the bounds of rectitude: ] a thing excessively, enormously, or beyond measure, foul, evil, bad, abominable, or unseemly; [ gross, immodest, lewd, or obscene: ] (Mgh:) or anything not agreeable with truth: (Lth, Mgh:) or a sin, or crime, that is very foul, evil, bad, &c.: or anything forbidden by God: (K:) or any saying, or action, that is foul, evil, bad, &c.: (TA:) and ↓ faHo$aA='u signifies the same as faAHi$apN ; (S;) or an enormity, or excessive sin, beyond measure foul, evil, bad, &c.; or a thing that reason disapproves, and the law regards as foul, evil, bad, &c.: (Bd in ii. 164:) the pl. of faAHi$apN is fawaAHi$u . (Msb, TA.) (Esh-Sháfi'ee.) And ↓ faHo$aA='u particularly signifies Niggardliness, tenaciousness, or avarice, (A, K,) in the payment of the poor-rate: or the abstaining [ altogether ] from paying it. (TA.) So in the Kur ii. 271. (A, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , applied to water, (T, S, M, &c.,) and furaAhN , both chaste forms, and well known, like taAbuwtN and taAbuwhN , (Towsheeh, MF, TA,) Sweet: (S, O:) or very sweet: (K:) or of the sweetest kind: (T, M, L:) or that subdues thirst by its excessive sweetness: (Bd in xxv. 55:) so called, accord. to Z, because it breaks the vehemence of thirst, and allays it; as though from rafata , and formed by transposition: (TA:) you say maA='N furaAtN , (S, M, O, K,) and in a copy of the K firaAtN also, (TA,) and miyaAhN furaAtN , (S, M, O, K,) and firotaAnN , (M, Msb, in copies of the K furotaAnN , and in the CK farotaAnN ,) like girobaAnN [pl. of guraAbN ], when furaAtN is pluralized, but this is rarely the case. (Msb.) ― -b2- AlfuraAtu signifies also [ The Euphrates; ] the river of ElKoofeh; (S, Mgh, O, * K; *) a great, celebrated river, which issues from the limits of Er-Room, then passes by the borders of Syria &c., and, after meeting with the Tigris, forms therewith one river, and pours forth into the Sea [or Gulf ] of Persia. (Msb, TA.) And AlfuraAtaAni is an appellation applied to [ The Euphrates and Tigris; i. e.] AlfuraAtu and dijolapu : or, accord. to the S [and O] AlfuraAtu and dujayolN [ The Euphrates and Dujeyl, which latter is a branch of the Tigris]. (TA.) ― -b3- Also The sea: (M, K:) so in a verse of Aboo-Dhu-eyb describing pearls as found therein. (M.)
