sourceDefinition: , (S,) aor. , (Mgh,) inf. n. naS~N , (Mgh, TA,) He raised the thing; syn. rafaEahu [which is here to be understood, like the English equivalent by which I have rendered it, in several senses, as the sequel will show]. (S, Mgh, TA.) This is the primary signification: (TA:) or, accord. to As, it is from naS~a Aln~aAqapa , q. v. infra. (S.) You say, naS~a AlEaruwsa , (M, K,) or naS~atohaA , (A, Mgh,) or naS~ahA Aln~isaA='u , (Msb,) aor. as above, (A, Mgh,) and so the inf. n., (Msb,) He, or she, or the women, raised, (A, Msb,) or seated, (K,) or raised and seated, (Mgh,) or showed, or displayed, (M,) the bride upon the minaS~ap , (M, A, Msb, K,) or upon the manaS~ap . (Mgh.) And naS~ati AlZ~aboyapu jiydahaA The doe-antelope raised, or elevated, her neck. (M, TA.) And nuS~a fulaAnN say~idFA (tropical:) Such a one was set up as a lord, or chief. (A, TA.) And naS~a AlmataAEa , (M, K,) inf. n. as above, (M,) He put the furniture, or goods, or utensils, one upon another. (M, K.) Hence, (TA,) naS~a AlHadiyva , (M, Msb, TA,) or naS~ahu A_ilaY SaAHibihi , (A,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M, Msb, TA,) (tropical:) He traced up, or ascribed, or attributed, the tradition to the author thereof, resting it on his authority, by mentioning him, or mentioning, uninterruptedly, in ascending order, the persons by whom it had been handed down, up to the author; or mentioning the person who had related it to him from the author, if only one person intervened; syn. rafaEahu ; (M, TA;) [i. e.] rafaEahu A_ilaY mano qaAlahu : (Msb:) IAar says, (TA,) Aln~aS~u signifies AlA_isonaAdu A_ilaY Alr~ay^iysi AlA^akobari (tropical:) [ the tracing up, or ascribing, or attributing, a tradition, in the manner explained above, to the greatest person of authority, here meaning Mohammad, or the author of the tradition]; (K, TA;) [i. e.] naS~u AlHadiyvi signifies A_isonaAduhu warafoEuhu A_ilaY Alr~ay^iysi AlA^akobari . (Mgh.) You also say, naS~a AlHadiyva A_ilayohi , (K,) or A_ilaY fulaAnK , (S,) (tropical:) He ascribed, or attributed, or traced up, the tradition to him, or to such a one, in the manner explained above; syn. rafaEahu . (S, K.) See also A^anaS~u . ― -b2- naS~a Al$~aYo'a (assumed tropical:) He made the thing apparent, manifest, plain, or evident; he showed it, exhibited it, manifested it, evinced it, discovered it, or revealed it. (M, * K.) [The verb seems to be thus used because a thing is rendered conspicuous by being raised. See naS~a AlEaruwsa , above.] ― -b3- [Hence, naS~a EalaY $aYo'K m~aA , aor. and inf. n. as above, (tropical:) He, or it, (generally said of a passage in the Kur. or a trad.,) made a statement, or a plain, explicit, unequivocal declaration, respecting some, or any, particular thing, not capable of application to any other thing: and he mentioned something, or anything, particularly, or specially; he particularized, or specified it by words; very frequently used in these senses: and such we are to understand from the saying] Aln~aS~u also signifies Alt~awoqiyfu waAlt~aEoyiynu EalaY $aYo'K m~aA : (K:) [for which I would rather read Aln~aS~a EalaY $aYo'K m~aA also signifies Alt~awoqiyfu waAlt~aEoyiynu : adding the observation that Altwqyf as syn. with AlnS~ is restricted in art. wqf in the K to a special relation to the law: and that Aln~aS~u EalaY Al$~aYo'i is often found explained as signifying taEoyiynuhu ; as, for instance, in p. 377 of Har.:] these significations of Aln~aS~u are tropical, from that word as denoting “ elevation ” and “ appearance. ” (TA.) See also naS~N below. ― -b4- [From naS~ahu signifying “ he raised it, ” and consequently “ he made it apparent, ” are derived several other significations, here following.] ― -b5- yanuS~uhumo [app. for yanuS~u maA Einodahumo ] occurs in a trad. respecting Heraclius, meaning (assumed tropical:) He elicits, and makes apparent, their opinion: (TA:) or naS~a Alr~ajula , (S, M, &c.,) inf. n. as above, (M,) signifies (tropical:) he went to the utmost point in questioning, or asking, the man respecting a thing, (S, K,) so as to elicit what he possessed [ of information respecting it ]; (S;) i. e. (TA) (tropical:) he importuned the man in questioning, or asking, and urged him to tell the utmost that he knew; (A, TA;) or (assumed tropical:) he questioned, or asked, the man respecting a thing so as to elicit the utmost that he possessed [ of information respecting it ], (M.) [See also 3.] ― -b6- [In like manner you say,] naS~a Aln~aAqapa , (S, M, Mgh, K,) and Ald~aAb~apa , (M, Msb,) aor. as above, (M,) and so the inf. n., (S, M,) He made the she-camel, and the beast, to exert herself to the full, or to the utmost, or beyond measure, in going, or pace; or to go the pace termed marofuwE ; syn. rafaEahaA fiY Als~ayori : (M, Mgh:) or he elicited her utmost pace; (K, TA;) from Aln~aS~u as signifying Alr~afoEu ; for the phrase rafaEahaA fiY Als~ayori necessarily implies the eliciting the utmost of her celerity of pace: (TA:) or he went a vehement pace so as to elicit the utmost that she possessed [ of celerity [: (As, S:) or he put her in motion so as to elicit her utmost pace: (A'Obeyd, TA:) or he urged, or incited, her, and elicited her pace: (Msb:) naS~a , alone, also occurs in a trad., (M, Msb,) as meaning rafaEa naAqatahu : (M:) and naAqatahu ↓ naSonaSa signifies the same as naS~ahaA . (IKtt, TA.) You do not say of a camel naS~a , making him the agent, and the verb intrans. (O, * TA.) [In the M, however, I find it said, that Aln~aS~u and Aln~aSiySu signify Als~ayoru Al$~adiydu ; app. indicating that they are inf. ns., of which the verb is naS~a , aor., accord. to rule, , signifying He went a vehement pace, or vehemently: and Golius says, as on the authority of Ibn-Maaroof, that this verb is used intransitively, with naSiySN for its inf. n., as signifying valide incessit: but see naS~N below.] ― -b7- [Hence, app.,] Aln~aS~u also signifies The urging or inciting [a beast]; syn. AlHav~u . (M.) ― -b8- And naS~a Al$~aYo'a , (M, K,) aor. , inf. n. naS~N , (TA,) He moved the thing; put it in motion, or into a state of commotion; agitated it; stirred it; shook it; (M, K;) as also ↓ naSonaSahu . (S, M, K.) Hence the saying, fulaAnN yanuS~u A^anofahu gaDabFA (K, TA [in the CK, incorrectly, yaniS~u ,]) Such a one moves about his nose by reason of anger. (TA.) And ↓ naSonaSa lisaAnahu He moved about his tongue; (S, M;) like naDonaDahu ; (M;) which is a dial. form; (A'Obeyd, S;) the former being the original; the S not being, as some assert it to be, substituted for the D ; for these two letters are not of the same kind so as to be commutable. (M.) -A2- See also 8.

sourceDefinition: , (S, M, K,) inf. n. naSonaSapN , (Sh, M,) He, or it, became in motion, or in a state of commotion; became agitated, stirred, or shaken; moved, or moved about,; bestirred himself or itself; shook. (Sh.) He (a man) shook in his walk, being erect. (M.) He (a camel) shook, or became in a state of commotion, in rising from the ground. (M.) ― -b2- [Also,] said of a camel, it is like HaSoHaSa ; (S;) i. e., it signifies (TA) He (the camel) fixed, or made firm or steady, his knees upon the ground, and put himself in motion, or in a state of commotion, previously to rising. (Lth, K, TA.) [See also naDonaDa .] ― -b3- And He (a camel) made a hollow place in the ground with his breast, in order to lie down. (M, TA.) -A2- naSonaSa used transitively, see 1, latter portion, in three places.

definition: The end, or extremity, of anything;
sourceDefinition: The end, or extremity, of anything; (Az, S, M;) the utmost, or extreme, extent, term, limit, point, or reach, of a thing: this is the primary signification. (Az, TA.) It is said in a trad., (S, M,) of 'Alee, (S,) A_i*aA balaga Aln~isaA='u naS~a AlHiqaAqi , faAlEaSabapu A^awulaY bihaA mina AlA^um~i (S, * M, K, *) or naS~a AlHaqaAy^iqi , (K, * TA,) but the former is that which is commonly known; (TA;) i. e. When women attain the period of mature intellect, (Mbr, S, K, TA,) and know the real natures of things, (K, art. sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. naEotN ; and ↓ AntEt ; He described, or characterized, or designated, (S, K,) a thing; (S;) syn. waSafa : (S, K:) or he described a thing by mentioning what was in it, or what it possessed; whereas, in the waSof of a thing one may exaggerate: (L;) [ he distinguished a person or a thing by an epithet: and hence, he qualified a substantive by an epithet: and he used a word as an epithet ] or he described a thing by mentioning what was in it that was good, or goodly; not with reference to what was bad. or foul, or ugly; unless by a straining of the meaning one say naEotN sawo'N ; whereas waSafa is said with respect to what is good, or goodly and what is bad, or foul, or ugly: (IAth: or naEata signifies he described by mentioning the make, or form, or other outward characteristic, as tallness and shortness; and waSafa respects action, as beating: or, accord. to Th, naEata signifies he described by mentioning something in some particular place in the body, such as lameness; whereas waSafa is used with respect to what is common to the whole, as greatness, and generosity; therefore God is an object of waSof , but not of naEot . (TA.) ― -b2- naEata nafosuh bAloHayori [ He described himself as possessing, or characterized by, or distinguished by, goodness. ] (Msb.) ― -b3- naEata , aor , inf. n. naEaAtapN , He (a man) was naturally endowed with powers of description, and skilful in the use of those powers. (L, K.) ― -b5- naEata , (L,) or naEita , of the same measure as fariHa , (K,) He (a horse) affected, or endeavoured, or constrained himself, to be, or become, what is termed naEotN , i. e., generous, or fleet, &c. (Abu-l-'Abbás, K.)

sourceDefinition: , (M, Mgh, Msb,) aor. , (M, Msb, TA,) inf. n. naqoDN , (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) He undid it; took it; or pulled it, to pieces: untwisted it: unravelled it: unwove it: dissolved it: broke it: or rendered it uncompact, unsound, or unfirm,: after having made it compact, sound, or firm: (JK, M, A, Msb, K, TA:) namely a building, or structure: and a rope, or cord: (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K, TA:) and silk, or flax: (TA:) and cloth: (L:) and (tropical:) a compact, contract, or covenant; (S, A, Msb, K, TA;) and (assumed tropical:) a sale: (Mgh:) and (assumed tropical:) other things; (A, K, TA;) such as (assumed tropical:) an affair, or a case; and (assumed tropical:) the state of a place through which the invasion of an enemy is feared: (TA:) contr. of A^aboramahu , (M, A, K, TA,) as relating to a building or structure, and to a rope or cord, (A, K, TA,) and to a compact or contract or covenant, &c.: (K, TA:) or i. q. Hal~a baromahu , as relating to a rope or cord, and to a compact or contract or covenant: (Msb:) or i. q. hadamahu , as relating to a building or structure: (TA:) or the inf. n. signifies A_ifosaAdu maA A^aboramota , as relating to a building or structure. (JK, TA,) and to a rope or cord, (JK,) and to a compact or contract or covenant. (TA.) [It is said in the K, that Aln~aqoDu is the contr. of AlA_iboraAmu , like AlA_inotqaADu and Alt~anaAquDu : but this is a glaring mistake; and seems to be a corruption of the following passage in the M: Aln~aqoDu Did~u AlA_iboraAmi naqaDahu yanoquDuhu naqoDFA waA@notaqaDa watanaAqaDa , which is meant indicate that AntqD and tnAqD are quasi-passives of naqaDahu : and in like manner, the passage in the A, Aln~aqoDu fiY AlbinaA='i waAlHaboli wagayorihi Did~u AlA_iboraAmi waA@notaqaDa wanataq~aDa , indicates that AntqD and tnq~D are quasi-passives of naqaDahu . Further. it should be observed that naqaDahu , as relating to a building, is not well explained by hadamahu ; for you say, naqaDa AlbinaA='a mino gayori hadomK , (mentioned in the S and A, &c., in art. qwD ,) meaning He took to pieces the building without demolishing, or destroying. ] ― -b2- [Hence,] naqaSa fulaAnN watarahu [lit. Such a one undid, or untwisted, his bow-string ]; meaning (tropical:) such a one took, or had taken, his blood-revenge. (A, TA.) And Ald~ahoru *uw naqoDK waA_imoraArK [lit. Time, or fortune, has a property of untwisting and twisting tightly ]; meaning (tropical:) that which time, or fortune, [as it were] twists tightly, [or makes firm. ] it, at another time, [as it were] untwists, or undoes. (TA.) And naqaDotu maA A^aboramahu (tropical:) I annulled [ what he confirmed, or made firm ]. (Msb.) And yanoquDu Ealayohi (tropical:) [ He undoes, or annuls, or contradicts, what he (another) has said ]; said of a poet replying to another poet. (Lth, A, K.) ― -b3- nqD Alsqf , [i. e., app., naqoDu Als~aqofi ,] also signifies tHryk x$bh [i. e. taHoriyku xa$abihi , The moving, or shaking, of the pieces of wood, or rafters, of the roof ]. (TA. [But perhaps the phrase to be explained is Als~aqofu ↓ naq~aDa , and the explanation, correctly, taHar~aka xa$abuhu , i. e. The pieces of wood, or rafters, of the roof moved, or shook, (for this, I am informed, is agreeable with modern usage,) app. so as to produce a sound: see also 5.]) -A2- See also 4.

sourceDefinition: is (tropical:) The saying that which is contradictory in its meaning [or meanings; as though one of its meanings undid, or annulled, the other]: (S, * K, TA:) from naqoDu AlbinaA='i : and meaning (tropical:) the contending with another in words, [or in contradiction, ] each rebutting what the other said. (TA.) You say, nAqDhu fiY Al$~aYo'i , inf. n. munaAqaDapN and niqaADN , (tropical:) He contradicted him in, or respecting, the thing. (M, TA. *) And qulotu lahu niqaADFA (tropical:) I contradicted him with respect to his saying, and his satirizing of me. (M, TA.) And nAqD A^aHadu Al$~aAEirayoni AlA^axara (tropical:) [ One of the two poets contradicted the other ]. (A.) And nAqD qawoluhu Alv~aAniY AlA=w~ala (tropical:) [ His second saying contradicted the first ]. (A, TA.) And nAqD A=xiru qawolihi AlA^aw~ala (tropical:) [ The last part of his saying contradicted the first ]. (Mgh.) [See also 6.]

sourceDefinition: , (M, K, TA.) and AnqD EanohaA . (M, TA,) He removed the crust of earth from over the truffles: (M:) or he extracted, or took forth, the truffles from the earth. (K, TA.) -A2- AnqD Alkamo'u The crusts of earth broke up ( taqalofaEato ) from over the truffle; as also ↓ naq~aDa . (M, TA.) [See also 5.] ― -b2- AnqDt AlA^aroDu The earth showed [or put forth ] its plants, or herbage. (M, TA.) -A3- AnqD also signifies It produced, made, gave, emitted, or uttered, a sound, noise, voice, or cry: (S, M, K, TA:) and [particularly] a slight sound like what is termed naqorN : (S, TA:) said of a joint of a man, (M, K,) and of the fingers [when their joints are made to crack], and of the ribs, (A,) [see also 5,] and of a camel's saddle, (A, TA.,) and of a cupping-instrument when the cupper sucks it, (TA,) [&c., (see naqiyDN ,)] and of an eagle, (S, M, K,) and of a hen (S, A) on the occasion of her laying eggs, (A,) and of a chicken, (M, A, K,) and of an ostrich, and of a quail, and of a hawk, and of a scorpion, and of a frog, and of the [kind of lizard called] wazag , and of the wabor [or Syrian hyrax], (M, K,) and of a young camel, the sounds of which are denoted by A_inoqaADN and katiytN , as those of a camel advanced in age are by qaroqarapN and hadiyrN : (S:) or A_inoqaADN relates to animate things; and ↓ naqoDN , inf. n. of naqDa , aor. and , to inanimate things. (M, K.) [Accord. to the A, whether said of animate things or of inanimate, it is proper, not tropical, but accord. to what is said in the TA voce naqiyD , it is properly said of animate things, and tropically of inanimate; though, if any such distinction exist, the reverse seems to me to be more probable.] ― -b2- You say also, AnqD biAld~aAb~api , (K,) or biAloHimaAri . (Lth,) or, as As says, (M, TA,) biAlEayori , (M,) or biAlbaEiyri , (TA,) and biAlfarasi , (M, TA,) He made a sound to the beast of carriage, (M, K,) or to the ass, (Lth, As, M,) or to the camel, (As, TA,) and to the horse, (As, M, TA,) at the two sides of his tongue, after making it cleave to the roof of his mouth, (Lth, M, K, TA,) without removing its extremity from its place, (Lth, TA,) in order to chide the beast: (L:) or AnqD bihi signifies i. q. naqara bihi [q. v.]; (As, M, A, TA;) the object being a [camel such as is called] qaEuwd ; (A;) or whatever be the object. (As, M, TA.) And AnqD biAlomaEozi , (S, Sgh, K,) or biAlEanozi , (M, A,) He called the goats, (S, Sgh, K,) or the she-goat; (M, A;) accord. to AZ, (S, Sgh,) or Ks. (M, L.) And AnqD bihi He made a sound to him like as when thou makest a smacking with the tongue to a sheep or goat, [in the TA, kmA tnqr Al$Ap , for which I read kamaA tanoquru biAl$~aApi ,] deeming him ignorant. (TA.) And He made a clapping to him with one of his hands upon the other, so as to cause a [ sound such as is termed ] naqiyD to be heard. definition: ― -b2- AlA^aroDu Eani AlkamoA^api The earth clave, or cracked, or burst, from over the truffles;
sourceDefinition: : see 8. ― -b2- AlA^aroDu Eani AlkamoA^api The earth clave, or cracked, or burst, from over the truffles; (S, A, * TA;) syn. tafaT~arato . (S, TA.) In all the copies of the K, we find tnq~D Ald~amu , explained by taqaT~ara ; [as though meaning The blood was made to drop, drip, or fall in drops; ] but how likely is this to be a mistranscription. (TA.) [The right reading of the phrase is probably tnq~D Alkamo'u ; and of the explanation, tafaT~ara ; and if so, the phrase is like A^anoqaDa Alkamo'u , and naq~aDa , explained above: see 4, second sentence.] ― -b3- tnq~D Alaboytu The house, or chamber, became cleft, or cracked, in several places, so as to cause a sound to be heard (K, TA.) And tnq~D is also said of a building, [app. in the same sense,] like ↓ naq~aDa . (TA.) [See naq~aDa Als~aqofu , in 1, next before the last break.] You say also, tnq~Dt EiZaAmuhu (tropical:) His bones made a sound [app. in being broken ]. (IF, K, TA.) [See also 4.]

definition: ― -b2- tanaAquDN also signifies (tropical:) Mutual contradiction, or repugnancy;
sourceDefinition: : see 8. ― -b2- tanaAquDN also signifies (tropical:) Mutual contradiction, or repugnancy; contr. of tawaAfuqN . (O, TA.) You say, fiY kalaAmihi tanaAquDN (A, Mgh, Msb, TA,) (tropical:) [ In his speech is contradiction, or repugnancy, between different parts; ] one part of his speech necessarily implies the annulment of another part; (Msb;) his second saying contradicted ( naAqaDa ) his first. (TA.) And tanaAqaDa AlqawolaAni , (A, Mgh,) or AlkalaAmaAni , (Msb,) (tropical:) The two saying, or sentences, contradicted each other; or were mutually repugnant; as though each undid the other; (Msb;) [ they annulled each other. ] And tnAqD Al$~aAEiraAni (tropical:) [ The two poets contradicted each other. ] (A, TA.) And tnAqD maEonaAhu (tropical:) Its meaning was contradictory. (S, * K, TA.) -A2- [It is also used transitively:] you say, tanaAqaDaA AlbayoEa (assumed tropical:) They two mutually dissolved the sale: as though compared with the saying taraA='awuA AlhilaAla , meaning “ they [together] saw the new moon; ” and tadaAEawuA Alqawoma , meaning “ they [together] called the people; ” and tasaA='aluwhumo , meaning “ they [together] asked them; ” notwithstanding that tnAqD is [properly] intransitive. (Mgh.) And tanaAqaDuwA Euhuwdahumo (assumed tropical:) [ They mutually dissolved, or broke, their compacts, contracts, or covenants ]. (T, voce tnAkvwA .)

sourceDefinition: i. q. ↓ manoquwDN [ Undone; taken, or pulled, to pieces: untwisted: unravelled: unwoven: dissolved; broken: &c. (Mgh, Msb.) ― -b2- (tropical:) Emaciated, or rendered lean, (S, M, K,) by travel; (S, K;) upon which one has journeyed time after time: (O:) Seer says, as though travel had unknit its frame; (M, TA;) thus indicating it to be tropical: (TA:) applied to a male camel, (S, M, K,) and to a horse, (M.) and to a female camel, (S, K,) or the female is termed niqoDapN : (M, K:) pl. (M, K.) ― -b5- Accord. to the K, i. q. nifoDN ; but the latter is a mistranscription; (TA;) Honey that has in it [ worms of the kind called ] suws ; wherefore it is taken, (M, K in art. nfD ,) and pounded, (K, ubi supra,) and the place of the bees is smeared ( yulaT~axu [in a copy of the M yuTobaxu , which is doubtless a mistranscription,]) therewith, together with myrtle ( A=s ) and the bees then come to it, and deposit their honey in it; (M, K, ubi supra;) on the authority of El-Hejeree: (M:) or the dung of bees in the place where they deposit their honey: (IAar, AHn, K, ubi supra:) or the bees that have died therein. (Sgh, K, ubi supra.) -A2- See also naqiyDN .

definition: (tropical:) A contradictor: applied to a man: fem.
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) A contradictor: applied to a man: fem. with p . (M, TA.) You say [also], *aA nqyDu *aAka (tropical:) This is a contradictor [i. e. the contrary ] of that: (A, TA:) [or this is inconsistent with that: for] Aln~aqiyDaAni laA yajotamiEaAni walaA yarotafiEaAni [ what are termed nqyDAn cannot be coëxistent in the same thing, nor simultaneously nonexistent in the same thing ]; as existence itself and nonexistence, and motion and rest. (Kull, pp. 231, 232) You say also, h`*ihi qaSiydapN naqiyDu qaSiydapi fulaAnK (tropical:) [ This poem is a contradictor of the poem of such a one ]. (A.) And Aln~aqiyDapu in poetry is (tropical:) That by which one undoes or annuls or contradicts [ what another poet has said ]: (S:) or naqiyDapu Al$~iEori consists in a poet's putting forth poetry, and another poet's undoing or annulling or contradicting it, by putting forth what is different therefrom: (Lth, K, * TA:) the subst is naqiyDN : [or rather this seems to be an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant, and syn. with naqiyDapN :] and the act of the two is termed ↓ munaAqaDapN : the pl. of naqiyDapN is naqaAy^iDu : (TA:) you speak of the naqaAy^iD of Jereer and El-Farezdak. (A, TA.) -A2- A sound, noise, voice, or cry; (Lth, S, M, O, K:) as also ↓ niqoDN accord to the K; but this is an enormous error: (TA:) the former, of the joints (Lth, M, K) of a man, (M,) [a meaning also assigned to niqoDN in the K,] and of the fingers, and of the ribs, (Lth, M, A,) and of camels' saddles, (S, K,) or of a camel's saddle, (M, O, K, [but in CK, for Alr~aHol , we find Alr~ijol , the foot,]) and of camels' litters, (S, K,) and of tanned skins, (K,) or of a tanned skin, (M,) and of a bow-string, (M, K,) and of nisoE [q. v.] (O, K,) when new, (O,) and of the sucking of a cupping-instrument; (K;) [in all these senses said in the TA to be tropical; but see 4;] and also the former, (S, M, TA,) in the K, erroneously, the latter word, (TA,) of an eagle, (S, M, K,) and of chickens, and of an ostrich, and of a quail, and of a hawk, and of a scorpion, and of a frog, and of the [kind of lizard called] wazag , and of the wabor [or Syrian hyrax; &c., see 4] (M,)

sourceDefinition: is applied to Men, and to jinn, or genii; (S, Msb, K;) but its predominant application is to the former: (Msb:) it is said by some to be applied to both in the former of the last two verses of the Kur, A@l~a*iY yuwasowisu fiY Suduwri Aln~aAsi mina Aljin~api waAln~aAsi [ who suggesteth what is vain in the breasts of people of the jinn and mankind ]; unless by it be meant Aln~aAsiY [the forgetting]; or mn Aljn~p wAlnAs is added in explanation of a preceding word, AlwasowaAs , or of Al*Y , or it is in dependence upon ywsws ; (Bd;) [but what corroborates the first explanation is the fact that] men and jinn are both termed rijaAl in the Kur, lxxii. 6; and the Arabs used to say, raA^ayotu naAsFA mina Aljin~i [ I saw people of the jinn ]: (Msb:) it is a pl. of A_inosN , (K,) originally A^unaAsN , (S, K,) a pl. which is rare [as to form]; (K;) or A^unaAsN is pl. of A_inosaAnN ; (M, art. A^ns ;) and nAs has the article Al prefixed to it, (S, M,) but not as a substitute for the suppressed ' , because, were it so, it would not be found prefixed to the original, A^unaAsN , whereas it is found prefixed to this latter: (S:) this derivation, however, from A^unaAsN , contradicts its belonging to art. nws : (MF;) [but some hold that it does belong to this art.; and the form of its dim., to be mentioned below, favours their opinion: Fei says,] it is a noun applied to denote a pl., like qawomN and rahoTN ; and its sing. is A_inosaAnN , from a different root: it is derived from naAsa , aor. yanuwsu , signifying “ it hung down and was in a state of commotion: ” and [agreeably with this derivation it is said that] its dim. is nuwayosN : (Msb:) some, again, said that Aln~aAsu is originally Aln~aAsiY . (L, TA, voce A_inosN .) See also A_inosN , throughout. -A2- See also nuwaAsN .

(TA.) ― -b2- ha*abahu , aor. , inf. n. ha*obN ; (K;) and ↓ h*~bh , inf. n. taho*iybN ; (S;) He cleansed it; purified it; cleared it. (S, K.) ― -b3- ha*iba , aor. , inf. n. ha*abN , It was pure, clear. (K: but only the inf. n. is there mentioned.) ― -b4- maA fiY mawad~atihi ha*bN There is no purity in his love. (TA.) ― -b5- ha*abahu , aor. , inf. n. ha*obN ; and ↓ h*~bh , (inf. n. taho*ybN , TA); He put it into a right, or proper, state; put it to rights; trimmed, adjusted, repaired, mended, amended, reformed, or improved, it. (K.) ― -b6- ha*aba Aln~axolapa He trimmed the palm-tree by clearing it of the fibrous substance called liyf . (K.) ― -b7- MF says, on the authority of the etymologists, that the original signification of ↓ taho*iybN and ha*obN is The clearing, or trimming, of trees, by cutting off the extremities of the branches, in order that they may increase in growth and beauty; that they were then used to signify the cleansing, or purifying, of anything; and putting it into a right, or proper, state; trimming it; or adjusting it; and clearing it of any dirty or filthy things, or the like, mixed with it; so that these became their proper meanings by general acceptation: and that they were then used to signify the trimming and embellishing of verse, and clearing it of whatever might vitiate it in the opinion of the chaste in language, and the philologists: but the truth is what is said in the L; that the original signification of th*yb is the clearing the colocynth of its pulp, and preparing its seeds so that they may lose their bitterness, and become sweet. (TA.) -A2- ha*aba , (aor. , inf. n. ha*obN , TA,) It (a thing) flowed. (K.) ― -b2- ha*aba , (aor. , TA,) inf. n. ha*obN and ha*aAbapN ; (K;) and ↓ Ah*b , (K,) inf. n. A_iho*aAbN ; (S;) and ↓ h*~b , (K,) inf. n. taho*iyb ; (S;) and ↓ haA*aba ; (K;) He (a man, &c., K, as a horse in his running, and a bird in his flying, TA,) was quick, or swift, (K,) in his pace or course: (TA:) he was quick in flying, in running, and in speech. (S.) ― -b3- ha*aba He ran vehemently. (As.) ― -b4- yh*b Alr~ukuwEa [app. yuha*~ibu yuho*ibu ] He makes the inclinations of his head and body [ in prayer ] in quick succession. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b5- See also art. hb* . ― -b6- ha*aba Alqawomu The people were very noisy, or clamourous, (K,) and loquacious. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [ (tropical:) The twanging of a bow, on the archer's loosing the string after drawing it; and of a lutestring: in the TA, i. q. ran~pN : pl. A^ahozaAjN and pl. pl. (TA.) ― -b8- hazajN Lightness, or agility. (TA.) ― -b9- Quickness in the falling, and putting down, of the legs [ upon the ground ]. (TA.) ― -b10- (tropical:) The sound of thunder. (S.) ― -b11- (assumed tropical:) The buzzing of flies. (L.)

definition: (tropical:) He called his companion.
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) He called his companion. And in like manner, A^ahabotu bihi A_ilaY Alxayori (tropical:) I called him, or invited him, to what was good. (MF.) ― -b2- AhAb biAlA_ibili He called to the camels, in driving them or urging them, by the cry haAbo haAbo . (K.) ― -b3- AhAb biganamihi He (a pastor) cried out to his sheep, or goats, in order that they might stop, or return: and AhAb biAlbaEiyri [ He cried out to the camel, for the same purpose ]. (S.) AlA_ihaAbapu is The crying out to camels, and calling them. definition: , with the s quiescent, is an adv.
sourceDefinition: , with the s quiescent, is an adv. n.; [as such written wasoTa , meaning In the middle of: in the midst of; or among; ] (S, M, IB, Mgh, K;) and it is for this reason that it has its middle letter quiescent, (S, IB,) like bayona (IB) with which it is syn.; (IB, Msb;) [for] it may be used in any case in which bayona may be substituted for it; (S, IAth, K;) and, like bayona , it does not denote a part of the thing denoted by the noun to which it is prefixed, wherein differing from ↓ wasaT . (S, IB, K.) You say, jalasotu wasoTa Alqawomi (S, IB, Msb) I sat [ in the middle of, or in the midst of, ] or among, the people, or company of men, (IB, Msb;) not being one of them. (IB.) And wasoTa raA^osihi duhonN [ In the middle of his head is oil ]; not meaning a component part of the head. (IB.) And it is said in a trad. AljaAlisu wasoTa AlHaloqapi maloEuwnN [ The sitter in the midst of the ring is cursed ]: for he must of necessity turn his back towards some of those who surround him, and so displease them; wherefore they curse him and revile him. (IAth.) ― -b2- It may not [properly] be used as a decl. n., (IB,) i. e. as an inchoative, (Mgh,) nor as an agent, nor as an objective complement; (IB, Mgh) &c.; thus, also, differing from ↓ wasaT ; unless it have the adverbial particle [ fiY ] prefixed to it; in which case it has the sense of wasaT , and you say, jalasotu fiY wasoTi Alqawomi and fY wasoTi raA^osihi duhonN [like as you say jalasotu wasoTa Alqawomi and wasoTa raA^osihi duhnN , explained above]: and sometimes it is used as a subst., preserving the quiescence [and the adverbial form], like as bayona is used as a subst. though virtually an adv. n., in cases like that where it is said in the Kur, [vi. 94,] laqado taqaT~aEa bayonakumo [meaning maA bayonakumo , or, as explained in the Expos. of the Jel., waSolukumo bayonakumo ]: (IB:) or wasoT is sometimes used for ↓ wasaT , improperly; (S;) or it may be so used; (Msb;) or it is so used by poetic license; (M;) or, as some say, each of them may take the place of the other; and this seems the most likely: (IAth:) or one says wasoT , with sukoon, only, of that whereof the component parts are separate, or distinct, (IAth, K *,) such as a number of men, and beasts of carriage, &c.; (IAth;) and ↓ wasaT , (IAth,) or both, (K,) of that whereof the component parts are united, (IAth, K *,) such as a house, and the head, (IAth,) or such as a ring: (K:) it is related, as on the authority of Th, that Al$~aYo'i ↓ wasaTu and wsoTuhu [both meaning The middle, or midst, of the thing ] are said when the thing is solid; but when its component parts are separate, or distinct, the word is wasoTN , with sukoon, exclusively. (M.)

definition: [The middle, midst, or middle part, of a thing;
sourceDefinition: [The middle, midst, or middle part, of a thing; i. e.,] properly, the part of which several lateral, or outer, portions are equal; as, for instance, the middle finger: but also meaning the part which is surrounded, or enclosed, on its several sides, although unequally: (Msb:) or the part that is between the two sides or extremities of a thing; (M, IB, Mgh, K;) [or the part, or point, that is between every two opposite extremities of a thing; and properly when equidistant; ] as, for instance, the centre of a circle: (Mgh:) as also ↓ A^awosaTu , (M, K,) which is [likewise] a subst., like A^afokalN and A^azomalN [but imperfectly decl. because originally an epithet]: (M:) wasaTN has its middle letter with fet-h in order that it may agree in measure with its contr., which is TarafN ; the like agreement being frequent: (IB:) and it is only used in cases in which bayona may not be substituted for it, herein [and in other respects, mentioned in the next preceding paragraph,] differing from wasoT : (S, IB, K:) [respecting the similar and dissimilar usages of wasaT and was~T , sufficient observations have been made in the next preceding paragraph, which see throughout, and more especially in its latter part:] the pl. of wasaTN is A^awosaATN ; and that of its syn. ↓ A^awosaTu is A^awaAsiTu ; or this may be a pl. of ↓ waAsiTN , and originally wawaAsiTu . (M.) You say, jalasotu fiY wasaTi Ald~aAri [ I sat in the middle, or middle part, of the house ]; (S, Mgh, Msb;) because wasaT is a subst. (S.) And A_it~asaEa wasaTuhu [ The middle, or middle part, thereof, became wide ]. (Mgh, Msb.) And Darabotu wasaTa raA^osihi [ I smote the middle, or middle part, of his head ]. (Mgh, * Msb.) And kasarotu wasaTa Alr~umoHi [ I broke the middle, or middle part, of the spear ]. (IB.) And wasaTuhu xayorN mino Tarafihi [ The middle, or middle part, thereof is better than the extremity ]. (Mgh, Msb.) And xayaru AlA^umuwri A^awosaATuhaA The best of affairs, or actions, or cases, are such of them as are between two extremes. (M. [See R. Q. 1, in art. Hq .]) It is sometimes put in the accus. case as an adv. n.; as in the saying, jalasotu wasaTa Ald~aAri ; but this is an instance of departure from the original usage; and [the meaning is jalasotu fiY wasaTi Ald~aAri signifying as explained above; so that] it is not here syn. with bayona , like as wasoTa is. (IB.) ― -b2- It is also used as an epithet: (IB, Mgh:) [as such signifying Middle; intermediate; midway, or equidistant, between the two extremities or extremes; in place, or position: but in this sense superseded in usage by ↓ A^awosaTu and ↓ waAsiTN and ↓ mutawas~iTN : and in time; but in this sense also superseded in usage by ↓ A^awosaTu :] middling; of middle sort, kind, or rate; (Msb;) as also ↓ A^awosaTu (S, * M, Mgh, Msb, K) and ↓ mutawas~iTN (M, Mgh, Msb) and ↓ wasuwTN (M, TA) [and ↓ wasiyTN ]; between good and bad; (Msb, TA;) as also ↓ A^awosaTu : (Msb:) conforming, or conformable, to the just mean; just; equitable: (Zj, S, K:) good; (Zj, M, Msb, K;) as also ↓ wasiyTN : (M:) most conforming, or conformable, to the just mean; most just; most equitable; applied to what is so of a thing; (S, M, K;) whatever it be; (S, K;) as also ↓ A^awosaTa : (M:) best; (Msb;) as also ↓ A^awosaTu : (S, * Msb, K *:) most generous: (M:) and when used as an epithet, it is applied alike to a masc., fem., sing., dual, and pl., subst.: (Mgh:) the fem. of ↓ A^awosaTu is wusoTaY ; (Mgh, Msb;) and the pl. masc. A^awaAsiTu ; and pl. fem. wusaTN . (Msb.) Hence, (Msb,) ↓ AlA_iSobaEu AlwusoTaY (S, Msb, K) The middle finger. (Msb.) And ↓ Alyawomu AlA^awosaTu [ The middle day ]. (Msb.) And ↓ All~ayolapu AlwusoTaY [ The middle night. (Msb.) And ↓ AlEa$arapu AlA^awaAsiTu , meaning The [ ten middle ] days. (Msb.) And AlEa$oru ↓ AlwusaTu , meaning The [ ten middle nights: not ↓ AlEa$oru AlA^awosaTu ; for this is a vulgar mistake, into which relaters of traditions have fallen; or it may be a mistake of transcription. (Msb.) And ↓ AlS~al`wpu AlwusoTaY , (M, Mgh, &c.,) mentioned in the Kur, [ii. 239,] (M, K,) meaning The middle prayer (Bd, TA) between the other prayers, (Bd,) or between the prayers of the night and the day; (TA;) or the most excellent of them in particular: (Bd:) i. e. the prayer of the afternoon; ('Alee Ibn-Abee-Tálib, I'Ab, and others, Mgh, Bd, K;) because the prophet said, on the day of the Ahzáb, “ they have diverted us from AlSlwp AlwsTY , the prayer of the afternoon: ” (Bd:) or the prayer of daybreak; (also said to be on the authority of 'Alee, Mgh, Bd, K;) because it is between the prayers of the night and the day; (Bd;) for the saying of the prophet mentioned above does not contravene this and other assertions, since what is meant in the trad. is not what is meant in the Kur: (K:) or, (M, K,) accord. to Abu-l-Hasan, (M,) the prayer of Friday; (M, K;) because it is the most excellent of the prayers; (M;) and he who says otherwise errs, unless he trace up the assertion to the prophet: (M, K:) these three opinions are of the strongest authority; (B;) and the first is that which commonly obtains: (Mgh:) or the prayer of noon; (Mgh, Bd, Msb, K;) because it is in the middle of the day: (Bd:) or the prayer of Friday on the day thereof; but on other days the prayer of noon: (K, and also said to be on the authority of 'Alec:) or the prayer of sunset: (Mgh, Bd, K:) or the prayer of nightfall: (Bd, K:) or [ the night-prayer called ] Alwitor : (K:) or the prayer of the breaking of the fast: (K:) or the prayer of sacrifices: (K:) or the prayer of the period called the DuHaY : (K:) or the prayer of the congregation: (K:) or the prayer of fear: (K:) or the prayers of nightfall and daybreak together: (K, and said to be on the authorities of 'Omar and 'Othmán:) or the prayers of daybreak and the afternoon together: (K:) or any of the five prayers; because before it are two prayers and after it are two prayers: (K:) or all the divinely-appointed prayers: (K:) or certain prayers not particularized: (K:) or prayer of middling length, between long and short. (K.) Hence also, $aYo'N wasaTN A middling thing; a thing of middle sort or kind; (Msb;) between good and bad; (S, Msb;) as also ↓ A^awosaTu : (Msb:) and in like manner it is applied to a male slave, and a female slave, (Msb,) and two male slaves, and two sheep or goats. (Mgh.) And maA tuToEimuwna ↓ mino A^awosaTi A^aholiykumo , in the Kur, [v. 91,] Of the middle sort of that which ye give for food to your families, (Mgh, Msb,) between what is prodigal and what is niggardly. (Mgh.) And ↓ Aln~amaTu AlA^awosaTu The middle class of men: occurring in a saying of 'Alee, cited in full in art. gT . (M.) And Eal~imoniY ↓ diynFA wasuwTA Teach thou to me a religion of the middle sort: occurring in a saying of an Arab of the desert to El-Hasan, cited in full voce faraTa . (M, TA.) And jaEalonaAkumo A^am~apF wasaTFA , in the Kur, [ii. 137,] (S, Mgh, Msb,) [ We have made you to be a nation ] conforming, or conformable, to the just mean; just; equitable: (Zj, S, IB, Bd, K:) or good. (Zj, Bd, Msb, K.) And maroEFY wasaTN Choice pasturage. (M.) And rajulN wasaTN A good man; as also ↓ wasiyTN : (M:) or a man having good grounds of pretension to respect. (TA.) And fiY qawomihi ↓ fulaAnN wasiyTN , (S, K *,) or bayonahumo , (as in some copies of the K,) Such a one is the best of his people (↓ A^awosaTuhumo ) in race, and the highest of them in station. (S, K.) And Ald~aAri waAlHasabi ↓ fulaAnN wasiyTu [ Such a one is of good quality, or of the best quality, in respect of tribe, and of grounds of pretension to honour ]. (Lth.) And huwa mino wasaTi qawomihi , and ↓ mn A^awosaTihimo , He is of the best of his people. (Msb.) And in like manner, huwa mino wasaTi Al$~aYo'i , and ↓ mn A^awosaTihi , It is of the best of the thing. (Msb.) And qaAla ↓ A^awosaTuhumo in the Kur, lxviii. 28, The best of them said: (Jel:) or the most rightly directed, of them, to the truth: (Msb:) or it means ↓ A^awosaTuhumo raA^oyFA [ the most remote, of them, from either extreme, in judgment ]; or sin~FA [ in age ]. (Bd.)

definition: A man (S) having his neck broken: (S, K:) and so mawoquwSu AlEunuqi : (A:) the fem.
sourceDefinition: A man (S) having his neck broken: (S, K:) and so mawoquwSu AlEunuqi : (A:) the fem. is with p : and ↓ waAqiSapN occurs in the sense of mawoquwSapN in a trad. of 'Alee, in which he is said to have given judgment in the case of the qaAriSap and the qaAmiSap and the ↓ waAqiSap , that the price of blood, or fine for homicide, should be paid in thirds; these being three girls, who were playing together, and mounted, one upon another; and the lowest pinched the middle one, who thereupon leaped off, so that the uppermost fell, and her neck broke; wherefore he imposed a third of the fine for the killing of the uppermost upon the lowest, and the like upon the middle one, annulling the third of the uppermost because she aided against herself: (Mgh, TA, in art. qrS , and Msb,) here, [accord. to those who hold that waqaSa is trans. only,] ↓ wAqSp is like raADiyapN , in the phrase Eiy$apN raADiyapN ; (TA, in art. qrS and in the present art.;) and is used in the place of mwqwSp for the sake of agreement in form with the two other epithets: (Mgh, in art. qrS , and Msb:) ↓ waqiySapN , also, signifies having her neck broken; and its pl. is waqaAy^iSu . (Meyd, as in Freytag's Lex., excepting that the pl. is there written waqaAyiSu .) You say also EunuqN mawoquwSapN A broken neck. (Msb.) And mawoquwSN is also applied to a camel, signifying, Become diseased in his back, and without motion. (Khálid Ibn-Jembeh.)

definition: , (S, M, A, Msb, K,) mina Al$~aYo'i , (S, A *, Msb,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, A, Msb, K,) mina Al$~aYo'i , (S, A *, Msb,) aor. yayoy^asu and yayoy^isu , (S, M, Msb, K,) the latter of which is extr., (Sb, S, M, K,) like yaHosibu , aor. of Hasiba , and yanoEimu , aor. of naEima , (As, S, TA,) and is of the dial. of the higher classes of Mudar, as are also the similar instances, but the former is of the dial. of the lower classes of the Mudar; (AZ, S, Msb, TA;) or, as Sb says, accord. to his companions, the verb was originally of two forms, yay^isa , aor. yayoy^asu , and yaA^asa , aor. yayoy^isu , and a compound [which is yay^isa having yayoy^isu for its aor.] was then formed from the two; but as to wamiqa , aor. yamiqu , and wafiqa , aor. yafiqu , and warima . aor. yarimu , and waliYa , aor. yaliY , and waviqa , aor. yaviqu , and wariva , aor. yarivu , in each of these only one form is allowable, with the kesr; (S, TA;) and some change the second Y of the aor. of yay^isa into A , and say yaAyasu and yaA='asu ; (Mbr, S, TA;) and I'Ab reads, in the Kur. xii. 87, yiyy^asu , after the manner of the dial. of those who pronounce the first letter of the aor. with kesr excepting such as is with Y [for its first letter], (K, TA,) which dial, is that of Temeem and Keys and Hudheyl and Asad; (Ks, Lh, TA;) the case of Y being made an exception by them because kesr with that letter is difficult of pronunciation; (Sb, TA;) but some of the Benoo-Kelb pronounce Y also with kesr, which is extr.; (Fr, Lb, TA:) and this is done in the instances of yiyy^asu and yiyjalu because one Y is here strengthened by another; (K, TA;) [I find also, in a copy of the M, yay^iysu , as an extr. form of the aor. of this verb, on the authority of Sb; but it is doubtless a mistranscription for yiyy^asu ; and there is another evident mistranscription in a quotation from Sb immediately following in that copy, relating to aors. of the form of yiyy^asu , which has been rendered correctly above, in the present work, from the TA;] inf. n. yaA^osN (S, M, A, Msb, K) and yaA^asN , (TA,) or yaA=sN , (as in a copy of the M,) and yaA=sapN ; (Ibn-'Abbád, M, K, TA [but in a MS. copy of the K I find it written yaA^asapN ; and in the CK, yaA^osap ;]) and A_iyaAsN is also used as an inf. n. of this verb, though properly an inf. n. of 4; (Msb;) He despaired of the thing; syn. of the inf. n. qunuwT , (S, A, K,) contr. of rajaA='N : (M, A, K:) or he cut off hope of the thing: (A, K: *) or his hope of the thing became cut off: (Mgh:) and ↓ A_isotayoy^asa signifies the same, (S, A, K,) in like manner followed by mano ; (S;) and so does ↓ A_it~aA^asa , (S, K,) [originally A_iytaA^asa ,] of the measure A_ifotaEala , but with incorporation [of the Y into the t ]. (S.) It is allowable to transpose the letters of yay^isa , so as to say A^ayisa ; but not those of the inf. n. (Msb.) There is not a word in the Arabic language commencing with Y followed by ' except yay^isa [and its derivatives] (IKtt) [and yaA^ayaA^a and its derivatives, and words commencing with an augmentative Y followed by a radical ]. The expression laA yaA^osa mino TuwlK . occurring in a description of Mohammad, means that his stature was such as would not make [one] to despair of his height; for he was nearer to tallness than he was to shortness: (K, * TA:) yA^s is here an indeterminate noun governed in the accus. case by the negative lA : (TA:) or, accord. to one relation, the words are, laA yaAy^isa mino TuwlK , [in the CK, erroneously, lA yAyasu ,] meaning, that his height was not despaired of; i. e., he who vied with him in tallness would not despair of him on account of his excessive height: (K, TA:) so that yaAy^is is here in the sense of mayow^uws , like maA='N daAfiqN in the sense of madofuwqN . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] yay^isato AlmaroA^ahu The woman was, or became, barren. (Msb.) ― -b3- yay^isa , (S, M, A, Msb, K,) aor. yayoy^asu and yayoy^isu , (M,) also signifies (tropical:) He knew; syn. Ealima ; (S, M, A, Msb, K;) in the dial. of En-Nakha'; (S, Msb;) or, accord. to El-Kelbee, (M,) or Ibn-El-Kelbee, (TA,) in the dial. of Wahbeel, a tribe of En-Nakha'; or, accord. to El-Kásim Ibn-Maan, of the dial. of Hawázin. (M, TA.) So in the Kur. (M, TA;) but I' Ab (M, TA) and 'Alee and others (TA) used to read A^afalamo yatabay~ani A@l~a*iyna A=manuwA ; and I'Ab said that he thought that the writer had written yayoy^as in a state of drowsiness. (M *, TA.) Soheym Ibn-Wetheel El-Yarboo'ee also uses the verb in this sense, in a verse cited in art. ysr , voce yasara , q. v. (S, M *). [Z-says,] You say, qado yay^isotu A^an~aka rajulu SidoqK , meaning, (tropical:) I have known [ that thou art a good man ], because with eager desire is restlessness, and with the cessation thereof is quiet and tranquility; wherefore it is said, AlyaA^osu A^aHadu Alr~aAHatayoni [ Despair is one of the two states of rest. ] (A, TA.)

definition: in rhetoric, [ Complication and explication, involution and evolution;

(TA, passim.) See Har, p. 383.
